home_pitcher_note: Peavy is coming off a season in which he unanimously won the NL Cy Young, also becoming just the second pitcher in 22 years to win the pitching Triple Crown. He'll face his buddy Roy Oswalt -- the two hunt in the offseason -- in this Opening Day tilt.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt will make his team-record sixth consecutive Opening Day start when he takes the mound at PETCO Park. Since joining the Major Leagues in 2001, Oswalt leads all pitchers with 112 wins.

home_pitcher_note: Young was on his way toward a big season, having gone 8-3 in the first half with a Major League-best 2.00 ERA and an All-Star Game appearance. But in July, he suffered an oblique injury that may have ultimately caused a lower back problem. Young is now healthy, having worked on strengthening his core during the offseason.
away_pitcher_note: The 2008 season could be a big one for Backe, who appears to be fully recovered from the September 2006 Tommy John elbow reconstruction surgery that kept him out of action for almost all of the '07 campaign. Backe made five starts in September, posting a 3-1 record and 3.77 ERA. He is 20-13 over 47 career starts, all with the Astros, with a 4.36 ERA. Backe has a 2-1 record and a 2.45 ERA over three games against the Padres, allowing five runs over 18 1/3 innings. The right-hander has a career road record of 8-10 with a 5.52 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Maddux won 14 games in his first season with the Padres to raise his career total to 347. He enjoyed a blissful stretch where he didn't walk a batter over 59 2/3 consecutive innings. In addition to winning another Gold Glove, Maddux issued 25 walks, his fewest since the 1997 season, while averaging a Major League-best 1.1 walks per nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez set a career high in strikeouts in 2007 with 158, the most among Astros pitchers. His home ERA of 2.94 was the lowest among National League left-handers, but he struggled on the road, going 3-10 with a 6.37 ERA. Rodriguez made a career-high 31 starts last year, posting a career-best 4.58 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf, a 2003 All-Star while with the Phillies, signed a one-year deal worth $4.75 million in the offseason. He spent last season with the Dodgers, but didn't pitch after July 3, and he underwent shoulder surgery in September to repair a frayed labrum. Wolf was 9-6 with a 4.73 ERA in 18 starts with the Dodgers. He's completely healthy now.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon, who signed on with the Astros after Spring Training was already under way, won a spot in the rotation with a solid spring showing. The right-hander went 4-3 with a 3.52 ERA over 60 relief appearances for the Pirates in 2007, and he was 1-1 with a 5.59 ERA over four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hill had a spring he'd probably rather forget. The young lefty did not walk a batter in 15 2/3 innings in 2007, but in 1 1/3 innings this year, he walked six. It wasn't pretty. He has to concentrate on keeping his shoulders level, and his mechanics in line, and then he'll be fine. He was 1-0 with a 3.32 ERA in three starts against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Sampson, who made the season-opening rotation for the second consecutive year, was 7-8 with a 4.59 ERA and a career-high 51 strikeouts over 24 appearances (19 starts) for the Astros in 2007. He struck out a career-high eight batters on April 28 against the Brewers, allowing one run over 6 1/3 innings for his third win of the season. He missed the last several weeks of the season with an elbow strain.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis battled all spring for this spot, competing with Ryan Dempster and Jon Lieber. Marquis was 1-0 with a 1.46 ERA in two games against the Brewers last year. He worked with someone this offseason on the mental part of the game in hopes of having a good full season, not a half. Marquis was 12-0 in 17 starts in which he went at least six innings. He's got to go deep.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt lost his Opening Day start to reigning Cy Young Award winner Jake Peavy, who shut out the Astros through seven innings. Oswalt said he had no feel for his breaking pitches, which forced him to use the fastball 85 percent of the time. As a result, hitters were fouling off multiple pitches, causing Oswalt's pitch count to skyrocket. The right-hander set a club record with his sixth consecutive Opening Day start. Oswalt has a career mark of 5-4 with a 5.28 ERA over 11 games at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano had to leave his start on Opening Day because of cramps in his right forearm. He did not give up a run over 6 2/3 innings, serving up three hits and walking one against the Brewers. He's had this problem before. What does he need to do? "Drink water," Zambrano said.
away_pitcher_note: Backe pitched well but took the loss in his first start of the year on Tuesday in San Diego. He yielded two runs over five innings in a 2-1 loss. Backe, who had Tommy John elbow reconstruction surgery in September 2006, displayed decent control, but he left a 90 mph fastball up in the zone to Scott Hairston, who deposited it into the left-field seats to give the Padres a two-run lead. Backe made one start against the Cubs last year, allowing four earned runs over five innings. Lifetime vs. Chicago, he is 2-1 with a 4.97 ERA over six games.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez will pitch the home opener looking for his first win of the season. The left-hander took a no-decision on April 2 against the Padres after yielding four runs over five frames. Rodriguez performs well at Minute Maid Park, as evidenced by his 6-3 record and 2.94 ERA at home last year. He made two starts against the Cardinals in '07, going 1-1 with a 2.40 ERA. He yielded four runs over a combined 15 innings. Lifetime versus St. Louis, Rodriguez is 1-4 with a 6.59 ERA over six games.
away_pitcher_note: The story for Wellemeyer remains the same: he's effective, but he needs to be more efficient. His first start of 2008 was much like a lot of his starts from 2007, as Wellemeyer tossed five good innings but threw too many pitches to be brought out for more than that. He's got the stuff to put hitters away, but his command is iffy at times. He's made three career relief appearances at Minute Maid Park, and the numbers aren't pretty -- a 14.54 ERA in 4 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chacon had an impressive first game with the Astros, pitching six solid innings against the Padres and getting a no-decision. He gave up two runs on five hits. He gave up a two-run homer to Kevin Kouzmanoff in the first inning, but settled down. He did have a little trouble with his command, walking four, but he also struck out four and got stronger as the game went on. The right-hander went 4-3 with a 3.52 ERA over 60 relief appearances for the Pirates in 2007, and was 1-1 with a 5.59 ERA over four starts. He started last year in the bullpen, moved to the rotation in May and back to the bullpen to finish the season. It appears that he will be part of the Astros' starting rotation this season. As manager Cecil Cooper noted, "if he pitches like he did against the Padres, he's going to win a lot of games for us."
away_pitcher_note: Thompson showed just how good he can be in his first start. Now he just has to do it again. The right-hander has a wicked sinker, but at his best, he can mix in a quality changeup and breaking ball as well, just as he did on Thursday. The pressure is on Thompson, because Joel Pineiro could return from injury as soon as Thompson's next scheduled turn. Either Thompson or Todd Wellemeyer would likely be the odd man out once Pineiro comes back.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson took a no-decision but pitched brilliantly against the Cubs on April 4, holding them to two runs over 6 2/3 innings. Sampson retired 13 of the first 14 batters he faced and yielded three hits over the first six innings. The right-hander was 1-1 with a 4.26 ERA over two games against the Cardinals last year, allowing six runs over 12 2/3 innings. Lifetime versus St. Louis, Sampson is 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This is what the Cardinals hoped they would be getting when they moved Looper to the starting rotation last season. He was quite effective at times in '07, but often didn't resemble the groundball specialist he had been in previous years. But in his 2008 debut, Looper induced 12 groundball outs against just three in the air, a very encouraging sign as he moves into his second season of starting.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt struggled again with his breaking pitches on April 5 against the Cubs at Wrigley Field, allowing six runs (five earned) on 10 hits over 6 2/3 innings. He felt a slight twinge in his right arm in the middle of the outing but assured his manager and head athletic trainer that the sensation went away in a short time. Oswalt gave up four hits to Derrek Lee, including a solo home run in the third inning. Oswalt faced the Marlins twice last year and allowed just two runs over 12 1/3 innings for a 1.46 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: In all probability, Nolasco will make this start, although it hasn't been made official. The right-hander projects to rejoin the rotation in this spot because Rick VandenHurk was optioned to Double-A following a loss to Pittsburgh on Sunday. Nolasco has made two long-relief stints, last throwing 2 2/3 scoreless innings in relief of VandenHurk. For the season, he has logged 5 2/3 scoreless innings. Before VandenHurk was optioned, Nolasco was going to phase into the fifth starter spot on Sunday at Houston. Now, he likely will slide up two days.

home_pitcher_note: Backe pitched well in his most recent outing on Sunday against the Cubs but had to settle for a no-decision in an eventual Astros loss. He yielded two runs over six innings, reaching the 100-pitch mark for the first time since 2006. Backe allowed 11 baserunners but worked out of several jams, including a bases-loaded situation with none out in the second. He coaxed a double-play ball from Carlos Zambrano and struck out Alfonso Soriano. Backe has faced the Marlins five times in his career and has a 0-1 record with a 2.70 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The team is exercising patience with the 22-year-old lefty. While he has a world of talent, Miller is definitely struggling. In two starts, he has logged a total of 7 2/3 innings, including a 3 1/3-inning outing at Washington on Monday. Miller was lifted in the fourth inning after he watched a four-run lead shrink to one. He was not involved in the decision on a night he threw 91 pitches. He's struck out nine and walked three while hitting a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez was in line for his first win of the season during the home opener on April 7, but Jose Valverde blew a three-run lead, forcing Rodriguez to take a no-decision. The outing was one of the strongest of Rodriguez's career, and manager Cecil Cooper said the left-hander "grew up a little bit" during that start. He shut out the Cardinals over 7 1/3 innings, allowing three hits while striking out six. He was efficient also, throwing just 91 pitches into the eighth inning.
away_pitcher_note: One of the six players acquired from the Tigers as part of the Dontrelle Willis-Miguel Cabrera trade, the 25-year-old Badenhop will be making his first MLB start. Impressive in Spring Training, Badenhop opened the season at Double-A Carolina, where he made one start before being promoted to replace Rick VandenHurk (optioned to Double-A) in the rotation. In his lone start for Carolina, he gave up one unearned run in 6 1/3 innings. A sinkerball pitcher, Badenhop logged 408 1/3 Minor League innings before getting his first callup.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has turned in two quality starts for the Phillies so far in 2008, rebounding nicely from a rough 2007. Eaton held the Mets to three runs in six innings on Thursday, before New York went on to win it in the 12th. Manager Charlie Manuel said that he has been impressed recently by Eaton's aggressiveness in the strike zone. In six career starts against Houston, Eaton is 3-1 with a 4.42 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon turned in a quality start in his last outing on April 8, but he did not factor in the decision. He yielded three runs over six innings in a Houston loss to St. Louis. He had control issues early, throwing more than 30 pitches in a second inning during which he walked three. Chacon said he didn't think he'd go deep in the game after throwing so many pitches so early. Chacon pitched in three games against the Phillies last year, allowing four runs over 2 2/3 innings. In his career, Chacon is 1-2 with four saves and a 5.87 ERA over 10 games vs. the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: The sophomore right-hander had a rough outing Wednesday, walking a career-high six in 2 1/3 innings. When he found the plate and forced the Mets to put the ball in play, his defense let him down, causing only one of the seven runs scored on his watch to be earned. He has never faced the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt is 0-3 for the first time in his career. The Houston ace has been hit hard, allowing 16 runs in as many innings and 32 baserunners. Opposing batters are hitting .400 against Oswalt, or 142 points higher than the career batting average against the right-hander. Oswalt is 5-1 with a 3.02 ERA against the Phillies for his career, though he allowed 10 earned runs in 12 innings (two starts) against Philadelphia last season.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Myers looked as comfortable as he's been since his return to the starting rotation. He allowed three runs over eight innings while striking out five and walking none to earn his first win of the season by beating the Cubs. In six lifetime starts against Houston, Myers is 2-2 with a 5.59 ERA. Myers' most recent start against the Astros was his final start of 2007 before becoming the Phils' closer.
away_pitcher_note: Backe teamed up with relievers Geoff Geary, Doug Brocail and Jose Valverde in a combined nine-hit shutout of the Marlins in his last start on Saturday, the righty's first victory since Sept. 29, 2007. Backe needed 105 pitches, including just 58 strikes, to get through five innings in a performance that he called "effectively wild." His defense bailed him out on a several occasions as the Marlins stranded 14 baserunners. Backe will need to have better command against a dangerous Colorado lineup. Backe is 1-0 with a 2.57 ERA in three career appearances vs. the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson struggled somewhat in his last start against the Cardinals. In that game on April 9, he gave up six hits and three earned runs in four innings. In two starts this season, Sampson has surrendered 12 hits and five earned runs in 10 2/3 innings. He has consistently been around the plate with just two strikeouts and one walk thus far.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching six scoreless innings against the Diamondbacks in his first start of the year, Morales struggled on Saturday, giving up seven runs and seven hits in just four innings, with Justin Upton's three-run homer in the fifth chasing him. Morales had his best stuff for just one inning, the fourth. He has dominating stuff, but his inexperience shows when he gets into trouble and can't make adjustments.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is enjoying a solid April, and his seven strong innings in Houston's 5-1 win over Florida on Sunday is making people take notice of the little lefty with the big curveball. Rodriguez's 2.33 ERA ranks among the Major League leaders, as does his strikeout total, which climbed to 19 with the seven he recorded against Florida. He's also spectacular at home. Rodriguez has allowed one earned run in 14 1/3 innings at home this season, good for a 0.63 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: For the second time, Cook pitched when the Rockies were in a losing streak and helped the club win. Cook went six innings and held the Diamondbacks to three runs and eight hits on Sunday. He ran into trouble in the fifth, when he left several sinkers up and eventually gave up a two-run triple to Jeff Salazar. But the anxiousness that dogged Cook in the past, especially when he was tabbed the Rockies' ace and had trouble controlling the urge to do too much, is not present this season.

home_pitcher_note: Chacon was brilliant in his last outing at Philadelphia, scattering four hits over eight scoreless innings. Despite lowering his ERA from 3.75 to 2.25, he didn't pick up the win as the Phillies rallied for four runs in the bottom of the ninth inning to win, 4-3. Chacon struck out five and walked two and threw 68 of his 109 pitches for strikes. This was Chacon's second straight quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez pitched well for four innings at PETCO Park on Tuesday night, displaying top-shelf velocity and an effective slider. But in the fifth, he committed a throwing error and relied too heavily on his fastball. The result was a six-run Padres inning in a 6-0 loss for the Rockies. Jimenez has bordered on dominant at points in all his starts, but must learn how to quickly find his rhythm when things get tight.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt had his best outing of the season with a strong seven-inning performance in a 2-1 victory over the Phillies on Wednesday. Oswalt lowered his ERA from 9.00 to 6.65 by scattering five hits and one earned run over the seven innings. He threw 92 pitches, 65 for strikes, and had excellent command of both his fastball and curveball.
away_pitcher_note: Germano allowed his first runs of the season in his Tuesday start against the Rockies as the Padres fell, 3-2. Germano's command early was shaky, as he walked two in the first inning. One of those walks came around to score. But to his credit he yielded just one run over his final five frames. This will be Germano's first look at the Astros this season. He lost to the Astros in his only start against them last season, allowing three runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Backe had a rough outing in his previous start at Philadelphia, giving up 10 hits and six runs -- five earned -- in three-plus innings of work. Backe only threw 61 pitches, walked two and also allowed a home run to Chase Utley. His command was off and he seemed to have a difficult time finding his rhythm early in the game. As a result, his ERA climbed from 2.25 to 4.26.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy was dealing Thursday when he pitched eight shutout innings against the Rockies. He struck out 11, walked three and gave up just four singles. The eight-inning stint was his second-longest outing of the season, eclipsed only by a complete-game victory over the Dodgers. On Opening Day this season against the Astros, Peavy tossed seven shutout frames and went 1-for-1 at the plate with a walk, a sacrifice fly and two RBIs.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo pitched 5 2/3 innings and allowed five runs (four earned) on eight hits with three walks and four strikeouts in a 5-2 loss to the Brewers on Friday. High pitch counts have continually marred his outings. He threw 26 first-inning pitches before finishing with 116. Arroyo is also putting the leadoff batter on base a lot. He did it in four of the six innings he pitched.
away_pitcher_note: Sampson had the shortest start of his career in his previous outing, lasting just two-thirds of an inning in an 11-5 loss to Colorado on Friday night. The right-hander changed his pregame routine and was also coming off the flu and a long layoff. He may have been too strong, as most of his pitches were up in the zone. Sampson said he would go back to the drawing board before this start. He's pitched well against Cincinnati, going 1-0 with a 2.93 ERA in 15 1/3 career innings, including two earned runs in seven innings in a start at Great American Ball Park last year.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto, who has not won since his first start of the season, will try to close out the Reds' homestand with a win. It will be his first time facing the Astros, and Cueto will be making his fourth straight start against an NL Central foe. In his last start against Milwaukee, Cueto walked two -- one more than he had all season -- while giving up two earned runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros are expected to call up Cassel from Triple-A Round Rock to make the start in place of the injured Wandy Rodriguez. Cassel, 27, was 1-1 with a 3.97 ERA in six games, including four starts, for San Diego last season. This will be his season debut for the Astros. The right-hander is 1-1 with a 2.50 ERA in three starts or Triple-A Round Rock. He appeared in five games, including a pair of starts, for the Astros during Spring Training, going 1-2 with a 4.85 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: It was ugly last time out for Looper, but that was somewhat in tune with what the Cardinals saw last year. Looper has rarely been so-so as a starter. When he's good, he gets deep into games and keeps the ball on the ground. When he's bad, he gets pounded. Looper must make the most of his rocky games while continuing to churn out the occasional gem. He has yet to go more than six innings in a start this season.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon has been Houston's hard-luck pitcher. He's pitched well enough to be 4-0, but has four no-decisions for his efforts despite going six innings or more and allowing three earned runs or less in each of his starts. His ERA for the season is 2.77. In his most recent outing, he gave up three runs on seven hits in six innings against his former team, Colorado, but was not involved in the decision. He pitched eight scoreless innings at Philadelphia on April 15, but didn't get the win because of a blown save by Jose Valverde. Chacon faced St. Louis at Minute Maid Park on April 8 and limited them to three runs on four hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright keeps churning out quality starts, keeping the Cardinals in games and giving the bullpen a breather. He's done a lot of good things this year, like allowing only one home run all season, but his calling card has been innings. In every start this season, Wainwright has pitched at least seven innings -- and yet only once has he gone past 107 pitches. Wainwright continues to establish himself as one of the NL's best.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt earned his second win of the year with a convincing performance against the Padres on Monday, holding San Diego to three runs over seven innings. Oswalt said he finally had a feel for his breaking stuff, which eluded him in his first three outings. The right-hander has allowed four runs over his last two outings after losing his first three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse gave up more than two runs for the first time in a game this season when he allowed four in four innings in a 9-8 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday. Lohse walked two batters and was constantly behind in the count. "I can't fall behind that many guys," said Lohse. He was tagged for four earned runs on eight hits.
away_pitcher_note: Backe pitched well enough to win in his last outing on Tuesday but had to settle for a no-decision when the bullpen blew a four-run lead against the Padres. Backe yielded three runs, all on one home run by Adrian Gonzalez during his seven-inning outing. The right-hander has held opponents to three or fewer runs in four of his five outings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Haren had a bit of a rough outing against the Dodgers his last time out as he allowed six runs -- five earned -- in just 4 2/3 innings. The Dodgers made the right-hander work hard early and simply wore him down. Haren threw 29 pitches in the first inning, 21 in the second and 26 in the third. Though he felt good coming out of the bullpen to start the game, Haren did not have his usual good command and that combined with the patient approach by the Dodgers proved to be his undoing. Haren was acquired by the D-backs from the A's in an eight-player deal in December.
away_pitcher_note: Sampson avenged his poor outing against the Rockies with a stellar start versus the Reds on Wednesday, allowing two runs over seven innings with a walk and six strikeouts. Sampson was efficient, needing just 88 pitches. The right-hander said he worked on several things in between his shortest start of his career and this one, including working to avoid flattening his sinker, which hurt him in his prior outings. He's trying to stay back on his back leg and drive more toward the plate. Sampson made two appearances versus the D-backs last year, allowing six runs over a combined 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez picked up his first win of the year in his last start on Wednesday as he allowed three runs on seven hits over 5 1/3 innings at Dodger Stadium. The D-backs prevailed, 6-4. His first start of the year came in Denver against the Rockies and he allowed just one run over five innings. He did not get a decision in the game, which Arizona won in 10 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cassel likely earned himself another start by performing well during his Astros debut on April 24 in Cincinnati. The right-hander yielded three runs over five innings and held the Reds scoreless through his final three frames. Cassel is not a hard-thrower, but he's consistently in the strike zone and gets quick outs. His effort vs. the Reds resulted in his second career big league win.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson had his finest outing last time out against the Padres at PETCO Park. The Big Unit picked up career win No. 285 by allowing just one run over six innings. Johnson has now made three starts since beginning the year on the disabled list due to back surgery and he appears to be rounding into form. His fastball picked up a couple mph's last time out and he seemed to have better command of it.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon has produced a quality start in each of his five outings with nothing to show for it. The right-hander walked six in his last start on April 25 against the Cardinals, but held them to two runs and took a no-decision when the Astros came back to win, 3-2. Chacon faced the Diamondbacks in one relief appearance in 2007, allowing one earned run over two-thirds of an inning. In his career, Chacon is 2-6 with five saves in 18 games against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt took a no-decision in his last outing on Saturday in St. Louis, allowing three hits over six innings and leaving with the game tied at 3 after the sixth. Oswalt has held opponents to three or fewer runs in his last three starts after starting the season 0-3 with a 9.00 ERA. Oswalt faced the Brewers three times last year, taking two losses and a no-decision. He yielded a combined 12 runs over 19 2/3 innings. Lifetime versus Milwaukee, Oswalt is 11-8 with a 3.66 ERA over 23 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva recorded his second straight quality start -- and no-decision -- when he battled the Florida Marlins on Saturday. The right-hander permitted two runs on six hits in six innings and did not walk a batter -- a welcome circumstance after 11 walks in his first 23 innings of the year. While seldom overpowering, Villanueva has done his best to remove his name from consideration for a demotion to the bullpen when Ben Sheets returns to the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Backe had four good innings and one really bad inning against the Cardinals on Sunday. The right-hander allowed three hits through the first four innings but was roughed up for four runs in the fifth, including a two-run double by Ryan Ludwick and a two-run home run by Troy Glaus. In five innings, he allowed four runs on five hits, walked five and struck out four. In six starts this season, Backe has only pitched more than five innings twice and has allowed three or more runs in each of his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Parra had a so-so outing on Sunday against Florida, allowing two runs on six hits with three walks in 5 1/3 inning. Parra's inability to escape the sixth inning in any of his starts this season remains a significant factor. "That's the only important thing to me right now," Parra said. "Obviously keeping the team in the game, but if you're going deep in the game, you're probably keeping your team in the game."

home_pitcher_note: Sampson yielded five runs over 4 1/3 innings but felt he pitched better than his stat line indicated. He had one big inning in the fourth, when he yielded a leadoff walk to Orlando Hudson and later gave up a two-run double to Mark Reynolds. Of Sampson's last three outings, he was effective only once. He'll face the Brewers for the first time this season and the fourth time in his career. In 2007, he appeared twice against Milwaukee, allowing three runs over seven innings. Lifetime, Sampson is 1-0 with a 4.00 ERA over three appearances, having allowed four runs over nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets returned to action after missing a turn in the rotation with a sore triceps and was not at his best. He set a career high with seven walks in just five innings, but he also limited the Cubs to three hits and escaped with his perfect record in tact and his 10th career win over the Cubs. He also has 10 wins over the Astros to go with a 3.78 lifetime ERA in 24 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Chacon had his least effective outing of 2008 in his last start on Wednesday, yielding five runs over five innings in an eventual loss to the Diamondbacks. Still, Chacon took a no-decision in that game, which brings his number of starts without a decision to a grand total of six. His most recent outing was the only one that didn't qualify as a quality start. Chacon faced the Nationals three times last year, allowing four earned runs over seven innings. Lifetime versus Washington, Chacon is 3-2 with one save and a 4.30 ERA over 11 appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Hill is coming off his best game of the season, when he gave up one run on four hits in eight innings against the Braves. He retired 14 of the first 16 batters he faced, but he ran into trouble in the sixth inning, when Yunel Escobar singled to right field to drive in Blanco and give Atlanta a 1-0 lead. A tough critic on himself, Hill was satisfied with his outing, but he still needs to work on his breaking ball.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt won his third consecutive decision in his last start, though he still says he has not had his good curveball on a consistent basis. Oswalt gave up four runs on six hits, including a pair of homers, in that outing May 2 against Milwaukee, but picked up the victory when the offense cranked out five home runs. Oswalt's personal winning streak is his longest since his six-game streak of July 20-Aug. 29, 2007. The right-hander is 3-1 with a 2.45 ERA in eight career games against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Perez ended up pitching another quality game last Thursday. He went seven innings and gave up the two runs on three hits against the Pirates. However, he got no decision for the fourth time this seaosn. Perez continues to say that he is not frustrated that he hasn't picked up a win this season.

home_pitcher_note: Backe picked up his second win of the season Saturday night with a good outing against Milwaukee. In 5 2/3 innings Backe gave up two runs on five hits. But he struggled with his control, walking five. He also hit his third career home run. Backe has faced the Dodgers just once, allowing three earned runs in six innings two years ago in a start at Minute Maid Park, and will be making his first start at Dodger Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: One thing that Lannan proved last Friday night: He is human. After three straight solid outings, Lannan was hit hard as the Nationals were pounded by the Pirates, 11-4. Lannan was out of the game after three innings. He gave up six runs, five of them earned, and all of them occurred in the third inning. The biggest blow came when Jose Bautista hit a three-run homer. Even in the first two innings, during which he didn't give up a run, it appeared that Lannan was in for a long night. The first hitter Lannan faced -- Nate McLouth -- was hit by a pitch. After two innings, Lannan had already reached 44 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: With the day off on Thursday, the Dodgers shift back into a four-man rotation and Lowe starts against the Astros. He went 1-0 against them in two starts last year, allowing one run in 11 innings. He's 2-2 lifetime with a 2.23 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Wandy Rodriguez's strained left groin still hasn't improved enough to allow him to throw a simulated game, so the Astros were prudently giving Moehler some simulated innings in preparation for this game or Friday's at Los Angeles. It will be Moehler's first start since Sept. 29, 2006, when he was with the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley pitched into and out of jams against the Mets, but despite four walks, he was good enough to limit the damage to one run over six innings for his second win. He faced the Astros twice last season, going 1-1 with a 3.86 ERA. He will be pitching on his regular four days' rest, as the Dodgers utilize days off to go with a four-man rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Sampson will receive an extra day of rest this time, with hopes that he can regain control of his fastball. Sampson has had two poor outings in a row, having allowed five earned runs in each start. The right-hander spent extra time between starts working with pitching coach Dewey Robinson in an effort to regain the control that has given him success in the past.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda had a tough night against the Mets. He lasted only 3 1/3 innings and was pitching out of the stretch almost constantly. He allowed eight hits and three walks and further complicated his job with a throwing error. He even lost command of his fastball, which has been his most consistent pitch this year. It was his sixth consecutive start without a victory.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon extended his club record of consecutive starts without a decision to seven when he faced the Nationals on May 6. The right-hander allowed four earned runs over seven innings but left with the score tied in a game the Astros eventually won. Chacon has a career record of 4-7 with three saves and a 5.85 ERA against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Zito pitched capably on Wednesday in his return to the starting rotation, allowing two runs in five innings in a 3-1 loss at Pittsburgh. Both runs Zito allowed came on a Xavier Nady homer in the fourth inning. Zito regained command of his fastball, for the most part, and changed speeds well with his curveball and changeup. He also struck out a season-high five batters. The Giants didn't score while Zito was in the game, which has been a common occurrence. They have averaged one run per outing while he's in the game. Zito defeated the Astros in his only career appearance against them last May 23, allowing one run and four hits in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt took a no-decision after yielding three runs over seven innings in his start against the Nationals on Wednesday. He yielded a two-run homer to Ryan Zimmerman in the first inning but also stuck out eight batters in the first three frames as part of a nine-K performance. Manager Cecil Cooper lamented the fact that Oswalt didn't get the win, saying, "he was the old Roy tonight." Oswalt has a 2-5 record and a 4.07 ERA over 10 career appearances vs. the Giants. Last year, he took a loss and a no-decision in two games but allowed only four runs over 14 innings for a 2.57 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Cain took a 4-2 lead into the seventh inning at Pittsburgh but was charged with three runs in a 5-4 Giants loss. This season has been somewhat of a disappointment so far for Cain, who has recorded three quality starts in eight outings. San Francisco is 3-5 when he starts. Cain did not face the Astros last season and is 0-1 with a 3.86 ERA against them in two career appearances. One of them was a relief stint of two perfect innings in May 2006 that turned Cain's season around.
away_pitcher_note: Backe lost his last start on May 8 against the Nationals, allowing four runs over six innings while striking out a season-high nine batters. Cecil Cooper said this was probably Backe's best outing of the year, stuff-wise. The right-hander has three career appearances versus the Giants, compiling a 1-0 record and a 2.03 ERA. He's allowed three runs over 13 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Misch has yet to win in 22 Major League appearances, including six as a starter. This will be his third start of the season, one as Barry Zito's replacement when the Giants' reputed ace spent a brief stint in the bullpen and two others as Kevin Correia's fill-in as the No. 5 starter. Misch lasted six innings in his most recent start, Friday against the Phillies, allowing four runs and six hits and leaving with the score tied.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros weren't sure what they were going to receive from Moehler when he slid into the rotation on Friday in Los Angeles to make his first start since September 2006. What they received from the veteran right-hander exceeded all expectations: five shutout innings on five hits, one walk, five strikeouts. Considered a stop-gap until Wandy Rodriguez returns from the DL, Moehler has earned himself at least another start.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum is having a terrific sophomore season but his last start may have been his most impressive. Facing the Phillies for the second time in six days, he made his longest outing of the year, going eight innings. He allowed only four hits, walked only one and struck out eight. So he gave up two runs (for only the third time in eight starts). No need to quibble: the Giants won, 8-2.
away_pitcher_note: Sampson bounced back from two poor outings to shut out the Dodgers through seven innings on Saturday, coasting to his second win of the season. The right-hander induced nine groundouts over a 103-pitch outing, walking one and striking out three. He's faced the Giants twice in his career, with good results. He allowed two runs over a combined 12 innings for a 1.50 ERA, logging one win and one no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Ponson struggled in his last outing, Sunday against Oakland, allowing six runs (all earned) on seven hits with five walks and a strikeout over 5 1/3 innings. He gave up four runs in the first, but then settled down and was able to make it to the sixth inning. Ponson said he didn't have command of any of his pitches and relied mostly on mixing up pitches. In his career against the Astros, Ponson is 0-2 with a 2.08 ERA. In Interleague Play, Ponson has a lifetime record of 8-14 with a 4.47 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: It's not exactly a record he's proud of, but it's a record nonetheless. Chacon has made eight starts this year and has yet to record a decision, the longest such streak in franchise history. He's also tied for the all-time MLB record for the most starts to begin a year without a decision. The right-hander has six quality starts, the most among all of Houston starters.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla hasn't pitched against the Astros since June 30, 2006, when he beat them, 4-1, at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington. He allowed just four hits and a walk in eight innings and struck out five. That was his first career victory against the Astros. Prior to that, he was 0-4 with a 5.68 ERA in 10 games, including five starts, against them. Lance Berkman is 8-for-16 with five doubles and a home run off Padilla.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt completed eight innings for the first time this year during his start on Monday against the Giants. He yielded three runs early but decided to stop pitching to contact and just be more aggressive. He struck out five in his final three frames to improve to 4-3. Oswalt lost his only start against the Rangers last year, allowing three runs over 6 1/3 innings. In his career, he's 4-3 with a 3.53 ERA in nine games versus Texas.

home_pitcher_note: Gabbard allowed two runs in 5 1/3 innings in his last start against the Mariners on Tuesday and was not involved in the decision when the Rangers won, 5-2. Gabbard has still never lost a home game in his short career. He has made 10 home starts for the Red Sox and Rangers and is 6-0 with a 2.70 ERA. He is 1-0 with a 4.30 in five starts for the Rangers at the Ballpark in Arlington. This will not only be Gabbard's first start against the Astros, but also his first start against any National League team.
away_pitcher_note: Backe lost his fifth game of the year in his last outing on May 13 in San Francisco, allowing four runs over six innings in a game the Astros were dominated by Giants pitching. Backe allowed three innings in the first, thanks in part to a mental error by Michael Bourn and a passed ball by J.R. Towles. Backe has faced the Rangers five times in his career, compiling an 0-2 record and a 9.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wandy Rodriguez will have to complete a Minor League rehab assignment before rejoining the Astros' rotation, so Moehler will receive his third consecutive start in place of the left-hander. Moehler took a no-decision after allowing three runs over five innings against the Giants on May 14.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly has reached double-digit strikeouts in back to back games for the first time in his career. On May 9, he fanned 10 Diamondbacks, and in his last start, he struck out 11 Padres. The lefty picked up wins in both games, and is now 3-0 in May. Against San Diego, Lilly gave up four runs on six hits over six innings. All the K's don't make him a power pitcher, though. Lilly still has to work on his breaking pitches, but he has been able to find one that works effectively in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson struggled in his last outing against the Giants on May 15, yielding seven runs -- five earned -- on 10 hits over six innings. It was a step back from his previous start, when he induced nine ground-ball outs over seven shutout frames against the Dodgers. Sampson faced the Cubs in his first start of the season on April 4 at Wrigley Field, taking a no-decision after allowing two runs over six frames.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster struck out a career-high 12 batters in his last outing against the Padres, and nearly posted a complete-game shutout. It's the first time he's pitched in the ninth inning since his days as a closer at the end of last season. The right-hander gave up six hits over 8 1/3 innings in his longest outing of the season. The Cubs now are 7-2 when Dempster starts.

home_pitcher_note: Chacon set the Major League record for most consecutive starts without a decision to start the season with his ninth in his last outing, but he needed help from the offense to get it. In his worst start of the season Chacon was raked for eight runs (five earned) on six hits and four walks in 3 1/3 innings against the Rangers. The right-hander said he didn't have good command of any of his pitches and that lack of control cost him dearly as he allowed a pair of homers to Josh Hamilton.
away_pitcher_note: Gallagher picked up his first big league win and decision in his second start, beating Pittsburgh, 7-4. The right-hander, who is the fifth youngest to start for the Cubs in the last 10 years, gave up one run on four hits and three walks over six innings. He benefited by the Cubs opening a 6-0 lead after two innings. He threw first-pitch strikes to 17 of the 24 batters he faced, which is a good ratio.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt was hit hard in his last start, allowing six runs on 11 hits before leaving the game in the seventh inning with a strained right groin. He is listed as day-to-day and his status for this start is uncertain. Oswalt had recorded six consecutive quality start before the outing at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington, and the 11 hits were the most the right-hander had allowed since Opening Day. Oswalt beat the Phillies at Citizens Bank Park on April 16 with a seven inning effort, allowing one run on five hits.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick's previous outing was a wash, literally, when a two-hour, four-minute rain delay ended his day after one perfect inning. Not including that inning, the right-hander has allowed three earned runs in each of his previous four outings, and pitched at least six innings in all of them. He has one career start against the Astros, and lost despite allowing two runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Backe turned in perhaps his best outing of the season in his last start, when he held Texas scoreless for 6 1/3 innings at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington before back-to-back homers by Milton Bradley and David Murphy ended his day in the seventh. Backe did not walk a batter for the first time this season, and combined with his one walk performance in his previous start, it's an encouraging trend for the right-hander.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander continued his downward spiral in his previous start. He was pulled after allowing four runs in five innings and allowed the first three batters to reach in the second inning, then surrendered a grand slam to Rod Barajas. The poor performances threaten his status as a starter, as manager Charlie Manuel could flip Chad Durbin to the rotation and demote Eaton to the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: This may be Moehler's last start, considering Wandy Rodriguez is due to come off the disabled list sometime early next week. Moehler yielded three runs over five innings in a loss to the Cubs, evening his record at 1-1. The right-hander threw a season-high 95 pitches, walking two (one intentionally) and striking out one.
away_pitcher_note: The struggling right-hander made some progress in his previous outing, Monday vs. the Nationals. He allowed three runs in six innings, and had a few positive results in tight spots. Considering how his season has gone, that has to be viewed as an improvement. He's 3-2 with a 4.91 ERA in seven career starts vs. Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson's up-and-down season experienced an upswing during his last start, after he held the Cubs to two runs over 6 2/3 innings in a winning effort that raised his record to .500. The right-hander yielded a two-run homer to Aramis Ramirez in the fourth inning, but retired nine of his next 10 batters. Sampson has not faced the Phillies yet this year. Lifetime versus Philadelphia, he's 0-2 with a 6.19 ERA over four games.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty hasn't given up a run since the fourth inning of a May 9 game against San Francisco, a span of 19 innings. Seven of those frames came in his previous outing against the Nationals, when he allowed four hits and struck out 11. It was almost unfair watching him make it look so easy. In four career starts against Houston, Hamels is 3-0 with a 3.14 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The good news: Looper hasn't allowed more than four runs in any of his past six starts. The bad: he hasn't allowed fewer than three runs in any of his past four starts. Still, there were some positive indicators in his last start. He struck out five, more than he had in three previous May starts combined. And for the second game in a row, he kept the ball on the ground. He's been good at home, and his best start of the year came against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon finally stopped a record he didn't want in the first place when he notched a win in the win column during his last start versus the Cubs. The right-hander previously had a nine-game streak of no-decisions, the most in history to start a season. Chacon was shaky in the first inning, yielding a two-run homer to Derrek Lee as part of a three-run frame, but he cruised through his final six innings, holding the Cubs scoreless on two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright righted himself, just as he expected he would, on Friday at Dodger Stadium. Now he comes home, where he's pitched very well this year (3-0, 2.70 in five starts). And he goes up against a Houston team he held down in an impressive, gutty performance earlier this year. He's the Cards' ace, and he seems to be back on track.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez, who has been on the disabled list since April 20 due to a strained groin, will be activated for this start at Busch Stadium. The only lefty in the rotation, Rodriguez is 1-4 with a 5.25 ERA in 10 career appearances aginst St. Louis, but he beat the Cardinals on April 7 with 7 1/3 scoreless innings (three hits allowed) with no walks and six strikeouts in a start at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse comes back home, where he's been pitching very well so far this year. He has a 3.48 ERA in seven starts at Busch Stadium, with 20 strikeouts against just eight walks. He turned in an excellent performance against the Astros at Busch Stadium earlier this year, and he'll be trying to do it again. He's coming off a pair of solid starts in a row.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt didn't fare well in his first start since suffering inflammation in his right hip, allowing five runs in a loss to the Phillies. Oswalt yielded 11 hits, the fourth time this year he's allowed double-digits in hits. The right-hander faced the Cardinals earlier this year on April 26, taking a no-decision after yielding three runs over six innings. He walked three and struck out five.

home_pitcher_note: Parra had mixed results in his outing in Washington, but was saved by an offensive comeback and recorded a no-decision. He struggled towards the end to keep pitches away from the center of the plate, and when he served up a 91-mph fastball to Aaron Boone that turned into a home run, it was the end of his day. He remains a solid starting option, but has work to do to become as consistent as teammates Ben Sheets or Jeff Suppan.
away_pitcher_note:
Backe has been pitching well of late, with consecutive wins (at Texas and vs. Philadelphia) in his last two outings. Better command has been a factor as Backe has walked just two batters total in his last three starts. 
Backe lost at St. Louis on April 27 when he allowed four earned runs in five innings in a 5-1 loss to Kyle Lohse and the Cardinals. The right-hander is 2-2 with a 5.86 ERA in 11 career appearances vs. St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets had a solid outing against Washington, picking up a no-decision after leaving the game in a pinch-hitting situation with a total of 86 pitches. He allowed a pair of runs early before settling into a groove and pitching four scoreless innings. His fastball was sharp, hitting 96 regularly on the radar gun, and he was in command of his breaking pitches. Sheets is one of the team's best players right now, and will open the series against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Although he was considered a fill-in for the injured Wandy Rodriguez, Moehler will remain in the rotation while Chris Sampson moves to the bullpen. Moehler made a case to stay in the rotation after going 2-1 with a 3.43 ERA over four starts. He pitched five innings in his first three outings and six innings in his most recent, which translated into a win over the Phillies. In his career, Moehler is 3-6 with a 4.21 ERA over 17 appearances versus Milwaukee, including eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bush surrendered solo home runs in each of the first two innings on Tuesday against Atlanta, then found a groove. He faced one batter more than the minimum over his final 5 2/3 innings of work, and pitched seven full frames for the first time this season. His only relief appearance this season came in Houston, just after Bush was recalled from a very brief stint in the Minor Leagues. He has surrendered at least one home run in five straight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon extended his winning "streak" to two games after logging a very convincing win over the Cardinals in his last start. The right-hander held St. Louis to two runs over seven innings, yielding two solo homers. Chacon also didn't walk anyone and struck out seven. He will face the Brewers for the first time this year. Lifetime versus Milwaukee, Chacon is 1-2 with a 3.33 ERA and two saves over 12 appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Who would have thought that Dumatrait would become the most consistent starter on this staff? His last start -- seven innings, two hits, seven strikeouts and no earned runs -- was further evidence of just that. The left-hander's confidence continues to creep higher, and matching it is the success he is having with his newfound changeup. The pitch sets up his fastball beautifully, and his propensity to throw it at any time in the count has really proven to leave hitters off guard. This will be Dumatrait's first career start against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez didn't do well in his first outing in six weeks, allowing six runs (three earned) in a loss to the Cardinals on Wednesday. The lefty threw 27 pitches in the opening frame and had thrown 76 through four. Rodriguez, who missed six starts because of a strained left groin, didn't have his curveball working, nor was his changeup very good. The left-hander was 0-2 with a 7.20 ERA over four games vs. the Pirates last year. Lifetime vs. Pittsburgh, Rodriguez is 2-3 with a 5.65 ERA over eight games.

home_pitcher_note: Duke pitched well to both sides of the plate his last time out and kept his pitches low -- always a barometer for success -- on his way to another quality start. No run support kept him from picking up his third win of the season. On another encouraging note, Duke allowed just five hits in six innings after struggling to limit the number of baserunners in most of his starts earlier in the season. Duke is winless in seven appearances (six starts) against the Astros in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt pitched well in his most recent outing vs. the Cardinals, despite taking a loss. He allowed three runs over seven frames, with the final blow being a decisive solo homer by Albert Pujols. Oswalt has a career record of 11-5 against the Pirates with a 2.49 ERA. Last year, he was 1-0 over three starts with an 0.87 ERA, allowing two earned runs over 20 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Dumatrait is scheduled to come off the disabled list after being sidelined with bursitis in his left shoulder. Dumatrait was roughed up in his two previous starts in Baltimore and Chicago prior to going on the DL, surrendering 14 runs in 10 innings. Dumatrait missed one scheduled start, on June 25 against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Backe yielded five runs in a losing effort his last trip to the mound against the Brewers on Friday. He yielded three homers, including a two-run shot to Prince Fielder. Backe had six days of rest between starts, which may have been too much of a layoff. The right-hander won his only start against the Pirates last year, holding them to two runs over six innings. Lifetime vs. the Bucs, Backe is 4-1 with a 2.86 ERA over eight games.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler absorbed his second loss after yielding four runs to the Brewers over five innings. He yielded a two-run homer to Prince Fielder on a poorly-placed changeup that sealed the loss. Moehler has faced the Cardinals once this year, in a relief appearance. He allowed one run in one inning of work.
away_pitcher_note: Looper's been decent lately, but it's been a while since he enjoyed a really good start. He's allowed at least three runs in each of his past six starts, and hasn't gone more than six innings since May 6. Even so, the right-hander hasn't been bad; he's only gotten knocked around twice this year, and for the most part he's keeping the team in the game. Looper has faced the Astros three times already this year, with two solid starts and a very rocky one the last time he saw them.

home_pitcher_note: Chacon suffered his first loss of the season in abbreviated fashion, throwing 40 pitches over one inning during a landslide defeat by the Brewers. Chacon yielded four runs, walked two and hit two. The right-hander has faced the Cardinals twice this year. He took a no-decision on April 8 at home, yielding three runs over six innings. On May 27, Chacon allowed two runs over seven innings in a winning effort at Busch Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright was inconsolable after his last outing, in which he was brilliant through six innings only to fall apart in the seventh. Historically, that's been a good sign. When Wainwright is disappointed in his game, he tends to bounce back extremely strong. He also loves facing the rival Astros, against whom he's tossed two excellent games already this season.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez earned his first win since April 13 after shutting out the Pirates on five hits over six innings. He regained control of his curveball, which had given him problems in his prior outing, which was also his first start after a five-week stay on the DL. Rodriguez faced the Cardinals earlier this season at Minute Maid Park, throwing 7 1/3 shutout innings and taking a no-decision in an eventual Houston win.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse endured an early-May slump, but it's definitely in the past now. He's working on a hot streak these days. Over Lohse's past four starts, he's allowed a total of four earned runs, with one home run and one walk. He's also been very efficient, averaging 14 pitches per inning in that time. It will be interesting to see how he recovers from his last start, in which he pitched only five official innings but sat out two lengthy rain delays and threw a great deal on the side.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt's breaking stuff was better in his last start, against the Pirates on Wednesday, but it still wasn't enough to win. The right-hander, with no help from a sluggish defense, yielded four runs (three earned) over six innings in a loss. Oswalt faced the Brewers in Houston on May 2, earning his third win after yielding four runs (three earned) over six frames.
away_pitcher_note: McClung's two hits against Arizona's Randy Johnson might have been the story on June 3 had McClung not pitched so well. He allowed a run on six hits in six solid innings and might have kept pitching had the Brewers not taken their first lead of the game in the bottom of the sixth inning. McClung did not walk a batter and was only at 79 pitches, but manager Ned Yost elected to remove him from the game with a chance to win it, and two relievers preserved McClung's victory. He has not faced the Astros this season in any of his 11 relief appearances or his three starts.

home_pitcher_note: After winning two games in a row, Backe has lost his last two starts. His most recent defeat came against the Pirates, who scored four runs off the right-hander over six frames. Backe faced the Brewers at Minute Maid Park on May 3, earning the win after holding Milwaukee to two runs over 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Parra has strung together consecutive quality starts, allowing one run and four hits in each of his last two outings. He worked six innings to beat the Astros on May 30, then came back to pitch a career-high seven innings on June 4 against the D-backs. He matched a career high with eight strikeouts in his most recent start and retired the last 14 hitters he faced. "We believe that we found my key, mechanically, so if I start rushing a little bit, Mike [Maddux, the pitching coach] is able to tell me a little key word that kind of gets me back on track," Parra said.

home_pitcher_note: Brian Moehler is coming of his best outing of the season, a seven-shutout-inning, two-hit effort against the Cardinals on Friday. The Astros have won four of his six starts. The right-hander lost to the Brewers on May 31 at Miller Park after allowing four runs over five innings, including a two-run homer to Prince Fielder.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets finally conquered Coors Field in his last outing, limiting the Rockies to a run in six innings of a no-decision on Friday. He should greatly benefit from the move back to sea level after abandoning his signature curveball in the thin Denver air. Sheets took a no-decision in a start at Minute Maid Park on May 5, when he surrendered four runs in 6 1/3 innings and was in line for the win before an Eric Gagne blown save.

home_pitcher_note: Chacon has faced his former team only twice, and is 0-1 with a 14.54 ERA against them in a 4 1/3-inning sample. After pitching generally well the first two months of the season, Chacon has been hit hard in back-to-back defeats. He lasted one inning at Milwaukee on June 1, when he gave up four earned runs on two hits. In his most recent start, the Cardinals hit for the cycle in the second inning while scoring seven times. Chacon wound up going five innings, so over his last two starts, that's 11 earned runs allowed on 12 hits over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Chamberlain threw a career-high 4 1/3 innings against the Royals in his second outing as a Yankees starter Sunday. The right-hander gave up five hits and three runs (two earned) before exiting to record the no-decision at Yankee Stadium. Chamberlain avoided deep pitch counts early on, throwing just 13 pitches in the opening inning, compared to 38 in his debut. The improvement allowed him to stay into the fifth inning before leaving with a pitch count of 78. Chamberlain again relied on his fastball and slider to strike out five, though he added an occasional curveball and changeup to the mix.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez could have, and should have, won his last outing, had it not been for a terrible defensive showing by his teammates. Rodriguez handled the Cardinals beautifully through six shutout innings, but the bottom fell out in the seventh, and the Cardinals scored four unearned runs. Rodriguez's home ERA continues to shine. The left-hander has a 1.08 ERA at Minute Maid Park over four starts this year, allowing three runs over 25 innings. Rodriguez has never faced the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Mussina came away with a no-decision in another impressive performance Monday afternoon against the Royals. The righty gave up seven hits and just two runs in eight innings. Mussina blanked Kansas City through the first six innings before giving up a two-run home run in the seventh. He got quick outs and avoided deep pitch counts, limiting his total to 89 throws. Mussina recorded three strikeouts and no walks in his 14th start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt turned in his best outing of the season during his last start against the Brewers, allowing Milwaukee's only run on a homer to right field by Ryan Braun in the third inning. In 99 pitches, the right-hander gave up just five hits while striking out a season-high 10 batters in seven strong innings. Oswalt has pitched only one inning against the Yankees in his career. He started the game that eventually became a six-pitcher no-hitter, but threw only one inning before leaving with a groin strain.
away_pitcher_note: Wang rediscovered his bread-and-butter sinker to throw 7 1/3 innings of one-run ball, defeating the A's on Tuesday at McAfee Coliseum and snapping a career-long six-start winless streak. Though it wasn't his most efficient start, Wang reviewed videotape and found he was lifting his left leg too slowly, which was causing drag on his arm speed. He will be making his first career start against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Olson found himself in trouble from the very first inning in his last start at Boston. He allowed five runs in the first frame against the Red Sox, an inning that included a three-run home from Jason Varitek, two walks, one wild pitch and an Olson error. But the lefty allowed two runs or less in each of his three starts leading up to that contest at Fenway, a stretch that included 13 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Backe yielded three home runs and gave up a total of five runs over four innings in a losing effort against the Brewers in his last outing. Backe has lost three starts in a row and has allowed 14 earned runs over that span. The right-hander has faced the Orioles five times in his career, allowing seven earned runs over 9 1/3 innings for a 6.75 ERA. He's 0-1 lifetime against Baltimore.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie has received little support in the seven games he's been charged with a loss. That didn'tt change against the Red Sox on Thursday, when Guthrie held the Boston lineup to one run on three hits through four innings before serving up a grand slam to Mike Lowell in the fifth. But Guthrie has allowed two runs or fewer in eight outings this season. Still, he's lost four of his past five decisions.
away_pitcher_note: After throwing his best outing of the season, Moehler had one of his worst, allowing seven earned runs over 4 2/3 innings in a home start against the Brewers. The right-hander yielded three homers, walked three and struck out one over an 86-pitch outing. Moehler has made six career appearances versus the Orioles, all starts. He's 1-1 with a 4.73 ERA lifetime against Baltimore.

home_pitcher_note: Burres had a rocky start last time out, when he allowed six earned runs in the first four innings but managed to escape the fifth and sixth unscathed. Prior to that outing, Burres had been knocked out before the end of the fifth inning three straight times. Burres went 2-1 with a 2.59 ERA in April and has gone 2-4 with a 6.70 ERA since then.
away_pitcher_note: Chacon bounced back from two bad outings to pitch well against the Yankees in his last outing. The right-hander allowed one run over 6 1/3 innings but took a no-decision. Chacon said he threw mostly sinkers and only a few changeups in that outing. Chacon has faced the Orioles four times in his career, recording a 2-1 record with one save and a 4.02 ERA. He allowed seven earned runs over 15 2/3 innings pitched. He did not face Baltimore in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Garza will be making his 13th start of the season and his first career start against the Astros. Saturday night at Tropicana Field, the 24-year-old right-hander earned his fifth win of the season after holding a tough-hitting Marlins squad to one run on three hits and one walk while striking out three in seven innings. Garza has a mid-90s fastball that sinks, a curve, a slider and a changeup.
away_pitcher_note: After turning his best start of the season on June 10, Oswalt took a step backwards against the Yankees in his last start, allowing seven earned runs on nine hits and four walks in 5 2/3 innings. Oswalt wasn't helped by some of plate umpire Marty Foster's calls, but he still threw too many hittable pitches and too often failed to put away hitters when he had the chance. Oswalt, 9-6 in 22 career Interleague starts, has never faced the Rays.

home_pitcher_note: The Rays right-hander is appealing his suspension, and it is likely he will not receive his appeal date before Saturday's start. Jackson is coming off Sunday's loss to the Marlins, in which the flamethrower was haunted by the long ball. A pair of three-run home runs ended up being Jackson's demise, as he was yanked after allowing six earned runs in five innings. He is at his best when he is mixing in offspeed pitches, and is often overreliant on his fast stuff. Saturday's start is expected to be Jackson's last appearance until June 28 in Pittsburgh, as the Rays have hinted at having the right-hander drop his appeal after facing the Astros, to avoid a shift in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Staked to a 3-0 first-inning lead against the Yankees in his last start, Rodriguez gave up five runs in the next two innings -- including walking in one run -- and left the game after five, trailing 5-3. It was the most earned runs Rodriguez had allowed in a game this year. The left-hander will be looking to put his control problems behind him and bounce back at Tampa Bay against a Rays team he hasn't faced before.

home_pitcher_note: The Rays' ace did not factor into the decision on Tuesday night for the first time this year. Kazmir was his typical dominating self, fanning seven Cubs and not allowing Chicago a hit until the fifth inning. Unfortunately, his season-high four walks drove the pitch count up quickly, and he was yanked after loading the bases with two outs in the fifth inning. It was the shortest appearance for Kazmir since May 4, his first start off the disabled list (left elbow strain). The Texas native will be facing the Astros for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Backe had one of his better outings of the year in his last start against the Orioles, but took a no-decision when the bullpen blew the lead late in the game. Backe yielded three runs over 5 2/3 innings, including a two-run homer to Aubrey Huff. The right-hander will face his former team, the Rays, for the first time since he was traded from Tampa Bay to Houston in December 2003.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler pitched brilliantly in his last outing, holding the Orioles to one run over 6 1/3 innings, walking two and striking out four. Moehler has held opponents to three earned runs or fewer in seven of his eight starts this year. Against the Rangers, Moehler has a lifetime record of 5-4 with a 4.96 ERA over 11 games versus the Rangers, including nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hurley has two no-decisions in his first two Major League starts, but the Rangers have lost both games late. His last start was against the Braves on Wednesday and he allowed just two runs in five innings. He allowed four in five innings in his first start against the Royals. Hurley was 2-5 with a 5.30 ERA in 13 starts at Triple-A Oklahoma before being called up but had a 2.67 ERA in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt was his old self in his last start against the Rays, allowing two runs over 7 2/3 innings with two walks and five strikeouts. The right-hander was locating his fastball well and had all of his breaking pitches working. Oswalt last faced the Rangers on May 17, exiting early with a tweak in his groin area. He yielded six runs over six innings in that start.
away_pitcher_note: To get another victory, Feldman might just have to toss a shutout. Against Atlanta in his last start, Feldman allowed just two runs in seven innings on five hits and three walks while striking out four. He departed with a 4-2 lead, but the bullpen cost him the victory. Nevertheless, if Feldman continues to pitch like he did against the Braves, his next victory will follow. Feldman faced the minimum in four of his seven innings and he retired 12 of the last 13 batters he faced. Feldman will take the mound in Houston on Wednesday with an extra day of rest. In 5 1/3 career innings against the Astros, Feldman is 0-0 with a 6.75 ERA, having allowed four runs on six hits and two walks with four strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez was in good form during his last outing on June 21 in Tampa Bay, allowing two runs over 5 2/3 innings while taking a no-decision. The lefty didn't allow a hit until the fourth frame and struck out six during his 100-pitch outing. At Minute Maid Park this year, he's 1-2 with a 2.10 ERA over five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood is 3-0 with a 4.22 ERA in five starts since coming off the disabled list on May 30. In 32 innings since then, he has walked 10 and struck out 25. He is 1-3 with a 4.40 ERA in seven starts on the road as opposed to 4-0 with a 4.86 ERA at home. Left-handed hitters are batting just .262 off him while right-handers are hitting .342. He is 6-3 with a 3.48 ERA in 10 starts in his career vs. the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez takes over Shawn Chacon's spot in the rotation and will face the Red Sox Friday at Minute Maid Park. The 30-year-old right-hander is 6-3 with a 3.72 ERA over 15 starts for the Triple-A Round Rock Express this year. He's allowed 35 earned runs over 84 2/3 innings and has allowed 11 home runs. He's issued 23 walks while striking out 63. Opponents are hitting .233 against him. Hernandez has made two career starts against the Red Sox, taking no-decisions in both. He has a 4.85 ERA over those two games, having allowed seven earned runs over 13 innings. His last outing versus Boston occurred on Aug. 10, 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka came off the 15-day disabled list for his last start against the Cardinals, and he looked nothing like the 8-0 starter that mowed down opposing lineups before suffering a right rotator cuff strain on May 27. Coming into his start against St. Louis, opponents were hitting .195 off the right-hander. But the Cardinals touched him up for four runs and five hits in the first inning alone. He faced 12 batters, leaving without recording an out in the second and giving up seven earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Backe earned his first win in a month when he beat the Rays in his last outing. The right-hander yielded a two-run homer to Evan Longoria in the second inning but held the Rays scoreless through the remainder of his 6 2/3 innings. Backe has appeared in four games against the Red Sox, all in relief. He has allowed eight runs over 5 1/3 innings for a 13.50 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lester is becoming one stingy innings-eater for the Boston Red Sox. In the month of June, he hasn't given up more than two runs in any outing while at least pitching into the seventh inning in all four starts. He's 5-1 since the beginning of May, and the Sox have won each of the five outings he's pitched in since May 31.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler has been the most reliable arm since joining the rotation. Counting his impressive performance against Texas on Tuesday night -- 6 1/3 innings, one run allowed on five hits -- the Astros are 5-4 in Moehler's nine starts but could easily be 7-2. Moehler is 4-3 with a 4.03 ERA. The 36-year-old right-hander is 4-2 with a 4.01 ERA in eight career starts against Boston.
away_pitcher_note: Beckett has allowed just two runs in his last two starts, against Arizona and Cincinnati, logging 15 innings in the process. Unfortunately for Beckett, his last outing, against the D-backs, went to waste when the Red Sox ran into Dan Haren, dropping a 2-1 decision at Fenway Park. Beckett is 2-2 lifetime against Houston and owns a 2.92 career ERA at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Though he took the loss in his last start, 3-2 to the Rangers on Wednesday night, Oswalt pitched well and has had five quality starts in his last six tries. He gave up three runs on seven hits in seven innings against the Rangers and is 2-4 with a 3.35 ERA in his last six starts since May 29. Oswalt is 4-3 with a 3.96 ERA in six career starts against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Stults, in only his ninth Major League start, threw a four-hit, complete-game shutout against the White Sox his last time out. Overlooked most of his Minor League career, he's the only Dodgers starting pitcher with a winning record. He was called up to make an emergency start in place of an injured Brad Penny, but now seems to have earned a spot in the rotation. He's a crafty lefty who throws strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez tied a career-high with nine strikeouts in his last start, a 7-2 win over the Rangers. The lefty held the top scoring offense in baseball to a run on five hits in eight innings. Rodriguez has allowed two earned runs or less in seven of ten starts. His ERA at Minute Maid Park over the last two seasons is 2.64. Rodriguez is 2-1 with a 2.29 in four career games (three starts) against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw continues to have the command problems to be expected for a 20-year-old. He issued two leadoff walks to the White Sox in his last start and both scored. He was lifted after four-plus innings, still winless, but all indications from manager Joe Torre was that the left-hander would remain in the rotation. Kershaw has issued 22 walks in only 33 innings and eight of the 16 runs he's allowed have reached base via walks.

home_pitcher_note: The 30-year-old right-hander went five innings against Boston in his season debut Friday night, allowing a three-run homer to J.D. Drew but not much else in a 6-1 loss at Minute Maid Park. Hernandez hit 96 miles per hour with his fastball but his offspeed pitches were inconsistent. He beat the Dodgers 3-2 in his only career start against them on June 14, 2005, when he gave up two runs in six innings of work in a start at Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda returns from almost three weeks on the disabled list to face the Astros. In his only start against Houston, Kuroda allowed only one run in 6 1/3 innings and left leading, but a bullpen meltdown cost him the victory. The Dodgers aren't sure how much to expect from Kuroda, so Chan Ho Park will be on standby. Park is coming off six scoreless innings against the Angels on Friday night.

home_pitcher_note: If Backe's roller-coaster ride continues, he's due for a good outing. Backe earned his first win in a month when he beat the Rays on June 22 with seven strong innings. The next time out he gave up six runs on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings against Boston Saturday night. Backe has no record and a 4.50 ERA in six career innings vs. the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Billingsley has a three-game win streak, the most recent being a bizarre victory in which the Dodgers scored the game's only run without a hit. Billingsley's outing was nearly overlooked, but he pitched seven scoreless innings, allowing only three hits while striking out seven. When he minds his tempo and doesn't rush, he's becoming close to dominating.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson was in the midst of a good season until Interleague Play, during which he went 1-3 with a 7.17 ERA.  In three career starts against the Astros, he’s compiled 24 innings and allowed just three earned runs. In his past two starts against them, he's totaled 17 innings and allowed just seven hits. The veteran right-hander is 6-1 with a 2.24 ERA in eight home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler has been impressive since joining the rotation, and in his last two starts -- 6 1/3 innings, one run allowed against Texas and 5 2/3 innings, one run allowed against Boston -- he was particularly impressive. The 36-year-old right-hander is 1-4 with a 5.12 ERA in 12 career appearances (five starts) against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes allowed one run on six hits in seven strong innings on Sunday against the Blue Jays, but he was saddled with the loss when the Braves dropped another one-run road game, this time 1-0. Reyes stranded a runner on third base in four innings. The 23-year-old left-hander was much more effective with his fastball than he was in his previous start, when he pitched 2 1/3 innings and gave up four runs. He is 1-0 with a 5.59 ERA in two career starts against the Astros, both of which came last season.
away_pitcher_note: Sampson gets the start in place of Roy Oswalt, who is healing from a hip abductor strain. Sampson opened the season in the rotation but moved to the bullpen after going 3-3 with a 6.04 ERA in 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Morton experienced the first rocky start of his young career on Tuesday, when he allowed the Phillies five earned runs and eight hits, including two homers in two innings. The 24-year-old right-hander hadn't allowed a home run in any of his previous 15 starts -- including 12 for Triple-A Richmond -- this year. Used primarily as a reliever last year, he has already thrown 18 1/3 innings this year, more than he did last year and within two innings of his 2006 total.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had a rare poor home start his last time out, allowing five earned runs over five innings, walking four and striking out five. Rodriguez has had more good outings than bad this year, and the club is confident he can be a force in the rotation now and in the future. Rodriguez has faced the Braves three times in his career, twice as a starter. The lefty is 1-1 with a 10.13 ERA vs. Atlanta, allowing 12 earned runs over 10 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Dumatrait is expected to come off the disabled list in time to make Monday's start. The lefty went on the DL with bursitis in his left shoulder, but is continuing to work through a throwing program in which he has had no setbacks. Dumatrait had been one of the Pirates' most reliable starters before his shoulder started giving him problems in June.
