He allowed a combined 14 runs in his past two starts (both five innings) after posting a 3.27 ERA in six May starts. Dumatrait took the loss in a start against the Astros earlier this season despite allowing just two runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez had a rough second outing, against the Dodgers on Wednesday, giving up four runs (three earned) on six hits in just five innings. He threw 79 strikes in the loss, including a solo home run to Andre Ethier. The right-hander, who now has given up seven runs on 11 hits with nine total strikeouts, has never faced Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Tuesday is the earliest that Snell is eligible to come off the disabled list, and the right-hander is expected to be ready. He took a week off from throwing to let the inflammation in his right elbow subside and has reported finally feeling better than he has in weeks. Snell threw his first bullpen session off the mound on Wednesday, and will throw at least one more before this start. Snell is 2-3 with a 3.91 ERA in nine career appearances (eight starts) against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Backe yielded five runs against the Dodgers in his most recent outing, giving up three runs in the first and solo home runs in the third and fifth frames. Backe has allowed a combined 11 earned runs over his last two outings. The right-hander has faced the Pirates once this year, allowing four runs over six innings in a losing effort. In his career, Backe is 4-2 with a 3.32 ERA over nine games versus Pittsburgh, including six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Van Benschoten jumps into the rotation as a result of the Pirates' decision to option Tom Gorzelanny to Triple-A. This gives Van Benschoten his chance to show that he is a capable Major League starter, something that he has not yet proven in his career. The righty has an 8.82 ERA in 16 career starts and has won just once. He is 0-2 in two spot starts this season and has allowed 12 earned runs in 6 1/3 innings. He has shown to be more aggressive in his outings out of the 'pen, so the hope is that he can bring that into this start.
away_pitcher_note: Location was a problem for Moehler in his last outing, a loss to the Braves during which he yielded five runs over six innings. The right-hander walked three, and two of those baserunners scored. Moehler has not faced the Pirates yet this year. Lifetime versus the Bucs, he's 3-4 with a 4.54 ERA over 10 games, including seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Redding didn't allow hits to translate into runs in his last outing in Cincinnati. The veteran right-hander allowed eight hits but just one run in six innings of work in the Queen City, striking out four. The game turned into his ninth consecutive no-decision, however, in a 3-2 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt is slated to slide back in the rotation after missing two starts with a sore left hip. Oswalt's most recent outing against the Dodgers on June 30 was cut short because of the injury, which was too bad for the Astros, considering the ace righty looked better than he had all year. Oswalt struck out nine Dodgers during his six-inning, 79-pitch outing.

home_pitcher_note: Balester struggled a bit more in his second Major League start than in his first, but he still turned in an efficient outing. The rookie right-hander gave up five runs and four hits over 5 2/3 innings, walking three and striking out three. He threw 102 pitches, 59 for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Assuming Sampson goes back to the 'pen and Roy Oswalt isn't ready to return to the mound, Rodriguez will remain on his regular schedule and open the series in Washington. The left-hander yielded three earned runs over 5 1/3 innings in his most recent outing in Atlanta. Rodriguez allowed seven earned runs over 5 1/3 innings in a start versus the Nationals last year. Lifetime against the franchise, he's 2-1 with a 5.34 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Perez didn't last long in his last start against the D-backs -- he was ejected after 2 2/2 innings for arguing a second balk called against him. The southpaw had just given up a run prior to the second balk that was directly related to the first balk. During the start, Perez walked one and struck out two. The Nationals bullpen pitched 6 1/3 innings of relief and allowed just one unearned run, but Brandon Webb shut down Washington's offense for a 2-0 Arizona win.
away_pitcher_note: Backe will get the nod for the final game before the All-Star break, and he should be well-rested. He threw only 48 pitches in his last start versus the Pirates, which was cut short when the game was delayed, twice. Backe pitched three scoreless innings in that game. He's 1-1 with a 3.85 ERA over two career games versus the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler ended his first half on a positive note, allowing four runs over six innings in a win over the Pirates. The right-hander allowed one run over three consecutive starts before yielding five to the Braves on July 4. Moehler faced the Cubs once this year, taking a loss after yielding three runs over five innings. Lifetime vs. the Cubs, Moehler is 1-1 with a 4.18 ERA over seven games (four sarts).
away_pitcher_note: Lilly is looking forward to getting off to a better start in the second half. The lefty did win nine games, but in his last outing July 10 against the Reds, he was pulled after 2 2/3 innings. It was his shortest start of the season. Lilly gave up four runs on six hits, including two home runs, in the loss. He was 7-4 in the second half last year.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has a 3-4 record and a 4.50 ERA over eight career games vs. the Cubs. He allowed eight hits over 5 1/3 innings against the Nationals on July 12, getting a win despite four earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: The All-Star right-hander will try to pick up where he left off in the second half. Zambrano held the Reds to one hit over eight innings in his last start prior to the break. Big Z was limited to 100-105 pitches in that game because it was his second start after being on the disabled list with a strained right shoulder. In his two starts since coming off the DL, he's given up one run on five hits over 14 innings. This was the second straight first half in which Zambrano won 10 games. Let's see if he can match that in the second half.

home_pitcher_note: Backe had one of his best outings of the season against the Nationals on July 13, shutting Washington out through seven frames on five hits. His previous start against the Pirates lasted only three innings thanks to a nearly three-hour rain delay -- he allowed no runs on three hits. He's 4-2 all-time against Pittsburgh with a 3.09 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster ended the first half on a sour note, suffering his first loss at Wrigley Field in 12 starts. The right-hander gave up four runs, seven hits and three walks over 6 2/3 innings in the outing. It's the second time in his dozen starts at home that he's given up four runs. Dempster faced the Astros once this season, May 20, and took the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez will look to avenge his last outing, which resulted in 10 runs over four innings in a start against the Pirates, after which he was optioned back to Triple-A Round Rock. He is still winless with the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Once again, the Pirates will need a spot starter. With no definitive replacement for Tom Gorzelanny, John Van Benschoten will likely get another chance to pick up his first win as a starter since 2004. Van Benschoten is 1-2 with a 9.77 ERA in seven appearances (three starts) for the Pirates this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Astros recalled Cassel from Triple-A Round Rock following Monday's game to replace the injured Roy Oswalt in the lineup. The righty won his sixth straight outing on July 18, allowing two runs on five hits against Omaha, and he has a 1.92 ERA in 10 starts for the Express. He recorded his first Major League win over six scoreless innings against Pittsburgh in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: A five-run outing over six innings in Colorado bumped Maholm's ERA up over 4.00 after he lowered it in each of his last five starts. Maholm was perfect for three innings, never letting a ball out of the infield.  His next three innings were a different story, allowing eight hits, including seven for extra bases.  He ran into trouble when he started elevating his pitches, and lost the lead on a broken-bat, two-run homer on a first-pitch changeup away. The loss broke a string of nine starts without Maholm suffering defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler continued his consistent performance on the mound with a no-decision against the Cubs in his last start. He allowed one run, a homer, on four hits in seven innings, striking out three. Moehler won his previous start against Pittsburgh despite four earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: Snell showed encouraging signs in his first start out of the break as he allowed three earned runs in six innings against the Rockies. Once again, his fastball velocity was consistently in the mid-90s, which, as a result, had Snell saying he felt as good as he has all season. Also, the July 18 start broke a string of four straight starts in which Snell was unable to pitch past the fifth. Snell is 2-3 with a 3.81 ERA in 10 appearances (nine starts) against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Parra is doing his best to imitate the Brewers' new co-aces. "With what CC [Sabathia] does and Ben [Sheets], it ups the ante," Parra said. "It makes you kind of want to taste the same thing they are and not have to use the bullpen." He came close on Sunday in San Francisco on the way to winning his eighth straight decision. Parra worked a career-best 7 2/3 innings, allowing only four hits through seven frames before the Giants rallied for three hits and two runs in the eighth. Both runs scored when Aaron Rowand's double popped in and out of Corey Hart's glove as Hart retreated to deep right field. Parra also set a career high with nine strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Rodriguez's first career start against Milwaukee in his fourth season in the Majors. Rodriguez comes off a very successful outing against the Cubs on Saturday, allowing just one run on nine hits against the division leaders. Rodriguez has been hit-or-miss this season but has showed a bit more effectiveness in his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: It's Bush's turn in the Brewers' fifth starter platoon. With the acquisition of CC Sabathia and Jeff Suppan being activated from the disabled list, there was not room for both Seth McClung and Bush in the rotation, so the Brewers are using them both. Bush gets the nod in home starts; he is 4-2 with a 2.49 ERA in nine starts at home and 1-6 with a 6.95 ERA in nine games, eight of them starts, on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Despite taking the loss, Backe pitched fairly well in his last appearance, a four-run outing against the Cubs. He left a few pitches up that the hard-hitting Cubs lineup took advantage of, but Astros manager Cecil Cooper was still impressed by the righty's performance. Backe lost his last start to the Brewers, giving up five runs on seven hits, including three homers, in just four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan returned from the disabled list on Tuesday and surrendered two Cardinals runs on four hits in his first inning. But he settled in after that, allowing four more hits and only one run through the seventh, leaving the Brewers in position for a comeback. Suppan was on the DL because of a tender elbow, and the "finish" returned to his pitches against the Cardinals, according to catcher Jason Kendall.
away_pitcher_note: Acquired from San Diego on Tuesday, Wolf will make his first start for the Astros in Milwaukee. Wolf was 6-10 with a 4.74 ERA in 21 starts for the Padres this season, allowing 14 home runs. The start will be Wolf's first against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Pending removal from the disabled list with a strained left hip abductor, Oswalt is scheduled to start against Cincinatti. His last start, against the Nationals on July 11, lasted just one inning as the righty threw 17 pitches. Oswalt has been struggling with the strain since June 30 and has seemed to get worse. He has not faced Cincinatti this season, but is 19-1 with a 2.46 ERA against the Reds all-time.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto reached his highest pitch count of the season -- 120 -- through just six innings of work against the Padres on Tuesday, but will be pitching on an extra day of rest. He gave up three runs on four hits with three walks and a season-high-tying 10 strikeouts. He last struck out 10 in his first start of the season April 3 against the Diamondbacks. All three of his earned runs against the Padres came in the sixth, after which Cueto still lobbied to pitch another inning. He was instead taken out and saddled with a no-decision. He is 0-1 through his last three starts and 2-4 through his last eight. Cueto last faced the Astros on April 24 when he pitched seven innings, giving up five runs on eight hits with two walks and two strikeouts in receiving the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler, who has been the most consistent starter for the Astros all season, had an uncharacteristically bad performance in his last outing. The righty lasted just 2 1/3 innings last Wednesday and gave up six runs -- five of which were earned -- on nine hits. He'll be making his first start of the year against the Reds, and it will come at home, where he is 3-2 with a 4.32 ERA in 11 appearances this season.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo has won five straight games since he suffered the worst outing of his career on June 24 at Toronto. In his last start, he beat the Padres with seven solid innings, allowing just three runs on four hits with no walks and seven strikeouts. Through his last five starts, Arroyo is 5-0 with a 3.19 ERA. He last faced the Astros on April 23 when he gave up eight runs on 10 hits with a walk and five strikeouts in 3 2/3 innings of a losing effort.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had a brilliant performance in his last start on the road against the Brewers. The Astros rode the lefty's strong performance to a 3-1 win as allowed just one run on three hits over six innings of work. Houston had come into the game having lost four in a row, but Rodriguez snapped the streak with his great outing. He'll have a tough test against Cincinnati, against whom he's struggled over the last three seasons (2-2, 5.60 ERA in seven starts).
away_pitcher_note: Volquez struggled for the second consecutive outing and once again had problems getting and staying ahead in the count. The result was an uninspiring four-inning performance in which he gave up five runs on seven hits with no walks and two strikeouts. He threw 99 pitches in the short outing, with just 59 of them going for strikes. He's allowed nine runs over his past two starts and has had his share of trouble with commanding the strike zone and locating his pitches. His strikeout totals have also fallen off considerably. Though he struck out 10 on July 12 at Milwaukee, he's struck out more than three batters just once through his past six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Backe had a decent start in his last time out, earning a no-decision in the Astros' 6-4 loss to the Brewers. The Houston offense had a tough time at the plate with runners on base, scoring just four runs in support of Backe even though they racked up 14 hits. Backe will be making his firsts start of the season against the Mets and has historically doesn't have much experience against them, going 1-1 with a 4.41 ERA against New York over the last three seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Jerry Manuel is hoping that Martinez -- who has been grieving his father's death in the Dominican -- can be ready to start the opening game of the Astros series Friday. By then, his time on the bereavement list will have passed, and Manuel hopes to have Martinez pitching against Minor League hitters in Port St. Lucie or with the Mets in Miami. If he pitches on Tuesday, Martinez will be ready for a Friday start, and if the warm-up session is moved to Wednesday, Johan Santana can move up to Friday and let Martinez slide back to Saturday. Martinez hasn't pitched since before the All-Star break when he tweaked his right groin in a four-inning, zero-run affair against the Rockies July 12.

home_pitcher_note: Assuming Oswalt stays on his regular schedule with four days of rest between starts, he'll take the hill for the middle game against the Mets. Oswalt won his last outing in his first start back from the disabled list, topping the Reds after allowing four runs over five innings. Oswalt compiled a 1-1 record and a 4.50 ERA over two starts against the Mets in 2007. In his career versus the Mets, Oswalt is 5-4 with a 3.52 ERA over 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Santana pitched the Mets' first complete game since Oliver Perez turned one in in 2006, allowing six hits and one run to the Cardinals on Sunday. He faced the minimum through the first four innings, and Santana's lone blemish came on a solo home run in the seventh inning. After taking some heat for bowing out before the ninth inning in a start against the Phillies, Santana demanded the ball in the final frame and finished with 118 pitches -- three above the number manager Jerry Manuel had in mind. In five innings at Minute Maid Park, Santana has allowed one career run.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf will slide in behind Oswalt, which means he gets an extra two days of rest before this start. Wolf made his Astros debut in Milwaukee on July 27, allowing four runs (three earned) over 4 1/3 innings. Wolf faced the Mets once this year while with the Padres, allowing one run over seven inning in a winning effort. Wolf has good career numbers against the Mets -- 10 wins, 5 losses and a 3.35 ERA over 26 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Because the Mets scratched John Maine from Sunday's start with a mild strain of his right rotator cuff, Perez will take his turn in the rotation. Perez, thanks to an off-day on Thursday, will pitch on regular rest. Despite the relative brevity of his outing last Tuesday -- he had lasted at least seven innings in three of his previous five starts -- Perez was every bit as effective as he has been in recent weeks. Over his six most recent outings, Perez has posted a 1.36 ERA with 44 strikeouts and 15 walks.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster held the Brewers to one run on five hits and struck out nine over seven innings in his most recent start. The right-hander picked up his second straight win on the road, so that's not a problem any more. He was able to hide his delivery so well, the Brewers couldn't tell when he was throwing his fastball and when it was his split. His approach was to get ahead in the count, and it worked. He is 1-1 vs. Houston this year, with a win July 20.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler fell one out shy of his 11th career complete game and his first in eight years during his last start against the Reds, but the right-hander still walked away with his sixth win of the year. Moehler pitched well in his last outing against the Cubs, allowing one run over seven innings while taking a no-decision on July 18 at Minute Maid Park. He also faced them on May 19, allowing three runs over five innings in a losing effort.
summary: 2008-08-04 - Houston Astros @ Chicago Cubs (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Harden finally got his first win with the Cubs. The right-hander had fanned 10 in each of his first three starts for Chicago, but in his fourth against the Brewers, he struck out nine and got the "W." Harden gave up one run on a solo homer by Prince Fielder. In fact, he's given up three runs in his four starts with the Cubs, and all have been on solo homers.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struggled in his last start against the Reds, even though only one of the five runs he allowed was categorized as earned. Rodriguez allowed six runs on nine hits, including two home runs to Adam Dunn and another three-run shot to Ken Griffey Jr. in the series finale. The last time Rodriguez faced the Cubs, he dominated. On July 19 at Minute Maid Park, he yielded one earned run over 6 2/3 innings in a winning effort.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis took the loss in his last outing, against the Pirates. The right-hander gave up three runs on eight hits over six innings and struck out two, but he didn't get any run support, as the Cubs were shut out at home for the first time this season. Marquis did post his ninth quality start, but he has lost his past four decisions. The Cubs have scored one run or fewer when he's on the mound in five of his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Backe took a no-decision in his last outing but pitched well enough to win, allowing three runs over six-plus innings to the Mets in a game later won on Mark Loretta's pinch-hit homer. Backe last faced the Cubs on June 20 at Minute Maid Park and yielded four runs over 6 2/3 innings, striking out eight. Backe is 3-6 with a 4.50 ERA over 13 games on the road this year. He has allowed 35 runs over 70 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Fogg gave up three earned runs and six hits over 5 1/3 innings after recovering from a shaky first inning. He worked out of jams in the second and third innings and had a much better outing that his previous one when he was shelled in an 11-0 loss. This time after being in line for a win, the bullpen blew a two-run lead as Cincinnati went on to a 10-6 loss to the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt seems to be back to normal following his second start off the DL. He gave up four runs on six hits in a comeback win against the Mets in his last outing, but Cooper said he pitched better than his numbers showed. Oswalt said he feels better, although it still takes him a bit to get warm. Oswalt is 20-1 with a 2.61 ERA all-time against Cincinnati, the lone loss coming in 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto got roughed up early before settling down on Sunday in Washington, D.C. He struck out the first two batters he faced, but a Lastings Milledge homer sparked a four-run first inning, all the Nationals would need in a 4-1 win over the Reds. Cueto struck out four and walked one, throwing 86 pitches -- 53 for strikes -- over his six-inning start.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf looked much more effective in his second outing for Houston, tossing five shutout innings in which he struck out seven and walked three. Wolf is 7-2 with a 3.20 ERA lifetime against Cincinnati. He won his only game against the Reds this season, allowing two runs on four hits in seven innings, striking out nine.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo had his best outing since the Fourth of July in holding the Brewers to one run over six innings in his last start. At times, he looked dominant. Mixing his pitches masterfully, Arroyo gave up four hits, struck out six and walked a pair. His 111 pitches included 72 strikes, which is the kind of strike-to-ball ratio any pitcher can live with. He displayed pinpoint control, something that highlighted his work a season ago but that has eluded the righty time and again this season. But on a team that says it's not giving up on the season, Arroyo pitched as if something were at stake. Can he duplicate it against the Astros?
away_pitcher_note: Moehler pitched five shutout frames in his last outing, earning the win after the game was called because of inclement weather. Moehler allowed four hits, did not issue a walk and struck out four. The right-hander has allowed two runs over his last two outings, totaling 13 2/3 innings. He hasn't lost since July 4. He last faced the Reds on July 29, when he nearly pitched a complete game. Instead, he settled for giving up two runs over 8 2/3 frames in his strongest outing of the year.

home_pitcher_note: Harang has been antsy to return. He'd done his rehab in Triple-A Louisville, and he'd had a couple of bullpen sessions this week to test his right forearm. It passed muster, which was why manager Dusty Baker put his ace back into the Reds rotation. From where Harang sat, his three weeks on the disabled list looked like an eternity, particularly as he watched his teammates flounder. They need Harang if they plan to right what remains of the 2008 season, and he said he's ready to help. He's returning, he said, with no limitations, which is what Baker wanted to hear.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has had two subpar outings in a row after allowing six runs over five innings in a loss to the Cubs. The lefty has allowed 12 runs over his last two starts and cited command issues as a reason for his troubles. Rodriguez last faced the Reds on July 30 at Minute Maid Park, taking the loss after yielding six runs over 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Backe had one of his poorest outings of the year in his last start against the Cubs, allowing 11 runs over 3 1/3 innings in a landslide loss at Wrigley Field. In his prior two starts, he allowed five runs over a combined 11 1/3 innings. Backe faced the Giants once earlier this season, taking the loss in San Francisco on May 13 after allowing four runs (three earned) over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez wasn't great in his last start, but he pitched drastically better than he had in the month of July. The lefty blanked the Braves through four innings before giving up a three spot in the fifth and taking his fourth consecutive losing decision. Sanchez struck out five, and for the first time this season, didn't walk a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt had one of his strongest outings of the year against the team he's dominated his entire career -- the Reds. The right-hander allowed one run over seven innings, ending the Astros' two-game losing streak. He last faced the Giants on May 12, earning the win after allowing three runs over eight innings. Lifetime versus the Giants, Oswalt is 3-5 with a 3.99 ERA over 11 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Another start, another superb performance for Lincecum. In Wednesday's win against the Braves, the righty tossed eight innings of two-run ball while fanning eight batters. Lincecum's fastball topped out in the low-90s -- slower than usual -- but he used his ever-improving changeup and array of breaking pitches to notch his 12th win of the year. The only worry regarding Lincecum's recent starts is his high pitch count. He threw 117 pitches against Atlanta and has thrown at least 115 pitches in seven of his past eight outings.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf took a no-decision in his most recent outing versus Cincinnati, allowing four runs over six innings in a game the Astros won in extras. Wolf faced the Giants twice this year as a member of the Padres' pitching staff. He did not earn a decision in either outing but compiled a 2.25 ERA, allowing three earned runs over 12 innings. Lifetime versus the Giants, Wolf is 5-4 with a 3.80 ERA over 12 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Zito was marred by a five-run third inning that cost him the game against the Dodgers on Aug. 8 at AT&T Park. The lefty allowed a solo-homer Danny Ardoin and a three-run double to Jeff Kent and exited after five innings. Zito said his velocity was down, but it was his changeup that did him in. He gave up two doubles on hanging changeups and only struck one batter in the outing. Zito is 1-0 with a 2.77 ERA in two career starts against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler extended his winning streak to three games with another dominating performance over the Reds in his last outing. The 36-year-old right-hander compiled an 11-inning scoreless streak over two outings and has held opponents to three runs over his last three starts. Moehler faced the Giants in San Francisco on May 14, taking a no-decision after yielding three runs over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: He didn't get a win, but Correia had his best outing since early April in his last start. Against the rival Dodgers, the righty tossed six innings of one-run ball, his second consecutive effective appearance. He has allowed just three runs in his past 12 1/3 innings and says he's finally getting into a groove. He felt he was pitching well earlier this year before he landed on the disabled list for nearly two months with a left side strain.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had one of his best outings of the year against the Reds in his last start, allowing two runs over 6 2/3 innings. He was perfect through 4 2/3 and used mostly two-seamers and fastballs for the first three frames before turning to his curveball in the fourth. Rodriguez is 2-2 over four career starts vs. the Diamondbacks and has a 4.50 ERA. He has not faced Arizona this year.
away_pitcher_note: It's been the same old story for Webb recently. The Cy Young frontrunner has put together seven consecutive quality starts and has won his last four outings. The last time out, Webb was a double threat, as he got the job done on the mound and with the bat, belting a two-run double off Braves starter Mike Hampton. At Minute Maid Park, Webb is 2-0 with a 1.21 ERA in 22 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Backe bounced back from one of his worst performances of the season to throw one of his best, allowing one run on four hits in seven innings against the Giants. He struck out six and said he felt much more comfortable with his fastball, which he used about 80 percent of the time. He will face Arizona for the first time this season and just the second time in his career. Backe allowed five runs in 12 innings against the D-backs in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Petit last saw game action on Aug. 7, when he allowed two runs over five innings against the Braves at Chase Field. As the fifth starter, his spot was skipped when the D-backs had this past Monday off. His versatility has been important for the D-backs as he has spot started when needed before finally joining the rotation. As a starter this year, Petit is 1-2 with a 3.00 ERA in four games. In nine relief appearances, he is 0-1 with a 3.29 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt did not have his best start against the Giants, but it was enough to survive as he was able to strand nine baserunners. He allowed three runs and struck out four on 10 hits. Oswalt is facing Arizona for the first time this season. He is 6-1 with a 2.57 ERA all-time against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson continued his march towards 300 wins as he was victorious last Tuesday night against the Rockies in Coors Field. The Big Unit, who now has 294 wins, allowed just two runs on five hits over six innings. In his last seven starts, Johnson is 6-1 with a 1.77 ERA. His lone loss came against the Pirates when he allowed just two runs in 7 1/3 innings, but was outdueled by Jeff Karstens, who took a perfect game into the eighth.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia calls his current run of success "pretty good." If this is pretty good, his new teammates would love to see what else he has in store. Sabathia has won 10 straight decisions dating to his final days with the Cleveland Indians, and is 7-0 with a 1.55 ERA in eight Brewers starts since a July 7 trade to Milwaukee. He had to work a bit against the Padres on Wednesday, but still managed to pitch seven innings while allowing only one run on nine hits. He pitched a five-hit shutout against the Nationals in his last start at Miller Park.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf had his best outing of the four he's made since his trade to Houston in his last start against the Giants. The veteran left-hander no-hit the Giants through four and cruised to the win after allowing two runs over seven innings. Wolf made his Astros debut against the Brewers in Milwaukee on July 27, when he took a no-decision after yielding four runs (three earned) over 4 1/3 innings. The Astros are 4-0 in games he's started.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets dueled Jake Peavy on Thursday in San Diego and didn't have his good curveball, but still managed to blank the Padres on only one hit through six innings. Sheets ran into trouble in the seventh, allowing four hits and three runs on the way to a tough 3-2 loss. According to MLB.com's unofficial pitch tracker, 77 of Sheets' 110 pitches were fastballs, or 70 percent. Over his final 1 2/3 innings, 24 of Sheets' 30 pitches registered as fastballs. "It was not good," Sheets said of his curve. "But, you still have to throw it. It just wasn't a good pitch today."
away_pitcher_note: Moehler wasn't as sharp in his last outing as he was the previous three, ending a streak of three starts during which he yielded two or fewer runs. Moehler allowed four runs over 5 1/3 innings but took a no-decision in an Astros win. Moehler last faced the Brewers on June 12 at home, absorbing the loss after allowing seven runs over 4 2/3 innings. Moehler is 4-2 with a 3.64 ERA over 10 road games (eight starts) this year.

home_pitcher_note: Parra's frustration is mounting, even though he has pitched well in his first full season in the Majors. But since rattling off eight straight wins, Parra has gone 1-4 in his past nine starts, including a loss at Dodger Stadium on Friday in which he matched his career and season high by allowing 10 hits. Parra was working with what he called his best pure "stuff" of the season, but he couldn't locate. "Right now, everything is finding a hole, and I'm paying for a lot of mistakes," he said. "Maybe it's the way I'm pitching right now that's making me feel this way. ... With this team being where we're at, fighting the way we are, that's not going to do it."
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struggled with location in his last outing, and the Diamondbacks took advantage, scoring four runs off the left-hander over 2 1/3 innings. Rodriguez tied a career-high with six walks and struck out four. The lefty last faced Milwaukee on June 25 at Miller Park, logging the win after yielding one run over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: The overstated, unrealistic expectations the public developed when the Mets acquired Santana were met on Sunday, when the left-hander shut out the Pirates on three hits and no walks. Santana managed that partially because the young Pirates hitters weren't particularly selective about Santana's pitches and because plate umpire Ed Hickox had a strike zone that would have been the envy of Tom  Glavine and other strike-zone stretchers. Santana threw 113 pitches, few of them stressful, in pitching his fifth big league shutout. Next, he faces the team he opposed on Aug. 2. That start produced a no-decision in a 10-inning Mets loss. Santana allowed one run on three hits and two walks in 6 1/3 innings in the outing.
away_pitcher_note: Astros manager Cecil Cooper called Oswalt's last start the second-best outing he has seen from the ace. In the start, Oswalt one-hit the Diamondbacks over eight innings. The right-hander struck out 10, tying his season high, and walked two. He gave up four runs on six hits in his previous start against New York, taking a no-decision over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Maine's sore shoulder is likely to limit him to about 100 pitches per start. And pitching coach Dan Warthen says Maine's fastball likely will be compromised for the rest of the season. Maine has pitched five innings in each of his last two starts and has exceeded five once in six starts. He hasn't faced the Astros this season.
away_pitcher_note: Backe's rollercoaster season took another nose dive in his last start, when he gave up 11 runs on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Diamondbacks. Backe has shown control at times and lacked command at others, so the Astros aren't quite sure what they will get from start to start. He got a no-decision in his last start against the Mets this season, giving up three runs on 10 hits in six innings, and he is 1-2 all time against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Perez pitched through control problems on Tuesday but managed to hold the Mets within range, allowing three runs to the Braves in 6 1/3 innings. Five walks proved his lack of command in the no-decision, but manager Jerry Manuel could still say after the game that Perez is one of his most consistent starters. All of the damage came in the third inning after Perez loaded the bases with no outs. But he'd survive, handing off to Mexican countryman Luis Ayala in the seventh inning with two on. He'll next face the Astros, against whom he holds a 2-2 record with a 3.31 ERA in 35 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf was ineffective in his last outing, allowing six earned runs over four innings in a loss to the Brewers. He yielded five runs in the fourth inning, including a two-run single to pitcher CC Sabathia. Wolf, a former Phillie, has extensive experience against the Mets. This year, he's 2-0 against them with a 0.75 ERA, having yielded one run over 13 innings. Lifetime versus the Mets, he's 11-5 with a 3.25 ERA over 27 games, all starts.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey put aside manager Jerry Manuel's concerns that the 24-year-old would tire late in the season, surviving all nine innings Wednesday and holding the Braves to three runs on three hits. After loading the bases in the sixth, Pelfrey maturely utilized the hard sink on his pitches to induce a key double play ball, limiting the inning's run total to two. Pelfrey said after the game that he was more efficient because he was marking the catcher's glove at precise locations rather than firing it in toward the plate, throwing 62 of his 108 pitches for strikes Wednesday. While he didn't face the Astros during the two teams' last encounter, he has struggled against them with a 6.32 ERA in 15 2/3 career innings.
away_pitcher_note: Despite feeling off mechanically, Moehler earned his ninth win of the season in his last start, holding the Brewers to two runs (one earned) over 5 1/3 innings to extend his winning streak to five. The right-hander hasn't lost since July 4 and since then has logged five wins and three no-decisions. Moehler last faced the Reds in Cincinnati on Aug. 9, when he allowed one run over seven innings in a winning effort.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez issued five walks in his last outing versus the Brewers, including four which led off an inning. Still, the lefty kept the damage in check, allowing three runs (two earned) over 5 1/3 innings. Rodriguez last faced the Reds in Cincinnati on Aug. 10, earning the win after allowing two runs over 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Although the Reds were no-hit by Ted Lilly through five innings, Arroyo was also stingy and gave up one earned run and three hits for a 2-1 Reds win over the Cubs Wednesday. Arroyo tied a career high with five walks and struck out four but used two double plays to escape trouble early and retired nine in a row and 10 of his last 11 batters. It was his third quality start over his last four games. In three starts vs. Houston this season, Arroyo is 0-3 with a 9.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt would only have to regret the first two innings after Friday�s loss to the Mets. He went eight innings and allowed three runs -- all in the first two frames -- and would go on to retire his last 20 batters after allowing a two-run home run in the second inning. The tough-luck loss was Oswalt's first since June 15 and snapped a streak of six straight wins. Next he faces the Reds, who he held to one run in seven innings on Aug. 7.
away_pitcher_note: Fogg's return to the rotation from a seven-day break (that included one relief appearance) did not go well. He gave up three runs in four innings to the Cubs, including a home run to opposing pitcher Carlos Zambrano. Fogg hasn't won or gone at least six innings since July 19. Houston pounded the University of Florida product for six runs in four innings earlier this month. Fogg has a 6.92 career ERA versus the Astros, which is actually lower than his overall mark this season.

home_pitcher_note: Backe recovered from two bad outings with another solid one, retiring his first 14 batters before going seven innings and allowing three runs to the Mets on Saturday. He kept his two-seam fastball down and attacked the strike zone to hold the Mets to six hits. At one point, combining with Roy Oswalt's 20 consecutive retired batters to end the game on Friday, Backe helped extend the Astros' streak of retired batters to 34. Next he'll face the Reds, who he hasn't opposed this season.
away_pitcher_note: Harang had one of his best outings in a forgettable season for an 8-5 win over the Rockies Friday night. The right-hander, who was moved back a day because of neck spasms, threw six scoreless innings with six hits and three walks and four strikeouts. The best moment came when he had the bases loaded and no outs in the fifth inning and retired the heart of Colorado's lineup in order to escape cleanly. Harang, who refined his mechanics recently, had more life on his fastball and routinely threw it in the 93-94 mph range.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf gave the Astros six solid innings against the Mets on Sunday, bouncing back from early struggles to settle into a rhythm. He gave up four earned runs, including two homers, and he walked in one run with the bases loaded. But Wolf went on to retire nine of the final 11 batters he faced to keep his team within striking distance. He surrendered seven hits, striking out four with three walks. Wolf has not faced the Cardinals as a member of the Astros staff, but in his last start against St. Louis with the Padres he gave up eight hits and six runs (four earned) in 5 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After a great first half, Lohse has cooled off quite a bit. He's lost three straight decisions, and the Cardinals are 1-5 in his last six starts. Lohse has not allowed fewer than three runs in a start since July 17, his first start after the All-Star break. Over his past six games, he has a 6.42 ERA and has allowed six homers in 33 2/3 innings. It's also worth noting that he's struggled on the road, with a 5.31 ERA away from St. Louis (3.16 at Busch Stadium).

home_pitcher_note: Moehler was hit hard early against the Mets, allowing a three-run home run in the first inning, which doomed him to a loss in a game where the Astros' bats were silenced. He remained solid in the second through fifth innings, though, holding down the Mets' offense until he was pulled with runners on first and second in the sixth, and a sacrifice fly would surrender fourth run on Moehler's tab. The loss broke a streak of five-straight wins for Moehler. He'll now face the Cardinals, who he held scoreless in seven innings on June 6.
away_pitcher_note: It's a short list of pitchers who are going better than Looper. He's pitched seven innings in six straight starts, and has allowed three runs or fewer in seven in a row. His ERA over his past seven outings is 2.30, and he has 52 strikeouts against 17 walks since June 6. He's also fared well in Houston, posting a 2.92 ERA as a starter at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struck out a career-high 10 batters in his one-run, three-hit start against the Reds. The lefty moved the position of his glove from below his chest to in front of his face, which he said made him more comfortable. He's 0-2 in three starts against St. Louis this season, with a 1.45 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer deserved better his last time out. He could easily have finished with one or two runs in six innings. But his defense betrayed him, and then he was asked to give one more inning than he had in him. Either way, it's been a fine second half for Wellemeyer, who has made a full return after elbow problems bothered him in June and even into July.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis looked like a frontline starter against the Pirates in his last outing, when he threw seven scoreless innings, struck out three and walked none for his ninth win of the year. Catcher Henry Blanco said Marquis' repertoire was in full gear and his fastball had bite. The right-hander continues to give the Cubs plenty of innings. Only once this season has he been unable to pitch past the fourth inning. Marquis is 9-5 with a 5.22 ERA against the Astros in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt recorded his 22nd win against the Reds in a 4-1 victory on Wednesday. He is 6-2 in his last 10 starts with a 3.02 ERA, averaging 5.7 strikeouts a game. Oswalt is 11-11 all-time against Chicago, losing his only game against the Cubs this season. He earned five runs on 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Cubs tweaked their rotation to give Zambrano extra time because of a tired arm. He had been scheduled to start Sunday. Big Z is 7-1 in 14 starts at Wrigley Field. His velocity had dropped in August, and the Cubs are hoping an extra day or two will help. He did throw a short side session on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Backe strung together two consecutive successful outings with a 3-2 series finale win over the Reds, something that has eluded the right-hander this season. Backe has suffered from inconsistency but is solid when he can keep his pitches low in the zone. He gave up two runs over 6 2/3 innings against Cincinnati, throwing 64 pitches and allowing three hits in six shutout frames. He gave up two in the seventh before being pulled. Backe has lost two of three against the Cubs this season, recording a no-decision in the third. He gave up 11 runs on nine hits over 3 1/3 in his last visit to Wrigley Field, walking six as two Chicago players went deep.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster was given an extra day between starts. He'll be vying for a career-high 16th win. He did not get a decision in his last start against the Phillies, giving up four runs on eight hits over six innings and striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf had another strong outing for the Astros, who are 6-1 when he is on the mound. He gave up one earned run, allowing another on a double-error, in a 3-2 win against the Cardinals in his last outing, and the lefty said he feels the strongest he has ever been. Wolf is 2-6 over 13 career games against Chicago with a 4.98 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Ubaldo Jimenez struggled with his control in his last start, against the Padres on Aug. 30. When he did throw strikes, the Padres had difficulty producing, and Jimenez's inability to regain his rhythm in the fourth inning cost the Rockies the game. In that inning, Jimenez walked four batters and saw three runs cross the plate. He would eventually leave the inning after lasting only 3 2/3 innings, allowing six runs on two hits, while striking out two and walking five. Jimenez would later say that it was a mechanics issue that led to his struggles.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler answered a one-year contract extension offer from the Astros by earning his 10th win of the season against the Cardinals on Saturday. The righty gave up a three-run homer to Rick Ankiel in the first inning before settling in, allowing just four hits through the second through sixth innings. Now he'll start against Colorado for the first time this season after throwing three innings in relief against the Rockies, where he gave up three runs on five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Continuing a hard-luck season, Francis held the Padres to one run and six hits in seven innings on Sunday, but he left the game trailing. He finished with a no-decision in a 2-1 loss. But the good news is Francis struck out six and walked two, and the biggest hit against him came courtesy of a fielding misplay. Francis is 1-1 with a 1.93 ERA in two career starts against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt had his longest outing of the year in his last start, throwing 8 1/3 innings in a winning effort versus the Cubs. He is 5-1 with a 1.59 ERA over his last six games, allowing eight earned runs over 45 1/3 innings. Oswalt hasn't faced the Rockies this year. In his career, he's 5-1 with a 2.14 ERA over eight starts against Colorado, allowing 13 earned runs over 54 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: There's a long way for the Rockies to go to equal last year's magic, but if the pixie dust falls the way of the Purple Pinstripes, De La Rosa could be a huge part of the reason. De La Rosa is 3-1 in his last five starts, and pitching better each time. He showed tremendous change-of-pace on Monday while holding the Giants scoreless on four hits in a 4-0 Rockies victory.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is scheduled to pitch in the finale of the Astros' series with the Rockies, but that could change since he was pulled from his last start with a strained right oblique muscle. Rodriguez had thrown 5 2/3 scoreless innings, allowing seven hits, while striking out four on 93 pitches. After his last outing, manager Cecil Cooper expressed optimism the lefty would make his next scheduled start.

home_pitcher_note: Arias will make a spot start in place of Brandon Backe, who is experiencing soreness in his elbow. Arias, whom the Astros picked up off waivers from the Rockies on July 31, was 1-0 with a 1.52 ERA and one save in eight appearances, including three starts, for Triple-A Round Rock. Arias appeared in 18 career big league games over a two-season span with the Rockies, compiling a 1-0 record and a 3.43 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Snell has now won each of his last two decisions and appears on track to finish the season on a strong note. The right-hander has pitched at least six innings in four of his past five starts after doing so only three times in all his June and July starts combined. Snell again did a better job of attacking the strike zone and getting ahead early, both keys to his recent success. Snell will be making his third start of the season against Houston. Though he didn't factor in either decision, Snell allowed six earned runs in 6 2/3 combined innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf had his best Astros outing in his last start at Wrigley Field on Wednesday, throwing his 12th career complete game and seventh shutout in a 3-0 Houston win. Wolf has allowed one run over his past two outings, spanning 15 innings. The left-hander has not faced the Pirates this year. In his career, he's 5-1 with a 3.61 ERA vs. the Bucs over eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start, Ohlendorf didn't factor in the decision despite putting up a respectable performance. He allowed four runs (three earned) on seven hits in six innings. Though his velocity didn't reach the high 90s as anticipated, he was steadily throwing in the mid-90s range and attacked the zone with consistency. You can expect to see that velocity return before the season ends. Ohlendorf has made two career relief appearances against Houston while with the Yankees. In two innings, the righty allowed two hits, one walk and one run. He struck out one.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Moehler had one of his shorter outings since he joined the starting rotation, allowing five runs over 4 2/3 innings in a loss to the Rockies. The right-hander has faced the Pirates twice this year, both as a starter. He earned the win on July 9 in Pittsburgh after yielding four runs over seven innings, and on July 23 at home, he took the loss in his shortest outing of the year, allowing six runs (five earned) in 2 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Staked to a 5-0 lead after an inning and a half against the Reds in his last start, Gorzelanny couldn't take advantage, getting knocked out by the Reds before completing four innings. Although his strikeout-to-walk ratio has shown some slight improvement since he was called up on Aug. 23, Gorzelanny still has more walks than strikeouts for the season (68 to 65). Gorzelanny has just four quality starts in his past 17 outings.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt extended his scoreless-innings streak to 23 1/3 frames with a shutout of the Rockies in his last outing, throwing only the second one-hitter in Coors Field history. Oswalt has won eight of his past nine decisions and hasn't yielded a run since the second inning of his start against the Reds on Aug. 27. The right-hander last faced the Pirates on June 4 at PNC Park, taking the loss after allowing four runs (three earned) on nine hits over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: One-game aberration or full-blown turnaround? This start will go a long way toward proving which phrase best describes Duke, who snapped an 0-9 stretch with a 6.82 ERA in a most emphatic manner on Friday: He throttled the Giants on six hits, all singles, for his second career shutout. Duke recorded 17 groundouts in the victory and had the Giants biting on his sinker, even though they knew it was coming, time and again.

home_pitcher_note: In 14 career starts vs. the Cubs, Wolf is 3-6 with a 4.46 ERA, but he did pitch his 12th career complete game and seventh shutout in a 3-0 win over the Cubs at Wrigley Field on Sept. 3. He has allowed just five earned runs over his last three outings, a span of 22 innings. He held the Pirates to three runs on four hits in seven innings in his last start. Houston is 8-1 in Wolf's nine starts since the club acquired him from San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano has been sidelined because of some discomfort in his right shoulder. An MRI exam revealed tendinitis, and he was shut down. If he can't go, Sean Marshall will get the start. Zambrano last pitched Sept. 2 against the Astros and did not get a decision. The right-hander gave up three runs on five hits and three walks over five innings, his first start since getting an extra day because of a tired arm. Zambrano threw 86 pitches in the outing and the stadium radar gun did show that his fastball had some life to it.

home_pitcher_note: If the Astros play the third game of their series with the Cubs on this day as expected, Moehler will likely get the start, pitching on regular rest. The right-hander earned his 11th win of the year in his last start, holding the Pirates to two runs over six innings. Moehler is 6-2 with a 4.02 ERA over 11 starts since the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly is coming off a victory over the St. Louis Cardinals in his last start. The lefty threw eight innings, gave up one run on five hits and struck out five. He matched his season high in innings pitched. One more win, and Lilly will match his personal high of 15, set the last two years. He's 2-1 with a 3.06 ERA in five starts against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad left last Tuesday's start against the Phillies early after being struck by a hard comebacker off the bat of Carlos Ruiz in the third inning. Volstad finished off the frame but was replaced for the top of the fourth, finishing the night giving up one run on two hits with two strikeouts in the no-decision. After the game, the injury was described as a bruised right shin for the 21-year-old rookie, who was icing it but did not get an X-ray. Because of the off-day on Monday, the Marlins could push Volstad back to Wednesday for precautionary reasons.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt was brilliant again in his last outing, throwing his second shutout in a row in a win over the Pirates. Oswalt set a club record for consecutive scoreless innings with 32 1/3, breaking JR Richard's mark of 31, set in 1980. Oswalt last faced the Marlins on April 11 at Minute Maid Park, with disastrous results. He yielded eight runs on nine hits and lasted just four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chalk it up as yet another solid outing by Nolasco last Wednesday. In a win against the division-rival Phillies, the 25-year-old gave up three runs in 7 2/3 innings. In that game, Nolasco struck out eight batters while only waling one -- a stat indicative of his recent success. Over his last nine starts -- which has seen him go 4-1 with a 2.68 ERA -- Nolasco has struck out 71 batters while only walking five.
away_pitcher_note: Backe was told he was a go for Wednesday in Florida, which will mark his first start since Sept. 2. The right-hander missed one start due to elbow soreness but never thought he'd be sideline for long. Backe is 1-1 with a 1.96 ERA over six career games (three starts) versus the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: At last, Olsen is working off a win. By beating the Nationals in his last outing, the 24-year-old lefty ended a string of nine straight starts without a victory. He had gone from July 19 against the Phillies until now. He did win two straight from July 9-19. Olsen had dropped six consecutive decisions. He won despite walking four and allowing six hits. Admittedly, he didn't have his best stuff. Olsen has logged 183 2/3 innings on the season, a career most. He threw 180 2/3 innings a year ago.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros put Arias in injured starter Wandy Rodriguez's place several days ago because they didn't want to take Chris Sampson out of the bullpen and Arias was the only other long relief option. It was a eureka decision, as Arias pitched a career-high five scoreless innings against Pittsburgh in his first career start Monday night.

home_pitcher_note: Snell's roller coaster 2008 season took a dip down in his last start on Saturday against the Cardinals. St. Louis collected six runs on nine hits and chased the Pittsburgh right-hander from the game after only four innings. Snell found trouble in the game after continually missing his spots high and the Cardinals made him pay for it. He is 2-4 with a 4.41 ERA against the Astros in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf had his shortest outing since joining the Astros against the Cubs on Sunday in Milwaukee. After traveling all day from Hurricane-damaged Houston to Milwaukee for the first of two "neutral site" games with the Cubs, Wolf allowed four runs over 2 1/3 innings. Wolf has good career numbers against the Pirates -- 6-1 record, 3.64 ERA over nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: General manager Neal Huntington said Barthmaier's next likely start for the Pirates will come on Saturday. In the right-hander's Major League debut, the Rays gave Barthmaier a rude welcoming. Tampa Bay scored three first-inning runs and knocked the 24-year-old out of the game after seven earned runs and 2 1/3 innings. He'll get a chance to make a better second impression against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler yielded five runs for for the second time this month during his last outing, a five-inning effort against the Cubs at Miller Park. Moehler is 5-4 with a 5.14 ERA over eight career games (five starts) vs. the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf struggled in his three innings against the Dodgers on Monday, surrendering three runs on five hits. His fastball, which was lauded by Pirates management when they received the right-hander in a trade from New York, was met with several thunderous swings from Los Angeles' lineup. Now in three starts with the Pirates, Ohlendorf has given up 11 earned runs in 13 innings pitched. He is 0-1 with a 10.50 ERA against the Astros in his young career.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt saw his franchise-record 32 1/3 consecutive scoreless innings get snapped early in a loss to the Marlins on Tuesday. The 31-year-old threw 29 pitches and gave up four runs in the first inning, which doomed his Astros the rest of the night. Oswalt did end on a good note, giving up just one hit while striking out six in his last four innings, but his struggles against Florida this season continued. In two games against the Marlins in 2008, Oswalt is 0-2 with a 9.90 ERA (11 earned runs in 10 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez will make his first start since leaving with a strained oblique muscle after one inning and 18 pitches in Colorado on Sept. 7. Rodriguez threw a 37-pitch simulated outing Saturday and was deemed healthy enough to open the series with the Reds on Tuesday. If that goes well, Rodriguez could pitch the season finale Sunday against the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Getting win No. 17 has proved very elusive for Volquez, who is 0-1 with a 4.91 ERA and just one quality outing over his last four starts. He is closing in on two other bench marks -- 200 strikeouts and 200 innings. He has 197 strikeouts and 188 2/3 innings. For the second straight game during Thursday's 5-4 loss to the Cardinals, Volquez gave up a career-high six walks. He gave up four runs on three hits over seven innings, with Albert Pujols' three-run homer in the third inning being critical. Volquez said his four-seam and two-seam fastballs lacked command and planned to work on those pitches during his in-between-starts bullpen session.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf had one of his better starts in his last outing against the Pirates, allowing one run on three hits over seven innings in a winning effort. Wolf made two starts against the Reds this year, earning one win and one no-decision. He allowed six earned runs over 13 innings for a 4.15 ERA. In his career, Wolf has faced the Reds 11 times, compiling a 4-4 record and a 3.76 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Ramirez pitched six innings and earned his first Major League win during Friday's 11-2 pounding of the Brewers. Ramirez gave up two earned runs and seven hits with two walks and five strikeouts during a well-pitched game. All three of the rookie's starts have been quality ones.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt held the Pirates to one run over six innings in a 79-pitch outing in his last start, exiting the game early with a slightly sore neck. He'll pitch on short rest against the Reds, whom he has dominated throughout his career. Oswalt is 3-0 with a 2.84 ERA over three starts versus the Reds this year, and lifetime versus Cincinnati, he's 22-1 with a 2.51 ERA over 27 games (25 starts).
away_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old Cueto proved his achy right arm was fine. Making his 30th start of the season, he pitched six strong innings on Saturday against the Milwaukee Brewers, a team reeling under the pressure of a playoff race. The last thing they needed to see was the flame-throwing Cueto in good form. He held them to a pair of runs on six hits and no walks, leaving behind a 4-2 lead. His outing against the Astros will be the last in a season that has made him an important piece in the Reds' rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler lasted only one inning in his last start against the Pirates, allowing five runs before being lifted in the second inning for a pinch-hitter. Moehler made one start against the Braves in Atlanta earlier this year, allowing five runs over six innings in a losing effort.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo will be making the final start of what has been a memorable rookie season. The 29-year-old right-hander, who didn't join the Braves' rotation until May 20, will be displaying his offspeed repertoire against the Astros for the first time this season. Campillo limited the Mets to two runs in six innings on Saturday to win for the first time in eight starts. He was 0-3 with a 6.88 ERA in his previous seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Astros haven't announced their starter for this one, but Backe is a likely candidate considering he hasn't pitched since giving up five runs in 1 2/3 innings at Florida on Sept. 17. Over his last two starts, both on the road, Backe has allowed eight earned runs in six innings. But the right-hander has always pitched better at home than on the road, and in his last start at Minute Maid Park he held the Reds to two earned runs in 6 2/3 innings back on Aug. 28. Backe is 2-1 with a 5.59 ERA in five career appearances vs. Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Parr is coming off the worst start of his young career, having lasted just 1 2/3 innings against the Mets on Sunday. The 22-year-old right-hander began his Major League career by tossing six scoreless innings in consecutive starts earlier this month. But in his past two outings, he has totaled six innings, allowed 14 hits and been charged with eight earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is the projected starter here, though the club hasn't officially made a decision. Rodriguez, in his first start since leaving his Sept. 7 start at Colorado due to a strained oblique muscle, allowed just two unearned runs in five innings against Cincinnati on Tuesday. He's faced Atlanta once this season, a no-decision (5 1/3 innings, 3 ER) back on July 6.
away_pitcher_note: Instead of pushing rookie right-hander Jair Jurrjens any further, the Braves have decided to start Mike Hampton in their season finale. Hampton, who has gone 2-2 with a 3.63 ERA in his past eight starts, looks forward to the opportunity to make another good impression before heading into free agency. The 36-year-old southpaw relocated his cutter on Tuesday night, while limiting the Phillies to two run in six innings of a victorious effort.

summary: 2009-03-02 - New York Yankees @ Houston Astros (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt led the Astros in wins for a franchise-record fifth consecutive season in 2008. He also set a franchise mark with 32 1/3 scoreless innings, the longest streak in the National League and second-longest in the Majors last year. In his last nine starts of last season, Oswalt was 7-2 with a 1.47 ERA, and he posted a 2.24 ERA over 13 second-half starts, recording wins in 10 of his 12 decisions during that span. He was the first pitcher to throw consecutive complete-game shutouts in 2008. Since he joined the big leagues in 2001, Oswalt leads all Major League pitchers with 129 wins. In that time, he ranks third in ERA and is seventh in winning percentage. His .668 overall career winning percentage ranks first in Astros history, and his 3.13 ERA also is the best in club history among pitchers with at least 80 innings pitched. Oswalt has had double-digit win totals in all eight of his Major League seasons, including 20-win seasons in 2004 and 2005. Among players who began their careers after 1957, Oswalt is the sixth-fastest to 100 in terms of appearances among pitchers.
away_pitcher_note:
This has been a relatively quiet spring for Zambrano. No boasts about winning a World Series or Cy Young or even 20 games. "I don't have to prove anything," he said. "I've been in the big leagues for eight years. They know what I'm capable of doing." This will be Big Z's fifth Opening Day start, and he's still looking for his first win. He has a 5.57 ERA in his four previous season openers. Last year, Zambrano did not get a decision in a 4-3 loss to the Brewers. He gave up three hits over 6 2/3 innings, striking out five. In 2007, he took the loss as the Reds scored five runs on six hits and five walks in five innings for a 5-1 win. Zambrano did not get a decision on April 3, 2006, against the Reds, giving up five runs on seven hits and five walks over 4 2/3 innings. He also got a no-decision on April 4, 2005, as the Diamondbacks scored three runs on seven hits and four walks over 4 2/3 innings.
Only Fergie Jenkins (1979-83) and Rick Sutcliffe (1985-89) have started five consecutive Opening Days for the Cubs. Rick Reuschel is the only other Cubs pitcher with at least four Opening Day starts without a win. The Cubs were 0-4 in his starts from 1978 to 1981.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has won nine games in each of his four Major League seasons and ranks in the top 10 among all NL left-handers in wins (sixth), innings pitched (ninth) and opponents batting average (seventh) during that span. Rodriguez was 5-5 with a 2.99 ERA over 14 home starts in 2008, and he posted three months with a sub-3.00 ERA: April (2.31), June (2.30) and September (1.38).
away_pitcher_note: Dempster proved last season that you can go home again. He successfully made the transition back to starting and won a career-high 17 games. Named to the All-Star team, the right-hander became just the second pitcher since 1969 to record 25 or more saves in a season, then win at least 17 games the next year. John Hiller was the last to do so in 1973-74. There's no place like Wrigley Field for Dempster, who was 14-3 at home. It's the most wins in Chicago since Fergie Jenkins won a franchise-record 15 in 1967.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler was the surprise of the rotation in '08, logging 11 wins after working himself into the rotation once the season started. Moehler originally was a fill-in for the injured Wandy Rodriguez, but he pitched so well that he maintained his starting job even after Rodriguez returned. Moehler ranked second in wins among Astros pitchers and third in games started last year. He recorded a five-game winning streak from July 9-Aug. 19, his longest since he won six straight in 2000. The Astros were 16-10 in his 26 starts last season, and he allowed four runs or fewer in 20 of those.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly set career highs in wins and strikeouts (184) last season, and tied his career high with 34 starts. The lefty pitched for Team USA in the World Baseball Classic, making two starts. This spring, he's worked on getting his changeup going; it was one of the reasons he got off to a slow start last year, going 1-4 with a 6.46 ERA in six April starts. "We'll really find out where I am once the season kicks off," he said. "That counts the most. My goal is to make sure I'm prepared to get off to a good start."

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro was angry after he was not chosen to start for Puerto Rico in the World Baseball Classic, but he may have found an outlet for that energy. He had an excellent spring, leading to hopes that he'll pitch more like he did late in 2007 than in a frustrating 2008. An effective Pineiro would make an enormous difference for the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton will be attempting to log his first full season since 2004. The left-hander has dealt with a rash of injuries over the last four years, but his solid finish with the Braves in '08 -- he was 3-4 with a 4.85 ERA from July 26 through the end of the season -- was enough to convince the Astros he was worth a shot. Hampton is beginning his second tour with Houston. He posted a 69-40 record and  a 3.40 ERA from 1994-99 and played in three postseasons with the Astros (1997-99).

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright's first regular season start looked a lot like most of his games in the spring. There was plenty to like, starting with seven strikeouts. But there was also plenty to give pause, most notably five walks, tying a career high. Wainwright needed 94 pitches to get 16 outs, and that's not going to be good enough. He must be more efficient and get deeper into games.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt will stay on schedule to pitch every fifth day, which pushes the fifth starter, Russ Ortiz, out of the rotation the first time through. Oswalt was 0-1 with a 4.15 ERA over two starts vs. the Cardinals last year. He is 9-6 with a 2.90 ERA in his career against St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: It will be interesting to see how Lohse responds after a pretty tough assignment in his first start. He grinded out seven innings, with the last two being fairly eventful, and needed 108 pitches to do so. Those certainly aren't red-flag numbers, but Lohse did work hard on a chilly night early in the season. It's reasonable to expect him to show no ill effects, but if he does look a bit winded against Houston, his battle against the Pirates may partly explain it.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez will stay on his regular schedule despite Thursday's off day. The lefty was 1-2 with a 1.11 ERA over four starts against the Cardinals in 2008, allowing three runs over 24 1/3 innings. In his career, Rodriguez is 2-6 with a 4.08 ERA against St. Louis. He's allowed 24 earned runs over 53 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Duke gets the nod to pitch the home opener, and while it just so happened that way because of the rotation order, he certainly deserves the honor after his first start. Duke followed up a great Spring Training with a solid start to the regular season. He limited the Cardinals to one earned run in 6 1/3 innings, largely by establishing his fastball command early and working off of that. He's also showing more confidence in pitching inside and is doing so effectively. Despite having a 1-4 career record in nine career appearances (eight starts) against the Astros, Duke has a respectable 3.81 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler was the surprise of the rotation in '08, logging 11 wins after working himself into the rotation after the season started. Moehler originally was a fill-in for the injured Wandy Rodriguez, but he pitched so well that he maintained his starting job even after Rodriguez returned. Moehler ranked second in wins among Astros pitchers and third in games started. He recorded a five-game winning streak from July 9-Aug. 19, his longest since he won six straight in 2000. The Astros were 16-10 in his 26 starts last year, and he allowed four runs or fewer in 20 of them.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf came out on the wrong end of a pitcher's duel in his first start of the season, despite allowing just two runs in six innings. He kept the Cardinals scoreless through his first six frames. Ohlendorf continues to rely very heavily on his two-seam fastball, which has been a dominant pitch for him through Spring Training and into the season. He's also shown no apprehension in pitching inside. Ohlendorf has made four career appearances (two starts) against the Astros. He is 0-2 with a 9.00 ERA against Houston in those outings.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton will make his second start of the season when he faces the Bucs after the off-day. He yielded three runs on four hits over five innings in his first start against the Cardinals, taking the loss. The lefty did not face the Pirates last year. In his career, he is 10-3 with a 2.71 ERA over 22 games versus Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens' scheduled season debut was rained out Friday in Cincinnati. He was temporarily moved to the bullpen in preparation for his scheduled start. Karstens earned the rotation's final spot in the last week of Spring Training by beating out fellow right-hander Virgil Vasquez. It was a subpar spring for Karstens, who makes a living on being efficient and having stellar command. He's not going to overpower hitters, but he's on when the ground balls are coming easily. Karstens, who came to Pittsburgh in a July deadline deal with the Yankees, allowed 11 earned runs in his final 13 2/3 spring innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ortiz will make his first start of the season when he takes the hill against the Pirates in the series finale. The right-hander threw 73 pitches in a relief appearance on April 8 after Moehler was knocked from the game in the second inning. That outing, during which he allowed three runs on four hits over three innings, marked Ortiz's first in the big leagues since 2007. Ortiz has had success over the Bucs through his career, logging eight wins and one loss and a 3.20 ERA over 14 games (13 starts).

home_pitcher_note: The results weren't in Oswalt's favor his first two starts, but that could change when the team returns from its road trip. Oswalt is very, very good against the Reds -- almost perfect, in fact. He's faced them 28 times in his career, and has a record of 23-1, with a 2.47 ERA. He was 4-0 against them in 2008, allowing seven runs over 25 innings for a 2.52 ERA. Oswalt allowed six runs in his last outing, against the Cardinals on April 11. Albert Pujols knocked a grand slam off him in the fifth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto pitched six innings and gave up four earned runs and eight hits -- including five for extra bases -- with one walk and nine strikeouts during a 10-2 loss to the Pirates on Saturday. The 23-year-old, who was pitching a day behind schedule because of a rainout on Friday, did rally and retire his last seven in a row -- including four on strikeouts. In an issue typical from last season, Cueto threw a lot of pitches early -- 107 total -- and ran into three-ball counts to six of his 26 batters faced. Last season in four starts vs. Houston, Cueto was 0-3 with a 7.84 ERA and 32 hits allowed in 20 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had a quality outing in his last start, holding the Cardinals to three runs over six innings. He was tagged with the loss, however, as the Astros were one-hit by Kyle Lohse. Rodriguez has allowed four earned runs over two start this year. He was 1-2 with a 4.24 ERA against the Reds last year. In his career versus Cincinnati, Rodriguez is 3-4 with a 5.07 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Harang is coming off of a fantastic performance on Sunday, when he dealt the Pirates a three-hit shutout for a 2-0 victory. The right-hander went to a three-ball count just once and a two-ball count only seven times. Of his 108 pitches thrown vs. Pittsburgh, 80 were for strikes. Last season in two starts vs. the Astros, Harang was 0-2 with a 9.00 ERA and 16 hits allowed over 11 innings. Lifetime vs. Houston, he is 8-7 with a 4.45 ERA in 19 games.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino will be recalled from Triple-A Round Rock in time for this start, replacing the injured Brian Moehler. Paulino had two very good outings for the Express, allowing one earned run over a combined 12 innings with five walks and 12 strikeouts. He was in the running for the fifth starter job briefly during Spring Training, but poor performances early knocked him out of contention.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez was expected to spend his time between starts working on his command and tightening up his mechanics after he's struggled through his first outings. The right-hander allowed six runs and seven hits, including two home runs, with four walks and four strikeouts in Monday's 7-6 win over the Brewers. He threw 99 pitches in the short amount of time and was up to 55 through two innings. Opposing hitters are waiting out Volquez to throw strikes, which is running up his pitch counts. His fastball velocity is sound but the command hasn't been there and that has prevented him from being able to effectively use his changeup. In two starts vs. the Astros last season, Volquez was 2-0 with a 1.32 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton is coming off his first win as an Astro since the end of the 1999 season. He pitched a gem on Wednesday, tossing six shutout innings against the Pirates, striking out eight, to end Houston's five-game losing streak at the time. He's faced the Reds 23 times in his career -- 18 starts -- compiling a 6-5 record and a 3.95 ERA over 107 innings.
away_pitcher_note: With 6 1/3 strong innings, Arroyo was a key in the Reds' 6-1 win over the Brewers on Tuesday. He allowed one earned run and four hits with four walks and three strikeouts. He threw 105 pitches before becoming worn out enough to come out. The right-hander felt no effects from the carpal tunnel soreness in his right arm that bothered him at the end of Spring Training and the beginning of the season. Arroyo was sharp with his sinker early on and went to a fastball in the later innings and said he felt strong with it even into the seventh inning.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz had his longest performance so far this year in his last outing vs. the Pirates, allowing three runs over 4 2/3 innings in an Astros win. He still seeks his first win of the season and will do so against the Dodgers, whom he's faced plenty of times in his career. The former Giant has made 22 appearances vs. the Dodgers, including 21 starts. He has a record of 8-9 and a 5.07 ERA, with 57 walks and 76 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Clayton Kershaw pitched a masterpiece of a no-decision against the Giants, allowing only one hit and one run over seven innings with 13 strikeouts. All he had to show for it was a no-decision, as the bullpen blew the save. But Kershaw was able to contain a veteran lineup despite lacking command of his change-up, becoming the youngest Dodger to strike out 13 since Sandy Koufax was 19.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Oswalt threw 108 pitches over six innings but didn't allow any runs against a Reds team that he has dominated throughout his career. Oswalt took a no-decision when Jose Valverde blew a save opportunity in the ninth. Oswalt faced the Dodgers once last year, earning the win after allowing one run over six innings. In his career, the right-hander is 5-3 with a 3.63 ERA against L.A., spanning eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf showed his resiliency on the mound as he bounced back from a rough first inning against the Rockies on Friday.
