He allowed three runs in the first, including a two-run home run, but then pitched five scoreless innings. In all, Wolf tossed six innings, allowing three runs on four hits while striking out a season-high nine batters. He is 4-4 with a 3.76 ERA in 11 starts against Houston in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez tied a career high with 10 strikeouts during one of the best outings of his career in his last start, against the Reds. Rodriguez threw 105 pitches in seven innings, allowing two hits and walking two. He stuck out five at one point early in the game, catching three consecutive batters looking at called third strikes in the third. Rodriguez allowed five runs over five innings in his only start against the Dodgers last season, taking a no-decision. In his career, he's 2-1 with a 3.65 ERA over five games against Los Angeles.
away_pitcher_note: Billinglsey was nearly unhittable through five innings against the Rockies on Saturday but struggled in the sixth. He walked Seth Smith to open the frame, then allowed a single by Todd Helton before surrendering a three-run triple to Brad Hawpe that went by a diving Manny Ramirez. Hawpe then scored on a sacrifice fly, and Billingsley was lifted after the inning. In all, Billingsley allowed three runs on just four hits in six innings, while striking out six. The right-hander will face the Rockies again on Friday at Coors Field, where he has struggled in his career. He is 1-2 with a 6.87 ERA in four career games in Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino "opened some eyes," as Cecil Cooper said, after his last outing, during which he held the Reds scoreless over a six-inning, 97-pitch performance. That was Paulino's first big league start of the season after having two impressive outings for Triple-A Round Rock. Paulino has faced the Brewers twice in his career, allowing 10 runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo had much to be happy about in his last start. Even though he took a no-decision in a game the Brewers lost, 1-0, to the Mets in New York, the starter matched two-time Cy Young Award winner Johan Santana pitch for pitch. Gallardo worked six shutout innings, striking out seven and walking two. Even better, he didn't have his breaking ball in the early innings and recorded outs with his fastball until he found the touch on his breaking ball. Gallardo is 2-0 against the Astros during his young career and threw a season-high eight shutout innings in a 6-0 win against Houston in his only start at Minute Maid Park, which came on Sept. 7, 2007. Gallardo was born in Mexico, but he moved to Texas at and early age.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Hampton pitched well enough to win but took a no-decision when the bullpen blew a lead against the Reds. Hampton yielded three runs in 6 1/3 innings, walking one and striking out five. The left-hander did not face the Brewers in 2008, but he has appeared in 11 games against Milwaukee in his career, going 4-2 with a 2.87 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan struggled mightily in his first two starts of 2009, but he pitched a gem to help the Brewers salvage a win in their series against the Mets. New York scored in the first inning against Suppan on two hits, a walk and a wild pitch, but he settled in after that, yielding just three hits over the next four innings and surviving a pair of two-out hits in the sixth. Houston presents a challenge; Suppan is 2-7 with a 5.34 ERA in his career against the Astros, including 1-2 with a 6.26 ERA at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz wasn't efficient in his last outing versus the Dodgers, but it was enough to earn his first win of the season. Ortiz threw 116 pitches over five frames, allowing three runs on three hits while walking five. Ortiz has made nine starts against the Brewers, going 4-3 with a 5.23 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Parra continued a poor start to the season by allowing five runs and 10 baserunners -- seven hits, three walks -- in four innings of work against the Phillies on Tuesday and dropped to 0-3. He's allowed at least three runs in all three of his starts and has issued nine walks in 14 1/3 innings this season. Parra has a 5.47 ERA in five career starts against the Astros but has a 3-2 record in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto pitched a fantastic game Wednesday, working seven scoreless innings for a 3-0 Reds win over the Cubs at Wrigley Field. He allowed four hits -- all singles -- and struck out two. Most importantly, he did not walk a batter. Cueto avoided his penchant for nibbling around the plate and falling into deep counts. Throwing 108 pitches, he was aggressive with his fastball and worked ahead. In his previous matchup vs. Houston and Oswalt on April 17, Cueto lasted only 4 2/3 innings and gave up two hits but had six walks. Both starters got a no-decision when the Reds won 2-1 with a ninth-inning homer.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt is still looking for his first win, and, based on history, there's no better team for him to be facing in his next outing. Oswalt is very good against Cincinnati -- he's 23-1 over 29 career games, including 27 starts. He has a 2.39 career ERA versus the Reds. He last faced them on April 17, taking a no-decision after throwing six shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Harang resumed his good pitching in a 7-1 win over the Cubs on Thursday. In seven innings, plus one batter, the right-hander gave up just one unearned run on seven hits with one walk and two strikeouts. His previous outing vs. Houston wasn't so strong as he allowed five earned runs and 10 hits in a 7-0 loss on April 18. He left trailing by a 3-0 score but had two more runs inherited by the bullpen score. All three of the early runs came with two outs. The Reds' lineup only provided two hits in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez took a hard-luck loss in his last outing, dropping a decision to the Dodgers after he was outdueled by Chad Billingsly. Rodriguez allowed one run over six innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.80.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez allowed just one hit, Jeff Francoeur's solo homer, through 4 2/3 innings, but he couldn't get past the fifth inning Friday in a 4-3 loss to Atlanta. Volquez's was undone by seven walks, including five in the fateful fifth inning. Two of his walks came with the bases loaded. Volquez's wildness nearly resulted in a brawl when he hit Braves shortstop Yunel Escobar in the back in the third inning. Both benches emptied, but no punches were thrown. Volquez says he feels fine physically, but at times he doesn't know where the ball is headed. He plans to do additional bullpen work on the side to determine the problem.
away_pitcher_note: This is tentative, because Brian Moehler could return to the rotation and slide into this spot. Paulino yielded four runs on 10 hits over six innings in his previous outing against the Brewers, striking out four. He has made one career appearance against the Reds, allowing five earned runs over three innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe limited the Reds to two runs over seven innings on Saturday to notch his first win in a span of four starts.  The 36-year-old sinkerballer was pleased with the fact that he showed better efficiency than he had in his previous two outings, during which he threw more than 100 pitches and didn't pitch more than six innings. He is 2-3 with a 3.15 ERA in seven career starts against the Astros.  In his lone start against them last year, he allowed six earned runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton yielded four runs over six innings in his last start versus the Brewers, taking a no-decision for the second game in a row. Hampton, a former Brave, will face his old team for the 21st time in his career. He's 4-9 versus Atlanta, with a 4.22 ERA. He's 1-1 with a 2.45 ERA over two starts on the road this year, having allowed three runs over 11 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens has gone 0-2 while posting a 1.32 ERA in his past three starts. The Braves have scored a total of three runs during those starts and just one of those came while he was still the pitcher of record. The 23-year-old right-hander has been much more efficient than he was while winning his first two starts of the year with a 3:8 strikeout-to-walk ratio. The only two walks he issued during Monday night's loss to the Cardinals came during the second inning, setting the stage for him to allow a costly two-out single to Rick Ankiel. In his past 20 1/3 innings, Jurrjens has allowed three earned runs and issued six walks.
away_pitcher_note: After a less-than-stellar start to the season, Oswalt has begun to settle down. On April 17, he pitched six shutout innings and had no decision against the Reds, and last Monday, facing Cincinnati again, he threw seven innings and allowed six hits and one run. It's unfortunate for him he can't face the Reds every game. Although he's 0-2 through his first five starts this year, one shouldn't forget that he began last season 0-3 with a 9.00 ERA. He finished the year 17-10 with a 3.54 ERA. It looks like Oswalt is starting to get back into that groove.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes has gone 14 consecutive starts without a win.  But while limiting the Cardinals to one run in seven innings on Tuesday, the 23-year-old southpaw gave reason to believe that he has started to understand what it will take to be successful at the Major League level.  Braves manager Bobby Cox said Reyes' latest outing was the finest of his young career and further proof that the young hurler has ended his days of attempting to be a flamethrower.   In 12 2/3 innings this year, he has registered just two unintentional walks and recorded 22 ground-ball outs.
away_pitcher_note: Wandy Rodriguez continues to show why his early-season success is no fluke. Against the Reds in his last start, Rodriguez was dominant, allowing five hits and a run while striking out five in seven innings. He's among the league leaders in ERA, and in his past three starts, he's held opponents to a .176 batting average while recording a 0.90 ERA. He's registered quality starts in all five of his outings this season.

home_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Lannan had one bad inning and it proved costly. The contest was scoreless until the third. After Shane Victorino singled with one out, Chase Utley drove an 0-2 pitch over the right-field wall for a two-run homer. Lannan tried to throw the pitch in the dirt, but it stayed up in the zone. Lannan was able to get the second out of the inning, but found himself in trouble again. Jayson Werth reached on an error by shortstop Alberto Gonzalez. Lannan said the shoddy defense didn't rattle him, but he continued to have problems on the mound. After Raul Ibanez walked to put runners on first and second, Pedro Feliz hit a three-run homer to make it 5-0. Two innings later, Utley hit his second homer of the game, a solo shot over the right-field wall to give Philadelphia a 6-0 lead. Lannan pitched five innings and gave up six runs (three earned) on nine hits.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler slides back into the rotation after missing nearly three weeks with a sprained right knee. The right-hander made two rehab starts, reaching 90 pitches in his most recent outing at Double-A Frisco on April 29. Moehler has faced the Nationals 12 times in his career, including seven starts. He has a 2-4 record and a 5.95 ERA vs. Washington, allowing 26 earned runs over 39 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: MacDougal may not be used. When the game resumes in the bottom of the 11th inning tied at 10-10, the Nationals will have a runner on first with one out and can win the game. However, if the game continues into the 12th, MacDougal will take the mound. Manager Manny Acta said that he will have six of seven relievers available, with the exception being Julian Tavarez.
away_pitcher_note: LaTroy Hawkins was on the mound for the Astros when their May 5 game against Washington was halted by rain and the Astros see fit for him to continue his outing when the game resumes. Pitchers Roy Oswalt, Chris Sampson and Tim Byrdak are not eligible to pitch because they were used and removed from the game on May 5.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton's return to Atlanta didn't go in his favor, and he ended up tagged with a loss after allowing six runs (five earned) over 4 1/3 innings. The Braves scored four off him in the fifth, due partly to a Lance Berkman error that allowed the bases to be loaded with one out. Hampton has pitched well against the Cubs through his career, compiling a 9-4 record and a 2.98 ERA over 23 games (19 starts).
away_pitcher_note: Harden struggled with his control in his last outing against the Marlins. He walked four, matching a season high, and was pulled after 3 2/3 innings. It was his shortest outing since a 3 2/3-inning start against Texas on May 11, 2008. Harden had struck out 35 in 21 innings prior to the Florida game, when he fanned just two. He did not face the Astros on the Cubs' first trip to Houston, and did not get a decision in his only start against them last year. It also was the 17th time in his career he's given up five or more runs in a game.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz was skipped during the last time through the rotation due to Oswalt's availability after making a 17-pitch start in a rain-delayed game in Atlanta. Ortiz earned his second win of the season after allowing two runs over five innings in a 96-pitch outing against the Brewers in his last start. Ortiz walked four, but only one walk resulted in a run scored. He's frustrated that he's not going deeper into games, which is taxing the bullpen. Ortiz is working on getting ahead earlier in the count, which is something that has eluded him the last couple of starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly will have to pretend he's at Wrigley Field. So far, the lefty has given up one earned run over 21 2/3 innings at home, and has held opponents to a .151 average. In his last outing, he gave up five hits, including a solo homer by Florida's Cody Ross, and went eight innings in a 6-1 win. Lilly struck out 10, the 13th time in his career he's reached double digits. He also recorded only one groundout; the rest were strikeouts or fly-ball outs. And the wind was blowing out. He did beat the Astros in Houston on April 8, but has given up 10 earned runs over 10 innings in two road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez threw only 86 pitches and five innings in his last start against the Braves, his shortest outing of the year. The lefty balked during a shaky final frame but still held Atlanta to three runs. It was the lefty's first outing this year that did not qualify as a quality start. Rodriguez made one start against the Padres last year, taking a no-decision after yielding four runs over five innings. In his career, Rodriguez is 1-2 with an 8.10 ERA verus San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Gaudin wasn't able to replicate the success of his first start with the Padres on April 28, when he tossed five scoreless innings during a no-decision against the Rockies. Gaudin allowed three runs in the first inning of his May 3 start against the Dodgers, including an RBI double off the bat of Andre Ethier that went in and out of the glove of left fielder Chase Headley. Gaudin settled down thereafter and didn't allow another run until the sixth inning, an RBI single with two outs to his counterpart, Chad Billingsley. All told, Gaudin six runs over 5 2/3 innings on eight hits with three walks and five strikeouts. In all fairness, three of those runs scored when reliever Arturo Lopez allowed two hits after Gaudin left the game.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler lasted five innings in his first start back from the disabled in a start against the Nationals. He allowed two runs but took a no-decision in an eventual loss. Moehler faced the Padres once last year in a relief appearance, allowing one run over two-thirds of an inning. In his career, he's 1-1 with a 4.29 ERA over seven games against San Diego.
away_pitcher_note: Correia's quest for win No. 1 on the season continues. He's 0-2 after four starts, his last outing being the worst of the season. Correia surrendered five runs, eight hits and two walks in his shortest appearance in more than a year. The righty racked up two strikeouts in the first inning, but allowed two runs in the next. He needed 75 pitches to get 10 outs.

home_pitcher_note: The bone bruise on Oswalt's right index finger is not expected to force him to miss a start the next time through the rotation. Oswalt left his start versus the Nationals after five innings with the injury. The right-hander was 1-1 with a 4.38 ERA over two starts versus San Diego last year. Lifetime versus the Padres, he's 8-2 with a 2.62 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Geer took a shutout into the eighth inning in his last start on Tuesday before allowing a home run to Colorado's Chris Iannetta. Geer was left with a no-decision, but that certainly didn't take the shine off a start during which he allowed five hits over eight innings. "He had command of his fastball, pitched to both sides of the plate, changed speeds and kept them off-balance," Padres manager Bud Black said. "He has a good feel for what he needed to do as a pitcher. He's a pretty heady pitcher." The start was reminiscent of Geer's first start with the Padres this season in Philadelphia on April 18, when he was promoted from Triple-A Portland to replace Walter Silva after Silva suffered a strained right forearm. He worked fast, threw a lot of strikes and, as he always does, pitched to contact. "I don't like walks," Geer said.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez had his best outing of the season, especially when put back-to-back with a quality seven-inning start in San Francisco in his previous start. He regained command of his fastball and used it with confidence on both sides of the plate, masterfully setting up a big curve that froze hitters consistently. He held the Giants scoreless for seven innings, finally giving up a run when he tried to pitch into the eighth and left with runners on second and third and nobody out.
away_pitcher_note: Paulino replaces Russ Ortiz, who was moved to the bullpen. Paulino was very successful in his three games as a starter this year, but not so much as a reliever. As a starter, he compiled a 2.55 ERA, allowing five earned runs over 17 2/3 innings. He allowed three runs over seven innings as a reliever, however, for a 21.00 ERA. Paulino has never faced the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis had only his second uneven outing of the season against the Giants Thursday, giving up seven runs (five earned) on eight hits over six plus innings. His command was good enough that he issued no walks, but his sinker wasn't at its best, and the Giants, seeing him for the second time in a week, were able to take advantage.  Marquis uncharacteristically hurt himself in the field, making errors on two bunt plays that each led to extended innings and an unearned run in each case.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton's defense didn't help him much during his last outing versus the Cubs, which resulted in two unearned runs of the five he allowed. Hampton did not face the Rockies last year. In his career, he's 9-3 with a 4.56 ERA over 21 games versus Colorado. At Coors Field, which he called home from 2001-02, he is 17-10 with a 5.79 ERA in 33 games.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time in three starts, Hammel was unable to pitch at least five innings. In his last start at home against the Marlins, the right-hander went 4 1/3 innings and he gave up six runs on eight hits to pick up the loss. Hammel has been Jekyll and Hyde this season. In three appearances at home, Hammel has a 10.80 ERA but has yet to allow an earned run in 10 innings on the road. Hammel has never faced the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez threw a gem in his last outing, lasting eight shutout innings against the Padres while yielding five hits. Rodriguez has been the Astros' most consistent starter by a landslide this year, producing quality outings in all but one of his starts. Rodriguez has a career 3-1 record and a 3.50 ERA over seven starts versus the Rockies. He's 2-1 with a 3.93 ERA at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Wells acquitted himself admirably in his first Major League start Friday, pitching five shutout innings and extending his scoreless-innings streak to 10 1/3 to start his career. Wells wasn't terribly efficient, however, tossing 19 pitches in the first inning, 23 in the third and stranding two runners in each of the first three frames. Still, he settled and faced the minimum in the final two frames before the Cubs' bullpen took over and surrendered a late home run that cost Wells his first Major League win. The 26-year-old should get another shot with Carlos Zambrano still on the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler had his best outing of the season in his last start, holding the Padres to one run over seven frames on Saturday. Since his return from the disabled list, he's allowed three runs over 12 innings spanning two starts. Moehler made his season debut against the Cubs at Minute Maid Park on April 8, but was knocked out after just 1 2/3 innings, during which he allowed seven earned runs. In his career, Moehler is 2-1 with a 3.09 ERA over 11 games (eight starts) versus the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Wells acquitted himself admirably in his first Major League start Friday, pitching five shutout innings and extending his scoreless-innings streak to 10 1/3 to start his career. Wells wasn't terribly efficient, however, tossing 19 pitches in the first inning, 23 in the third and stranding two runners in each of the first three frames. Still, he settled and faced the minimum in the final two frames before the Cubs' bullpen took over and surrendered a late home run that cost Wells his first Major League win.
