away_pitcher_note: Oswalt finally earned that elusive first win in his last start, against the Padres, holding them to four runs over six innings in a landslide Houston win. Oswalt, mainly a fastball-curveball pitcher, admitted he's using his slider more, for no other reason than "I don't know what I'm doing right now. I've kind of lost my mind." Prior to that win, Oswalt took five consecutive no-decisions after losing his first two starts of the season. Oswalt faced the Cubs on Opening Day, taking the loss after allowing three runs over seven frames. In his career against the Cubs, Oswalt is 12-12 with a 3.88 ERA over 27 career games, 26 of which were starts.

home_pitcher_note: Harden picked up the win in his last outing against the Padres, giving up two runs on four hits over six innings. He walked one, and that was encouraging. Obviously, he doesn't want to put runners on, but not walking batters also, obviously, helps keep his pitch count down. Harden did give up a two-run homer to Adrian Gonzalez in the first, so next project is to get off to a better start. He beat the Astros on May 6 in Houston, holding them to three runs on eight hits over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler had his best outing of the season in his last start, holding the Padres to one run over seven frames. Since his return from the disabled list, he's allowed three runs over 12 innings spanning two starts. Moehler made his season debut against the Cubs at Minute Maid Park on April 8, but was knocked out after just 1 2/3 innings, during which he allowed seven earned runs. In his career, Moehler is 2-1 with a 3.09 ERA over 11 games (eight starts) versus the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton was the beneficiary of the Astros' 24-hit, 15-run drubbing of the Rockies in his last outing, during which he contributed two hits and allowed five runs over six innings. Hampton walked two and struck out three in the landslide win at Coors Field. Hampton returns to Minute Maid Park to face the Brewers, whom he last faced at home on April 25. He allowed four runs over six innings in that game, which the Astros lost in extra innings. Hampton is 0-1 with a 5.09 ERA over three home starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Bush was originally slated to start Game 2 of this three-game series in Houston, but was bumped up a day after the Brewers' rainout in St. Louis. He will nonetheless be pitching on regular rest. Bush has been good for seven innings in each of his last three outings, matching his season high with seven strikeouts in two of those games, and he has put together a quality start in six of his seven starts this season. He missed the Astros when the Brewers went through Houston last month, but he's 5-1 against them in his career with a 3.50 ERA. All of that success has come in Milwaukee, though; Bush is 0-1 at Minute Maid Park with a 4.31 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struck out a career-high 11 batters in his last outing at Coors Field to record his team-leading fourth win of the year. Rodriguez has won three of his last four starts and hasn't allowed more than three runs in any of his eight outings this year. Rodriguez will face Milwaukee for the first time this year. In 2008, he was 1-1 with a 2.38 ERA over two games. In his career, he's 3-5 with a 4.55 ERA over 12 games.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo threw only 30 pitches in St. Louis on Friday before the game was rained out and the statistics -- Gallardo had surrendered a two-run home run to up-and-coming Cardinals outfielder Colby Rasmus -- were washed away. Instead of slotting him into the makeup game in St. Louis on Monday, Brewers manager Ken Macha opted to keep Gallardo in his regular spot in the rotation. "You know what? If you just look at the short term, you probably say that's a tough thing to do," Macha said. "But I think long-term, it will be good for him. He's got some innings right now, and he's also had some stressful innings." Gallardo is 3-0 with a 1.80 ERA over his last five starts, including his first career complete game at Houston on April 24.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt turned in another quality outing in his last start vs. the Cubs, but took a no-decision in an eventual Houston loss. Oswalt yielded three runs over six innings, but the Astros didn't score until he was already out of the game. The Astros have scored one or no runs six times this year when Oswalt is on the mound. Oswalt has not faced the Brewers yet this year. In 2008, he was 2-0 with a 2.77 ERA in two starts vs. Milwaukee. Lifetime, he's 13-8 with a 3.59 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan was stupendous against his former club on Saturday, holding the Cardinals scoreless on six hits in seven of his best innings this season. It marked the first time this year that Suppan took a shutout into the fifth inning, but he has been a consistent innings-eater for Milwaukee, working at least six frames in five of his last six outings while posting a 2.77 ERA. He took a no-decision in Houston on April 25, when Suppan allowed four runs, three of them earned, on four hits in six innings. He struck out a season-high six batters in that game.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino didn't fare well in his first start since he was promoted to the rotation. In a May 12 outing at Coors Field, he allowed eight runs (seven earned) on seven hits over four innings. Prior to that outing, Paulino hadn't allowed more than four earned runs in any of his first three starts. He has never faced the Rangers.

Moehler allowed three runs over five innings while facing the Cubs in his last outing, earning his first win of the season. The veteran right-hander has allowed five runs over three starts since returning from the disabled list. Moehler made one start against the Rangers last year, earning the win after holding Texas to one run over 6 1/3 innings. In his career, he's 6-4 with a 4.63 ERA over 12 games versus Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman is 2-0 with a 2.17 ERA as a starter, with both victories coming on the road. He pitched six scoreless innings in the Rangers' 3-0 victory over the Angels on Sunday. He has now made 30 Major League starts in the past two years and is 8-8 with a 4.67 ERA in that role. He has a 5.79 ERA in five career games against the Astros without a decision. As a hitter playing under National League rules, he is 1-for-3 with a single last year against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton had to leave his last start against the Brewers early with a small cut on his left thumb. Hampton received a no-decision after allowing two runs on three hits while walking three and striking out four before coming out after the fourth inning. Hampton will return to the mound at Minute Maid Park to face the Rangers still in search of his first win at home this season. Hampton is 0-1 with a 9.53 ERA in two career starts against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: McCarthy went seven innings and allowed four runs for his second consecutive start. He surrendered single runs in each of the first three innings on a night when the high-octane Texas offense only managed one hit. The righty gave up just two hits in his final four innings. McCarthy has appeared three times against the Astros, making one start. He allowed two earned runs in those three outings. Catcher Ivan Rodriguez has gone 6-for-10 lifetime against him with two doubles and two RBIs.

home_pitcher_note: Using his fastball effectively, Harang (4-4) went after the Phillies' aggressive hitters and earned a 5-1 win with seven well pitched innings. All four hits allowed were for extra bases, but only Raul Ibanez's homer did damage. Harang also walked two and tied a season high with nine strikeouts. In two starts vs. the Astros this season, Harang has allowed 10 earned runs over 11 innings. Take away those two outings, and he has a 2.05 ERA over his other seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez earned his fifth win of the season last time out, beating the Brewers by throwing seven innings and giving up one run on six hits while striking out five. He has now won four out of his last five starts and has still yet to give up more than three runs in any of his starts this season. This will be the third start this season against the Reds for Rodriguez. In his first two starts he was brilliant, going 2-0 with a 0.64 ERA, giving up only seven hits and one earned run while striking out 15 and walking four combined in both appearances. In 2008, he was 1-2 with a 4.24 ERA in four games. In his career, he's 5-4 with a 4.24 ERA over 13 games.

home_pitcher_note: In a 12-5 loss to the Phillies on Thursday, Owings gave up five earned runs and six hits over just three innings, walking three walks and striking out three. The right-hander left trailing, 5-0. He was coming off a 5 2/3-inning emergency relief appearance during a 16-inning loss to the Padres. In two career starts against Houston, Owings is 1-0 with a 1.69 ERA. In 10 2/3 innings, he walked one and struck out eight, allowing 11 hits.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt scattered 10 hits and gave up three runs in 6 1/3 innings against the Brewers in his last outing. He struck out seven and walked one to earn a no-decision. Oswalt has faced the Reds twice this season and has pitched very well, only giving up one earned run on 11 hits in 13 innings, but he has recieved a no-decision in both of his starts. In 2008, he was 4-0 with a 2.52 ERA in four starts versus Cincinnati. Lifetime, he's 23-1 with a 2.35 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo had one of his best efforts of the season during a 3-1 Reds win over the Indians on Friday. He gave up one earned run and five hits, walking two and striking out two over eight innings to earn the win after Cincinnati broke a 1-1 tie in the bottom of the eighth. The right-hander also induced three ground-ball double plays. The only Cleveland run came on Grady Sizemore's first-inning homer into the right-field bullpen. It was only Arroyo's second win at home. On April 20 at Houston, he was a 4-3 winner after allowing three earned runs and nine hits over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on nine days' rest, Paulino gave up four earned runs on seven hits against the Rangers in hist last start, striking out three and walking two over 5 1/3 innings to receive a no-decision in the Astros' 6-5 loss. Paulino has started twice against the Reds this season but hasn't received much run support in the two outings, going 0-1 despite having a 0.77 ERA, having allowed only one earned run. He is 1-1 with a 3.24 ERA in three career appearances against Cincinnati.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf had nothing to hang his head about after his last outing, a 7 2/3-inning start in which he allowed three earned runs on six hits. The start was the longest of Ohlendorf's career, and it was also the first start this season in which he had surpassed the 100-pitch plateau. The right-hander threw 114 pitches in all. The key for Ohlendorf, as always, was keeping his pitches down and maintaining a quicker tempo on the mound. Ohlendorf is still looking for his first career win against the Astros. He is 0-3 with an 8.44 ERA in five appearances (three starts) against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Moehler had his first shaky outing since returning from the disabled list, giving up six runs on nine hits over five innings against the Rangers in a losing effort. He had allowed five runs in three previous starts since recovering from a sprained right knee. Moehler has faced the Pirates once already this season, taking the loss after giving up five runs on seven hits in 2 1/3 innings. Last season, he was 2-1 with a 9.39 ERA in four starts against Pittsburgh. In his career against the Pirates, Moehler is 5-6 with a 6.37 ERA in 15 appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Karstens allowed three two-out runs in his last start, which lasted 5 1/3 innings. He hasn't won since his second start of the season and has yet to pitch past the sixth in any of his eight outings this year. His starts haven't been bad, per se, but they've all pretty much been mediocre, leaving the Pirates still looking for more out of their fifth starter. On a positive note, after walking 13 in his first four starts, Karstens has issued only three free passes in his four starts since. He allowed three runs on four hits and five walks in his start against the Astros earlier this year.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez threw only 78 pitches in a rain-shortened outing in Cincinnati in his last start, so it's safe to say he'll be well-rested for the finale in Pittsburgh. Rodriguez allowed six runs -- all unearned -- in a defensively sloppy loss to the Reds. He last faced the Pirates in 2008, logging one win after holding the Pirates scoreless over six frames. In his career, Rodriguez is 3-3 with a 4.96 ERA over nine game.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm was nowhere near his usually efficient form, needing 93 pitches to finish only four innings. His night would end there, too, as he allowed seven runs for the second time this season. He is now winless in his last six starts and has seen his ERA swell from 2.03 to 4.41 in that span. He struggled to throw his breaking ball for strikes last time out and left too many pitches up, rarely something he struggles with. Maholm is 5-3 with a 4.91 in nine career starts against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton is still winless at home after giving up five runs on eight hits and walking one in five innings pitched against the Rangers on Sunday. Hampton won his only start against the Pirates this year, throwing six innings of shutout ball and striking out eight in the Astros 4-1 win on April 15. He is 11-3 with a 2.57 ERA versus Pittsburgh in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt was uncharacteristically wild toward the end of his last outing versus the Reds, walking in the tying run with a four-pitch walk to Jonny Gomes in his final inning. Oswalt, who took a no-decision in that game, was pitching with a bruised hand after fielding a grounder with his pitching hand. He continues to search for his second win of the season, in his 11th start. Oswalt won his only start versus Colorado in '08, pitching a complete game shutout. In his career, he's 6-1 with a 1.84 ERA over nine starts versus the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: For the most part, Cook pitched well Tuesday night. But a fourth inning that saw him walk two, then give up a three-run double to Casey Blake, left him with the decision in a 7-1 loss to the Dodgers. For Cook, not being able to locate one sinker where he wanted was the difference between a good outing and a poor one. Interestingly, Cook threw his first career shutout at Atlanta on May 21, but still has a 5.76 road ERA this season.

home_pitcher_note: Cecil Cooper guaranteed Paulino would receive another start regardless of the results of the right-hander's last outing, so Paulino will pitch against the Rockies in the second game of the four-game home set. Paulino allowed three home runs in a loss to the Reds his last time out, giving up five runs (four earned) on seven hits over six innings. Paulino last faced the Rockies on May 12 in Denver, allowing eight runs (seven earned) over four innings in a losing effort.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez sailed for much of six innings, but faltered with two down in the seventh and took the loss against the Dodgers on Wednesday at Coors Field. There was plenty to like, however. He went to a two-seam fastball and bordered on dominant. He didn't have 20 pitches in an inning until the seventh. It'll be just Jimenez's second start at Houston's Minute Maid Park (0-0, 4.76).

home_pitcher_note: Moehler was stellar in his most recent start, tossing his first complete game in almost nine years during a 6-0 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates Friday. Since being reinstated from the disabled list May 4, Moehler is 2-1 with a 3.90 ERA. He has not been too good against Colorado in his career (1-2, 6.85 ERA), nor at Minute Maid Park this season (0-2, 9.22 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: Right-hander Jason Marquis has been the Rockies best pitcher the first two months and he showed it in his last start against the Padres. Marquis relied on his sharp sinker for eight shutout innings, scattering six hits and striking out six to notch his seventh win. In his last start against the Astros, Marquis gave up nine runs in 3 2/3 innings, easily his worst performance this season.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has struggled mightily over the course of his past two starts after being arguably the best starter in the National League through his first nine outings. He didn't get out of the fifth inning either May 25 at Cincinnati nor Saturday at Pittsburgh, being charged with a combined 11 runs (five earned) on 19 hits and five walks in 9 2/3 innings, losing each time. He had allowed only 12 earned runs in his first 63 innings this season, leading the NL in ERA before Saturday. Rodriguez is 4-1 with a 3.35 ERA in eight career starts against Colorado.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel threw plenty of strikes in his last start against the Padres -- 48 of them in 65 pitches -- but he left a few pitches up in the strike zone and paid the price. In 3 2/3 innings of work, Hammel didn't have his fastball command and yielded a three-run home run, an RBI double and an RBI triple, but got a no-decision. Hammel's next start should be on the road, where he's been much more comfortable (1.64 road ERA vs. 8.53 home ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Hampton has to be pleased about making his second consecutive start against the Pirates. He has won his past eight decisions against them -- having not lost to the Bucs in more than nine years -- and is 2-0 with an 0.69 ERA against them this season. His most recent start was in Pittsburgh Sunday, when he allowed one run on three hits in seven innings. Hampton is 0-2 with a 5.74 ERA at Minute Maid Park this season.
away_pitcher_note: Karstens had one of his best starts of the season in his last game, when he went seven innings and gave up just two runs against Houston. The seven innings were the most he's pitched since a complete-game shutout against Arizona last August. After struggling with his command early in the season, Karstens has just four walks in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Start No. 12 was a lucky one for Oswalt, who finally captured his second win of the season. Oswalt bounced back from his uncharacteristically wild outing against the Reds to hold Colorado to one run on six hits in his last start, striking out eight and walking two over seven innings. Oswalt was 2-1 with a 1.71 ERA in three starts against the Pirates last season. In his career, Oswalt is 13-6 with a 2.40 ERA over 24 starts against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: It will be back-to-back starts against the Astros for Maholm, who lost to Houston in his last start despite allowing only two runs -- one earned -- in seven innings. Though Maholm is now winless in his last seven starts, that outing last Sunday seemed to get Maholm back on track after his previous start, which lasted but four innings. There are still some consistency issues with Maholm's fastball, but nothing that he feels can't be fixed before his next start. He is now 5-4 with a 4.50 ERA in 10 career starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino justified his spot in the starting rotation, at least for the time being, by holding the Rockies to five hits and two runs and striking out a career-high seven batters in six innings in his previous start Tuesday. Despite giving the Astros their fourth quality start in five games, Paulino took a no-decision. The Astros have scored just 12 runs in his seven starts. Paulino's only career outing against the Pirates came in 2007 when he threw one inning in relief.
away_pitcher_note: Snell's struggles continued in his last start, when he gave up five runs in six innings while tying a season high with five walks. All of the runs came before the fourth inning, however, as he rebounded in the last three frames to take a no-decision. Despite the turnaround, Snell remained winless in his past eight outings. Since pitching seven shutout innings on April 18, Snell has given up 29 runs in 42 innings. He is 2-5 in 13 career appearances against the Astros, including 12 starts. He has yet to face Houston this season.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler started his last game strong, allowing only two hits in the first four innings, but he ran into trouble after that. The right-hander gave up four runs over the next two innings and came out after having given up seven and one walk while striking out two in six innings of work, getting a no-decision. Moelher has faced the Cubs twice already this season, going 1-1. In his most recent start against Chicago he gave up three runs on five hits and struck out four over five innings to earn the win. He was 1-2 with a 3.68 ERA in four starts versus the Cubs last year. In his career, Moehler is 3-3 with a 5.05 ERA in nine starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly turned in his team-best eighth quality start last Wednesday, allowing two runs (one earned) over seven innings in a no-decision at Atlanta. He gave up six hits, walked one and struck out seven. Lilly is 4-1 with a 1.29 ERA at home, but 2-3 on the road. The left-hander has always had good success against Houston, no matter where the game is. He was 2-0 against the Astros last year with a 1.40 ERA and is 3-1 with a 2.52 ERA lifetime. The only loss occurred in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: After giving up just 12 earned runs in his first 63 innings this season, Rodriguez has struggled. He's 0-3 in his last three starts and has given up a combined 18 runs (12 earned) on 29 hits and five walks in 14 2/3 innings. In his last start, Rodriguez gave up seven runs on 10 hits in five innings, surrendering four home runs to the Rockies. Rodriguez has faced the Cubs once already this year and picked up a win, giving up one run on four hits over six innings. Last season he was 1-0 with a 5.40 ERA in two starts vs. the Cubs. In his career, he is 4-4 with a 4.39 ERA against Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano notched his 100th career victory in his last start against the Reds. The right-hander threw 6 2/3 scoreless innings, giving up two hits and striking out seven. He's the 21st pitcher in franchise history to reach 100 wins. This was his first start after serving a six-game suspension, and the only problem was that he walked five. None scored. He beat Houston on Opening Day, April 6, holding the Astros to one run on five hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz pitched 4 1/3 innings of scoreless relief on Sunday, coming in to replace Felipe Paulino, who was forced to come out with a right groin strain. Ortiz will again step in for Paulino, who is sidelined with the groin injury for his next start. Ortiz has put together a 12 1/3-inning scoreless streak. As a starter this season he is 2-1 with 5.82 ERA and hasn't allowed more than three runs in any start. His last start came on May 7 against the Cubs, who he'll face again Thursday. Ortiz is 3-5 with a 5.71 ERA in 12 games against Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster did not get the win in his last start against the Reds. He gave up three runs, all unearned, on six hits over six innings and struck out seven. The right-hander was pulled after 84 pitches, his second-shortest outing of the year as far as his pitch count goes. He has faced Houston once, and that was in his first start, on April 7. In that game, Dempster gave up two runs on six hits over six innings, but did not get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Haren's last start was emblematic of the way his season has gone -- he pitched outstanding, but came away with no decision. The right-hander allowed just one run on four hits over seven innings Sunday afternoon against the Padres and left with a seemingly safe 6-1 lead. The bullpen, though, gave up five runs in the ninth and the D-backs wound up winning 9-6 in 18 innings. In his previous start against the Dodgers, Haren left with a 5-1 lead after seven innings. This time the bullpen imploded in a five-run eighth inning as the D-backs went on to lose 6-5. The frustration started early this year for Haren when the D-backs scored a total of one run in his first three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton is coming off two strong outings against Pittsburgh to even his record. He held the Pirates to three hits and one run in seven innings on May 31 in Pittsburgh, and he allowed just one run on five hits on June 5 in Houston, moving past Jim Deshaies and into third place on the club's all-time left-handed strikeout list in the process. Hamtpon is 7-8 with 5.56 ERA in his career versus Arizona. He lost his only outing against the D-backs last season.

home_pitcher_note: He was not pinpoint with his command, but Garland managed to get through the first four innings against the Padres in his last start without allowing a run. He was eventually charged with six runs on seven hits in 6 2/3 innings for the loss, his fourth in a row. Garland has not won a game since giving up two runs in six innings against the Marlins on May 19, but still racks up innings. He's pitched at least six innings nine times in his 12 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt's next start was pushed back a few days because of a sore wrist. His up-and-down season suffered another road bump in his previous start, against Pittsburgh on Saturday, when he allowed nine hits and six earned runs in six innings. Oswalt went 0-2 with a 3.94 ERA in April, 1-0 with a 5.34 in May and won his first start in June before losing on Saturday. The right-hander won his only start against Arizona last season and is 7-1 with a 2.25 ERA in nine starts versus the D-backs in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Buckner will be the first to admit that he didn't have his best stuff and that he struggled with his execution his last time on the mound. Against the Giants, he was charged with eight runs and 13 hits in 5 2/3 innings for the loss. After an efficient start, he struggled in the middle innings and was doomed when the Giants had consecutive three-run innings in the fifth and sixth. His mettle was  tested after giving up a 433-foot home run to Pedro Sandoval. Buckner has never faced the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: For the second time this season, Moehler didn't make it past the third inning against Chicago. Moehler gave up five runs on eight hits and was taken out after the third against the Cubs in his last start. In his first start of the season, the 37-year old gave up seven runs on eight hits and was taken out after just 1 1/3 innings on April 8 versus Chicago. In his career, Moelher is 1-1 with a 5.82 ERA over four starts versus the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood won his sixth game of the season after holding the Blue Jays scoreless over 7 2/3 innings on Thursday. Despite a 2.72 ERA, this was only his second consecutive victory this season. Millwood has 2.19 ERA at home. He has now thrown 100 or more pitches in 11 of 13 starts and finished at least the seventh inning in 10 of 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: After going 0-3 in his last three starts and giving up a combined 18 runs (12 earned) on 29 hits and five walks in 14 2/3 innings, Rodriguez settled back into a groove on Tuesday. There had been rumblings that he may had been tipping his pitches the last few times out, but he rediscovered his form last time out. Rodriguez gave up just one run over seven innings against the Cubs, striking out six. He received a no-decision for his effort. Rodriguez didn't pitch against Texas earlier this season. Last year he beat the Rangers in his only start against them, giving up one run over eight innings. He has never lost to the Rangers in his career, winning all three starts against them, compiling a 3.26 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison returns to the Rangers rotation after making two Minor League rehab starts. He threw 74 pitches (44 for strikes) Thursday for Double-A Frisco over four innings. He allowed one earned run, walked three and struck out one. Harrison has been on the disabled list since May 26 with left shoulder inflammation. He is 4-4 with a 5.43 ERA in nine starts this season and 5-2 with a 5.94 ERA in his career at home.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander threw 5 1/3 scoreless innings in his previous start June 11 against the Cubs to extend his scoreless innings streak to 17 2/3, the longest such streak by an Astros pitcher this year. He threw 4 1/3 scoreless innings in relief June 7 against Pittsburgh before being put back in the rotation when Felipe Paulino was forced to miss a start with an injured groin. Ortiz is 7-6 with a 3.75 ERA all-time in Interleague Play in 26 games (including 22 starts). Against the Rangers, he's pitched in 20 2/3 innings in seven games (two starts) and has yet to pick up a decision against them.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla needed 108 pitches to get through five innings as the bullpen came through to complete an eight-hit shutout of the Los Angeles Dodgers on Friday. Padilla threw 71 pitches for strikes, 39 were foul balls. He threw his curve ball and slider for strikes. Padilla has bounced back from being place on waivers by winning consecutive games against two of baseball's best teams, Boston and Los Angeles. He has won four of his last five starts, going 4-1 with a 3.82 ERA over that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: With Mike Hampton going on the disabled list with a strained groin following Tuesday's game, Backe will get the chance to make his first start of the season. Backe struggled as a starter last year, going 9-14 with a 6.05 ERA in 31 starts in his first full season since undergoing Tommy John surgery. He led the league in earned runs (112) and home runs (36), but missed two months when he injured a ribcage muscle in early March. As a reliever this year, Backe has pitched nine innings in four games and allowed 17 hits and 12 runs while striking out 10 batters. He's 1-2 with a 7.77 ERA in six career games (three starts) against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey produced a season-high 10-strikeout game in his last outing, a 7-4 victory against the Cubs on Friday. He surpassed his previous season high of eight strikeouts by the fifth inning. In fact, 10 of Slowey's first 16 outs came via the strikeout, and he struck out the side in both the second and fifth innings. He faltered a bit in the sixth, allowing three runs, but he protected the lead to earn his team-high ninth victory.
away_pitcher_note: Working on six days' rest worked wonders for Oswalt in his last start on Saturday, when he held Arizona to five hits for seven innings and claimed total control of both his fastball and curve for the first time this season. A touch of tendinitis in his right wrist had pushed back that start, and the little breather may prove to have been enough to launch him on an extended streak. Oswalt certainly sounded confident following the victory over the D-backs, which restored his faith in his breaking pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Baker yielded two runs on five hits while striking out five and walking none in seven innings, earning a no-decision against the Cubs on Sunday. He was in command for much of the game, throwing 70 of his 98 pitches for strikes. It marked his third consecutive quality start and his fifth on the season. Over his last three starts, Baker is 2-0 with a 2.86 ERA. He has never faced the Astros but owns a 6-2 mark in Interleague Play in nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler picked up his third win of the season Sunday in Arizona by holding the Diamondbacks to three runs and six hits in six innings in another twist in his up-and-down season. The outing prior to beating the Diamondbacks, he gave up eight hits and five runs in three innings in a loss to the Cubs. Because he pitched so many years with Detroit, Moehler is not stranger to the Twins. He's 2-4 with a 4.65 ERA in 10 career starts against Minnesota, and is 8-10 with a 4.07 ERA in 33 games (27 starts) in Interleague play. He's never won in two career starts in Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins allowed just two runs on seven hits over six innings Tuesday in his first start after coming off the disabled list. The left-hander walked one and struck out four while earning the win. It was a bit of an up-and-down start for Perkins. He retired the side in three of his six innings but gave up a two-run homer in the third and loaded the bases with one out in the fifth before getting an inning-ending double play. Perkins will next face the Astros, a team he has never faced. But Perkins holds a 3-0 record with a 3.96 ERA in four Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off one of his better performances of the 2009 season June 10 against Chicago, the left-hander was roughed up Tuesday against the Texas Rangers in Arlington when he gave up six hits, including three home runs, six runs and walked six batters. Rodriguez started the season 5-2, but has lost four of his last five starts and four consecutive decisions. In his only previous career appearance against the Twins, he pitched 6 2/3 innings and allowed three runs (two earned) on June 21, 2006, in Houston. Rodriguez is 5-5 with a 4.59 ERA in 13 career Interleague starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz, who entered his previous start, Wednesday at Texas, having thrown 17 2/3 consecutive scoreless innings, gave up seven hits and four runs -- three earned -- and struck out five batters in six innings against the Rangers in his sixth start of the season. He's 7-6 with a 3.75 ERA in 26 career Interleague games (22 starts) and has no record and a 3.21 ERA in two career starts against the Royals. His .778 winning percentage at Minute Maid Park is tied for the highest in the stadium's history by pitchers with at least nine decisions.
away_pitcher_note: It's been four starts now since Greinke, at one time 8-1 and an early-season sensation, has won a game. He's been stalled with two losses and two no-decisions. Last Wednesday night, the D-backs drove up his pitch count early and took advantage of two errors to go ahead. Mark Reynolds finished him off with a two-run homer, just the third blast Greinke has allowed in 101 innings. He struck out nine, boosting his total to 106 against only 18 walks. This will be the first time Greinke has faced the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt tossed his first complete game of the season and 16th of his career by throwing 126 pitches in eight innings in Friday's 5-2 loss to the Minnesota Twins in Minneapolis. The pitch count was tied for the third-highest of his career, and it was his most since May 11, 2005, in Florida. Despite the loss, Oswalt's performance against the Twins was perhaps his grittiest of the season. This will be only his second career start against the Royals. He held Kansas City to seven hits and one run in eight innings on June 18, 2005, in Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: After throwing a complete game on 80 pitches against the Reds on June 12, Hochevar returned to earth in his last start against the Diamondbacks. He pitched into the fifth inning but couldn't record an out, and his final line showed nine hits and six earned runs. The real trouble came in the third inning, when he surrendered four runs. After the best start of his career lowered his ERA to 5.60, Hochevar's performance against the D-backs raised it back to 6.61. The Royals will hope Hochevar can revert back to the form he showed against the Reds when he makes his first career start against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler beat the Minnesota Twins in his previous start Saturday, allowing only four hits in six innings. Three of the hits were solo homers, which Moehler doesn't mind giving up as long as he's not walking batters. He's won two consecutive starts for the first time this year. Considering he spent six-plus years in the American League with Detroit, he has faced the Royals seven times in his career. He's 2-1 with a 4.62, allowing 53 hits in 39 innings in those games, all starts.
away_pitcher_note: Since being knocked around on June 3 at Tampa Bay, Bannister has been on a three-game roll. He has just one victory to show for it, along with a no-decision and a loss, but his ERA in those three games is 1.29. He's gone eight innings in each of his last two starts, a win over the Reds followed by a loss to the Cardinals. In the St. Louis game, he was just outpitched by a more superb Chris Carpenter. Bannister gave up six hits and walked none. This is his first career appearance against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is coming off perhaps his best start of the season, holding the Minnesota Twins to two hits and one run while striking out eight batters in seven innings Sunday. He snapped his four-game losing streak with his first win since May 20, allowing just one hit in the first 22 batters he faced. Rodriguez has faced the Tigers only once previously, and it wasn't pretty. He gave up 10 hits and seven earned runs in 6 2/3 innings in an 8-5 loss on June 26, 2006, in Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers broke up the back-to-back tandem of Verlander and Edwin Jackson to help out a rotation that has two rookie starters, but the break means little for teams that have to face Verlander these days. His eighth win in his last 11 outings, 10 of them quality starts, saw him overcome a first-inning home run to hold down the Brewers for 7 2/3 innings and outpitch budding star Yovani Gallardo on Sunday at Comerica Park. He continues to build on his Major League strikeout lead, but his pitch counts are allowing him to work deeper into games. His one career matchup with the Astros saw him outpitch Andy Pettitte for eight scoreless innings and seven strikeouts on June 28, 2006 in Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino will make his first start since June 11 after being on the 15-day disabled list. He was forced to leave his last start against the Pirates in the middle of the second inning, having thrown just 34 pitches, after straining his right groin. Paulino has never faced the Tigers. The only Interleague start of his career came earlier this season against the Rangers, where he gave up four runs on seven hits over 5 1/3 innings, receiving a no decision.
away_pitcher_note: Figaro, the latest rookie to crack Detroit's rotation, gave up eight hits over five innings in his Major League debut last Saturday against Milwaukee, but he also showed the pitches that elevated him up the Tigers' prospect list before he got the call. Armed with four potential big league pitches, Figaro struck out seven hitters, the first Tigers pitcher to do that in his big league debut since Dave Borkowski fanned eight in 1999, and his fastball topped out at 97 mph on the Comerica Park radar gun. Just as important, the 24-year-old showed an impressive ability to stay relaxed in tight situations.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz's 17 2/3 consecutive scoreless innings was broken up against the Rangers and Ortiz looked to get another streak started against the Royals last time out. Ortiz gave up runs in the second and third innings but held the Astros in the game, allowing just the two runs on five hits over seven innings, his longest outing of the season. Ortiz is 7-6 in 27 career Interleague games (23 starts) and has no record and a 6.14 ERA in two career appearances (one start) against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: The signs of Jackson's maturity as a pitcher are best seen when he doesn't have his best stuff, and Tuesday was one of times. With a biting slider that was moving almost too much to command, Jackson had the bases loaded with Cubbies three batters into the game, escaped that jam with a lone run allowed, then allowed one more run over his next six innings for a no-decision in his duel with Carlos Zambrano. His ratio of hits per nine innings is down to 7.016, best among American League starters, and his 2.39 ERA stands second in the league to the Royals' Zack Greinke.

home_pitcher_note: Geer took his second no-decision in as many starts last Wednesday against the Mariners, allowing three earned runs over six innings. He was hurt by a three-run home run in the second inning, though allowing just one home run was a marked improvement from Geer's previous two starts, when he allowed a combined six home runs. Geer struggled with the movement on his two-seam fastball early in the game, which led to an uncharacteristic two walks. "It still hurts to give up home runs," said Geer, who has allowed 17 home runs in 70 2/3 innings. "It's the worst thing you can do. You never want to give up a three-run home run. They can kill you."
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt, coming off a complete-game loss at Minnesota on June 19, pitched well and took a no-decision last Wednesday against the Royals. Oswalt held Kansas City to seven hits and one run and struck out eight batters in six innings, leaving the game for a pinch-hitter in the sixth. Oswalt has allowed one earned run in three of his past five starts. He is 9-2 with a 2.87 ERA in 14 career appearances against the Padres, including 12 starts. He's 2-1 with a 3.09 ERA in four career starts at PETCO Park.

home_pitcher_note: Banks takes Wade LeBlanc's spot in the rotation after LeBlanc was demoted to Triple-A. Banks provided the Padres with long relief after LeBlanc was knocked out early in both of those starts. As a starter in his career, Banks has posted a 2-6 record with a 5.40 ERA over 81 2/3 innings pitched. In five appearances as a reliever, he has a 1.64 ERA over 11 innings pitched. Banks is 0-0 with a 2.84 ERA this season.
away_pitcher_note: Tuesday will be Hampton's first start since straining his groin on the last pitch he threw June 12 against the D-backs in Arizona. In that outing against Arizona, Hampton walked a season-high five batters and gave up three runs on eight hits over five innings, taking the loss. Hampton is 4-5 with a 4.70 ERA in 12 starts this year for the Astros. He has not faced the Padres since 2005. In his career, the left-hander is 6-10 with a 5.17 ERA over 25 starts vs. San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: Silva posted his worst start of the season on Friday against the Rangers. He allowed nine runs -- eight earned -- over 2 1/3 innings, as well as seven hits and four walks. It was his fourth Major League start. Silva has never faced the Astros. In two starts at PETCO Park, he is 0-0 with a 4.36 ERA over 10 1/3 innings pitched. Silva has yet to win his first Major League game.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler fell victim to sloppy defense in his last start, against the Kansas City Royals. Moehler received a no-decision after giving up four runs over five innings, but just one of those runs was earned, as the Astros committed three errors behind the right-hander. He has faced the Padres once this season already, picking up the win on May 9 with a seven-inning start in which he allowed one run on five hits and struck out six.

home_pitcher_note: Correia posted his fifth consecutive quality outing Saturday, holding the Rangers to three runs over seven innings. He struck out a career-high nine batters and faced the minimum in four innings. Correia needed only 95 pitches. In 20 games (11 starts) at PETCO Park, he is 3-3 with a 4.36 ERA over 74 1/3 innings. Over his last five outings, Correia is 4-1 with a 2.40 ERA. Over that stretch, he has a 29-to-3 strikeout-to-walk ratio and opponents are hitting .155 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez wasn't spectacular last time out against the Detroit Tigers, but he kept the Astros in the game, allowing them to come back for a win on Friday. Rodriguez received a no-decision, giving up a home run in the first and second innings, but allowing the Tigers to score only one run after that. He began the season giving up just one home run in his first 11 starts, but has allowed a long ball in each of his past five outings. Rodriguez has faced the Padres once already this season and was brilliant, picking up the win on May 8, allowing no runs and striking out seven over eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Sadowski was a sensation in his Major League debut last Sunday at Milwaukee, allowing four hits in six shutout innings as the Giants prevailed, 7-0. Sadowski, who struck out only two batters, can reach the low-90 mph range with his fastball but relies mostly on location and late movement. He displayed adequate control against the Brewers, issuing three walks. Sadowski became the first Giants pitcher to win his Major League debut since Joe Nathan in 1999.
away_pitcher_note: Paulino turned in his best performance of the season last time out against the Tigers. Making his first since June 7 after being on the disabled list with a strained right groin, the right-hander set career highs in strike outs and innings pitched, fanning nine over seven frames of three-hit ball. Paulino allowed just one run and retired the last 10 batters he faced, earning his first win as a starter this season. Paulino has never faced the Giants in his career. He is 0-1 with an 8.01 ERA in two starts against the National League West this season, both coming against the Colorado Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum outdid himself last Monday at St. Louis, firing a two-hit shutout. It was the third shutout of his career and second of the season. Lincecum remains overpowering -- he struck out 12 two starts ago at Oakland -- but he has relied more and more on "pitching to contact" and putting batters away earlier in the count, thus reducing wear and tear on his valuable arm. Nevertheless, Lincecum's 21-4 with a 2.06 ERA when he strikes out at least eight batters in a game. He's 1-0 with a 2.13 ERA in four career starts against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Ortiz solidified his spot in the starting rotation by holding Detroit to six hits and two runs while striking out five batters in 7 1/3 innings on Sunday. He would have won the game had closer Jose Valverde not blown the save in the ninth inning. Ortiz enjoyed some of his best years in San Francisco, going 69-47 in six seasons with the Giants, including an 18-9 record in 1999. Against the Giants, he's 0-3 with a 7.46 ERA in seven starts. Ortiz is 20-15 with a 3.64 ERA in 56 career games at AT&T Park, including 53 starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Big Unit picked up career victory No. 303 last Tuesday at St. Louis. Two Albert Pujols home runs marred his 5 1/3-inning performance, but Johnson yielded just two other hits as the Giants prevailed, 6-3. If Johnson's pitching, expect reliever Brian Wilson to follow at some point. Wilson has saved each of Johnson's victories, marking the eighth time in big league history that one pitcher saved a teammate's first eight wins in a season. Johnson, who was 10-1 for the Astros in the second half of the 1998 season, is 4-1 in seven career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: After winning one game in the first two months of the regular season, Oswalt went 3-2 with a 3.14 ERA in six starts in June. He's coming off his best start of the season, a two-hitter at San Diego on Monday, in which the only run scored on a wild pitch. He's 4-5 with a 3.98 ERA in 12 career starts against the Giants, and 2-5 with a 4.96 ERA in eight career starts at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton returned from the disabled list in his previous start Tuesday at San Diego and pitched well, holding the Padres to four hits and one run in six innings. This will be his fourth start this year against Pittsburgh, a team he has dominated in 2009 and in his career. He's 3-0 with a 0.90 ERA in three starts against the Pirates this year and 13-3 with a 2.44 ERA in his career. His .813 winning percentage against the Pirates his best against any team with more than one decision.
away_pitcher_note: Vasquez is 2-for-2 in the quality starts department since being called up to join the rotation in what was Ian Snell's spot. Vasquez finished six innings in his last start but allowed three runs to score on two home runs. Though he did have seven strikeouts in first start for the Pirates, Vasquez is not overpowering, relying mainly on his fastball but also on an improving changeup. This will be Vasquez's first career start against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler has won three of his past four starts, going 3-0 with a 3.13 ERA. In his previous start Wednesday in San Diego, he went six innings and held the Padres to four hits and one run, while walking four batters and striking out a season-high eight. He's 6-6 with a 5.66 ERA in 16 career games against the Pirates, including 13 starts. He threw a complete game against Pittsburgh on May 29, holding the Pirates to seven hits and one run at PNC Park.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm continues to battle problems with his sinker, a pitch that has always been his most reliable. The left-hander has had games where the pitch has worked effectively, but more often than not these last two months, it's been a major struggle. Maholm was knocked out after 4 1/3 innings in his last start and allowed six runs on 11 hits. In the past two months, five of Maholm's starts have not gone past the fifth. He had only three starts of five or fewer innings all of last year. Maholm is 6-4 with a 4.57 ERA in 11 career starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander won his second consecutive decision Thursday by holding San Diego to seven hits and one run while striking out five batters. Rodriguez is 3-4 with a 5.37 ERA in 10 career starts against the Pirates, but was roughed up by Pittsburgh in his only appearance against it this year. That came on May 30 in Pittsburgh when he gave up nine hits and five runs in 4 2/3 innings. Rodriguez is 25-20 with a 3.91 ERA in 65 career games (63 starts) at Minute Maid Park.
away_pitcher_note: Despite enduring two rain delays in his last start, Morton showed how effective he can be when he's finally healthy and able to pitch on normal rest. The lingering hamstring injury appears to be in the past, and Morton showcased exceptional movement on his pitches in a one-hit, six-inning shutout of the Marlins. He did walk four, however, while at times losing his control for stretches. Morton has made one career start against the Astros, that coming last season. Morton allowed six runs on eight hits in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: MacDougal may not be used. When the game resumes in the bottom of the 11th inning tied at 10-10, the Nationals will have a runner on first with one out and can win the game. However, if the game continues into the 12th, MacDougal will take the mound. Manager Manny Acta said that he will have six of seven relievers available, with the exception being Julian Tavarez.
away_pitcher_note: LaTroy Hawkins was on the mound for the Astros when their May 5 game against Washington was halted by rain and the Astros see fit for him to continue his outing when the game resumes. Pitchers Roy Oswalt, Chris Sampson and Tim Byrdak are not eligible to pitch because they were used and removed from the game on May 5.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz gave up nine eights and eight runs in his most recent start, last Saturday against the Giants. He was cruising through 4 2/3 innings before unraveling quickly and losing for the second time in three starts. He hasn't won a game as a starter since back-to-back wins on April 21 and 26. Ortiz is 11-6 with a 3.11 ERA in 18 career starts against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan ended up being the winning pitcher on Saturday, yielding three runs on nine hits over eight innings against the Braves. At 6-5, it's the first time since Aug. 1, 2007, that Lannan has a record over .500 during the season. The first run scored in the third inning when Nate McLouth singled up the middle to drive in Brooks Conrad. In the sixth, Chipper Jones and Garret Anderson had RBI singles, but Lannan was able to get out of the inning when Yunel Escobar hit into a double play.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt has regained his dominating form, going 3-1 with a 2.13 ERA in his past five starts. He threw a two-hitter on June 29 at San Diego and allowed one run on a wild pitch, then he held the Giants to three hits and one run in his last start, on Sunday in San Francisco. Oswalt is 3-1 with a 2.97 ERA in 11 career games (nine starts) against the Nationals. He allowed four runs on four hits in five innings in Washington, D.C., on May 5 in a game that was postponed because of inclement weather.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen came within one out of pitching the first complete game of his career and helped the Nationals defeat the Braves, 5-3, at Nationals Park on Sunday. Olsen gave up three runs on eight hits in 8 2/3 innings. He also went 2-for-3 and drove in a run. With two outs in the ninth inning, the Braves' Nate McLouth hit a two-run homer that knocked Olsen from the game after 116 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton was masterful once again against the Pirates. In his fourth start of year against Pittsburgh, Hampton allowed one run on three hits and struck out three over seven innings, improving to 4-0 with a 1.00 ERA versus the Bucs this season. Hampton as faced the Washington franchise 18 times in his career, the majority of his appearances coming when the organization was in Montreal. Since the move to the nation's capital in 2005, Hampton is 1-0 with a 2.37 ERA in three starts. His last start against the Nationals came last year. He gave up five runs (four earned) on eight hits and struck out five over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Despite pitching in a hitter's park such as Coors Field, Stammen more than held his own as he used his sinker to hold the Rockies to one run in a career-high seven innings. Unfortunately, he was the hard-luck loser as he was outpitched by All-Star Jason Marquis in a 1-0 loss. Stammen has only two quality starts in nine outings this season, but both have come in his last four starts. As a result, he has lowered his ERA by almost a full run (from 5.86 on June 12 to 4.88). He will be making his start against the Astros Saturday at Minute Maid Park -- another hitter's paradise.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler turned in another quality outing last time out against the Pirates but lost for the first time in his last five outings. The right-hander went 6 1/3 innings on Tuesday, allowing four runs on three hits and striking out four. After giving up a two-run home run in the third inning, he promptly sat down the next 10 Pirates batters in order. He faced Washington once this season, receiving a no-decision after allowing two runs on eight hits and striking out five in five innings. He is 2-4 with a 5.68 ERA in 13 career games against the Nationals, including eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann's run of five good-to-great starts came to an end in his last outing against the Rockies on Tuesday. The rookie had compiled a 1-1 record with a 2.12 ERA during that span but gave four runs, two earned, on seven hits with four walks in four innings against Colorado. Zimmermann showed a lack of command and couldn't locate his pitches. He has never faced the Astros, which he will face in the final game before the All-Star break.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf earned the win in his final start before the All-Star Break, holding the Mets to two runs over 6 1/3 innings. He scattered seven hits, striking out three. The left-hander has a .500 record against Houston in his career, going 4-4 with a 3.89 ERA in 12 starts. He took the loss in the Dodgers' 6-5 loss against the Astros on April 22, giving up four runs in seven innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander gets the nod to start the second half of the season for the Astros. He's coming off a masterful five-hit shutout of the Pirates on Wednesday at Minute Maid Park in which he struck out 11 batters and walked only one. He has won three of his past four starts and his last three decisions. He faced the Dodgers on April 23 in Houston, giving up five hits and one run in six innings and taking a loss. He's 2-2 with a 3.23 ERA in six career games against the Dodgers, including five starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his final start before the All-Star break, Billingsley had one of his worst outings of the year. He last just five innings and allowed five runs on five hits and four walks. The five runs allowed by Billingsley tied his season high. A couple of days later in the All-Star game, Billingsley pitched one inning and gave up two hits, one of which was an RBI double by Twins catcher Joe Mauer. Billingsley has a career ERA of 2.62 in five starts against the Astros, but has a 3-2 record to show for it.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt was forced to leave his last start against the Nationals in the seventh inning, exiting with numbness in a few fingers in his throwing hand as a result of an at-bat in the sixth. He threw 87 pitches, tossing six innings allowing three runs on five hits and striking out six, receiving a no decision. Oswalt is 5-3 with a 3.91 ERA in nine appearances (eight starts) in his career against the Dodgers. He has faced them once this year, tossing six innings and allowing four runs on eight hits on April 22. He received a no-decision after surrendered three home runs while striking out six.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw went six strong innings in his last start. He held the Mets scoreless, allowing three hits and striking out seven in an 8-0 win for the Dodgers. The 21-year-old lefty was saddled with his first loss of the season in his last outing against the Astros on April 21, when he gave up six runs on eight hits in 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off one of his best starts of the season, last Monday against the Pirates, Hampton was roughed up on Saturday in his final start before the All-Star break. He gave up nine hits and five runs in 3 2/3 innings Saturday against the Nationals. He is 8-7 with a 4.61 ERA in 22 career games (19 starts) against the Dodgers, including 3-6 with a 5.48 ERA in 14 games (12 starts) at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda had a rough time out in his last start, giving up four earned runs on eight hits in 4 1/3 innings. Kuroda has been spectacular in his two career starts against the Astros, with an ERA of .066 and 1-0 record.
away_pitcher_note: Ortiz made headlines when he criticized manager Cecil Cooper for taking him out of his final start of the first half last Thursday against the Nationals after only three innings for no reason. Ortiz had given up six hits and four runs and has since patched things up with his manager. He's 2-3 with a 5.26 ERA in 10 starts this year, picking up his first win of the season against the Dodgers on April 21 by allowing three hits and three runs in five innings. He's 9-9 with a 5.08 ERA in 23 games (22 starts) against the Dodgers, including 6-3 with a 4.46 ERA in 13 games (12 starts) at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler turned in a quality start in Houston's last game before the All-Star break, winning for the first time at home. The right-hander scattered seven hits, not surrendering a run over 6 1/3 innings at Minute Maid Park to earn his first win there in his last 10 starts dating back to last season. He has not faced the Cardinals this season, but was 2-0 with a 3.00 ERA in four appearances, including two starts, against them last year. Moehler has never lost to St. Louis in his career, posting a 4-0 record with a 4.13 ERA in 15 appearances and seven starts against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse has yet to be officially announced as the Monday starter, but it's all but certain he'll get the first game of the first post-break road trip. He wasn't great in his first game back from the disabled list, but did come through it healthy, and that was the main concern. Lohse will likely be quite a bit sharper in his second outing. The Cardinals are counting on him to give their rotation a boost in the second half.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez threw six scoreless innings against the Dodgers in his previous start Thursday, extending his scoreless innings streak to 17 over three starts. He has a 0.41 ERA in his last three starts, allowing one earned run in 22 innings. With 121 starts, he's tied with Dave Roberts for fourth place all-time among Astros left-handers, and with 703 innings he's in fifth place among Houston lefties. In his only appearance against the Cardinals this year, he gave up five hits and three runs in six innings at St. Louis on April 12.
away_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer hasn't been formally named to this start, but the Cards have shown no inclination to remove him from the rotation despite a rocky first half. He's been very good on occasion, but he's shown no ability to sustain the good feeling. Houston is not the best place to pitch for a hurler trying to find his way, and Wellemeyer has had more trouble on the road (5.90 ERA) than at home (5.34). The biggest issue, though, is that left-handed hitters have tattooed Wellemeyer -- they're batting .345 and slugging .604 against him.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt has won three of his past four starts and three consecutive decisions. He's coming off a masterful four-hit complete-game win over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Friday in which he struck out five batters. He's 3-0 with a 1.66 ERA in his past five starts. Oswalt faced the Cardinals on April 11 at Busch Stadium and allowed nine hits and six runs in his second start of the season. He's 9-7 with a 3.11 ERA in 26 regular-season appearances (25 starts) against St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter wasn't as sharp as he has been in other starts this year but was just as effective. The St. Louis ace allowed seven hits in eight shutout innings on Friday night against the Diamondbacks, striking out seven and using two double-play balls to escape jams. Carpenter kept the ball down and several of his hits just found holes on the infield, an encouraging sign for Carpenter and the Cardinals. He came within one inning of his 13th career shutout but was taken out after 103 pitches. There was no need for manager Tony La Russa and the Cardinals to push their ace any further with the recent arm troubles he has had and with the Cardinals having a comfortable 4-0 lead at the time.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton began the second half of the season by losing to the Dodgers on Saturday night in a strange game. He gave up seven hits and five runs (four earned) in 5 2/3 innings en route to losing his second consecutive start, but he retired 12 in a row from the second until the sixth inning and the was the victim of poor defense. He's 10-10 in his career against the Mets, his former team, with a 3.10 ERA in 30 games (28 starts). Hampton has only one win this year against teams other than the Pirates, against whom he's 4-0.
away_pitcher_note: Santana extended his streak of scoreless innings to 15 Saturday afternoon when he beat the Braves.  He allowed only five hits and two walks in his seven innings and then sweated out a Braves rally in their eighth. The victory was his 59th in 76 career decisions after the All-Star break. His career .776 winning percentage after the break is the highest in big league history among pitchers with at least 75 starts after the break.  Now he faces the Astros, a team he has dominated -- 0.98 ERA -- in three career appearances, two last season after the break. He won once and wasn't involved in the decision in the other start, allowing one run in 13 1/3 innings. Carlos Lee has a .313 average, eight strikeouts and three home runs in 32 career at-bats against Santana.

home_pitcher_note: Ortiz, who criticized manager Cecil Cooper for taking him out of the game after only three innings in his final start before the All-Star break on July 9, was allowed to navigate his way through six innings on a hot Sunday in Los Angeles, allowing five hits and two runs against the Dodgers. Ortiz is 9-7 with a 5.20 ERA in 18 career games against the Mets, including 17 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Fernando Nieve was to start the Mets' game against the Astros on Saturday, but he strained his right quadriceps running the bases Sunday in Atlanta and has been placed on the disabled list. The Mets have not yet announced who will take his spot, and manager Jerry Manuel said the decision may wait until Saturday afternoon. But the smart money is on Jon Niese, who has won his last five decisions for Triple-A Buffalo, and who holds a 0.72 ERA in his seven most recent starts. Niese has not faced the Astros in any of his five career starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start after the All-Star break, Moehler turned in a quality outing against St. Louis, tossing 6 1/3 innings giving up two runs on six hits and striking out five. He retired 10 of the first 12 batters he faced and threw 100 pitches against the Cardinals before being taken down in the seventh. Moehler hasn't faced the Mets this season. In his only game against the Mets last year, he allowed four runs on six hits and struck out four over 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez had struggled mightily going into his last start, as he had lost four straight including two outings that combined 15 runs in just seven innings. But at Nationals Park, Livan beat his former team for the third time in as many tries this season. Hernandez was staked to a 5-0 advantage after two innings and cruised for seven frames giving up five hits and a pair of runs. The savvy veteran said he took everything he did from his previous start against Washington and did the opposite in order to throw off hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano gave up a season-high 10 hits but got enough run support for a change to pick up his third straight win in his last start. He beat the Phillies, giving up five runs (four earned) over 6 2/3 innings. Big Z also struck out seven. He didn't get a hit, which is a surprise. Zambrano has faced the Astros twice this year, winning on Opening Day, April 6, and not getting a decision June 10 despite holding Houston to one run on three hits over eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez became Houston's first 10-game winner this season by winning his fifth consecutive decision last time out against St. Louis. He had his scoreless innings snapped against the Cardinals in the second inning but didn't waste any time in starting a new one. He had not allowed a run in 18 1/3 innings until Mark DeRosa hit a solo home run with one out in the second frame. After that, he did not allow another run, tossing seven innings, allowing four hits and giving up just the one run while striking out five. He has faced Chicago twice this season but has received tough-luck no-decisions in both starts. Last time out against the Cubs on June 10, he worked seven innings, allowing one run on five hits, striking out six. Rodriguez has a 1.38 ERA over 13 innings against the Cubs this season.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster has been on the disabled list since July 8 because of a broken right big toe, but his rehab went well, and he will be activated about a week earlier than expected. The right-hander warmed up with a simulated game last Wednesday in Philadelphia, throwing 60 pitches, and was to throw another side session over the weekend. Give him credit for keeping his arm in shape during his rehab time.
away_pitcher_note: Through six innings Oswalt was spectacular against the Cardinals, efficiently throwing 59 pitches through six, but he ran into control issues in the seventh, allowing two runs in the inning to be out-dueled by Chris Carpenter. He would allow three runs on seven hits and strike out four over seven innings, taking and receive and no decision. He has faced the Cubs twice this season, going 0-1 with a 4.15 ERA. In his last start against the Cubs on May 16, he tossed six innings allowing three runs and striking out seven to receive a no decision. In his career, Oswalt is 12-12 with a 3.90 ERA in 28 appearances, including 27 starts against Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: Wells seems to like facing National League Central teams. In his last start, against the Reds, Wells picked up his ninth quality start and a victory. So far, he's 2-1 with a 2.39 ERA against NL Central teams and 6-0 when he gets four runs of support or more. Against the Reds, Wells' only mistake was serving up Aaron Harang's first career homer. Wells was kicking himself after the game for the slider he hung. He's still a rookie.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the New York Mets, Hampton wasn't able to work out beyond the sixth inning, allowing four runs on eight hits over 5 2/3 innings, but he did provide the Astros with a boost at the plate, hitting his first home run since May 8, 2005, and the 16th of his career. He's faced the Cubs once this season already, taking the loss on May 6 after allowing five runs (three earned) on seven hits over 5 1/3 innings. In 24 career appearances, including 20 starts, he is 9-5 with a 3.07 ERA against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Hart thought his days as a starter would be over upon Ryan Dempster's return, but with Ted Lilly going on the DL, the Cubs will be counting on the rookie right-hander. Hart picked up his second win in his last start, against the Reds on Saturday. He posted his longest outing, six innings, and gave up one run on five hits. In his first two starts, Hart had walked 10 and struck out four. Against the Reds, he said he found his groove -- as well as his offspeed pitches -- so he didn't have to rely on his fastball alone. This is a makeup of a postponed game against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Ortiz labored through 4 1/3 innings against the Mets last time out. He threw 96 pitches, allowing six runs on five hits and walking four in his outing. Ortiz has three appearances, including two starts against the Cubs this season, posting an 0-1 record with a 5.06 ERA over 10 2/3 innings versus the North-siders this year. In his last outing against them on June 11, Ortiz allowed no runs and just three hits over 5 1/3 innings but recieved a no decision. In his career, he is 3-5 with 5.23 ERA in 13 appearances, including 11 starts, against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie will be recalled from Triple-A Memphis on Friday to take Todd Wellemeyer's spot in the rotation. Wellemeyer was demoted after struggling to the second worst ERA in the Major Leagues at 5.79. Boggs made four starts for the Cardinals earlier this year when Chris Carpenter was injured but was unable to pitch past the sixth inning in any of them. Boggs made eight appearances in 2008 but had a 7.41 ERA. He has struggled going deep into games but seems to have corrected that in Memphis. He gave up one earned run in his last three starts at triple-A before getting the recall. Said Cardinals manager Tony La Russa of Boggs: "I think he's pitched effectively down there. He's a developing pitcher and he's learning all the time."
away_pitcher_note: Moehler's streak of consecutive quality starts came to an end at four when he was roughed up Sunday against the Mets. He allowed eight hits and five earned runs in 4 2/3 innings, which was his shortest outing since back-to-back awful starts to begin the year. The good news is he's 5-0 with a 3.98 ERA in six games (five starts) against the Cardinals in his career. He held St. Louis to six hits and two runs in 6 1/3 innings on July 20 in Houston in his last start against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Even though he hasn't always been extremely sharp, Carpenter was very, very effective in July. In five starts, he went 4-0 with a 1.62 ERA, putting him in consideration for pitcher of the month honors. He remains the same pitcher - power sinker and cutter, curveball and changeup, all with quality command. He's been even better at home than on the road this year, allowing only one homer at Busch Stadium in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez held the Cubs to one run in seven innings Monday in his final start in what was a stellar July. The left-hander went 4-0 with a 0.75 ERA in five July starts and has won five consecutive decisions. His 10 wins lead the team and are tied for his career. He's faced the Cardinals twice this year, holding them to four hits and one run in July 21 in Houston. In his second start of the season April 12 in St. Louis, he allowed five hits and three runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright tamed the powerful Dodgers offense to the tune of eight scoreless innings on Tuesday night but didn't do it with his normal dominating stuff. Wainwright gave up eight hits and got into several jams but buckled down when he needed to and escaped damage. He also got several strong defensive plays, including two by shortstop Brendan Ryan and one by third baseman Mark DeRosa. The workhorse needed 111 pitches to get through eight innings, the 10th time this season that he passed the 110-pitch mark. He finished three outs short of his first career shutout. He last faced Houston on April 11 and tossed five shutout innings.
