Against the Giants on Tuesday, Hamels struck out nine and issued one walk, in the ninth inning. He threw seven 1-2-3 innings and at one point retired 21 straight batters. He has said it all clicked for him during his start against the Mets on Aug. 21. Since then, he has been pitching more relaxed. The 25-year-old lefty has never lost to the Astros, going 3-0 with a 4.41 ERA in five career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler was the victim of poor defense in losing his previous start Tuesday against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. He gave up only one unearned run in 5 1/3 innings, allowing six hits and three runs. He's lost five of his last six decisions. In his career, Moehler is 2-3 with a 6.38 ERA in 11 games, including seven starts, against the Phillies. Moehler beat the club the last time he faced it, giving up four hits and three runs in six innings on May 24, 2008 at Minute Maid Park.
away_pitcher_note: J.A. Happ was a late scratch because of a strained muscle in his side. The team said Monday that Happ hurt himself while taking batting practice Saturday. He was replaced by Moyer, who started 22 games this season before he was moved to the bullpen on Aug. 10. He pitched three innings in relief on Friday, giving up a run on one hit, a solo homer by Houston's Carlos Lee.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino returned to the starting rotation Wednesday and pitched well, allowing four hits and two runs and striking out seven batters in six innings. But Paulino suffered his third consecutive loss because the Astros were shut out by Ted Lilly. As a starter, Paulino is 1-0 with a 10.97 ERA in six starts this year, but he has a good track history against the Braves. He's 2-0 with a 1.12 ERA in two games (one start) against Atlanta. He threw six shutout innings against the Braves in the final game of the 2007 season.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez's troubles against the Marlins continued on Wednesday, when he allowed them five earned runs in just 5 2/3 innings. In four starts against them this year, he is 0-2 with a 5.68 ERA. In his other 23 starts, he has posted a 2.77 ERA. Oddly the 33-year-old right-hander has gone 3-4 with a 3.06 ERA in 14 home starts and 7-2 with a 3.30 ERA in 13 road starts. This will be his first start at Minute Maid Park since 2005. During his past three outings there, he is 1-2 with a 2.05 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez snapped a two-game losing streak by tossing seven scoreless innings and hitting a two-run double to lead the Astros past the Phillies on Friday. He held the Phillies to seven hits and struck out seven batters, escaping a bases-loaded jam in the seventh by getting Jimmy Rollins to fly out and striking out Shane Victorino. Rodriguez has held opponents to one run or less in 10 of his 12 starts. He's 2-1 with a 5.79 ERA in six career games (five starts) against Atlanta. He held the Braves to six hits and three runs in five innings May 3 in Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson, who is making a bid for NL Rookie of the Year, will be making his first career appearance against the Astros. He took a no-decision in his last start, at Florida on Thursday, allowing one run on two hits in five innings in an 8-3 Marlins win.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt held the Phillies to two hits through six scoreless innings Saturday before being forced to leave with tightness in his back. Oswalt wound up getting his 15th no-decision of the season, which ties Pete Harnisch (1992) and Jim Deshaies (1990) for the most in club history in one season. Oswalt started against the Braves on May 2 in Atlanta, but pitched only one inning because of a long rain delay. Atlanta is the only National League team Oswalt has never beaten in the regular season (0-2, 6.18 ERA in six starts).
away_pitcher_note: Lowe is coming off a tough 3-1 loss to Cincinnati in which he gave up three earned runs in seven innings, with five strikeouts. The loss snapped a streak of two straight wins for Lowe. Lowe has eight career starts against the Astros, going 3-3 with a 3.10 ERA. In 52 1/3 innings against Houston, Lowe has allowed 18 earned runs on 51 hits, with 23 strikeouts and 10 walks.

home_pitcher_note: Norris, who was coming off three poor starts, showed the kind of poise and fastball command that made him one of the organization's top-rated prospects by holding the Phillies to six hits and two runs in six innings last Sunday. He was the first Astros rookie to win his first three starts before falling on hard times; Norris had gone 0-3 with a 13.11 ERA in three starts prior to Sunday. This will be his eighth Major League start and first appearance against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Morton was pushed back three days in order to give his tender groin a little more time to heal. It also gave the right-hander a chance to have an extra side session with pitching coach Joe Kerrigan. Morton's season could be defined simply by the word inconsistency. He has shown flashes of being able to command the exceptional movement he has on his pitcheS, But there have only been flashes of that. Morton is 0-1 with a 9.90 ERA in two previous starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler held the Phillies to three runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings in his previous start Monday at Minute Maid Park. He had not allowed more than three earned runs in any of his last four starts, going 1-1 with a 3.57 ERA in those starts. The Astros are 3-1 in his last four starts. Moehler is 1-2 with a 5.09 ERA in three starts this year against Pittsburgh and 6-7 with a 4.67 ERA in 17 career games, including 14 starts, against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf pushed his ERA below 4.00 for the first time since May 13 after making his best outing of his young career in his last start. Ohlendorf pitched a career-high eight innings and struck out a career-high 11 in the outing, though he was denied a win because of no run support. The right-hander allowed just one unearned run. Simply put, things have just clicked for Ohlendorf since the All-Star break. He has a 2.70 ERA in the second half and has been benefiting tremendously from a much-improved slider.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino is coming off a pair of quality starts in which he lost both games because the Astros didn't score a run while he was in the game. He held the Cubs to four hits and two runs on a two-run homer to Derrek Lee in six innings Sept. 2 at Wrigley Field and gave up four hits and two runs on a pair of solo homers in six innings Tuesday against Atlanta. In his past two starts, he's allowed four earned runs and struck out 13 in 12 innings, but is riding a career-long four-game losing streak. In his only appearance against the Pirates this year, he pitched 1 2/3 innings in relief June 7 and allowed three hits, one run and struck out four.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm wasn't at his sharpest in his last start, but he battled well. His sinker has been more consistent over his past four outings than at times earlier in the season, which continues to be the biggest key for the left-hander. While Maholm still has an outside chance at reaching the 10-win mark before the end of the season, his primary objective over these next few weeks is just to find the consistency that will allow him to end the season on a high note. Maholm is 7-4 with a 4.44 ERA in 12 career starts against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: In a game lost by the Reds, 4-3, in the bottom of the ninth on Wednesday to the Rockies, Arroyo had his ninth straight quality start by pitching seven innings and allowing two runs and five hits with two walks and four strikeouts. He is 2-3 with a 2.19 ERA over his past nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez turned in another quality start Wednesday against the Braves, holding Atlanta to three hits and one run in seven innings in a no-decision. He's limited opponents to one run or less in 11 of his past 13 starts. He's thrown 182 2/3 innings, which is a career high. Rodriguez is 2-1 with a 0.50 ERA in three starts against the Reds this year. He's 5-5 with a 4.02 ERA in 14 career starts against the Reds, including 3-1 with a 3.22 ERA at Great American Ball Park.

home_pitcher_note: In a 5-1 loss to the Rockies on Thursday -- in which all five runs were scored with two outs in the third inning -- Wells pitched five innings and allowed five earned runs and six hits with three walks and three strikeouts. His downfall was not being able to cleanly field a two-out bunt by Eric Young Jr., which opened the door to the Colorado rally. Wells said he poorly located his slider during that inning, which led to a two-run double by Jason Giambi and a two-run homer by Garrett Atkins.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt was roughed Thursday against the Braves in Houston, giving up 10 hits and six runs in two innings in his second-shortest start of the season. The good news is he's facing a Cincinnati team he's owned in his career. He's 23-1 with a 2.46 ERA in 31 career games (29 starts) against the Reds, including 7-1 with a 3.29 ERA in 10 starts at Great American Ball Park. He's faced the Reds three times this year and has no decisions and a 2.37 ERA. Oswalt's 15 no-decisions this year are tied for a club record.

home_pitcher_note: During a 6-4 loss to the Cubs on Friday, Lehr lasted only 4 2/3 innings and allowed five earned runs and five hits with three walks and one strikeout. All three of his walks came with two outs and two of the runners scored.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Bazardo's first start since giving up eight hits and eight runs in two innings Aug. 28 at Arizona. He's started two games since being called up Aug. 8. He struck out all three batters he faced in a scoreless ninth inning Friday against Pittsburgh. He's 0-1 with a 13.50 ERA in two starts this year. He has never faced the Cincinnati Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson will make a second consecutive start in place of fellow lefty Manny Parra, who remains sidelined with a stiff neck. Parra underwent an MRI scan on Wednesday that yielded no further information, but it's clear that Narveson will be needed for at least one more turn through the rotation. Narveson pitched three good innings in Arizona last weekend but was out of the game before recording an out in the fourth. Narveson made both of his career appearances against the Astros in 2006, for the Cardinals, including a Sept. 22 start in which he allowed two runs on two hits in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris will start on six days of rest, having not pitched since giving up six hits and one run and striking out seven batters Sept. 11 against Pittsburgh. He's received decisions in all eight of his starts this year, going 3-0 with a 3.00 ERA to start his career before losing his next three starts (0-3, 13.11 ERA). He's 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA in his last two starts, beating the Phillies and Pirates. This will be his second career appearance against the Brewers. He beat them Aug. 7, giving up three hits and two runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan surrendered only three Cubs hits in seven innings Monday, but one of them was a Derrek Lee homer. Suppan allowed that lone run, but was on the wrong end of a 2-0 loss to Ryan Dempster that was highlighted by some spectacular Cubs defense. It continued a trend for Suppan, who has been very tough this season on the road but had struggled at Miller Park, where he's 2-7 with a 6.26 ERA in 13 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler is coming off a quality start against the Pirates, allowing seven hits and two runs in six innings. He is 0-1 in his past four starts and has lost five of his past six decisions. His only win in that span came Aug. 22, when he beat Arizona in Houston. He's 4-9 with a 4.75 ERA in 21 games (12 starts) in his career against the Brewers, including 1-3 with a 4.08 ERA in 10 games (four starts) at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Ken Macha said he would give Gallardo one last start before shutting the talented young right-hander down for the rest of the season. He'll be on the hill with a pitch count, though Macha declined to say what the magic number would be. It hasn't been a disappointing season for Gallardo, per se, but the right-hander will aim to lower his pitch counts and limit his walks in 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Paulino has three losses in his last three starts, but the Astros did not score a run while he was on the mound in any of those games. In those three starts, he's allowed five earned runs in 17 innings and struck out 20. Paulino hasn't won since holding Detroit to one run and three hits in seven innings June 27. He's 0-2 with a 9.69 ERA in his career against the Brewers, including 0-1 with a 6.00 ERA this year.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has been the Astros' most pleasant surprise of the season and their best option to bring an end to a seven-game losing streak. He also has been especially effective against the hard-hitting Cardinals, holding them to a .174 average in four starts, covering 24 innings this season. Rodriguez has a 1.58 ERA at Minute Maid Park this season. In his last 14 starts, he is 7-4 with a 2.15 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse will make the start on Monday after being skipped on Friday night in favor of John Smoltz. He missed a turn in the rotation after continuing to feel something amiss in his right forearm. However, an MRI cleared him, and it's a matter of when he's ready to get back on the mound. His velocity was fine in his last start, but his command definitely needs improvement. It's been a rough 2009 for Lohse after signing a four-year $41 million contract extension last September.

home_pitcher_note: Bazardo will be making his second straight start and fourth of the season. He went five innings last Wednesday and picked up a no-decision in the Astros' loss at Cincinnati. While still young, at 25, Bazardo has been around the block in his nine years of pro ball. The native of Venezuela also has pitched in the Florida, Seattle and Detroit organizations.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro said recently that he would like to remain with the Cardinals when his contract ends this season, but general manager John Mozeliak said that all talks with potential free agents wouldn't begin until after the season. Pineiro is having one of the best years of his career but has stumbled a bit down the stretch, posing a 4.62 ERA in four September starts.

home_pitcher_note: Norris gets a chance to face the Cardinals for the second time in his career. He made his first Major League start against St. Louis in Aug. 2 at Busch Stadium and threw seven scoreless innings, allowing just two hits, four walks and striking out five batters. He had decisions in his first eight Major League starts before throwing five innings and give up three hits and one run and striking out eight batters for a no-decision Friday in Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Smoltz returned on Sept. 18 after having mild shoulder tendinitis and gave up two runs on three straight doubles in the first inning against the Cubs. But he shut out Chicago for the next five innings -- moving away from using his fastball, which he wasn't especially pleased with -- and the Cardinals came back to win, 3-2.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler will be making his first start of the season against division rival Cincinnati. For his career, he's 2-4 with a 5.22 ERA in 10 games (seven starts) against the Reds. He's won one of his last 11 starts, going 1-5 during that span. He has not picked up a decision, but has pitched well in his last three starts, giving up six earned runs in 17 2/3 innings. He hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in his last seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Maloney earned his first Major League win on Sept. 17 with a 3-2 Reds victory over the Marlins. The lefty pitched five innings and allowed two earned runs and seven hits with one walk and three strikeouts. Although he had runners in scoring position in three of his first four innings, he worked out of the jams. It was Maloney's first game back after he missed a turn with a middle finger blister. Although he wasn't able to throw his cut-fastball, he made good use of his other pitches -- especially the changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino is 0-4 with a 3.52 ERA in his past four starts, but has been the victim of some poor run support. In his first three starts in September, the Astros didn't score a run while he was on the mound. He gave up eight hits and four runs in his previous starts Sunday at Milwaukee. He's 1-2 with a 3.97 ERA in four career starts against the Reds, including 0-2 with a 2.55 ERA in three starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Lehr gave up 11 hits over five innings on Sept. 16 but was fortunate not to have anyone on base when the Astros hitters really pounced with five home runs -- all solo shots, including three in the third inning. Cincinnati still carved out a 6-5 win while Lehr got a no-decision. The five homers Lehr allowed matched a team record last reached by lefty Brandon Claussen against the Cubs on July 18, 2005.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez saw his five-game home winning streak come to a close in Monday's loss to St. Louis, giving up nine hits and six runs in five innings. He's 8-3 with a 2.03 ERA at home this year in 15 starts, and this will be his final start at Minute Maid Park in 2009. Rodriguez is 2-2 with a 1.12 ERA in four starts against the Reds this year, and 5-6 with a 3.95 ERA in 15 career starts against Cincinnati.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto is 2-0 with a 2.95 ERA over his last four starts since returning from the disabled list. In a 10-4 win over the Pirates on Tuesday, he wasn't robust but effective enough. Over five innings, he allowed two earned runs and two hits without a walk while striking out two. He threw 101 pitches in his first start back after missing a turn in the rotation with the flu.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels has been pitching much better recently. He went 7-8 with a 4.78 ERA after his first 24 starts this season. The Phillies were just 12-12 in those starts, and his ERA was fifth-highest in the National League through Aug. 21. But he is 3-1 with a 2.01 ERA in his past six starts to get Phillies fans thinking he and Cliff Lee could be pretty dominating in the postseason.
away_pitcher_note: Bazardo is still searching for his first win in eight games with the Astros. He made his fourth start of the season Tuesday against St. Louis and retired seven in a row to start the game before having trouble getting outs. He lasted just 3 2/3 innings, giving up six hits and six runs to fall to 0-2. He's appeared in one career game against the Phillies, giving up two hits and one run in one inning.

home_pitcher_note: Happ hopes to continue to build his case for National League Rookie of the Year in what might be his second-to-last start of the season Tuesday against the Astros. He allowed six hits, two runs, two walks and struck out seven in 5 2/3 innings Thursday in a victory over the Milwaukee Brewers at Miller Park. Happ improved to 11-4 with a 2.79 ERA. His ERA is 10th-best in franchise history amongst rookies.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez is scheduled to make his first Major League start in place of Bud Norris, who was shut down Friday because of a concern for the number of innings he pitched. Lopez has appeared in five Major League games and has no decisions and a 10.38 ERA. He was 4-5 with a 4.73 ERA in 29 games, including 15 starts, at Double-A Corpus Christi this year.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez's start is tentative based on how the right side of his neck feels. He strained his neck Sept. 19 in Atlanta, which forced him to leave after three innings. He missed Saturday's start in Milwaukee as a result. He said he could have pitched if it were absolutely necessary, but with the postseason so close he did not want to risk further injury and an opportunity to pitch in the postseason, when he really wants to be at top form.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler gave up eight hits and seven runs in 2 1/3 innings in Friday's loss to Cincinnati in his shortest start since going 2 1/3 innings in his second outing of the season April 13. He's 1-6 with a 5.63 ERA in 12 starts since July 26. He got a no-decision against the Phillies on Sept. 7 after giving up five hits and three runs in 5 2/3 innings and is 2-3 with a 6.19 ERA in 12 career games, including eight starts, against Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Cliff Lee allowed nine hits and seven runs in just six innings Friday in an 8-4 loss to the Brewers at Miller Park. Lee went 5-0 with a 0.68 ERA in his first five starts with the Phillies, but is 2-3 with a 6.35 ERA in his last six. He has allowed 49 hits, 24 earned runs and three walks and struck out 29 in 34 innings in those six starts. Opponents have hit .336 against him. Lee has thrown 226 innings this season, which led the Majors after Friday. "I feel strong, if that's what you're getting at," Lee said. "I feel as strong as I have all year. That's what you work all offseason for is to prepare for a long season and hopefully something extra there at the end. I feel like I've done everything I need to do to be in a position where I'm at right now."
away_pitcher_note: Paulino was solid to start September with a 3.52 ERA in his first four starts, but fell apart on Saturday against Cincinnati, allowing eight runs on nine hits in five innings while taking the loss. He's been the victim of poor run support for much of the season, including his first three starts in September, when the Astros didn't score a run while he was on the mound. He hasn't faced the Phillies in his young career.

home_pitcher_note: Maine's second-to-last start of the season appeared to be his least becoming. Not only did he allow seven hits, two walks and seven runs in 4 2/3 innings against the Marlins Saturday night, he also hit two successive batters, threw two wild pitches and surrendered a rocket three-run home run to a player who rarely hits home runs, Cameron Maybin. And all that against a team he had dominated in his career -- 5-1 record in nine starts -- and in a ballpark in which he never had lost. Now Maine will oppose the Astros on Friday at Citi Field in his final start. He hasn't pitched against Houston this season. And in his lone start against the Astros last season, he allowed eight runs in 5 2/3 innings. But he has a 3-1 record and 3.77 ERA in five career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez won for the second time in seven starts Sunday when he struck out nine Reds and allowed nine hits in six innings. He's set career highs for starts (31), wins (14), innings pitched (199 2/3) and strikeouts (190). He's 2-1 with a 3.47 ERA in his career against the Mets but will be making his first appearance at Citi Field.

home_pitcher_note: From a most unlikely source, the Mets received their first shutout from a starter in more than a calendar year when Misch beat the Marlins Sunday in Miami. Having never reached the eighth inning in his 15 big league starts, Misch pitched an eight-hitter against an accomplished offensive team, walking three, striking out two and retiring the final 13 batters. The complete game was the Mets' second of the season. Their previous shutout had been pitched one year, to the day, earlier, by Johan Santana, also against the Marlins. Misch's next and last start comes against the Astros, an opponent he hasn't faced since May of last year. He pitched six innings then, allowed three runs and lost.
away_pitcher_note: Bazardo is coming off a nice win over the Phillies in which he allowed two hits, two runs and four walks in 5 2/3 innings on Monday in Philadelphia. It was his first win in the Majors since Sept. 25, 2007, when he was with Detroit and beat Minnesota. He went 9-6 with a 3.20 ERA in 23 games at Triple-A Round Rock before being called up by the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Figueroa gets the task of closing out the Mets' 2009 season, taking the ball against the Astros despite having lost each of his past five starts. Still, the right-hander showed flashes of effectiveness in September, holding his opponent to two runs in three of his five starts. Figueroa is winless in seven games (two starts) against the Astros in his career.
away_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start -- on Tuesday against the Phillies -- Lopez allowed six hits and five runs in 3 2/3 innings, taking the loss. He gave up a grand slam to Pedro Feliz in the fourth inning of a tied game. Lopez was recalled from Double-A Corpus Christi on Aug. 28 after going 4-5 with a 4.73 ERA, including 3-5 with a 3.91 ERA as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Norris, who allowed two runs and struck out seven in five innings on Tuesday, will start for the Astros. He's slated for the No. 4 spot in Houston's rotation.
away_pitcher_note: His last time out, Morrow gave up four runs and six hits in three innings on March 14. He's since missed a pair of starts due to a right shoulder injury.

home_pitcher_note: Roy Oswalt, who nursed a sore left hamstring in the final 10 days of Spring Training, makes his club-record eighth consecutive Opening Day start. In his seven Opening Day starts, Oswalt is 2-3 with a 3.35 ERA, and the team is 2-5 in those games. Oswalt went 8-6 with a 4.12 ERA last year in 30 starts and had a club record 16 no-decisions. He's 5-5 with a 3.70 ERA in 13 career starts against the Giants and 75-25 in his career at Minute Maid Park. He faced the Giants once last year and held them to three hits and one run and struck out six batters in eight innings July 5 in San Francisco.
away_pitcher_note: Lincecum has not pitched in Houston since Aug. 12, 2008, when a line drive hit by Brad Ausmus struck him in the right knee and forced him to leave the game. At the time, Lincecum was in the middle of one of his typical outings, having allowed only one hit while striking out seven in 4 1/3 innings. Fortunately for Lincecum, and the Giants, he made his next scheduled start en route to his first of two consecutive Cy Young Awards. Lincecum was unusually ineffective in his initial Opening Day start last year, working only three innings and allowing three runs. He joined Sandy Koufax (1966) as the only Cy Young winner to pitch as few as three innings one year after capturing the award. Lifetime, Lincecum is 2-0 with a 1.67 ERA in five starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a breakthrough season in which he led the team in wins, ERA, strikeouts and innings pitched, Rodriguez will make only his second career appearance against the San Francisco Giants. Rodriguez was 14-12 with a 3.02 ERA last year in 33 starts, including 9-3 in 16 starts with a 2.08 ERA at Minute Maid Park. He has pitched much better at home in his career, going 31-21 with a 3.61 ERA in Houston. His only other appearance against the Giants was in 2006, and he was rocked for 10 hits, 11 runs (six earned) and five walks in 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: This marks Zito's first attempt to sustain the momentum he established in last year's second half, when he went 5-4 with a 2.83 ERA in 15 starts. That ERA ranked 15th among NL starters. This continued a career-long pattern for Zito, who's 58-66 with a 4.23 ERA before the All-Star break and 75-40, 3.42 afterward. Keeping the ball in the yard is a key factor for Zito, who yielded 13 home runs before the All-Star break and only eight afterward a year ago. Zito has appeared just once in Houston, and it didn't turn out too well. He allowed six runs in 5 2/3 innings in a 6-2 San Francisco loss on Aug. 13, 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Brett Myers will make his Astros debut in the series finale against the Giants. He went 4-3 with a 4.84 ERA in 18 games (10 starts) last year for the Philadelphia Phillies, who parted ways with him after the season. Myers signed a one-year, $5.1 million deal with the Astros. In his career at Minute Maid Park, he's 1-1 with a 3.68 ERA in five games (three starts) and is 1-3 with a 6.92 ERA in seven career games (five starts) against the Giants, whom he hasn't faced since 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Cain will try to continue the progress he made last year, when he was a National League All-Star for the first time. He matched his career-high innings total from 2008 (217 2/3) despite making one fewer start. He trimmed his hits allowed from 206 to 184 and his walks from 91 to 73. But pitching in the clutch was Cain's true hallmark last year. Opponents hit just .161 off him with runners in scoring position. Cain is the first pitcher to work 200 or more innings in three consecutive seasons for the Giants since Livan Hernandez (2000-02). He's 1-2 with a 3.52 ERA in four career outings against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Norris was roughed up in his final spring outing Saturday against Toronto at Minute Maid Park. He has never faced the Phillies in his brief career, as he appeared in 11 games, including 10 starts, for the Astros in his Major League debut last year. He went 6-3 with a 4.53 ERA, going 3-0 with a 1.57 ERA in his final four starts of the year before being shut down as a precaution due to a heavy workload. He was named the Pacific Coast League Pitcher of the Year in 2009, going 4-9 with a 2.63 ERA in 19 starts at Triple-A Round Rock.
away_pitcher_note: Happ enters the 2010 motivated. He finished in second place in the 2009 NL Rookie of the Year voting to Marlins outfielder Chris Coghlan. He also has heard sabermetricians predict that he will regress after being the recipient of some good luck last season. Time will tell, but Happ has worked on a sinker this spring, which he hopes adds another dimension to his pitching repertoire and keeps hitters from making all the adjustments they need to make.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino battled back spasms at the end of Spring Training and was scratched from starting Saturday's exhibition finale against Toronto at Minute Maid Park, even though he told manager Brad Mills he was ready to pitch. The Astros wanted to be cautious with the often-injured right-hander who won the No. 5 spot in the rotation by having a good spring (1-1 with a 3.78 ERA in five games, including four starts). Paulino went 3-11 with a 6.27 ERA in 23 games (17 starts) for the Astros last year. He's 1-0 with a 1.80 ERA in one career start against Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer had three offseason surgeries, which many thought might put him behind schedule once Spring Training began in February. But Moyer came into camp in good shape and pitched well, earning him the fifth spot in the Phillies' rotation over right-hander Kyle Kendrick. It is nothing short of an accomplishment. Moyer is 47 years, 5 months old. Just five pitchers in baseball history have pitched at an older age: Hoyt Wilhelm (at 48 and 49 in 1970-71), Phil Niekro (48 in 1987), Jack Quinn (48-49 in 1931-33), Nick Altrock (48 in 1924) and Satchel Paige (58 in 1965).

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt makes his first appearance since holding the San Francisco Giants to seven hits and three runs in six innings in an Opening Day loss. He needs one win to pass Larry Dierker for sole possession of second on the club's all-time wins list. He and Dierker have 137 wins. Oswalt has pitched well against the Phillies in his career, going 6-1 with a 3.23 ERA in 11 games (nine starts). In his only start against them last Sept. 5 in Houston, he held the Phillies to four hits, two runs and struck out eight batters in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay stepped on the mound on Opening Day with high expectations. The Phillies sent three top prospects to the Blue Jays for him, and they also traded Cliff Lee to Seattle to clear salary and get prospects in return. Halladay allowed one run in the first inning against the Nationals, but finished throwing six scoreless innings in an 11-1 victory. Halladay allowed six hits, one run and two walks and struck out nine in the opener. The Phillies hope for more of the same against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Chris Carpenter got the Opening Day start, so Wainwright gets the home opener. As manager Tony La Russa said when he announced the decision, "It's not our first rodeo." Two aces, two Cy Young finalists, two honors. Wainwright was outstanding in his first start, and pronounced himself a good six weeks ahead of where he was at this point last season. His results were mostly good early last year, but he was walking far too many batters. This time around, he seems to be in a groove right away.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a solid first start of the season in taking a loss to the Giants on Tuesday, left-hander Wandy Rodriguez gets the ball in the series opener in St. Louis. Rodriguez held the Giants to three runs on seven hits and four walks and struck out four batters. He's 3-9 with a 3.95 ERA in 15 career appearances against the Cardinals, including 14 starts. He made five starts against St. Louis last year and was 1-3 with a 3.72 ERA. Rodriguez has held Albert Pujols in check. The Cardinals slugger is a career .161 hitter with no home runs and one RBI in 31 at-bats against Pujols.

home_pitcher_note: If one game is any indication -- and it isn't necessarily -- Penny is poised for a rebound. He turned in an excellent Cardinals debut, throwing strikes and keeping the ball down. Efficiency has been an issue for Penny in the past, but on Thursday he was efficient as well as effective. Penny has pretty much always been good when he's been healthy and pitching in the National League. He's back in the NL, and he looks healthy, so don't rule out the possibility of a very good year from the 31-year-old righty.
away_pitcher_note: Myers makes his second start for the Astros after giving up a career-high 12 hits in his Houston debut April 7. Myers allowed four runs, one walk and struck out three batters in a 10-4 loss to the Giants in his first start since May 27, 2009. He faced the Cardinals once last year at Busch Stadium and was rocked for nine hits and five runs in 5 1/3 innings. He's 4-2 with a 5.45 ERA in 13 career games against the Cardinals, including 11 starts, and is 2-1 with a 7.27 ERA lifetime in six appearances at Busch Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Wildness was the issue in Lohse's first start on Friday in Milwaukee. He walked three and gave up six hits and four runs in six innings against the Brewers in a game the Cardinals won on Nick Stavinoha's two-out, ninth-inning home run off Trevor Hoffman. "I got in trouble and I walked guys," Lohse said. "You can't walk yourself into trouble like that." Lohse is 6-5 with a 2.99 ERA in 12 games against Houston, but has been especially strong against the Astros the past two years. Since 2008, he is 5-1 with a 2.44 ERA in seven starts against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Norris, who burst onto the scene as a rookie last year and went 6-3 in 11 games, struggled in his first start in his sophomore season April 9 against the Phillies at Minute Maid Park. Norris gave up six hits, three runs and four walks in 2 2/3 innings, but he can take satisfaction that he's had good success against the Cardinals, having not allowed a run against them in 13 career innings. He threw seven scoreless innings in his first win in his first Major League start Aug. 2 at Busch Stadium, holding the Cardinals hitless through the first five innings. He beat them again Sept. 23 in Houston, throwing six scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Silva came out of his last start April 9 after throwing 71 pitches over six innings because of some discomfort in his right shoulder. He was limited last season because of shoulder problems, so the Cubs are giving him plenty of rest. The plan is to keep Carlos Zambrano, Ryan Dempster and Randy Wells on a five-day routine and insert Silva and Tom Gorzelanny when there are openings. Silva looked solid in his Cubs debut against the Reds, giving up one run on three hits and striking out three. This will be his first start ever at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old right-hander, who went 3-11 with a 6.27 ERA a year ago, got roughed up by the Phillies in his first start of the season when he allowed four runs (all earned) on four hits over five innings. He struck out four and walked four before leaving the game with his team leading 5-4.

home_pitcher_note: Gorzelanny did not get a win in his first start of the season on April 11 against the Reds. In that game, he gave up one run on four hits over 6 1/3 innings and struck out seven. It was a solid performance, but the Cubs lost the game, as the Reds rallied for two runs in the eighth. He will have to watch out for Carlos Lee, who loves to hit at Wrigley Field and has a .429 average against the Cubs lefty. The Cubs tweaked the rotation and gave Ryan Dempster an extra day, moving him to Sunday after the right-hander threw 114 pitches in his second start.
away_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander has deserved better in his first two starts, but the Astros struggled to get much offense going in those two games against Tim Lincecum of the Giants and Roy Halladay of the Phillies. Against San Francisco, Oswalt allowed three earned runs on seven hits over six innings. Against Philly, he allowed two earned runs on five hits in six innings, while striking out eight and walking two in a 2-1 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster is coming off his first win but not his best-pitched start of the young season. In his first outing, on April 7 against the Braves, he gave up one run on three hits over six innings but didn't get a decision. On Monday, in the home opener against the Brewers, he gave up five runs on seven hits and four walks over 6 1/3 innings and got the win. He admitted that he wasn't as aggressive as he would like. Dempster did throw 114 pitches, which is why the Cubs gave him an extra day and pushed him back to Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: The southpaw, who went 14-12 with a 3.02 ERA a year ago, has gotten mixed results in his first two outings of the season. Against the Giants, Rodriguez allowed three earned runs on seven hits in six innings. On Monday against the Cardinals, he was tagged for four earned runs on seven hits in 4 1/3 innings -- with St. Louis slugger Albert Pujols accounting for all four runs with an RBI single and then a three-run home run.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is coming off his best outing of the season, on Wednesday against the Cardinals in St. Louis. He suffered the loss in the game, but he threw seven innings and allowed just two runs (one earned), four hits and two walks while striking out seven batters. Myers is 6-11 with a 5.64 ERA in 32 career games, including 24 starts, against Florida. He's started more games against Florida than any other team in his career after spending the first eight years of his career in the National League East with the Phillies. Myers is 1-1 with a 4.18 ERA in six games (four starts) at Minute Maid Park.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old threw a career high 117 pitches in his last outing, which turned into a win over the Reds. Volstad worked 6 2/3 innings, and he was sailing along. The last pitch he threw was belted for a two-run homer by Paul Janish. Still, overall, Volstad had a quality start -- three runs in 6 2/3 innings. He did walk four, and struck out five. His previous high pitch mark was 115 at Tampa Bay last June 27. In his career, Volstad is 1-0 with a 4.97 ERA in two starts against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Norris is coming off his first win of the season, when he struck out nine Cardinals in a 5-1 win on Thursday in St. Louis. He lasted only five innings after allowing four hits and three walks and throwing 106 pitches. In two starts this year, he's given up 10 hits, three earned runs and struck out 12 batters in 7 2/3 innings. Norris faced the Marlins twice last year in consecutive starts on Aug. 12 in Miami and Aug. 18 in Houston. He's 1-1 with a 7.59 ERA in 10 2/3 innings in his career against the Marlins. Norris has allowed 19 hits, nine earned runs and struck out 10 in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson had his best outing of the season while getting his first victory against the Reds on Thursday. That night, he struck out 10 batters while walking only one and finished scattering just one run on five hits in his six innings. The 26-year-old recorded five of his first six outs via the strikeout, but he did not go deeper in the game because he accumulated 45 pitches through just the first two frames. After that, though, Johnson said he started getting his rhythm. And it showed, as he retired nine of the last 11 batters he faced. For his career against the Astros, Johnson has struggled, going 0-3 with a 7.36 ERA in three games (two starts).

home_pitcher_note: Paulino is still searching for his first win of the season after taking a hard-luck loss in Friday's series opener in Chicago. He held the Cubs to one run entering the seventh inning before giving up four runs and taking the loss. Paulino went six innings and allowed six hits, three walks and struck out three. He has walked seven batters and struck out seven in two starts covering 11 innings this year. This will be Paulino's first career appearance against the Marlins. Paulino is 5-1 with a 6.49 ERA in 30 career games, including 22 starts, all with the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Bottom line is his numbers haven't been pretty. But say this about Sanchez, he's found a way to do his part in preserving the bullpen. Sanchez gutted out six innings in his last start, a loss at Philadelphia. The way the game started, it didn't look like he'd last through the first inning. Yet he turned in six innings, giving up five runs on eight hits with four walks and a strikeout. In the first inning, he threw 35 pitches (15 strikes). The Marlins are 1-1 in games that he's started. In his career, he is 1-0 with a 0.75 ERA vs. the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt has quality starts in each of his first three outings of the season, allowing 17 hits and striking out 17 batters in 19 innings. He lost his first two decisions before throwing seven scoreless innings Saturday in Chicago to beat the Cubs and move past Larry Dierker into second place on the club's all-time wins list with 138. He's six shy of tying Joe Niekro for first. Oswalt is 13-7 with a 2.62 ERA in 26 career games against the Pirates, including 25 starts. He lost his only start against them last year, giving up nine hits and six runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm found an effective mix of fastballs, curves and sliders his last time out on the way to sealing his first win of the season. The lefty was also able to finish 6 2/3 innings, which was longer than either of his previous two starts had lasted. It's rare when Maholm isn't able to keep his team in the game with a quality start, and the Pirates need that consistency given some of the struggles in the rest of the rotation. The other good news is that the left-hander continues to pitch with good health, a benefit that he did not enjoy through all of 2009. Maholm is 8-4 with a 4.01 ERA in 13 career starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez, who led the Astros in wins last year with a career-high 14, is searching for his first this season. He lost his first two starts to the Giants and Cardinals but regrouped and pitched well against the Cubs on Sunday at Wrigley Field. He went seven innings and allowed two runs on six hits, striking out three batters and getting a no-decision.  Rodriguez is 4-4 with a 4.60 ERA in 11 career starts against the Pirates. He faced them twice last year and was 1-1 with a 3.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: It looks like Jakubauskas will get the call from Triple-A to make the spot start for the Pirates on Saturday. The right-hander has made two Minor League starts this season and was kept from making his next scheduled one on Thursday to get him ready for Saturday. In 10 innings, Jakubauskas has allowed five earned runs on 10 hits. He's walked four and struck out eight. Jakubauskas has Major League experience, all of that coming last season with the Mariners. In 35 appearances (eight starts) with Seattle last year, Jakubauskas went 6-7 with a 5.32 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is still searching for his first win with the Astros. He's pitched into the sixth inning in all three starts this year and threw seven innings in his previous two starts, April 14 at St. Louis and April 20 against Florida. In those two games, he allowed 12 hits, six runs (five earned) and struck out nine batters in 14 innings. Myers has made eight career appearances against the Pirates, including seven starts, and is 3-4 with a 2.64 ERA. He's allowed 41 hits and struck out 42 in 47 2/3 innings. He last faced Pittsburgh in 2008, going 1-1 with a 3.55 ERA in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Pirates continue to rave about Morton's potential, but potential has not come close to translating into results for the right-hander this season. An already bad start to the season got worse for Morton on Tuesday, when he was pulled after allowing the first five hitters in the second inning to reach base. Morton was charged with six runs (five earned) on six hits and three walks in one inning. He pegged a lack of aggressiveness as the main problem afterward, and it's obvious that Morton needs to trust his fastball more than he has so far. More bad news for Morton: He is winless with a 7.88 ERA in three previous starts against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Norris allowed three hits and four runs (three earned), two walks and struck out five batters in five innings in his previous start Wednesday against the Marlins. He was rocked by the Phillies and lost his first start of the season before holding the Cardinals to no earned runs in five innings to beat the Cardinals for his only win of the season, April 15. This will be his first career appearances against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Speculation ran rampant that Harang's turn in the rotation could be skipped or that the veteran might be temporarily moved to the bullpen, a la Carlos Zambrano in Chicago. For now, the struggling righty is still scheduled to start on Tuesday. With Harang's normal turn occurring on Monday's off-day, the Reds could have pushed him back in order to provide him more time to get right. In Wednesday's 14-6 loss to the Dodgers, Harang allowed seven runs and 10 hits in 5 2/3 innings. He has given up 29 hits and 22 runs, including six home runs, in 21 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino is 0-2 in three starts, but has pitched better than his numbers indicate. He lost his previous two starts to the Cubs on April 16 at Wrigley Field and to the Marlins on Thursday in Houston, allowing a combined 12 hits and 10 runs (seven earned). He gave up six hits and two earned runs in 5 2/3 innings in his previous start and lowered his ERA to 5.93 from 7.36. He's 1-3 with a 5.86 ERA in five career starts against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Leake, who has been the Reds' most consistent starter thus far, earned his first Major League victory on Thursday, and the first win by a Reds starter in 16 games. Against the Los Angeles Dodgers, the top offensive club in the Major Leagues, Leaked allowed five earned runs on eight hits in seven innings. He walked one and had five strikeouts. One of his few mistakes was allowing a two-run pinch-hit home run by Garrett Anderson. But the Reds rallied to earn the 22-year-old his first win. Leake, who had issued a combined 12 walks in his first two outings, displayed much better control on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt gets his first chance of the season to try to continue his domination of the Reds. Oswalt is 23-1 with a 2.58 ERA in 32 career games (30 starts) against the Reds, but has thrown only one complete game. He made four starts against the Reds last year and posted a 3.38 ERA, but had four no-decisions. After losing to Tim Lincecum and Roy Halladay in his first two starts, Oswalt is 2-0 with a 1.29 ERA in his previous two starts in wins over the Cubs and Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo had his worst outing of the season in a 10-4 loss to San Diego on Friday night at Great American Ball Park. Arroyo, who moved up one day in the rotation to give Johnny Cueto an extra day of rest, allowed eight earned runs on eight hits in three-plus innings. He walked two and had no strikeouts. Arroyo pitched to four batters in the fourth inning. It was his shortest outing since May 6, 2009, when he gave up nine earned runs to Milwaukee in one-plus innings. Arroyo says he felt fine physically in Friday's outing despite complaining of flu-like symptoms earlier in the day.

home_pitcher_note: The big right-hander has followed up his outstanding rookie season (11-4, 2.78) with a strong start to his sophomore campaign. After four starts, Hanson has a 1-2 record but an impressive 2.14 ERA and his last start was arguably his strongest. He allowed one unearned run on five hits and struck out eight in his five-inning rain-shortened complete game loss to the Mets on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Myers makes his fifth start for the Astros and is coming off his first win of the season, beating the Pirates on Sunday by allowing 11 singles and two earned runs in six innings. Myers has struggled against the Braves in his career. He's appeared in 28 games vs. Atlanta (21 starts) and is 4-9 with a 4.52 ERA. He's 3-3 lifetime at Turner Field with a 5.25 ERA in 12 games, including eight starts. He's 0-4 against the Braves since his win against them, which occurred in 2006. Myers has given up 35 hits and struck out 18 batters in 26 innings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson has rebounded well from the Tommy John surgery that limited him to seven starts in 2009. The right-hander allowed two earned runs in each of his first three outings before giving up three earned runs on six hits over six innings against the Cardinals on Monday night.
away_pitcher_note: Left-hander Wandy Rodriguez was scratched from his scheduled start Friday in Atlanta because of back spasms, but is ready to go Saturday. Rodriguez said his back began giving him issues last Saturday, when he pitched 7 1/3 innings and got his first win of the season by beating Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe struggled in four of his first five starts and has seen his ERA rise steadily since limiting the Giants to one earned run over six innings in his April 10 start. On Tuesday against the Cardinals, the 36-year-old right-hander allowed five earned runs on five hits over 5 2/3 innings with four strikeouts and two walks.
away_pitcher_note: Norris was roughed up in his last start, Tuesday against Cincinnati, allowing six hits, five earned runs and four walks in five innings. This will be his 15th career start and 16th appearance in a Major League game. He's 7-5 with a 4.79 ERA since he joined the Majors late last year and has struck out 77 batters and allowed 78 hits in 73 1/3 innings. Norris has never faced the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old right-hander is looking to earn his first win of 2010. Control has been one of his biggest problems, as Paulino has walked 14 batters in 21 2/3 innings, while recording 15 strikeouts. He's also had some tough luck, as over his last two starts, covering 10 2/3 innings, seven of the 11 runs he's allowed have been unearned. This will be Paulino's first career start against the Diamondbacks.
away_pitcher_note: Valdez will be called up from Triple-A Reno on Monday and start in place of the injured Kris Benson in Houston. Valdez was 1-1 with a 3.80 ERA in four starts for Reno this year, with 25 strikeouts and five walks in 23 2/3 innings. The 25-year-old got the nod over Kevin Mulvey, Billy Buckner and Bryan Augenstein.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt had his two-game winning streak snapped in his last outing, Thursday night against Cincinnati, dropping a 4-2 decision at Minute Maid Park. He allowed three earned runs and eight hits in seven innings, while striking out seven, including the 1,500th of his career. The loss was only the second in 25 career decisions against the Reds. The veteran righty, who is five-for-five in quality starts in 2010, looks to continue his dominance against the D-backs, against whom he is 9-1 lifetime with a 1.96 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy was outstanding last time out against the Cubs, though you might not be able to tell that from the box score. The right-hander cruised through seven innings, allowing just one run. With a worn out bullpen, he was left in for the eighth and Kosuke Fukudome hit a grand slam. Still, Kennedy got through eight innings, which helped save an exhausted pen. In his outing prior to that, Kennedy and the D-backs were foiled by Phillies outfielder Jayson Werth. The right-hander allowed two runs over a career-high eight innings. Both of the runs came on homers from Werth and Raul Ibanez. Kennedy left with the game tied at 2-2, but Werth's solo homer in the ninth off Juan Gutierrez won it for Philly. Kennedy appeared in just one game for the Yankees in 2009 and four in Triple-A after missing most of the year following surgery to remove an aneurysm near his right shoulder. The right-hander came in the same three-team trade that netted the D-backs Edwin Jackson.

home_pitcher_note: Myers provided another solid outing his last time out on Friday in Atlanta, allowing three earned runs and six hits over seven innings. But he gave up two home runs, including the decisive two-run shot in the third inning in a 4-2 loss. Myers has not gone fewer than six innings in any of his five starts in 2010. He is 2-2 in six games (five starts) with a 4.22 ERA lifetime against Arizona, but has not faced them since 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Lopez contributed to his own demise in his last start. The right-hander tried to field a pop fly in the infield and collided with first baseman Adam LaRoche, who had a better play on the ball. The Cubs went on to score four runs in the inning and eventually prevailed, 11-5. Lopez allowed six runs (two earned because of his error) in six innings. His start prior to that was not a good one as he allowed six runs on 10 hits against the Phillies at Chase Field. While not overpowering, Lopez has a good feel for pitching and manages a game well. Lopez came to Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and pitched his way into the No. 4 spot in the rotation, besting Billy Buckner and Kevin Mulvey. The right-hander has battled arm troubles since being the ace of the Orioles' staff early last decade. He throws a fastball, cutter, curveball, slider and change. Lopez appeared in seven games (five starts) for the Phillies last year and also started 18 games for Triple-A Lehigh Valley.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off back spasms that forced him to push his start back a day, Rodriguez surrendered five runs and 10 hits, both season highs, in a season-low five innings in Atlanta on Saturday afternoon in Houston's 10-1 loss. Only two of the runs were earned, however, and the diminutive lefty has allowed two earned runs or fewer in each of his past three starts, pitching to a 2.36 ERA (five earned runs in 19 1/3 innings). He's allowed three runs or fewer in four out of five starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Haren had a bit of a stomach bug the morning of his last start against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. Still, he managed to scatter 10 hits over six innings and depart with a 5-3 lead. The bullpen, though, let him down and the Cubs wound up winning, 7-5. Haren has pitched well this year, but he has not been the dominant first-half pitcher the D-backs have grown accustomed to. One reason he said is that he is still working to get his fastball control where he wants it. In his last outing prior to his last one against the Rockies at Coors Field, he allowed a pair of runs over eight innings and struck out 10. He's been a force at the plate this year, going 9-for-18 with a pair of doubles. Haren has been used as a pinch-hitter once this year already.

home_pitcher_note: Norris lasted five innings in his last start on Sunday in Atlanta, allowing eight hits and seven earned runs. He walked four and struck out three. Norris picked up his only win of the year on April 15 in St. Louis, when he pitched five innings, giving up just four hits and one unearned run. It was Houston's first win of the season after starting with eight straight losses. He has not lasted more than five innings in any of his five starts. The one positive is that he has not allowed a home run this season.
away_pitcher_note: Latos, who was coming off his shortest game of his career, working just 2 2/3 innings against the Marlins on April 26, responded with a strong outing against the Brewers in his last start. The 22-year-old allowed two runs on six hits over six innings. He walked three and had four strikeouts. Latos allowed a home run to his counterpart, Brewers pitcher Yovani Gallardo, but otherwise fared well against a dangerous lineup. This will be Latos' first start against the Astros. He's 0-1 with an 11.42 ERA in two road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino lost his fourth consecutive start on Monday at home against Arizona. He gave up five hits, including a homer, and four earned runs in six innings. He has lasted at least five innings in all five of his starts. He struck out eight D-backs, but has been hurt by walks this season. He has struck out 23 and walked 18 in 27 2/3 innings. He has thrown 106 pitches or more in four of his five games, with a high of 124 vs. Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Garland walked five over seven scoreless innings in his last start against the Brewers, but allowed three hits, and, as is the case when he's throwing well, got 12 ground-ball outs thanks in large part to his sinker. "You can't discount what the starters have done this entire season," Padres manager Bud Black said. "When Jon's on, you're going to see a lot of grounders."  Garland, a free-agent acquisition by first-year general manager Jed Hoyer, has pitched well since two not-so-good outings to open the season in Arizona and Colorado. "It's quality pitches, keeping the ball down and not making mistakes," said Garland, a line he's no doubt used countless times during his 10-year Major League career.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt has received little offensive support from his teammates. He has pitched seven innings in his past four starts and at least six innings in all six starts. Oswalt has not allowed more than three earned runs in any game. He surrendered five hits and one earned run on Tuesday against the D-backs, striking out eight and walking three, and still got beat, 1-0, which extended Houston's losing streak. Five of his six starts have been at home. He last won on April 23 vs. Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Stauffer fills in for scheduled starter Kevin Correia, who flew to California on Sunday morning after the death of his younger brother. The start is the first of the season for Stauffer, who has been excellent out of the bullpen, going 2-1 with a 0.49 ERA in nine appearances spanning 18 1/3 innings. He has issued just four walks while striking out 18. Stauffer was 4-7 with a 3.58 ERA in 14 starts for the Padres in 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Penny lost a 4-0 decision in Philadelphia his last time out on May 6. Penny left after needing only 75 pitches to clear six innings. Game situation rather than his performance dictated his removal from a 3-0 game. Penny has been sensational since hooking up with St. Louis pitching guru Dave Duncan, and it looks like he's headed for his best season in years.
away_pitcher_note: Myers helped Houston end its eight-game losing streak Wednesday when he pitched seven innings against Arizona, allowing six hits and two runs, in a game the Astros eventually won 4-2 in the bottom of the ninth. Myers has lasted at least six innings in all six starts this season. He won his only game April 25 vs. Pittsburgh at home. He has thrown 100 or more pitches in five of his six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse got roughed up at Philadelphia on May 6, surrendering five runs (three earned) off nine hits and one walk with three strikeouts over four innings. Lohse has been up and down through six starts. He's been shelled twice, had two decent outings and tossed two gems.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez's last start, Thursday at home against Arizona, was his worst of the season, as he gave up nine hits and five earned runs in 3 2/3 innings. He has gone at least six innings in all but one of his other starts, when he lasted just 4 1/3 innings April 12 at St. Louis. He has lost his last two starts after beating Pittsburgh April 24 at home, when he gave up just one earned run in 7 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter struck out eight and walked none in a no-decision against the Pirates on May 7. Carpenter allowed two earned runs on eight hits and his WHIP stands at a sparkling 1.07. He hasn't gone more than seven innings in any of his seven starts this season. Carpenter has yielded just four runs in 20 innings over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Norris continues to baffle the Astros, if not opponents. He lost his third straight start Friday when he surrendered four earned runs in four innings vs. San Diego. He hasn't won since April 15 at St. Louis, his second start of the season and Houston's first win of the year. He hasn't lasted more than five innings in any of his six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer received a no-decision in his most recent outing last Saturday at New York. He yielded three runs in the first two innings and ultimately settled down, though he lasted just 4 1/3 innings, allowing three runs and four hits. Wellemeyer also issued five walks and leads the team with 20 in 28 2/3 innings, which offsets his competent .229 opponents' batting average.
away_pitcher_note: The big right-hander is coming off his best start of the season Saturday against the Padres in Houston. He pitched seven innings and allowed five hits and two runs (one earned) and struck out 11 batters while not issuing any walks. Alas, he suffered the loss because the Astros scored one run. Paulino has lost each of his past five starts after getting a no-decision in his first start. Paulino's only previous career appearance at San Francisco was forgettable. He lasted only two innings and gave up nine hits and nine runs (eight earned) in a loss last July.

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum pitched like the two-time Cy Young Award winner that he is against Houston in the season opener, allowing four hits while walking none and striking out seven in seven shutout innings. Lincecum is 7-for-7 in quality starts, limiting opponents to a .193 batting average overall and recording a 2.01 ERA at home -- which actually exceeds his 1.73 ERA on the road. Lincecum has sharpened his control, issuing an average of 1.9 walks per nine innings -- down from last year's figure of 2.7. He's also averaging 11.9 strikeouts per nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt has delivered a quality start in all seven of his outings this year but only has two wins to show for it. He's coming off a solid start against the Padres on Sunday in which he struck out nine batters and gave up six hits and three runs in eight innings. He got a no-decision. He pitched against the Giants and Tim Lincecum on Opening Day and took the loss after allowing seven hits and three earned runs in six innings. He's 5-6 with a 3.76 ERA in 25 starts against the Giants in his career, including a masterful effort last July in which he allowed three hits and one run in eight innings. He's 3-5 with a 4.39 ERA in nine career starts at AT&T Park.

home_pitcher_note: Zito is coming off his first loss of the season, a 3-2 setback against the San Diego Padres in which he surrendered three runs in five innings and equaled a career high by walking seven. Zito set the tone for his season by sparkling in his 2010 debut at Houston, allowing three hits while walking one and striking out five in six shutout innings. Zito has been equally effective against left- and right-handed batters, limiting the former group to a .200 average and the latter to a .197 figure.
away_pitcher_note: Myers is coming off a win at St. Louis in which he held the Cardinals to eight hits and two runs in six innings. He's thrown six innings or more in each of his seven starts, marking the second time he has done that. In 2003, he went six innings or more in his first 11 starts with the Phillies. He got a no-decision when he faced the Giants in the second game of the season April 14 in Houston, giving up 12 hits and four runs in six innings. He's 1-3 with a 6.75 ERA in eight career games (six starts) vs. the Giants, and 1-1 with a 4.85 ERA in four career games (two starts) at AT&T Park. Myers lost his first three starts against the Giants before beating them in 2006. He pitched against them twice in relief in 2007 and made one start against them in 2008 and didn't get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Most winning teams get contributions from the least expected places, and that's the case with Ely, who gets Monday's start against the Astros. Rebounding from a wobbly debut, Ely has posted back-to-back impressive starts. He throws strikes, works both sides of the plate with four reliable pitches and isn't intimidated by Major League hitters or his lack of an overpowering fastball. He's a cheerleader in the dugout, energetic on the field and fun to watch. And to opponents, he's still something of a mystery. His next challenge will be to make the adjustments necessary as opposing teams get a more thorough scouting line on him.
away_pitcher_note: Still searching for the rhythm that made him a feared piece of the Astros' rotation last season, Rodriguez surrendered five runs (four earned) over six innings in a winning effort against the Cardinals in his last start. Still, Rodriguez hasn't posted a quality start in May. He'll look to pick up win No. 3 when he takes on the Dodgers, against whom the lefty is 3-2 with a 2.70 ERA in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda delivered another quality start in his return to Chase Field, site of last year's frightening drilling by a Rusty Ryal line drive. Kuroda admitted first-batter jitters led to a four-pitch walk, but he regrouped to allow two earned runs over 7 1/3 innings while striking out nine. Kuroda relied on his slider while lacking his customary two-seam fastball, but he's become the de facto staff ace this season by being able to win without his best stuff. He is 1-0 with a 1.93 in three career starts against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Norris is coming off the perhaps the best start of his career Thursday in St. Louis in which he held the Cardinals to six hits and one run and struck out eight batters without walking anybody to snap a three-start losing streak. He improved to 4-0 lifetime against St. Louis, which accounts for half of his career wins.  This will be the California native's first career start against the Dodgers. He's 4-2 with a 4.22 ERA in eight career games (seven starts) on the road in his career, including 2-1 this year.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino was rocked for eight hits and seven earned runs in 4 2/3 innings and issued four walks and two wild pitches in his previous start Friday in San Francisco. The Astros have lost in 14 of Paulino's past 15 starts since July 3, 2009. Paulino, who has received poor run support this year, is 5-18 since joining the Majors in 2007. He's 0-1 with an 8.10 ERA in two career starts against the Rockies, both of which came last season. Paulino has pitched much better at Minute Maid in his career, going 2-10 with a 4.91 ERA in 21 games (17 starts).
away_pitcher_note: Smith gracefully accepted reassignment to the bullpen last week, but before he makes his first appearance as a reliever, he's got one more task to attend to: Another start. Thanks to Colorado's rotation being thrown off by Friday's rainout and subsequent doubleheader on Saturday against Washington, manager Jim Tracy announced Smith would start this game at Houston. Smith has started seven games for Colorado this season and has a 1-2 record and a 6.35 ERA. In his last start, on May 10, the lefty went 5 2/3 innings against San Diego, allowing eight hits and four earned runs, while striking out six and walking four. Wednesday will mark his first career appearance against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt has lost three consecutive decisions in his previous four starts despite pitching well. He held the Giants to six hits and two runs and struck out seven batters in eight innings Saturday in San Francisco but was outdueled by Tim Lincecum for the second time this year. In his five losses this year, the Astros have scored four runs in the 33 innings he's been on the mound. He's dominated the Rockies in his career, going 7-1 with a 1.78 ERA in 10 starts. Oswalt faced the Rockies once last year and held them to six hits and one run and struck out eight batters in seven innings to get a win. He's five wins away from tying Joe Niekro's club record of 144.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez offered another brilliant outing against the Nationals on Saturday, silencing their bats for eight innings while yielding two runs on seven hits and a walk and striking out five. He paid for a couple mistakes, including hanging a split-finger fastball to Adam Dunn, who sent it 442 feet into the third deck at Coors Field for the first home run Jimenez has given up all season. He was efficient with his pitches, throwing 115, including 70 for strikes, and kept a tight game in hand, only trailing after giving up a first-inning run, then shutting down the Nats until the Dunn solo shot. Jimenez set the tone for the Rockies to sweep their first doubleheader since September 2007, a game into their 21-of-22 win stretch that catapulted the club to its first World Series appearance.

home_pitcher_note: Myers threw the Astros' first complete game of the season in his previous start Sunday in San Francisco, holding the Giants to five hits and four runs in eight innings. He gave up a pair of home runs and a wild pitch that accounted for all four runs, but was extremely sharp outside of those three pitches. He's pitched at least six innings in all eight starts and has five quality starts. Myers has never faced the Rays in the regular season, but he started Game 2 of the 2008 World Series against the Rays in St. Petersburg, Fla., and took the loss, allowing seven hits and three earned runs in seven innings. Myers is 5-5 with a 6.07 ERA in 20 Interleague games (18 starts), including two complete games (one shutout).
away_pitcher_note: Garza will make his ninth start of the season against Houston. Garza only gave up five hits, two walks and one run over six innings in his last start, but he didn't have his best stuff while earning a no-decision against the Mariners on Sunday. His fastball command was a little off, and he admittedly struggled to find the strike zone at times, throwing just 56 of his 106 pitches for strikes. Still, he battled through six innings, benefited from excellent defensive play behind him and kept his team around long enough to win. Friday will be the Rays' first Interleague game, and Garza will face the Astros for just the second time in his four-year Major League career -- and his first time against them away from Tropicana Field. The 26-year-old has gone eight or more innings in four of his starts, allowed one earned run or less in five, given up two runs or fewer in six of them and will hope for more of the same in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: The only left-hander in the Astros' rotation will be making his ninth start of the season. Rodriguez has lost three of his previous four starts, including Monday's game in Los Angeles in which he gave up seven hits and four runs (one earned) in 6 2/3 innings. He's 6-6 with a 4.81 ERA in 16 career Interleague starts and has pitched once previously in his career against the Rays. That was in 2008 in St. Petersburg, when he allowed five hits and two runs and two walks in 5 2/3 innings and took a no-decision. Rodriguez is 32-23 with a 3.65 ERA in his career at Minute Maid Park, including 1-2, 4.76 ERA in three starts this season.
away_pitcher_note:
Niemann will take the mound against the Astros for his ninth start of the season Saturday. The 6-foot-9 right-hander has worked into the seventh inning for quality starts in seven straight appearances and in all but one of his starts -- the sole exception being his injury-shortened first start of the season against Baltimore. He gave up a season-high 10 hits Monday night in a 4-3 win over the Indians, who scored three runs off Niemann. He admitted he wasn't as sharp as he could have been against Cleveland, but Tampa Bay's defense and bullpen helped make up for the starter's second-shortest outing of the season. 
Niemann has never faced the Astros in his short career, and this will be his fourth start in Interleague Play. He has recorded a win and two no-decisions in his previous outings, none of which went longer than six innings, but he did not allow more than three runs in any of them.

home_pitcher_note: Norris, whose only two wins of the season have come at Busch Stadium against the Cardinals, has failed to get past in the fifth inning in seven of his eight starts. He went 4 1/3 innings Tuesday night at Dodger Stadium and gave up seven hits and six earned runs and was hit by a line drive on his right arm during the game, though it didn't seem to affect his performance. He was among the league leaders in strikeouts per nine innings before fanning only three batters Tuesday. Norris has never pitched in Interleague Play and is 4-5 with a 5.89 ERA in 10 career home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Price will take on the Astros in his ninth start of the season after another impressive outing against the Indians on Tuesday. The American League's first six-game winner pitched six innings, scattered four hits, walked three, struck out five and gave up just one unearned run. He likely could have gone deeper into the game, but manager Joe Maddon has been limiting his starters to around 100 pitches. The left-hander had great control of his fastball against Cleveland, and he threw 65 of his 97 pitches for strikes. Price's first career start against Houston will be his fourth in Interleague Play. He is 1-2 in those outings and allowed five earned runs in two of the three starts -- both losses.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf was humming along through six innings on Wednesday in Pittsburgh, but he hit a wall in the seventh, allowing three runs on the way to his fourth loss in his last five starts. He was charged with six earned runs on 10 hits in 6 1/3 innings, five days after allowing six runs on seven hits in five innings against the Phillies in an outing he termed, "embarrassing." Wolf was similarly blunt after his loss to the Pirates. "I'm concerned about the fact that I stink," Wolf said. "I'm not going to candy-coat it." He had to ask how many batters he walked. The answer was five, one shy of the career-high he matched three starts earlier against the Padres. "That's horrible," Wolf said.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros won a game in which Paulino started for the first time this year when they beat Colorado Wednesday in Houston, but the big right-hander is still searching for his first win of the season. He had lost six consecutive starts before holding the Rockies to six hits, two runs and five walks in six innings.  He's worked at least five innings seven times in eight starts. Paulino is 0-3 with an 8.53 ERA in four career games against the Brewers, including three starts. He was 0-2 in two starts against them last year, allowing 18 hits in 12 innings. He's pitched two games previously at Miller Park (one start) and is 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson overcame a rough first inning in his last outing Thursday to pick up the win and help the Brewers snap a nine-game skid with a 4-3 win at Pittsburgh. After surrendering three runs on four hits in a 34-pitch opening frame, the southpaw settled down to allow just three hits over his next five innings and finish with 112 pitches, 71 of which went for strikes. Narveson has started two games and made three career appearances against the Astros, with 11 strikeouts in 11 total innings and a 2.45 ERA. It will be just the second home start of the season for the 28-year-old, who threw a Major League-high 130 pitches in his last start at Miller Park, a 10-6 loss to the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt will be making his first start since the Astros acknowledged his agent had asked owner Drayton McLane to trade him to a contender. Oswalt has began the season with nine consecutive quality starts, making him the first Astros pitcher to do so since Roger Clemens in 2005. He has a chance to become the first Houston pitcher since Bob Knepper in 1988 to have 10 consecutive quality starts to begin the season. Oswalt has been the victim of poor run support. The Astros are averaging 2.07 runs per game in Oswalt's starts, and they have scored four runs in 39 innings in his six losses. Oswalt is 13-8 with a 3.75 ERA in 27 career starts against the Brewers, including 5-6 with a 5.36 ERA in 14 starts at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: Things couldn't have been much worse for Bush in his last start. After delivering quality starts in each of his previous two appearances, the Brewers right-hander lasted just one-third of an inning against the Twins, surrendering seven runs on six hits while walking two. It was Bush's shortest outing of his career and according to Bush, "the worst outing I've ever had at any level." He'll look to turn things around at Miller Park against the Astros, a team Bush has had more wins against than any other team in his career. In 13 appearances -- 11 starts -- Bush is 6-1 with a 3.46 ERA against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Myers beat the Tampa Bay Rays in his previous start Friday, allowing six hits and one run and striking out seven batters in seven innings. He's pitched at least six innings in all nine of his starts this year, combining with Roy Oswalt to become the first Astros teammates to achieve that feat since Mike Hampton and the late Jose Lima in 1998. Myers has pitched well against the Brewers in his career, going 4-1 with a 1.77 ERA in eight games (four starts). His previous start against them came in 2008 for Philadelphia, and he threw a two-hit complete game.  He's 1-1 with a 2.84 ERA in two games (one start) at Miller Park.

home_pitcher_note: LeCure will make his Major League debut, replacing the injured Homer Bailey in the Reds rotation. A fourth-round Draft pick by the Reds in 2005, LeCure spent last year and the beginning of this season at Triple-A Louisville. In 2010, he's 5-2 with a 2.55 ERA in nine starts, walking 15 and striking out 51. He was recently named International League pitcher of the week after pitching 16 scoreless innings in his last two starts. Last time out against Scranton-Wilkes Barre, he threw a one-hit shutout in a 5-0 Bats win.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez picked up his fifth quality start of the season Saturday against the Rays by tossing six innings, allowing three runs on six hits. He's just one-third of an inning shy of tying Dave Roberts for fourth place on the Astros' all-time innings list by a lefty. Rodriguez is 6-6 with a 3.89 ERA in 16 starts against the Reds in his career, including 3-2 with a 3.19 ERA in seven starts at Great American Ball Park. That ballpark, and Coors Field in Denver, are the only two ballparks in which Rodriguez has a winning record with more than one decision. He's 21-34 with a 5.10 ERA in his career on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Harang's early-season struggles were finally pushed aside April 27, as the right-hander picked up his first win of the season against Bud Norris and the Astros in Houston. Harang allowed two runs and eight hits in six innings with one walk and six strikeouts to help propel the Reds in a game that started a sweep.
