Harang delivered a solid outing last time out, pitching 6 1/3 innings and allowing five runs (four earned) to pick up the win. He also helped himself offensively, hitting a single and scoring from first base on an Orlando Cabrera double. In his career, he's 10-9 with a 4.71 ERA against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler will make his first start of the season in place of the injured Bud Norris, who was sent to the 15-day disabled list. Although Moehler started 55 games the last two seasons for Houston, each of his 12 appearances in 2010 have come out of the bullpen. He's currently 0-1 with a 4.42 ERA in 18 1/3 innings. In 29 starts in 2009, Moehler finished 8-12 with a 5.47 ERA. Manager Brad Mills does not expect Moehler to pitch more than three or four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Although Leake hasn't picked up a win in his past two starts, he continues to frustrate opposing hitters. In two no-decisions, he's pitched a combined 13 1/3 innings and allowed four runs. The Reds squandered each of the starts, as they allowed seven runs in the ninth to lose to Atlanta on May 20 and managed just one run last Tuesday against the Pirates. Leake allowed a career-high 10 hits in the loss to the Pirates, but just two went for extra bases -- one of which was on a routine fly ball that should have been caught. In his only start against the Astros, Leake allowed one run and five hits in seven innings to beat Paulino on April 28.
away_pitcher_note: Paulino is trying to avoid becoming the first Astros pitcher in history to begin a season with eight consecutive losses. The big right-hander has actually pitched pretty well in his previous two starts, holding the Brewers to seven hits and two runs in six innings Tuesday in Milwaukee. Paulino faced the Reds on April 28 in Houston and gave up six hits, six runs and four walks in five innings. He's 1-4 with a 5.51 ERA in six career starts against the Reds, including 1-2 with a 5.40 ERA in three starts at Great American Ball Park. He's 3-9 with an 8.00 ERA all-time on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Despite a 3-6 record, Oswalt has posted a quality start in each of his 10 outings. With one more against Washington, he'll tie the franchise record set by Dave Giusti in 1968. In his last trip to the mound, Oswalt pitched eight scoreless innings and allowed just four hits with nine strikeouts in a win in Milwaukee. Although he has started six games in the past four years against Washington, Oswalt hasn't earned a decision against the club since 2005.
away_pitcher_note: Atilano has pitched only seven games during his career, but he bested Tim Lincecum on Wednesday, lasting 5 1/3 innings and giving up two runs on four hits. Atilano cruised through the first four innings. San Francisco, however, was able to get to him in the fifth, when Juan Uribe hit a solo homer. An inning later, when Pablo Sandoval came to the plate, Atilano left the game in favor of left-hander Doug Slaten. Sandoval doubled, scoring Andres Torres. The run was charged to Atilano, who said he was pleased with his performance. He wasn't behind in the count like he was in his most recent start and threw fewer pitches -- 76.

home_pitcher_note: Myers has pitched at least six innings in each of his 10 starts this year. In his last five games, he is 2-1 with a 2.65 ERA, although the Astros have scored more than four runs in just one of those starts. Myers will make his 34th career appearance against Washington, which is more than any other opponent. He's 10-9 with a 4.18 ERA against the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen was solid during the Nationals' loss to the Giants at AT&T Park on Thursday afternoon. Stammen lasted 6 1/3 innings, allowing two earned runs on five hits. It was his first quality start since May 7 against the Marlins. Stammen needed to have a good outing because he could be the odd man out of the rotation once right-hander Stephen Strasburg is called up next month. Before Thursday's game, Stammen was 1-2 with a 5.96 ERA. Manager Jim Riggleman did not indicate if Stammen is in danger of losing his spot in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had his roughest performance of the season his last time out, lasting just 3 1/3 innings and allowing eight runs in a 15-6 loss in Cincinnati. The left-hander said he is struggling with his curveball and needs to work on his command. The month of May was particularly rough for Rodriguez, as he went 1-5 with a 6.75 ERA after posting a 3.65 ERA in April.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan started for the Nationals and lasted seven innings, allowing two runs on seven hits. It was Lannan's first win since April 10 against the Mets. In his past three starts, Lannan has allowed four earned runs over 18 1/3 innings. His left elbow problems appear to be a thing of the past.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler began the season in the bullpen and made 12 relief appearances before making a spot start on Saturday in place of Bud Norris, who was placed on the disabled list with bursitis and biceps tendinitis. In that start, Moehler was rocked for 10 hits and eight earned runs in 2 2/3 innings, and he struggled with his location. He's 3-4 with a 4.87 ERA in 14 career games (nine starts) against the Nationals and is 10-14 with a 5.32 ERA in 67 career appearances (22 starts) at Minute Maid Park. Moehler is 80-99 with a 4.90 ERA in 245 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Martin made his first start of the season last Saturday at San Diego, allowing four hits and one earned run in six innings. He struck out five, walked none and gave up a home run, to Nick Hundley in his 88 pitches. He went 5-4 with a 4.44 ERA in 15 starts last year with Washington. Martin was called up last Friday from Triple-A Syracuse, where he was 2-1 with a 2.97 ERA, to replace outfielder Justin Maxwell on the Washington roster. It will be difficult for Martin to hold his spot in the rotation with left-hander Scott Olsen due back soon from a shoulder injury and right-hander Stephen Strasburg expected to debut between June 8 and 10 vs. Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino has started the season with seven consecutive losses, but it's not all because he's not pitching well. He has a respectable 4.40 ERA and has had the worst run support in the National League this season. Witness his most recent start Sunday against the Reds, in which Paulino threw eight scoreless innings and gave up four hits, four walks and struck out five batters. The game was tied at 0-0 before the Astros won in extra innings. In his Past three starts, he's allowed four earned runs in 20 innings. He's given up just two home runs all year in 59 1/3 innings, but walks continue to be a problem (34). Paulino faced the Cubs on April 16 in Chicago and took the loss, giving up six hits and five earned runs in six innings. He's 0-2 with a 7.82 ERA in three career games against the Cubs, including two starts.
away_pitcher_note:
This will be Zambrano's first start since April 20. The right-hander moved to the bullpen to 
make room in the rotation for Ted Lilly and also to give the team a potent setup pitcher. He was effective until May 14 against the Pirates, when he gave up three runs on four hits over one inning. Zambrano then said he wasn't comfortable in the role and wanted to go back to the rotation. Since that game against the Pirates, he has given up one hit over 4 1/3 scoreless innings. Big Z tuned up with a 73-pitch simulated game last Monday. In four starts, Zambrano was 1-2 with a 7.45 ERA. He's made 13 relief outings, including Saturday, when he needed just two pitches to get a double play and end the eighth against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt had his string of 10 consecutive quality starts to begin the season brought to an abrupt end in his previous start Monday when he was ejected in the third inning for what crew chief Gary Darling said was showing up an umpire. Despite piling up the quality starts, Oswalt has lost five of his past six decisions because he's received poor run support. In the start prior to his ejection, he threw eight scoreless innings at Milwaukee and got the win. Oswalt beat the Cubs earlier this year, firing seven scoreless innings and striking out six batters April 17 at Wrigley Field. He's 14-12 with a 3.67 ERA in 31 career games against the Cubs, including 30 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster threw a season-high 125 pitches in his last start Sunday against the Cardinals. The Cubs needed him to go deep because of an overworked bullpen. The right-hander said he didn't execute his pitches well, giving up six runs over 6 2/3 innings on nine hits, including two home runs by Albert Pujols. Dempster has lost five of his last six decisions. He did not get a decision against the Astros on April 18, giving up one run on four hits over 7 2/3 innings. He struck out eight in that game.

Wells pitched five shutout innings on two days' rest against the Pirates on Monday after failing to retire a batter in his previous start, a 7-1 loss on May 28 to St. Louis in which he allowed six hits on 16 pitches. Wells left the game against Pittsburgh with a 1-0 lead after tossing 90 pitches on a hot and very humid afternoon.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel held the Giants to one run, an Andres Torres home run, in 6 2/3 innings on Tuesday night in a game the Rockies eventually won, 2-1, in 11 innings. It was a breakthrough for Hammel, who stayed composed in a tight pitching contest with the Giants' Barry Zito. Despite his success, Hammel didn't have complete fastball command. If he can gain a handle on all his pitches and show consistency, a hot streak could be on the horizon.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struck out a season-high eight batters in five innings of a 5-1 win over Washington on Wednesday at home to snap his three-game losing streak. Rodriguez has allowed three earned runs or fewer in seven of his 11 starts. He's 3-1 in  with a 3.55 ERA in five career starts at Coors Field, beating the Rockies there last by holding them to two earned runs in seven innings. Overall, he's 4-2 with a 4.31 ERA in nine career starts against the Rockies. Rodriguez is 21-35 with a 5.24 ERA in 77 career games on the road.

home_pitcher_note: With each passing start, Francis shoves into the past any concerns about the shoulder problems that cost him last season. For the most part, he has provided reminders that he was the Rockies' No. 1 pitcher when they went to the 2007 World Series. But he gave up three two-out runs and four overall in 5 2/3 innings of a loss to the Giants in his last start, after starting the game with four stellar innings. So he needs to be a little more consistent.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler is making his third start of the year after working out of the bullpen to begin the season. He worked 5 2/3 innings against the Nationals on Thursday in Houston, allowing five hits, two runs, one walk and striking out three batters. Moehler is 1-2 with a 6.67 ERA in eight games (four starts) in his career against the Rockies. He's pitched in two games in his career (both starts) at Coors Field and is 0-2 with a 9.58 ERA. He hasn't pitched at Coors Field since 2008. Moehler is 37-55 with a 5.07 ERA on the road in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Cook gave up three runs and four hits in his last start, a no-decision at Arizona. He learned early, when Justin Upton homered in the first, that his sinker wasn't at its best, but he used his curve and four-seamer and spotted his sinker where it wouldn't hurt him. He left the game in position to win. The best news, though, is Cook is pitching at Coors Field, where he is 2-0 with a 2.63 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Paulino earned his first win of the season in his most recent start Thursday, beating the Cubs, 3-1, at Minute Maid Park. He went eight innings and gave up five hits and one run and struck out seven batters for his first win since his final start of the 2009 season. He has allowed one run in his past 21 innings in three starts. He faced the Rockies twice last year, going 0-1 with an 8.10 ERA. He's 0-1 with a 6.19 ERA in three career starts against the Rockies, including 0-1 with a 15.75 ERA in his only start at Coors Field. He's 3-9 with a 7.10 ERA in 16 career games (12 starts) on the road this year.

home_pitcher_note: Chacin struck out a career-high nine in 5 2/3 innings, but fell to the D-backs in his last start. Chacin is looking similar to a young Ubaldo Jimenez. He has impressive stuff, but, like Jimenez before this season, there is early-inning inefficiency. He needed 38 pitches to go two innings and 57 to go three.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt is coming off a start in which he allowed a season-high nine hits and six runs in an 8-5 loss to the Cubs at home. He's thrown at least six innings in 11 of his 12 starts, but at 3-8 has tied for his most losses before the All-Star break in his career. His 283 starts are the third-most in club history, and his 140 wins are the second-most in club history, trailing only Joe Niekro (144). Oswalt is 7-2 with a 1.88 ERA in 11 career starts against the Rockies and has never lost at Coors Field (3-0, 2.17 ERA in four starts). He threw a one-hit shutout against the Rockies in Colorado in his previous start against them in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte gets the nod against his former club as the Yankees open a three-game weekend series with the Astros. He will look to tie Phil Hughes for the team lead in victories, one start after taking a no-decision in 7 2/3 innings of two-run, five-hit ball against the Blue Jays in Toronto. Pettitte won four of five decisions in May and has never faced the Astros, for whom he was 37-26 with a 3.38 ERA in 84 games from 2004-06.
away_pitcher_note: Myers has been the most dependable starter on the Astros staff this season, posting a 4-3 record with a 3.01 ERA while lasting at least six innings in each of his 12 starts, a stretch ranking as a career high. He has gotten stronger with each month of the season, posting ERAs of 3.82 in April, 2.65 in May, and 1.98 through his first two starts of June to extend his streak of quality starts to four. In his last start, Myers held the Cubs to two runs on eights hits and a walk while striking out six over 6 2/3 innings for the win. He battled through traffic, as he has through much of the season, bearing down and executing his pitches when it mattered the most.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez will start the second game of New York's three-game series with the Astros on Saturday, looking for his third consecutive victory after beating the Orioles and Blue Jays earlier this month. Vazquez hurled seven innings of one-hit, two-run ball on June 6 at Toronto, walking four and striking out nine. Vazquez is 3-5 with a 4.41 ERA in 13 career starts against Houston, including hurling seven innings of scoreless, three-hit ball in a winning effort against them in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had a strong outing in Colorado on Monday, falling to the Rockies despite recording his sixth quality start in 12 trips to the hill.  Rodriguez allowed three runs on nine hits and two walks (one intentional) in seven innings. He had command of all his pitches and was able to throw his breaking balls and changeups effectively for strikes. He pitched through a lot of traffic, but he bore down when he needed to and executed quality pitches to strand Rockies runners, getting stronger as the game progressed and retiring the last seven batters he faced, getting deep into the game and sparing the 'pen. The most damage came on a pitch he intentionally threw out of the zone, high and inside, but Clint Barmes reached for it and sent it to the left field wall to plate the game-winning runs.

home_pitcher_note: Hughes will look to win his fourth consecutive start on Sunday as the Yankees complete a three-game set with the Astros. Hughes wasn't thrilled with his stuff on June 8, but it was good enough to beat the Orioles, hurling six innings of three-run, nine-hit ball, walking none and striking out four. Hughes said that the Orioles were more aggressive, so he wasn't even elated with the zero walks. Hughes has never faced the Astros and is 0-1 with a 2.77 ERA in six Interleague appearances (one start).
away_pitcher_note: Moehler had a critical outing in Colorado, surviving a first-inning Rockies rally that put the Astros down by three, then making key adjustments and coming up with five shutout innings as his team slowly inched its way back and finally took the lead for good in the eighth inning. Moehler sensed a need to curtail Colorado's aggressive approach at the plate, and he began coming inside more to keep the Rockies honest. He ended up with his first quality start of the season, pitching six innings and allowing three runs on nine hits and three walks (one intentional) while striking out four, and his determined battling after digging himself holes was an inspiration to his teammates.

home_pitcher_note: Davies relapsed into a lack-of-control mode in his last outing, walking five batters in a 6-2 loss to the Twins. He'd given up just six bases on balls in his previous five starts so this was a setback for him and the walks kept him in trouble. He'd doled out 17 walks in his first six starts of the season. In his five losses, the Royals have supported him with just seven runs and they've been shut out twice. Although he's a former National Leaguer, this will be the first time that Davies has faced the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Paulino extended a remarkable five-game streak of quality starts with eight innings of two-run ball Wednesday night in Colorado. He only has two decisions in those five games, but the team is 4-1 in the stretch, and his ERA is a miniscule 1.75 over the span. He had pinpoint control, throwing his mid-to-upper 90s fastball for strikes and pounding 74 of his 116 pitches into the zone. His biting slider helped him fan seven Rockies while walking two (one intentional). He scattered eight hits over his eight innings on the hill, allowing a run in the second and another in the sixth, but otherwise silencing the Rockies' bats and putting his team in position to earn the win in extra innings.

home_pitcher_note: Filling in for sore-shouldered Gil Meche, lefty Chen has made three starts with a no-decision and then two victories. Against the Twins last on Thursday, he took an 8-1 lead into the seventh inning before running into trouble. He wound up being charged with five runs, but still got the win. Chen doesn't throw real hard, but varies speeds on his fastball and works all four pitches on both sides of the plate, keeping hitters guessing.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt threw the fifth consecutive quality start for the Astros rotation Thursday in Colorado, holding the Rockies to two runs on four hits while striking out nine and walking two over seven innings. He got the run support he has often been missing-he had the third lowest run support in the league at 2.64 runs per game entering the contest-and the early cushion allowed him to be more creative and unpredictable on the mound. He threw both his fastball and curve in, and used his changeup in the zone. Despite matching his season high with nine strikeouts, he took advantage of the Rockies aggressive swinging by keeping the ball low in the zone to get seven groundball outs and help keep his pitch count to 96 pitches, 72 of which were strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Lerew has been brought up from Triple-A Omaha to take Luke Hochevar's spot in the rotation due to a right elbow sprain. Lerew was 5-3 at Omaha with a 2.84 earned run average in 14 appearances, including 11 starts. Lerew will be working one day short of his normal rotation rest, but insists that won't be a factor because of the adrenaline he anticipates having in a Major League setting. Lerew made three appearances (two starts) for the Royals last September, posting an 0-1 record with a 4.05 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Myers will look to climb one game above .500 as he wraps up a series of Interleague Play against the Royals on Thursday. In his last start, Myers lasted seven innings, giving up four earned runs, as he picked up his fourth loss of the season against the Yankees. He allowed only five hits and three walks, striking out five. Two starts ago, on June 6, Myers lasted 6 2/3 innings, giving up only two earned runs as he picked up his fourth victory of the season against the Cubs. He allowed eight hits and struck out six while only walking one.

home_pitcher_note: The reigning world champions had their way with Rodriguez in his last start. Rodriguez lasted five innings, surrendering eight earned runs on seven hits and five walks while striking out four. Rodriguez will look to lower his 5.60 ERA as he opens up a three-game series against the Rangers. A key for Rodriguez will be to limit the hits allowed, as he has given up 91 hits this season in 72 1/3 innings pitched.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman beat the Brewers, 4-3, on Saturday, holding them scoreless through six innings. He allowed four hits, three walks and hit a batter while striking out a season-high six batters. He is 3-2 with a 4.45 ERA in his last five starts, pitching at least six innings in four of those five starts. He is 2-4 with a 6.03 ERA in six starts on the road this season. Left-handed hitters are batting ,315 off him this season while right-handers are hitting .288. He is 2-4 with a 5.12 ERA in eight starts and 11 relief appearances in Interleague Play, but has never faced the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Making just his fifth start of the season, Moehler is still eyeing that elusive first victory. Through his first 16 appearances, Moehler is 0-3 and will look to pick up his first win against the Rangers. If he wants to find that first win Saturday, he will need to silence the hot bats of the Rangers. In his last start, Moehler lasted 4 2/3 innings, allowing four earned runs on four hits and five walks.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis is 3-2 with a 2.70 ERA in his past five starts. He beat the Astros, 7-2, on Sunday and had two hits and two RBIs. He also struck out 10 batters and is the first Rangers pitcher to have at least four 10-strikeout games since Nolan Ryan in 1991. Opponents are hitting .197 off him, including .147 with runners in scoring position. He is 2-4 with a 3.68 ERA in in eight starts on the road. He has made two starts this year against National League teams and is 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Paulino would like to forget his last start ever happened. On Tuesday night, Paulino was done in by a seven-run fifth inning by the Royals. He lasted just 4 2/3 innings, while giving up 10 runs (eight earned) and 11 hits, as he picked up his eighth loss of the season. Paulino will look to start inching closer to .500 as he faces the Rangers in the finale of a three-game home series.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson went six innings in his last start against the Marlins and allowed two runs on two hits while walking a season-high six batters. He is 2-0 with a 3.50 ERA in his past three starts after going 1-2 with a 4.62 ERA in six starts in May. He is 1-2 with a 3.13 ERA in five starts on the road. He has held left-handed hitters to a .107 average while right-handers are hitting .250. He is 1-1 with a 5.00 ERA in ten relief appearances against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: As the Astros kick off a three-game home series against the Giants, they will send their ace to the mound in search of his sixth victory of the season. Coming off a stellar performance in which Oswalt tossed seven innings, allowing only two earned runs on six hits with one walk and a strikeout, the hard-throwing right-hander will look to pick up right we he left off. With his last victory against the Royals, Oswalt now has 142 career victories, just two shy of tying Joe Niekro's franchise record.
away_pitcher_note: With two off-days in five days, the Giants will be given the chance to skip a turn in their rotation, and although skipper Bruce Bochy didn't come out and say it Wednesday, he hinted the Giants would do just that. With the two off-days, Lincecum will already be pitching on one extra day's rest, so why hold back a two-time National League Cy Young Award winner? In his last start, Lincecum mixed his historical dominance (10 strikeouts) with his recent struggles (four walks, eight hits) in six innings of work, earning his seventh win of the season. He exited after six innings after being grazed on the back of his right shoulder by a ball hit by Miguel Tejada. Bochy said Lincecum would have left after the inning regardless, having thrown 111 pitches, and Lincecum expects nothing to come from the hit.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Myers was done in by one inning. The right-hander coasted through 6 2/3 innings before the Royals lit him up for a four-run seventh inning, thanks in part to a three-run home run from Scott Podsednik. Myers ended the day hurling 6 2/3 innings, allowing seven hits and four earned runs, with two walks and three strikeouts. Four of those seven hits came in the seventh inning. Myers will look to get back on track and climb back to .500 as he takes on the Giants at Minute Maid Park. In his career, Myers is 1-4 against the Giants with a 6.30 ERA in nine games.
away_pitcher_note: Despite taking only his third loss of the season, Zito was fantastic Friday night against the Blue Jays, throwing his first complete game of the season. If not for a first-pitch changeup to Alex Gonzalez that was belted for an eighth-inning solo home run, Zito may have come away with the win. What is worrisome for the left-hander is that six of the seven home runs he has allowed this season have come over his past five starts. Zito will look to continue his success against the Astros, whom he is 3-1 with a 3.69 ERA against over five career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez got roughed up in his last start against the Rangers, where he gave up six runs in just three innings. He was sailing along through the first two until Rangers pitcher Scott Feldman hit a double off him with one out. From there, walks and hits led to a long inning, which would be his last in a 9-3 loss. Rodriguez will look to end his three-game losing streak against the Giants, who beat him 3-0 on April 6 in his first start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Cain's four-start winning streak ended in his last outing, though he pitched well enough to win in a 6-5 loss at Toronto. Cain blanked the Blue Jays through seven innings in that game but yielded Aaron Hill's two-run homer in the eighth and was charged with another run before departing. Cain's overall ERA ranked fourth in the National League, and his 1.65 ERA since May 1 was second only to Florida's Josh Johnson's 1.17 among Major League pitchers. Cain enters this game having allowed only five home runs in 100 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis beat the Astros, 2-1, with his first Major League complete-game performance on Saturday. He allowed two hits, struck out nine and did not walk a batter. He has won three straight games and is 4-2 with a 2.34 ERA in his last six starts. He has made three starts against National League teams and is 3-0 with a 1.57 ERA against them. Opponents are hitting .187 off him, including .143 with runners in scoring position.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler certainly pitched well enough to earn a win last Saturday against the Rangers. He only gave up one hit over six innings. Yet that one hit was a two-run homer to Justin Smoak, which was the difference in a 5-1 loss. Moehler gave up only the two earned runs but walked four in the defeat. Despite the fact that starter Bud Norris is available to be activated from the disabled list, Moehler's performance earned him another start against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson started against the Astros on Sunday and allowed four runs, two earned, in seven innings in a game the Rangers won in 10 innings. He is now 2-0 with a 3.24 ERA in his last four starts and he is 0-1 with a 4.34 ERA in his three starts against National League teams. He has made eight starts at home and is 4-1 with a 3.71 ERA. He has held left-handed opponents to a .105 average while right-handers are hitting .250.
away_pitcher_note: Banks, a non-roster invitee to Spring Training who has spent the entire season at Round Rock, is 8-5 with a 2.97 ERA in 15 starts. In 97 innings, he's allowed 92 hits, 40 runs (32 earned), 24 walks and struck out 34 batters. He is 4-7 with a 5.38 ERA in 26 career Major League games with the Blue Jays and Padres.

home_pitcher_note: The Rangers have won all four starts since Hunter has returned from the Minor Leagues. He left a start against the Marlins on June 16 with a strained right hip flexor and pitched just 2 1/3 innings. But he came back and started on Tuesday against the Pirates, holding them to three runs in six innings in a 6-3 victory. He is now 3-0 with a 2.14 ERA in three starts at home. This is his first start against the Astros and he is 1-1 with a 3.07 ERA in three starts in his career against the National League.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt's third attempt to beat Giants ace Tim Lincecum on Tuesday went similar to his first two. He pitched well enough for a win but didn't receive enough runs to get the victory. Oswalt pitched his 13th quality start of the season and fourth consecutive start of seven or more innings. In June he has an ERA of 2.25.

home_pitcher_note: Despite four wild pitches, Parra effectively limited the Twins offense in his last start, giving up just two runs in 5 2/3 innings pitched, as the Brewers took the 5-3 victory over the Twins. Parra tied a club record with four wild pitches in a game, set by Ed Sprague on May 14, 1975, against the Rangers. But as catcher Jonathan Lucroy was quick to point out, Parra only allowed two runners to score following a wild pitch -- first baseman Justin Morneau and third baseman Michael Cuddyer in the fourth -- and stranded runners in scoring position in the second, fourth and sixth innings after he made those wild pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Norris will make his first start since May 23 for the Astros. He has been on the disabled list with bicep tendinitis and completed his final rehab start with Triple-A Round Rock on Tuesday. Norris had a 3.06 ERA with the Express over three starts. He will look for his first win since May 13.

home_pitcher_note: Through 5 1/3 innings on Thursday, Yovani Gallardo was perfect. After nine innings, the Brewers' ace had turned in the best pitching performance of his career. Over his past six starts, Gallardo has allowed six earned runs on 29 hits in 44 innings for a 1.23 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Myers became the first Astros pitcher to throw six or more innings in each of his first 15 starts of a season. Against the Giants he threw seven innings and gave up three runs, only one of which was earned. He also helped his cause with two hits and an RBI.

home_pitcher_note: For Bush, who was pitching on nine days' rest instead of his usual four, the key last time out was overcoming some early struggles that could be attributed to the long layoff. Once he had the lead, Bush faced just 10 batters over the final three innings of his outing.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez earned his first win since June 2 against the Giants. He pitched six innings and gave up two runs, none of which were earned. Rodriguez also gave up just two hits and had one walk in the Astros' 7-5 win. He has not faced the Brewers this season.

home_pitcher_note: Garland outpitched Josh Johnson of the Marlins in his last start, allowing one run in 6 2/3 innings. Garland allowed four hits with four strikeouts and at one point retired 14 consecutive hitters. He even drove in the go-ahead run with a sacrifice fly for his eighth victory.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler earned his first win of the season last Friday against the Rangers. He will remain in the rotation as the team's fifth starter as long as Feliple Paulino is on the disabled list.

home_pitcher_note: Latos walked four in his last start but was still sharp in his homecoming in Miami. The 22-year-old allowed one run on five hits with five strikeouts. He lowered his ERA to 2.85 and was in line to pick up his ninth victory before the bullpen allowed the tying run.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt's bid to impress the Rangers, who are interested in acquiring him, was unsuccessful. He threw only his third non-quality start of the season, giving up seven earned runs in a 10-1 loss on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Correia continued to struggle Monday against the Rockies, allowing six runs in five innings. He walked six batters and gave up a pair of two-run homers to Carols Gonzalez and Ryan Spilborghs. After a 4-1 April, Correia has won just one of his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Norris' first start since May 23 started out very shaky after he gave up four earned runs over his first three innings. Yet he settled down and held the Brewers scoreless over their next two to keep the Astros in the game, which they would eventually win, 9-5.

home_pitcher_note: LeBlanc took the loss Tuesday vs. the Rockies despite giving up just two hits in 6 1/3 innings. He allowed three earned runs -- two of them coming on a seventh-inning homer by Clint Barmes  given up by reliever Edward Mujica -- and tied his career high with eight K's.
away_pitcher_note: Myers gave up a career-high four home runs Tuesday against the Brewers in a 7-5 loss. He had given up just seven before that start. Despite giving up seven runs, Myers managed to pitch at least six innings for the 16th consecutive start.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez won his second consecutive start after losing six of his previous seven decisions. He pitched seven innings and gave up just one run. Rodriguez also executed a suicide squeeze to give the Astros a 2-1 lead over the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: It took Lincoln five starts, but he doesn't have to worry about getting that first big-league win any longer. And if Lincoln pitches with as nasty a curve as he did Wednesday, there are a lot more coming. The key for Lincoln is not to be hesitant to attack the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: Moehler was in line for his second consecutive win after allowing one run in 5 2/3 innings on Thursday in San Diego, but the Padres rallied against the Houston bullpen to send the game into extra innings.
away_pitcher_note: McCutchen gave up just one earned run in his last outing on Thursday against the Phillies. He got ahead of 12 of the 23 batters he faced, earning his first win of the season, his first since last Oct. 2.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt retired the first 11 batters he faced on Friday in San Diego en route to tossing seven scoreless innings, but his counterpart, Mat Latos, did Oswalt one better with eight shutout frames.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf recorded his first win of the season Friday by shutting down the Phillies for seven innings. The right-hander struck out eight and flashed command of his fastball that hadn't been seen all season. Ohlendorf has lost both starts of his career at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Norris had a solid second start after returning from the disabled list. He held the Padres scoreless through seven innings and gave up three hits, not factoring in the decision. Norris always is at his best against the Cardinals in his career, going 4-0 with a 0.35 ERA
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright made it clear on Sunday that his All-Star selection was well deserved. Now he makes his last start of the first half in the opener of a division series at a tough ballpark. He's 2-0 with a 2.59 ERA for his career in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Myers returned to form Saturday against the Padres, keeping his streak of pitching six innings or more  intact. He gave up just four hits and two runs. Although he left in line for the loss, the Astros rallied before eventually falling to the Padres, 3-2.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan has shown some progress, but it appears that for now he's been bumped down to No. 5 in the rotation, with Blake Hawksworth now the fourth man. Minute Maid Park has been a rough place for him in the regular season -- he has a 5.87 ERA in seven career games there.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez won his third consecutive start overall Tuesday against the Pirates. He went seven innings and gave up just one run on four hits. Rodriguez also had 10 strikeouts and has a 0.90 ERA over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hawksworth keeps meeting challenges, so he keeps getting chances. He held his own on a tough night at Coors Field. Now he gets to try his luck at Minute Maid Park. If he keeps getting ahead with his fastball, it will allow him to keep finishing hitters off with his changeup.

home_pitcher_note: Duke will look to get back on track after a rocky stretch of outings and a visit to the disabled list while nursing a muscle strain in his pitching elbow. After two effective rehab outings, Duke will make his first start in a month.
away_pitcher_note: Myers had one of the most consistent first halves in baseball, pitching at least six innings in all 18 of his starts. He closed off the first half with a dominating eight-inning win against the Cardinals in which he gave up just five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf has quietly been a very effective pitcher over the last three starts, and doing his work without much offensive support. He's only allowed two earned runs in his past 20 innings (0.90 ERA), but the Pirates have scored only four runs in those three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris closed the first half by losing to the Cardinals but he was still impressive in the  outing. His only major mistake was giving up a three-run homer to Matt Holliday. He retired 18 of 19 Cardinals hitters during that start.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm deserved a better fate after a fine outing in his last start before the All-Star break. Maholm held the Brewers in check before a rare bullpen lapse led to a 5-4 extra-inning loss.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt threw a one-hit shutout in his last start in front of a number of scouts. The win put him one win behind Joe Niekro for the most wins in Astros history. Oswalt said he feels the best he has in his entire career.

home_pitcher_note: Silva's last start ended after 1 1/3 innings when he was ejected by umpire Brian Runge for arguing a close play at first. Silva had some soreness in right calf but has had plenty of rest.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez lost his first game in three starts, but he still pitched good enough to earn the win his last time out. He gave up three runs, all on a homer by Cardinals left fielder Matt Holiday in a 4-2 loss. He has regained his 2009 form after a tough start to the season.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster opened the second half on strong note, striking out nine Phillies. He's now five Ks away from reaching 1,500 in his career. But he's also served up 17 home runs; he gave up 22 in 200 innings last year.
away_pitcher_note: Wright will make the first start of his Major League career after Felipe Paulino suffered a recurrence of right shoulder tendinitis during his side session Friday. The 25-year-old has made six relief appearances for the Astros this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly rebounded from two bad starts to strike out 10 Phillies over seven innings in his last outing. He made some mechanical tweaks and they worked. His starts are being watched by teams looking for help.
away_pitcher_note: Myers is one of 53 pitchers since 1920 to begin a season with 19 straight starts of six-plus innings. Dan Haren did the same last year, and Myers can be the first to make it 20 in a row to start a season since Pedro Martinez and Mark Buehrle in 2005.

home_pitcher_note: Norris' 4 2/3-inning outing Saturday was his lowest since going 4 1/3 frames in a loss to the Dodgers on May 18. He got little help from his defense, giving up three unearned runs in the first. Just four of the seven runs he allowed against the Pirates were earned.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie Wood has made the most of his opportunities, yet can't get a win. After nearly throwing a perfect game in a Reds loss at Philadelphia, Wood gave up one run Sunday against the Rockies. However, for the second time in a row, the Reds lost his start, 1-0.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt lasted just four innings in his last start after suffering a left ankle contusion when he was hit by a Pedro Alvarez line drive in the second inning. Oswalt stayed in the game but had to adjust his mechanics and didn't come out for the fifth.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto continues to rack up strong starts and give the Reds chances to win. He's hasn't allowed more than two runs in a game since June 12, a span of six starts after hitting a rough patch at the beginning of June. He's lost just one start since April 24.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez struggled in his outing against the Cubs, but the Houston offense helped him earn the win anyway. The Astros gave him five runs in the first inning and he held on, giving up five runs in six innings. Rodriguez is looking for his fifth win in six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Leake has no-decisions in 10 of his 18 starts. Although he's lost just once, wins have been hard to come by. The bad luck nearly continued Thursday, as the bullpen almost blew an 8-1 lead after a lengthy rain delay cut Leake's outing short at five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wright's performance last Tuesday against the Cubs was enough for him to earn another start. In his first career start, Wright gave up five runs but they were all unearned after an error in the fifth derailed his four scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Silva failed to get past the first inning in his last start, the second straight game in which he's not gone beyond two innings. He is being given an extra day to work on the side with pitching coach Larry Rothschild.

home_pitcher_note: Myers pitched his 20th consecutive start of six or more innings last Wednesday against the Cubs. He gave up one run over seven innings and had eight strikeouts in a no-decision. Myers will look to extend his streak of quality starts to five games.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly just faced the Astros in his last start and will try to have similar results. He held them to one run over 7 1/3 innings while striking out six. He's been hot topic at trade deadline.

home_pitcher_note: Norris didn't factor in the decision his last start against the Reds, giving up four runs over six innings. This season he has held opposing team's leadoff hitters to a .131 average which is the lowest among MLB starters.
away_pitcher_note: Wells has turned things around in July. In his last four starts, he's given up four earned runs over 28 2/3 innings for a 1.26 ERA. He's thrown more than six innings in his last seven outings.

home_pitcher_note: Happ was acquired by the Astros on Thursday in the deal that sent ace Roy Oswalt to the Phillies. The left-hander was limited to three starts this season due to injury.
away_pitcher_note: With Jonathan Lucroy back behind the plate in place of George Kottaras on Saturday, Parra had his best start of the season, allowing just two runs on four hits and three walks over six innings for his third quality start of the season and first since June 18 in Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez had another quality start last Sunday against the Reds, giving up no runs in a win. He's gone 5-1 with a 2.30 ERA over his past six starts after starting the season 3-10 with a 6.09 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a rough outing against the Pirates, in which he surrendered 10 first-inning runs, Bush tossed six-plus strong innings Sunday against the Nationals, giving up just two earned runs on six hits. Bush recorded seven strikeouts vs. zero walks.

home_pitcher_note: Wright said he improved from his first career start to his second on Monday against the Cubs. He gave up four runs over his first three innings, but settled down to toss two scoreless frames before he exited.
away_pitcher_note: Wolf recovered from one of the worst starts of his career -- a 12-run stinker at Pittsburgh on July 21 -- with a gem against the Reds thanks in part to good curveball command. He pitched seven shutout innings against Houston on May 25.

home_pitcher_note: Westbrook makes his Cardinals debut against a depleted foe at friendly Busch Stadium, so expectations should be high. St. Louis has long coveted the sinkerballer, and the switch to the National League may benefit him quite a bit.
away_pitcher_note: Myers threw his first complete game of 2010 on Wednesday in a 6-1 win over the Cubs. He gave up just four hits and had 12 strikeouts for his seventh career complete game. Myers has started the year with 21 straight starts of six innings or more.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia once again gets an extra day of rest as the Cardinals try to protect him in his first full Major League season. He's actually been a touch less effective on long rest than on regular rest, however. Garcia has a 1.46 ERA at home in 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Norris earned his first win since May 13 on Wednesday in a win over the Cubs. He gave up no earned runs over six innings and had seven strikeouts. Norris will face a Cardinals team that beat him for the first time the last time he faced it.

home_pitcher_note: Carpenter will be looking to keep up his divisional dominance. Since the start of 2009, he's 11-0 in with a 1.58 ERA in 15 starts against NL Central foes. He's allowed five earned runs in 31 innings over four starts since the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Happ's debut with the Astros couldn't have gone better as he didn't allow a run over six innings for his first win since April 9. He overcame an early first-inning jam en route to the win. He'll look to keep it going against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Bush's roller-coaster ride continued in Houston last week when he allowed two runs in the first inning, three more in the second and allowed six runs on 10 hits in all during a five-inning stint. The 10 hits matched his season high.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez improved to 6-1 in his last seven starts by throwing eight scoreless innings vs. the Brewers. He had nine strikeouts to just one walk. Rodriguez hasn't allowed a run in his last 14 innings and will go for his 10th win of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Though he could have been pushed back to Tuesday with the off-day this week, Wolf is expected to make his start Saturday, just five days after taking a sharp line drive by Hunter Pence off his left wrist. Wolf said Wednesday he was, "Ready to go."
away_pitcher_note: Myers stretched his streak of throwing six or more innings to 22 starts Monday vs. the Cardinals. He didn't factor in the decision in a 9-4 win. Myers gave up two earned runs on just three hits against the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo matched his career high with 12 strikeouts in his last start and might have worked more than his six innings and 95 pitches had the Brewers not owned a 13-1 lead. He's 6-2 with a 2.72 ERA in eight career starts against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Wright is coming off his best start to date in win over the Brewers, giving up just two runs over a season-high seven innings. Wright has improved each start since being converted from a long reliever and is hoping for similar results.

home_pitcher_note: Benefiting from an Astros offensive outburst, Norris pitched well enough to win last time out, tossing six innings while giving up four runs on seven hits and one walk with six strikeouts. Norris is 0-1 with a 13.50 ERA in one start against Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Minor, the seventh overall selection in the 2009 Draft, will be make his Major League debut and attempt to capably fill the rotation spot vacated by the injured Kris Medlen. He went 4-1 with a 1.89 ERA in six starts with Triple-A Gwinnett.

away_pitcher_note: Santana is coming off back-to-back wins, as he blanked the Rox after throwing 7 1/3 scoreless innings in his previous start vs. Philly. As predicted by Jerry Manuel, he seems to gain arm strength as he moves further away from his offseason surgery.

away_pitcher_note: Zambrano is 7-0 with a 1.27 ERA and 55 strikeouts in his last 10 starts. He's held opponents to a .187 average in that stretch. His mother showed up for his last start in San Diego, finally getting a visa from Venezuela. She'll be in Houston, too.

home_pitcher_note: The Pirates are likely to have Burres spot start for Jeff Karstens again. In his first start of the year for Pittsburgh, Burres kept the Cubs to one run in 5 1/3 innings. His Achilles' heel all year has been serving up homers.
away_pitcher_note: Happ has pitched very well since his return to the Major Leagues, going 1-1 with a 0.69 ERA in 13 innings. He threw seven scoreless innings on Wednesday against the Pirates in what was his strongest outing of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Milone, making his Major League debut, hit a home run on the first pitch in his first at-bat in an 8-7 victory over the Mets on Saturday night. He gave up four runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings, receiving a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Norris is 1-2 with a 5.24 ERA in his past six starts, allowing 34 hits and striking out 36 batters in 34 1/3 innings in that span. He allowed nine hits and six runs (five earned) in his most recent outing Saturday vs. the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, Lannan lasted 5 1/3 innings and allowing a run on eight hits. He struck out four and walked two. Los Angeles' only run off Lannan came in the first, when Jamey Carroll touched home plate on a double by Matt Kemp.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez delivered a quality start for the Astros in his previous start Sunday against Milwaukee, but he suffered his 10th loss. He ranks second on the Astros' career charts for innings pitched by a left-hander with 1,151.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg pitched five shutout innings and allowed two hits before leaving the game with a 3-0 lead over the Dodgers, who would later rally off  Washington's bullpen for a 7-3 victory.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing four earned runs in each of his first three Major League starts, Sosa has responded by going 2-1 with a 2.00 ERA in his next three. He was acquired by the Astros in a July 19 trade with the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Myers will try for a second straight victory after ending a 13-start dry spell. He hasn't pitched badly, but Myers hasn't gotten much run support or luck.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt returns to Houston for the first time since the Astros traded him to Philadelphia in July 2010. He is 2-1 with a 3.33 ERA in his past four starts as he looks to get into a groove to hit the postseason throwing as well as possible.

home_pitcher_note: Happ has pitched better lately after losing four in a row. He's given the Astros good outings in his last three starts but will be tested against his former team.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels seems to be just fine after missing a couple starts last month because of inflammation in his left shoulder. In fact, Hamels is 1-0 with a 2.45 ERA in three starts since his return, allowing six runs and striking out 16 in 22 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Norris threw seven solid innings versus the Nationals last Friday but came away with a no-decision. He's won just once in his last 11 starts, but hasn't gotten much run support.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay seems to be in a three-man race for the NL Cy Young Award with Cliff Lee and Clayton Kershaw. Halladay threw eight strong innings Friday in a victory over Milwaukee, allowing four hits, one run and three walks and striking out nine.

home_pitcher_note: Garza did not get a decision in his last outing, but what else is new? He's now left seven starts with a lead but not factored in the decision. It'll be good for him to be back at Wrigley, where he has a 2.64 ERA, which ranks among NL leaders.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez continues in his quest to finish with a winning record for the third time in four years when he faces the Cubs at Wrigley Field. Rodriguez has allowed three earned runs in each of his last three starts, going 2-1.

home_pitcher_note: Lopez served up four home runs in his last start against the Reds, yet still got the win. He's failed to go past the sixth inning in his last eight starts. Says Mike Quade: "He's the fifth starter and gives us everything he's got."
away_pitcher_note: Sosa, acquired in the July 19 trade that sent Jeff Keppinger to the Giants, will try to break a two-game losing streak in only his eighth Major League start. He gave up a career-high five earned runs Sunday at Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Dempster threw 128 pitches in his last start, the third highest total in his career. He didn't get the win and is 0-4 in his last six starts. He'll get a chance at 200 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Myers has been terrific lately, going 2-1 with a 1.19 ERA in his last three starts. He's allowed just one earned run in each of those starts, including Monday against the Phillies when he allowed one run in eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wood was a late addition to step in for Dontrelle Willis, who was scratched from a second day running because of back spasms. Wood has pitched twice in relief since rejoining the Reds earlier this month, and has pitched 3 1/3 innings of no-hit ball.
away_pitcher_note: Since returning from a short stint at Triple-A Oklahoma City, Happ has righted the ship. He's 2-1 with a 2.25 ERA in four starts, allowing 16 hits in 24 innings. He beat the Phillies Tuesday, allowing one run in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: A blown save cost him a career-high ninth win on Thursday vs. the Cubs, but Bailey had a fine outing after a rocky beginning. He gave up a pair of two-run homers in the first inning to fall behind, 4-0, but retired 12 of his final 13 batters.
away_pitcher_note: Norris has won once in his previous 12 starts despite posting a good 4.04 ERA. He's 1-4 in 12 starts since July 16 and has six quality starts in that span. He's allowed three earned runs in 14 innings in last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Currently with a club record of 44 home runs allowed, Arroyo is four away from Jose Lima's NL record and six away from Bert Blyleven's Major League record of 50. Arroyo struggled with his command in his four-homer game vs. the Brewers on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has held opponents to three runs in each of his last four starts, going 2-1 with a 4.38 ERA in those games. His 73 wins rank third on the Astros' all-time list by southpaws, trailing Bob Knepper and Mike Hampton.

home_pitcher_note: Sosa has lost his Past three starts despite posting two quality starts in that span. Sosa, making his ninth Major League start, has given the Astros five quality starts in his Past six, going 2-3 with a 3.71 ERA during span.
away_pitcher_note: White has struggled to keep the ball in the yard since joining the Rockies' rotation in August. The right-hander has surrendered 11 home runs in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Myers has been terrific in his Past four starts, going 3-0 with a 1.19 ERA. He's allowed 19 hits in that span and struck out 22 batters, but most importantly is the fact he's allowed only one home run in 30 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The key component in the Ubaldo Jimenez trade has shown promise in his first two Major League starts, surrendering two runs over 10 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Happ has pitched well since he was forced to go to the Minor Leagues in August and work out some kinks. In his five starts since returning from Triple-A Oklahoma City, he's 2-1 with a 2.40 ERA. He hasn't faced Colorado this year.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel earned one final start after surrendering just one run over seven innings during a start against the D-backs on Sept. 6.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell will take the spot of Bud Norris, who has been shut down for the season with biceps tendinitis. Harrell tossed 5 1/3 scoreless innings on Sept. 2 against the Brewers, but he didn't get a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Kevin Millwood will fill in for Jhoulys Chacin in the finale against the Astros. It is the ninth start of the year for Millwood, who was roughed up in his last outing on Sept. 19, giving up seven runs in just 3 1/3 innings against the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez makes his final start of the season with a chance to finish with a winning record for the third time in his career. He was 9-7 in 2008 and 14-12 in 2009 before going 11-12 last year. He beat the Cards on July 28.
away_pitcher_note: After a rocky August, Garcia has come on very strong in September, allowing fewer than two earned runs in three of four starts. His troubles on the road are well known, but he's been solid in his last three away starts.

home_pitcher_note: Sosa won for the first time since Aug. 30 by holding the Rockies to three runs and scattering nine hits in 6 1/3 innings on Thursday in his ninth Major League start. He has delivered a quality start in five of his last six outings.
away_pitcher_note: Walks have begun to plague Westbrook again. He tamed the issue at midseason, but lately he's handing out too many free passes. Westbrook has walked four or more in four of his past nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is finishing the season with a flourish. He improved to 4-0 with a 1.24 ERA in his last five starts when he held the Rockies to four hits and one run on Friday. Myers has allowed only one home run in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter is finishing the year strong, even though he's not getting much run support. Over his past eight games, Carpenter has 48 strikeouts and 11 walks. Yet the Cardinals are 3-5 in those games.

summary: 2012-03-31 - New York Yankees @ Houston Astros (Completed Early: Rain)
2012-04-04 - Chicago White Sox @ Houston Astros (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: Wandy Rodriguez makes his first Opening Day start. Rodriguez went 11-11 with a 3.49 ERA in 30 starts last year. He's the first left-handed Opening Day starter in 38 years.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander is making his third Opening Day start in four years and is 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA in openers. Guthrie was 0-1 with a 4.79 ERA in Spring Training. A career American Leaguer before now, Guthrie has never pitched at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell was ruled out of contention for the rotation in mid-March, but pitched his way back into the mix. Claimed off waivers by the Astros last year, Harrell went 0-2 with a 3.46 ERA in six games (two starts) for Houston.
away_pitcher_note: The 49-year-old Moyer made an inspiring comeback from elbow surgery in 2010 while he was with the Phillies. Moyer signed a Minor League contract during the winter and went 2-1 with a 2.50 ERA in Cactus League action. His arm and body were fine.

home_pitcher_note: Norris is beginning his third full season in the Major Leagues and is eager to establish himself. He was inconsistent last year with the Astros, going 6-11 with a 3.77 ERA in 31 starts with 176 strikeouts in 186 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio, 25, was going through the normal rookie highs and lows before the Nationals' Ian Desmond hit a line drive off Nicasio's head that resulted in a broken neck. Nicasio won a job and became a heartwarming story with a fine spring performance.

home_pitcher_note: Happ is trying to re-establish himself after a difficult 2011 season. Happ was 4-14 with a 6.26 ERA in his first 22 starts last year and was sent to the Minors. He came back and went 2-1 with a 2.43 ERA in last six outings.
away_pitcher_note: Beachy will attempt to avoid the high early pitch counts that limited him to fewer than seven innings in 23 of his 25 starts last year. His 169 strikeouts last year were the most by a Braves rookie in the modern era.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired by the Astros in December in a trade with the Red Sox, Weiland won a spot in the rotation with a good spring. He pitched in some big games for Boston last year, going 0-3 with a 7.66 ERA in seven games (five starts).
away_pitcher_note: Hanson exited his Opening Day start feeling good about his shoulder in an effort marred only by a run surrendered in the sixth inning. He is 3-0 with a 0.97 ERA in five career starts against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: After a good run through the starting rotation to start the year, ace Wandy Rodriguez makes his second start in the series finale against the Braves. He didn't allow an earned run in 6 1/3 innings on Opening Day vs. Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado posted a 2.83 ERA while primarily using a fastball and changeup during his first seven starts last year. He has been working on gaining more confidence with a curveball that he showed more frequently in the Minors.

home_pitcher_note: An impressive eight-inning performance at Cincinnati moved Nolasco within three wins of matching Dontrelle Willis' franchise mark of 68. Nolasco is 65-51 all-time. He struck out five and didn't issue a walk at the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell pitched seven scoreless innings against the Rockies in his season debut Saturday, allowing three hits and striking out four. That was the first time in his career he went seven innings, and he's never faced Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Perhaps it was a case of nerves or an adrenaline rush, but Zambrano got off to a slow start in his Marlins debut, giving up three runs in the first at Cincinnati. He settled, fanning six in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Norris had a quality start in his first outing of the season Sunday against Colorado, giving up four hits and two runs in seven innings while striking out eight. He's 1-1 with a 6.65 ERA in four starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Splendid in his first start of the season, Sanchez looks to build on his 6 1/3-inning outing in Philadelphia. His command was sharp in his 95-pitch, 64-strike performance. He has responded from spring shoulder soreness.
away_pitcher_note: Happ threw six innings and got the win with a quality starts in his first outing of the season while beating the Braves on Monday. He's 2-2 with a 4.79 ERA in eight career games against the Marlins, including five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Last Wednesday against the Mets, Strasburg pitched six shutout innings, allowed two hits, struck out nine batters and walked three. He also threw a career-high 108 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Weiland, acquired from the Red Sox along with Jed Lowrie in a winter trade, was rocked for eight hits and four runs in five innings in his first start with Houston on Tuesday against Atlanta. He has never faced Washington.

home_pitcher_note: This past Thursday, Gonzalez started the game for the Nationals and showed why they traded four prospects to the A's to acquire his services last December. He was outstanding, pitching seven superb innings, allowing two hits and not walking a batter.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez held the Rockies to no earned runs in 6 1/3 innings on Opening Day, and gave up three earned runs in five innings Wednesday against Atlanta. The Astros have committed four errors in each of his two starts.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday, Zimmermann had another superb outing, pitching seven innings and allowing one run on three hits in a no-decision vs. the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell fell behind in the count too much in his most recent start Friday in Miami, allowing seven hits and four runs in four innings. He was terrific in his first start of the season in which he threw seven scoreless frames.

home_pitcher_note: On Saturday, Jackson gave the bullpen the rest it needed by tossing a complete game -- his first of 2012 and fifth of his career -- in his home debut, allowing one run on two hits. He fanned nine and walked one, with 67 of his 92 pitches strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Norris has delivered quality games in both of his starts this year, allowing six hits and four runs (three earned) in six innings Saturday against the Marlins. He's 1-0 with a 2.63 ERA in two career starts against Washington.

home_pitcher_note: Happ is off to a great start this season, giving the Astros a pair of quality starts in two outings. He's struck out 13 batters and walked only five in his 12 innings of work this year. His control was a problem last year.
away_pitcher_note: After starting the season on the DL with a strained neck, Lilly returned with seven strong innings in his 2012 debut. The lefty is 7-3 with a 2.64 ERA in 15 career starts vs. Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Weiland, who was beaten by Stephen Strasburg in his previous start, gets another tough assignment in facing Clayton Kershaw. Weiland has allowed 18 hits in 10 2/3 innings as he searches for his first win in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: The reigning NL Cy Young winner struggled a bit on Sunday, allowing three earned runs in 5 1/3 innings -- his shortest start at Dodger Stadium since last May. He has allowed just four earned runs in his three starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: It's been a tough-luck start to the season for Rodriguez, who has given the Astros two quality starts in three outings and is 0-2 with a 1.96 ERA. Rodriguez allowed five hits and one run in seven innings Tuesday vs. the Nats.
away_pitcher_note: Chad Billingsley had a rocky second inning in Milwaukee but finished a quality start by retiring the last 11 batters he faced. Billingsley is more successful challenging hitters this year after ironing out some mechanical flaws.

home_pitcher_note: The streak goes on the line again. The Brewers have won all 19 of Greinke's starts at Miller Park, including two games in last year's postseason. Greinke is 13-0 in those games, including 12-0 in regular-season starts.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell has delivered with two quality starts in three outings this year and has allowed 14 hits in 17 2/3 innings. He's looking for his first win since holding the Rockies to no runs in seven innings on April 7 in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf's loss against the Dodgers on Thursday counted as progress. Six days after allowing eight runs in 4 1/3 innings in Atlanta, he limited the damage to four runs in a season-high six innings at home.
away_pitcher_note: Norris had quality starts in his first two outings, but didn't have any wins to show for them. He got plenty of run support and picked up his first win of the season Thursday in Washington, giving up four runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum is 2-0 with a 1.80 ERA in three starts against Houston, all of them last season, including a pair of scoreless seven-inning outings.
away_pitcher_note: Happ is the only Astros starter to have given his club a quality start in his first three outings of the season. He's pitched six innings three times, allowing three earned runs twice and two earned once to start 2-0.

home_pitcher_note: Leake suffered one bad inning in his last outing against the Cubs, giving up four runs in the second to remain winless on the season. Leake is 2-3 with a 4.45 ERA in seven games (five starts) against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has been terrific this season, posting a 0.64 ERA in his last two starts. Since 2009 his 3.28 ERA ranks second among NL left-handed starters. behind Clayton Kershaw (2.60) and ahead of Cole Hamels (3.35).

home_pitcher_note: Cueto earned his second win of the season his last time out against the Cubs, allowing two runs (one earned) and striking out seven in 6 1/3 innings. The righty is 1-5 with a 4.01 ERA in 10 career starts against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: It's been hit-or-miss season thus far for Harrell, who hasn't won since throwing seven scoreless innings against the Rockies on the second day of the season. The Brewers got him for five runs in five innings on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Latos earned his first win as a Red on Tuesday with seven scoreless innings vs. the Giants and had his best outing of the young season. His fastball was in the mid-90s and he mixed in good off-speed deliveries.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles was recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City after going 4-0 with a 3.46 ERA in four starts. Lyles struck out 24 batters in 26 innings pitched with just 4 walks. He went 2-8 with a 5.36 ERA in 20 appearances for Houston last year.

home_pitcher_note: Norris is coming off his poorest outing, giving up nine hits, seven runs and three home runs on Tuesday in Milwaukee. After two quality starts to start the season, he's allowed 11 runs in 13 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Closed roofs are typically good for knuckleballers; humidity is even better. Dickey should enjoy one or the other in Houston after battling chilly or damp conditions in his first three starts. He was 0-2 vs. the Astros last season.

home_pitcher_note: Happ is the only Astros starter to have given his club a quality start in his first three outings of the season. He's pitched six innings three times, allowing three earned runs twice and two earned once to start 2-0.
away_pitcher_note: Niese was sharp yet again in his fourth start of the season and has now submitted four consecutive quality starts to open the year. The lefty lost his only start last year against the Astros, in large part because he walked five in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez was in control for six innings on Friday in Cincinnati, allowing just two runs on six hits. He walked two and fanned two. Rodriguez retired seven straight batters in one stretch, four via strikeout.
away_pitcher_note: Schwinden was in line to win his first start before allowing a record-setting inning, serving up a three-run home run and six total runs last Friday at Coors Field. Regardless, the Mets are giving Schwinden some rope in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell allowed six runs, five earned, and nine hits in six innings on Saturday. He walked one and struck out one over 86 pitches. A two-run double and a two-run home run by Jay Bruce spelled doom for Harrell.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse allowed as many runs in his last outing (three) as he had in his first four, but he still managed to become the National League's second four-game winner. Lohse had walked just two in 27 1/3 innings before issuing four free passes on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Norris will face the team he's had the most success against. He's 6-2 in his first three years in the Majors vs. the Cardinals. Norris was sharp for six innings in his last outing on April 30 against the Mets before faltering in the seventh.
away_pitcher_note: In a seven-inning start Sunday, Garcia allowed three runs, all immediately after he had a baserunning gaffe of his own. He also struck out a season-high six. Garcia has pitched at least seven innings in three of his five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Happ, who struggled last season with the Astros before being sent down to the Minors, has had four quality starts in his last five outings. The Astros are 3-2 in games started by Happ this season. Happ has 31 strikeouts in 29 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wainwright won his last start, even though he did surrender two more homers. He's now given up seven, nearly half as many as he allowed in 33 starts in 2010. He continues to search for consistent command, though his last two starts have been better.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is the ace of the Houston staff and has pitched like one of late, going 3-0 in his last three starts. The Astros are maximizing the lefty's use by starting him every fifth day, even when it means skipping another starter.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano has a string of four straight quality starts, and he has yet to log a win. Big Z has been in a tough-luck situation. In San Francisco in his last outing, he threw seven shutout innings. He faced Houston on April 14, a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Rodriguez's first big league appearance this year. Rodriguez, who went 1-6 with a 5.27 ERA in 43 games (eight starts) for the Astros in '11, was 1-3 with a 4.97 ERA at Triple-A. He's replacing Kyle Weiland.
away_pitcher_note: The last three starts have been impressive, as Sanchez has given up five earned runs in 21 innings. He has 38 strikeouts in 33 1/3 innings on the year and limited San Francisco to one run in seven innings in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell won for the first time in five starts on Friday, holding the Cardinals to three earned runs in 5 1/3 innings. He hasn't pitched as well as he did on April 7 when he threw seven scoreless innings against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson had a rough time in his last start, giving up six runs in the third inning in San Diego in a no-decision. He struck out one and was unable to hold a five-run lead. JJ still seeks his first win since April 19, 2011.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald turned a corner by perfectly adopting the approach the Bucs want all their pitchers to follow: Get quick outs if possible but, once you get two strikes on a batter, try to finish him off. He's finished off 25 in his last 21 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris will be making his seventh start of the season, and first against the Pirates. He's 4-4 in eight starts against the Pirates. Norris didn't allow an earned run in six innings in his last start Saturday vs. the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Morton spent time between starts trying to re-discover the hard sinker that has right-handed hitters pounding the ball into the ground, rather than hitting it out of the park. Has already allowed four homers to them, compared to one all last year.
away_pitcher_note: Happ allowed four walks and two homers, tying his season highs in both categories, in his previous start Sunday vs. the Cardinals. He's delivered quality starts for the Astros in four of his six starts (team is 3-3).

home_pitcher_note: The current king of misleading stats. Remove the 2 2/3-inning (12 earned runs) start in St. Louis, and Burnett's ERA is 1.71 for three other starts. Last time out, had his best curve in a while and relied on it almost exclusively, fanning 10 Nats.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is coming off his worst outing of the season stat-wise, but he still didn't pitch poorly. Rodriguez was the first Astros starter to work into the ninth, but he was done in by three homers Monday against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton, who can be a free agent at the end of the season, has shown signs of turning himself around after going 1-3 with a 4.34 earned run average in his first four appearances. In his last three starts he's 2-1 with a 2.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell has lasted just 5 1/3 innings in his previous two starts but is 1-0 in that span. He got a no-decision last time out after holding the Marlins to six hits and two earned runs. The team is 2-5 in his seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lee is still looking for his first win of the season despite a 2.17 earned run average and a .192 opponent's batting average. The Phillies, 0-4 when he starts, have scored two or fewer runs in three of his four games.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Lyles' second start of the season. He was recalled and started on April 29 at Cincinnati, allowing three runs in 6.0 innings of work in a 6-5 loss to the Reds (had no decision). He was optioned back to Triple A after that game.

home_pitcher_note: Norris struck out eight in six innings of work in a 1-0 win at Pittsburgh. Norris escaped a bases loaded jam in the sixth inning to record his third win of the year. Norris has allowed just three runs over 18 2/3 innings in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: With everything that happened after he left the game, Wolf's strong start got a bit lost in the shuffle on Friday night. Despite walking three batters, Wolf delivered his best outing of the season, with six scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Happ allowed five runs on six hits over six innings in a 5-2 loss at Pittsburgh. Happ settled down after a rough first frame and retired 13-of 15 batters but struggled in the fifth and allowed two runners to open the sixth to end his day prematurely.
away_pitcher_note: Retiring 16 of the last 18 hitters he faced, Marcum tossed seven innings in his last start, allowing one run on three hits, along with two walks and six strikeouts. He lowered his ERA to 3.07, best among Brewers starters.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez, coming off his best outing of the season Sunday in Pittsburgh, is among the NL leaders in ERA at 1.99. His 3.25 ERA in his 103 starts since the 2009 season ranks second among NL left-handed starters.
away_pitcher_note: Feliz threw six innings, allowing four hits and two runs in a win over the Angels on Sunday. He's 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA and 13 strikeouts in his last two starts and 1-1 with a 4.13 ERA on the road. Feliz is 0-1 in six career appearances vs. Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell's two victories this season came at Minute Maid Park. His three-highest strike totals came in his three starts at home. He hasn't pitched into the seventh inning since his first start of the season -- at home.
away_pitcher_note: Holland skipped his last start after Thursday's doubleheader in Baltimore. He threw a scoreless ninth inning against the Royals on Monday night and allowed three unearned runs in six innings of a 7-3 win over the Orioles on May 10.

home_pitcher_note: After being called up from Triple-A Oklahoma City on Tuesday, Lyles gave up one run in six innings in Philadelphia. He has given up three home runs in 12 innings this season after yielding 14 homers in 94 innings last season.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis has lost each of his last three starts, allowing seven runs, five of them unearned, in 5 2/3 innings of a 7-4 loss to the Royals on Tuesday night. He is 2-1, with a 1.97 ERA in his career against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Norris threw 117 pitches in his last start, an 8-3 victory against the Brewers. He went seven innings, striking out nine and giving up one run. He has a 0.47 ERA in his last three starts with 21 strikeouts and six walks.
away_pitcher_note: Garza felt much better in his last outing, which was his second since being sidelined with the flu. He gave up two runs on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings against the Phillies. He's slowly building up strength after losing 12 pounds while sick.

home_pitcher_note: Happ had his best outing of the season in his last start, going six shutout innings in a win against the Brewers. Hitters batting third in the lineup against Happ this season have a .579 batting average with a 1.772 OPS.
away_pitcher_note: Wood takes over for Chris Volstad, who was optioned to Triple-A Iowa. In his last start for Iowa, Wood gave up two runs on five hits over seven innings and improved to 3-3 with a 4.57 ERA. He also started May 6 for the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Against the Rangers on Friday, Rodriguez gave up a season-high 10 hits. Rodriguez, who has a 2.24 ERA, has pitched through the sixth inning in all but one of his outings. The Astros are just 3-6 in Rodriguez's starts.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija struck out eight over 7 1/3 innings in his last start against the White Sox, but two of the six hits off him were home runs. He will miss Wrigley Field, where he has a 1.52 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw tossed a six-hit shutout against the Cardinals on Saturday, using his slow curveball early in counts. Kershaw has been downright un-hittable at home, where he has a 1.41 ERA in his last 18 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell hasn't made it out of the sixth inning in any of his past four starts. He induced 15 swinging strikes in his last start, a season high. He's gotten more ground-ball outs than fly-ball outs in eight of his nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Against St. Louis, the right-hander showed improvement over a pair of starts in which he lasted just four innings in each. He allowed three earned runs in six innings on Sunday, but still struggled keeping runners off the basepaths.
