away_pitcher_note: Galarraga struggled in his last two outings, walking 13 total batters. The 30-year-old has pitched into the sixth inning in all three of his starts with the Astros, but hasn't been able to get out of the inning.

away_pitcher_note: Harrell, who leads the National League in innings by a rookie, has been the Astros' most reliable starter this season. He's given up two or fewer runs in each of his last six starts, going 2-2 over that span.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles is beginning to gain some consistency and stay away from the big inning. In his last two starts, he's allowed just 11 hits and struck out 11 in 14 innings. He hasn't won since June 26, a span of eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin is in his third stint with the D-backs this year. In three starts since his last recall, he is 2-0 with a 1.89 ERA. Last time out against the Nationals, Corbin allowed just two runs on four hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga finally got the walks under control in his most recent start, on Monday against the Cubs, but he was burned by a pair of two-run homers. He's yet to pitch deeper than 5 1/3 innings in four starts with Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy has struggled to find consistency this year after winning 21 games in 2011. After winning four straight starts and compiling a 2.54 ERA, Kennedy pitched poorly in his next two starts. He has allowed an NL high 23 homers.

away_pitcher_note: Harrell has been the Astros' most consistent pitcher in recent weeks. He is 3-2 with a 2.06 ERA in his last seven starts. He ranks first in the National League and second in the Majors in innings by a rookie.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse has turned in quality starts in 13 of his last 14 outings, and has allowed more than three earned runs in a start just three times this season. He blanked Arizona over 6 2/3 in his last start, and gave up one run over his last three outings.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander has struggled in the second half of the season. He gave up six earned runs in 3 1/3 innings in his last start against the Cubs. He hasn't earned a winning decision since May 21, when he was 5-1.

home_pitcher_note: A passed ball and a wild pitch brought in two runs in Westbrook's last start -- a loss to the Pirates that snapped a five-game winning streak. Westbrook has gone at least six innings in each of his last 13 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel has a 3.38 ERA in his last three starts, which all lasted at least six innings. Batters are hitting .300 off him over that span, but only slugging .343. He hasn't won since the second start of his career on June 23.

away_pitcher_note: The youngest starting pitcher in the Majors, Lyles allowed just two runs over seven innings in two successive starts before giving up five runs in four innings of a 12-4 loss to Arizona on Saturday.

away_pitcher_note: Abad will make the start -- the first of his career -- in place of Armando Galarraga, whom the Astros designated for assignment on Wednesday. Abad appeared in 30 games out of the bullpen for Houston before he was optioned to Triple-A on July 28.

away_pitcher_note: Harrell gave up six earned runs in five innings of a 7-0 loss at St. Louis on Tuesday. He had allowed two earned runs or less in his previous seven starts.

away_pitcher_note: Cain faces the Astros with a three-start winning steak in which he has a 1.61 ERA. He is 2-0 with a 0.58 ERA and 20 strikeouts against Houston this season, which includes his June 13 perfect game against them.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel sailed through the first three innings before giving up five earned runs in four-plus innings of a 13-5 loss in St. Louis on Thursday afternoon. Keuchel had recorded three successive quality starts prior to that outing.
away_pitcher_note: Zito rebounded from two poor outings with a dominant performance against the Braves, allowing two runs in eight-plus innings, both of which scored after he departed with two on in the ninth. He is 9-1 when receiving four or more runs of support.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles earned his first win since June 26 on Friday vs. the Mets, surrendering just one run over six innings. Lyles twice had two on with less than two outs, but escaped both jams and evaded the big inning that has been his Achilles heel in 2012.
away_pitcher_note: More disciplined mechanics allowed Vogelsong to rebound from two poor outings by allowing three runs in 6 1/3 innings in his last start. After only pitching 5 2/3 innings in his previous two starts, he allowed four hits, three of which were homers.

home_pitcher_note: Abad was recalled from Triple-A to start against the Mets on Saturday -- the first start of his career -- and he delivered four innings of one-run ball. He made 30 relief appearances with the Astros earlier this season before he was optioned in July.
away_pitcher_note: Although Leake gave up 10 hits over 6 2/3 innings on Saturday vs. the Cardinals, he gave up only two runs. Credit the pitcher for working out of trouble, keeping the hits on the ground and getting two double plays.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell gave up one run over seven innings against the Mets on Sunday, but he took a no-decision. The Astros, who scored their only run of the game after he exited, provided Harrell with zero runs for the third time in his last five starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his six-inning start that yielded five runs vs. the Cardinals on Sunday, five of Bailey's nine hits came with two outs. "He couldn't put them away," manager Dusty Baker said. "They bounced some balls up the middle on him. That's good hitting."

home_pitcher_note: Norris is still searching for his first win since May 21. His ERA at home is 2.09, the best home ERA in the National League. He gave up one run in 6 2/3 innings against the Giants at Minute Maid Park on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: In a 3-2 win over Arizona on Monday, Arroyo gave up two runs and five hits with one walk and three strikeouts to improve to 4-0 with a 2.86 ERA over his last four starts and 7-1 with a 3.44 ERA over his last eight starts. He also hit the game-winning home run to get the victory.

home_pitcher_note: Locke makes his first start after a pair of impressive relief appearances after first being called up in early August. He has averaged close to a strikeout an inning in the Minors. This could be the start of his tenure as a rotation mainstay.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros will call up Edgar Gonzalez from Triple-A Oklahoma City to start at PNC Park. He was 1-0 with a 0.69 ERA in two starts for the RedHawks this year after pitching for Monterrey in the Mexican League.

away_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old has been up and down this season, but has a couple of good starts under his belt. He's 1-0 with a 3.27 ERA in his last two starts. He lost to the Giants last time out, but allowed three runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Correia returns to the rotation in place of Jeff Karstens (strained hip flexor), seeking his ninth win in his last 12 decisions. He has made only seven appearances (including three starts) since getting pulled from the rotation on July 25.
away_pitcher_note: Abad was moved from the bullpen to the rotation earlier this year, and his first two starts were rough. He's 0-2 with a 7.56 ERA in two starts, at the Mets on Aug. 25 and against the Reds on Aug. 31 in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey is searching for his first win in five outings, despite pitching well enough for a 'W' on Saturday. Bailey gave up just three hits, including a solo homer to Houston, striking out nine, but fell victim to poor run support in the no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell has been the Astros' most consistent starting pitcher this year, accounting for 10 of the team's 42 wins. He ranks first in the Major Leagues in innings pitched by a rookie with 165 1/3, and second in the NL in strikeouts by a rookie (116).

home_pitcher_note: Despite failing to get the win, Arroyo continued his hot streak on Sunday in Houston. He surrendered one run on three hits in his six innings, and hasn't lost since Aug. 6. He's 8-2 with a 3.33 ERA in his past 11 outings.
away_pitcher_note: Norris, who hasn't won since May 21, tries to break his 10-game losing streak. He's 0-1 with a 1.93 ERA in his last three starts, but in his past 16 starts, is 0-10 with a 5.90 ERA. He pitched six scoreless vs. the Reds on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto suffered his first day game loss Monday against the Phillies, giving up four runs on eight hits in seven innings. Despite the loss, Cueto is 11-1 with a 1.87 ERA in day games this season.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez, making his first Major League start in nearly three years, held the Pirates to five hits and one run and struck out five Monday for his first win since April 24, 2008. The Astros signed him out of the Mexican League.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel returns to the Astros from a brief stint with Triple-A Oklahoma City, marking the start of a six-man rotation for Houston. He's searching for his second win of the season and first win since his second start back on June 23.
away_pitcher_note: With Jeff Samardzija shutdown for the season, Volstad and others need to pick up the slack. Volstad served up five runs on nine hits over five innings in his last outing vs. the Nationals, but does have two wins in his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles failed to last past the sixth for the fourth consecutive start Tuesday, leaving after just 4 2/3 innings with his pitch count at 92. He surrendered five runs (four earned) on seven hits and will be searching for his second win in eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Nationals roughed up Germano in his last outing, scoring seven runs over four innings. He has lost four straight starts, and teams are batting .296 against him. He did beat the Astros on Aug. 15.

home_pitcher_note: Abad will make just his fourth start of the season Wednesday, searching for his first win as a starter. He hasn't pitched more than 4 1/3 innings in any of his three starts and has given up five or more runs in each of his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Wood is coming off a solid outing against the Pirates. In his last two starts, he's given up two earned runs over 11 2/3 innings for a 1.54 ERA. He's 1-1 vs. the Astros this season, giving up two earned runs in 13 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell has been the Astros' most consistent starter this season, with the club going 12-16 in his 28 starts. He ranks first in the Majors in innings pitched by a rookie and ranks second in the NL in home ERA at 2.06.
away_pitcher_note: Cloyd will pitch on short rest for the first time in his career after throwing 76 pitches in the second game of a doubleheader Sunday against the Rockies. He lasted just four innings, so he should have enough to get through five.

home_pitcher_note: Since being promoted from Triple-A Oklahoma City after signing with the Astros out of the Mexican League, Gonzalez is 2-0 with a 1.74 ERA in two road starts. He's allowed seven hits and struck out 11 in 10 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels is 3-1 with a 2.26 ERA in seven starts since July 27. Opponents are hitting .229 with a .571 OPS against him in that stretch. He would like to win his 15th game Friday, which would tie a career high.

home_pitcher_note: After getting a complete-game victory over the Indians in his second Major League start on June 23, the lefty has gone 0-7 with a 6.35 ERA in his next 11 starts. He's allowed 66 hits in 56 2/3 innings in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick has been nothing short of brilliant over his last six starts. He is 5-1 with a 1.49 ERA in that stretch. He is a big reason why the Phillies have crept back into National League Wild Card contention after being 14 under .500 on July 13.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles picked up his second win in four starts Monday by holding the Cubs scoreless through five innings. In his last four starts, he's 2-1 with a 3.48 ERA, allowing 19 hits and striking out 16 batters in 20 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay allowed five runs in 6 1/3 innings, but it was good enough to earn the win in the Phillies' victory Tuesday over the Marlins at Citizens Bank Park. Halladay has 10 or more wins in eight consecutive seasons, and 10 of his last 11.

home_pitcher_note: Lohse gave the Cards another quality start on Wednesday, but for the 11th time this year, a quality start was not enough for him to get a win. Lohse's loss was his first since June 26; he remains among the league leaders in ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Abad's transition from reliever to starter has been a shaky one. He is 0-4 in four starts in the Majors with a 6.89 ERA. He went 3 1/3 innings in his last start, allowing one run on four hits while throwing 68 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Pushed back into the rotation last week because of an injury to Jake Westbrook, Lynn earned a longer stay. After sorting out his mechanics while pitching in relief, Lynn tossed six strong innings in L.A. on Thursday. He allowed one run and five hits.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell hasn't been happy with his performance in his last two starts. Against the Phillies on Thursday, he allowed four runs (three earned) on seven hits. He has walked nine batters in his last two outings.

home_pitcher_note: By manipulating the rotation around an off-day, the Cardinals were able to ensure that Garcia's next start comes at home. Though he pitched well on the road Saturday, Garcia has been much better at home, where he has a season ERA of 2.63.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros decided to give Norris some extra time between starts so the blister on his pitching hand can fully heal. The right-hander is still looking for his first win since May 21. His ERA since his last win is 6.04.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez has made three starts for the Astros since they signed him out of the Mexican League, where he was pitching for his native Monterrey. He won two road games before giving up six hits and five runs last Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Locke is winless in nine Major League appearances, including seven starts, and his "show us" rope may be getting shorter -- particularly after his most recent start, when he let a five-run lead over the Cubs turn into a 13-9 loss.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander is coming off his second career win, throwing 5 1/3 scoreless innings to beat the Phillies on Saturday. He had lost his previous seven decisions since throwing a complete game on June 23 against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Two months after being removed from the rotation to make room for Wandy Rodriguez, Correia is the Bucs' hottest starter (10 wins in last 14 decisions) as he goes for his 12th win, which would tie a career high.

home_pitcher_note: Lyles has had an up-and-down season in his second year in the Majors. The 21-year-old pitched five scoreless innings on Sept. 11, before giving up five hits and four runs in five innings last Sunday in a no-decision against Philly.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett has gone through a strange stretch, with his ERA continuing to go down as his losses go up. He is winless in his last six starts and has dropped four straight decisions; he has not lost five in a row since June 2010.

home_pitcher_note: Abad faced the Cardinals in his last start and gave up three runs on six hits over a career-high five innings. He also struck out a career-high six batters. The left-hander has lost all five of his starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn has made two starts since retooling his mechanics in the bullpen, and he looks like his first-half self. Showcasing a much smoother delivery, Lynn has limited opponents to one earned run in 12 1/3 innings since moving back into the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell is winless in his last six starts after picking up his 10th win of the season on Aug. 14. Against the Cardinals on Sept. 19, the rookie right-hander allowed three runs on five hits, two of them homers.
away_pitcher_note: This will be the final time this regular season that Garcia will have to pitch on the road, which has never been all that kind to him. Garcia has a career 4.60 ERA on the road and a 5.67 mark in 2012. His last road start, though, was a quality one.

home_pitcher_note: Norris, dealing with flu-like symptoms and a blister on his hand, is scheduled to pitch Wednesday. Astros interim manager Tony DeFrancesco is considering other options if Norris can't go. Norris hasn't won since May 21.
away_pitcher_note: Carpenter threw 77 pitches in his five-inning season debut on Thursday. He's still getting a feel for his pitches -- particularly the curveball and cutter -- but that should come with time. Carpenter is cleared to surpass the 100-pitch mark.

home_pitcher_note: A Gallardo start usually means good things for the Brewers, who are 22-10 when he takes the mound, including 11 straight wins. "He's our guy that we go to when we need to stop something bad," manager Ron Roenicke said.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez lasted only 1 2/3 innings in his previous start after straining his right hamstring. He came through a bullpen session on Tuesday feeling better. The right-hander is 2-0 in two road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada's last start turned sour after a two-out hit by the opposing pitcher, opening the door for a six-run Nationals outburst. He was much better in his two previous starts, allowing no runs over 13 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel's ERA over his last three starts in 1.10, but two of those starts were fewer than six innings in length. The Astros are 4-11 in Keuchel's starts this season. His 4.66 ERA is the lowest it has been since July.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers has been very good at home, pitching to a 2.97 ERA in 12 games, including 10 starts. He beat the Astros on Aug. 1 in Milwaukee by scattering eight hits and two runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old allowed three runs over four innings against the Pirates on Sept. 23. Getting through the fifth inning has been a problem for Lyles all season long -- his ERA in the fifth is 17.22 (19 1/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Berken was roughed up in his last start against the Rockies, giving up six runs on nine hits over four innings. He had trouble keeping the ball down, which can be a problem at Coors Field. This will be his last chance to make a good impression.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell leads all Major League rookies with 187 2/3 innings pitched and is second among NL rookies in wins. He hasn't won in his last six starts, though, going 0-2 with a 3.22 ERA. His last win was Aug. 21.

away_pitcher_note: Norris snapped a personal 12-game losing streak Wednesday, holding St. Louis to two hits and striking out seven in a season-high 7 1/3 scoreless innings. In his previous 18 starts, he was 0-12 with a 6.17 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wood seemed "tired" in his last start, according to manager Dale Sveum. Wood says he's fine. The Cubs want to see more life in his pitches in his final game. He has two wins in his last 12 decisions.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran has done a nice job since the Astros picked him up from Mexican league. He's 3-1 with a 4.15 ERA in five starts with the Astros and has been unbeatable on the road. He's 3-0 with a 2.81 ERA in three road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Norris makes his first Opening Day start, looking to rebound from a season in which he went 7-13 with a 4.65 ERA. He went 4-1 with a 1.71 ERA and 82 strikeouts at home last year and lives for big games like the opener.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison makes his first Opening Day start. He has never pitched in March but is 7-6 with a 4.89 ERA in 17 career starts in April. That's his highest ERA of any month. He is 0-1 with a 5.14 ERA in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell, the Astros' Pitcher of the Year last season, makes his debut against the Rangers. Harrell led Houston in wins and innings pitched last year, finishing 11-11 and going at least five innings in 27 out of 32 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Darvish went 4-0 with a 2.18 ERA in five starts in April in his rookie season. He won his only start against the Astros last season, holding them to two runs in eight innings in a 6-2 win on June 15 in Arlington.

home_pitcher_note: Humber, who helped Rice University win a college title 10 years ago, returns to Texas to pitch for the Astros. Humber had an up-and-down 2012 with the White Sox, but is coming of a strong spring and looking for a fresh start.
away_pitcher_note: Ogando returns to the rotation after spending last season in the bullpen. He won 13 games as a starter in 2011 and was selected to All-Star team. He is 3-0 with a 1.93 ERA in his career in April, his lowest ERA for any month.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock won the fourth spot in the rotation by allowing two earned runs in his final 16 innings in the Grapefruit League. He's facing an Oakland team that traded him to the Astros earlier after a so-so 2012 season in Triple-A.
away_pitcher_note: Straily led all of the Minors with 190 strikeouts last season, and he proceeded to tally 32 more in 39 1/3 innings with the A's upon his callup. But he also gave up 11 home runs, and he struggled with fastball command this spring.

home_pitcher_note: Norris starts for the first time since Opening Day by facing the Oakland A's for the first time in his career. He beat the Rangers on Sunday, allowing five hits and two runs in 5 2/3 innings on Opening Night.
away_pitcher_note: This will mark Colon's first Major League start since Aug. 18 of last year, four days before the right-hander was slapped with a 50-game suspension after testing positive for testosterone.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell went six innings and allowed one run and six hits and struck out four batters in his first start of the season on Tuesday against the Rangers. He's pitched at least five innings in 31 consecutive starts since last April.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson was dealt a tough-luck loss in his 2013 debut, after giving up just two runs on four hits through seven impressive innings against the Mariners on Monday. He struck out six but, out of character, also walked four in the outing.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty struggled in his Mariners debut, giving up seven hits -- including five doubles -- and four runs in four innings to the A's. He'll pitch the home opener at Safeco Field, where he's 6-0 with a 2.13 ERA in nine starts as a visitor.
away_pitcher_note: Humber gets the ball in the Astros' first road game of the season. He went 5 2/3 innings and allowed one run on five hits on Wednesday against Texas, lowing his ERA against AL West teams to 2.80 in 70 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Bedard, the only left in the starting rotation, is playing for his fifth team and making his first start of the season. He started on Opening Day for the Pirates last year, and went 7-14 with a 5.01 ERA in 24 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Beavan gave up six hits and five runs in five innings against the White Sox in his debut, pitching well until giving up two homers in the fifth. The big right-hander from Texas has never pitched against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Peacock took the loss Friday against the A's, yielding two earned runs on three hits and three walks with five strikeouts in 4 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Another local arm brought home by the Angels in a deal with the Braves, Hanson had an impressive debut for his new team in Texas. He held the Rangers to three runs across six innings on a day the ball was flying at Rangers Ballpark.
away_pitcher_note: Norris will try to turn things around on the road after going 3-12 with a 6.94 ERA in 18 starts away from home last year. In his last four starts dating to last season, he's 3-1 with a 1.46 ERA and a .191 average against.

home_pitcher_note: Richards will take the injured Jered Weaver's place in the rotation and make his first start of 2013 against the Astros. Richards is coming off a strong Spring Training and has appeared in four games out of the bullpen with a 2.08 ERA this year.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell makes his first road start after going 0-2 in two starts at home, losing to Texas and Oakland. He pitched well against the Rangers on April 2, but on Sunday allowed eight earned runs and five walks in 4 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson allowed three runs and walked three batters in the first inning against the A's on Tuesday. But after giving up a leadoff homer in the second, he retired 15 of the next 17 batters (seven on strikeouts) to get through six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Humber is off to a nice start this year, but is still searching for his first win. In 11 2/3 innings, he's allowed 10 hits, only four earned runs and had a quality start Monday in a loss to the Mariners in Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Milone has pitched just well enough to win both of his starts this season. He's still a better pitcher at home than on the road and has one career start against the Astros when he was with the Washington Nationals.

away_pitcher_note: The three-time AL Pitcher of the Month leads the league in ERA (2.22), innings pitched (career-high 206 2/3) and WAR (7.1). He’s 13-0 at home, but on the road he’s 4-7 with a 3.13 ERA, including a win at Texas in April.

home_pitcher_note: Lewis is nearing the end of one of his best seasons, having already eclipsed his career high in wins and coming off a two-hit shutout in which he carried a perfect game into the seventh inning against Oakland on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: He ranks first among AL rookie pitchers with a 2.6 WAR. McCullers hasn’t won since July 29, going 0-2 with a 4.97 ERA in his last five starts. He’s allowed 10.3 hits per nine innings, and the team is 1-4 in those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers left trailing and surrendered three earned runs -- all on solo homers -- in his seven-inning stint against the Angels on Sept. 13, but received a no-decision after the Astros staged a five-run, two-out rally in the ninth inning to win.
away_pitcher_note: Doubront is 2-1 in his last three starts despite registering an 8.27 ERA in that span. The left-hander gave up seven earned runs -- and three home runs -- in his most recent outing.

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir battled fellow Trade Deadline acquisition Cole Hamels valiantly on Monday but received no decision in the 5-3 loss. The Astros have lost Kazmir's last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gray has a 7.80 ERA in his last three starts and a 3.45 mark since the All-Star break, but his overall ERA (2.45) still ranks third among all American League pitchers.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh had his second-shortest start of the season, lasting just 3 2/3 innings and surrendering eight hits and five runs in a loss to Texas on Tuesday, after which he took "100 percent blame" for the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Brooks has seen his season ERA rise by two runs (from 5.47 to 7.68) over his last three outings. The 25-year-old has allowed 24 hits and 17 earned runs in his last 12 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel is coming off his worst start of the season, when he gave up nine runs over 4 2/3 in a loss at Texas. He's been flawless at home, though, sporting a 13-0 record and 1.49 ERA this season.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver was ejected from his last start after 4 2/3 innings for hitting Kyle Seager with a pitch after an exchange of words. The 10-year veteran is 7-11 with a 4.74 ERA on the season.

home_pitcher_note: In the midst of his first pennant race, the rookie has been close to sensational down the stretch. He's posted four quality starts in five appearances since rejoining the team on Aug. 23.
away_pitcher_note: Santiago was chased from his last start, giving up just five runs and netting five outs in the shortest start of his season. He threw 30 pitches in that start and Mike Scioscia said he could be an option out of the 'pen before his start on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers has been rock solid to offset Scott Feldman's absence, locking down a rotation spot while allowing 11 earned runs in his past seven starts. He's especially enjoyed his new home, going 1-0 with a 0.89 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Saturday’s doubleheader created the need for a sixth starter, so Tropeano gets his sixth start of the season. The 25-year-old limited the Mariners to two runs in five innings while filling in for an injured Matt Shoemaker on Sept. 15.

home_pitcher_note: Since winning his first start with the Astros by throwing seven scoreless innings July 24, Kazmir has gone 1-5 with a 3.70 ERA in 10 starts. In two starts against Texas in that span, he’s allowed three earned runs in 12 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gallardo is 0-2 with a 7.71 ERA in his last two starts. He has made 16 starts on the road this season and is 5-5 with a 3.29 ERA. Gallardo is 2-1 with a 6.14 ERA vs. the Astros this season and 15-4 with a 3.09 ERA in 20 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh has gone 8-2 with a 3.08 ERA in his last 12 starts, allowing 77 hits in 76 innings. He has given up exactly five earned runs in three of those 12 starts, including his Sept. 15 outing at Texas when he went just 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Holland is 0-2 with a 9.00 ERA in his last three starts. He allowed five runs in 5 2/3 innings vs. the Astros on Sept. 15. He is 3-2 with a 4.10 ERA in nine career starts against the Astros, including 0-1 with a 5.94 ERA at Minute Maid Park.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel is looking to finish off a perfect season at home. He’s the first pitcher in the Majors to go 14-0 at home. His 1.47 ERA at home is the lowest home ERA by a pitcher in the AL since Nolan Ryan's 1.07 ERA in 1972 with the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Perez will be making his second start in three outings vs. Houston. He beat them Sept. 16 in Arlington, allowing one run in seven innings. He is 4-0 with a 2.00 ERA in five career starts against them. He has walked 11 batters in his last 22 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The 27-year-old Cuban is 1-2 with a 3.30 ERA in five starts since being recalled from Triple-A Tacoma in late August. Elias is 1-2, 6.65 in four outings against the Astros this season, including a 5 1/3-inning no-decision with four runs on Sept 1.
away_pitcher_note: McCullers was the tough-luck loser on Tuesday, allowing four hits and three earned runs over seven innings in a 4-3 loss to the Angels. He's allowed three or fewer earned runs in each of his last four starts, but doesn't have a win to show for it.

home_pitcher_note: Nuno will pitch on just three days’ rest due to James Paxton’s finger problem. Nuno threw 67 pitches in 4 1/3 innings in an 8-4 loss in Anaheim on Friday. The left-handed swingman is 3-15 with a 4.51 ERA in 36 starts over the past two years.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers had first-inning struggles but managed to toss 6 2/3 innings of three-run ball in a 6-5 loss to the Angels on Wednesday. He's got a 2.44 ERA in eight starts as an Astro.

home_pitcher_note: Zych makes his first professional start. The right-hander has appeared in 11 games this season for the Mariners, all in relief.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir struggled mightily against the Rangers on Friday, lasting just 3 2/3 innings while surrendering 10 hits and six runs. He's gone just 3 2/3 innings in each of his last two starts and surrendered seven or more hits in three of his last five.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa gave up two runs on four hits and three walks in 5 2/3 innings in his last start, at the Padres, to pick up his 14th win. He has thrown a career-high 185 2/3 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel is trying to become the eighth pitcher in club history to win 20 games in a season. Keuchel went 15-0 at home this year, but is 4-8 with a 3.82 ERA in 14 road starts. The Astros are 6-8 in his road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson struck out five and allowed just one run on four hits over six innings in San Diego in his last start, but he still took the loss. He'll be in search of the fourth 10-win season of his career.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh has gone 9-2 with a 3.27 ERA in his last 13 starts, with the Astros going 9-4 in that span. On the road, he’s 6-4 with a 4.26 ERA in 15 outings, 11 of which have been quality starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ray took a no-decision in his last start, against the Rockies, after he allowed two earned runs on seven hits in six innings. He owns a 4.42 ERA in the second half after recording a 2.16 mark before the break.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros had lost five consecutive starts by McCullers until he beat the Mariners on Monday in Seattle. He hasn’t pitched poorly though. In his last five starts since Sept. 5, he’s 1-2 with a 3.19 ERA and four quality outings.

home_pitcher_note: The Yankees righty missed his second-to-last turn in the rotation with a hamstring strain before going five innings and allowing four runs in his final regular-season outing.
away_pitcher_note: The American League Cy Young Award contender will go on three days' rest after pitching six innings Friday against the D-backs and earning his 20th victory.
series_status: HOU wins AL Wild Card Game

home_pitcher_note: Ventura clearly has been the Royals' best starter the past two months. Since being demoted in late July and instantly recalled when Jason Vargas suffered a season-ending elbow injury, Ventura is 9-1 with a 3.10 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh will toe the rubber for the Astros in the ALDS opener. The only other time McHugh faced the Royals in his career, he didn’t allow a run, pitching seven scoreless frames while striking out nine on May 27, 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto struggled to a 4-7 record with a 4.76 ERA in 13 starts with Kansas City, and he was 3-4 with a 4.40 mark in seven starts at Kauffman Stadium. Cueto has made just three career postseason starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir will be making his first postseason start since 2009 (then with the Angels), and he'll be doing it for his hometown team. The southpaw posted a 2-6 record with a 4.17 ERA after being acquired by Houston in late July.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel fired six shutout innings in the Astros' AL Wild Card Game victory over the Yankees. Keuchel led the league in victories (20) and innings (232) and went 9-4 with a 2.85 ERA after the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez finished with 13 wins for the second straight year, and he cracked the 200-inning barrier for the first time in his career this season. The right-hander allowed 16 home runs in 34 appearances.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander gets the call for Game 4. He faced the Royals once this season, scattering four hits over seven innings of one-run ball while striking out six on June 29.
away_pitcher_note: After a Game 1 start shortened by rain, in which he pitched just two innings, Ventura gets the nod for Game 4. The right-hander allowed three runs on four hits in Thursday’s 5-2 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto takes the hill in the decisive Game 5. After a rough beginning to Game 2, Cueto retired 12 of the final 14 hitters he faced. The right-hander wound up throwing six innings, giving up seven hits and four runs. The Royals won, 5-4.
away_pitcher_note: In his first postseason start, in ALDS Game 1 at Kansas City, McHugh threw six innings, allowing one walk, two runs and four hits, including two homers. Including Game 1, he’s 2-0 with a 1.38 ERA in 13 innings vs. the Royals in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Tanaka will make the Opening Day start for the second consecutive season, beginning his third season in the Majors. It's a reprise of the pitching matchup from last year's AL Wild Card game, when Tanaka took the loss (two runs in five innings).
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a season in which he went 20-8 with a 2.48 ERA in 33 starts, the reigning AL Cy Young Award winner returns to the Bronx, where he shut down the Yanks in last year's Wild Card Game.

home_pitcher_note: Pineda is beginning his third season with the Yankees, having posted an AL-best 7.43 strikeout-to-walk ratio in 2015, the highest ever by a Yankee who hurled at least 150 innings. He was 0-2 with a 5.11 ERA vs. the Astros last year.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh, who finished second to Keuchel in the American League with 19 wins last year, is coming off a season in which he set career highs in starts (32) and innings (203 2/3).

home_pitcher_note: Eovaldi begins his second season with the Yankees looking to follow up on a career-best 14-win campaign, which tied for eighth in the AL. Eovaldi didn't face the Astros last year but is 1-0 with a 0.90 ERA in three career starts vs. Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers went 2-1 with a 3.32 ERA in 10 games (nine starts) after coming to the Astros from the Brewers in a trade in July, and overall, he set career highs in starts, innings pitched and strikeouts. He’s never faced the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired with third baseman Aaron Hill and infield prospect Isan Diaz on Jan. 30 from the D-backs, Anderson added some depth to Milwaukee's starting rotation. He struggled with the long ball during a subpar Spring Training.
away_pitcher_note: A trip to the DL with a knee injury and a sprained shoulder suffered in September held Feldman to 18 starts in '15. When he was healthy, he was effective. He went 5-5 with a 3.90 ERA in 18 starts, including 1-1 with a 2.79 ERA in his final 8 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta wasn't very good in his first Opening Day start, allowing five Giants runs (four earned) on six hits in four innings. He had eight hitters in two-strike counts before logging the first of two strikeouts in the game.
away_pitcher_note: Fister will make his Astros debut after signing a one-year, $7 million deal with Houston in January. He bounced between the bullpen and rotation last year with Washington while battling forearm soreness, but he had a healthy spring.

home_pitcher_note: Nelson didn't throw a pitch past the seventh inning of any of his final 15 starts last season, but he did so in his 2016 debut, limiting the Giants to two runs in 7 1/3 innings of a tough-luck loss.
away_pitcher_note: The AL Cy Young Award winner beat the Yankees on Tuesday, allowing two runs, three hits and four walks in seven innings. He made three starts against the Brewers in 2012, allowing 18 runs (16 earned) and 20 hits in 12 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh, a 19-game winner in 2015, was roughed up in his first outing of the season Wednesday in New York against the Yankees. He recorded one out and gave up six runs (five earned) and three hits while throwing 43 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Young makes his second start of the season. He pitched five innings against the Mets last Tuesday and gave up three hits and two runs, while striking out four, in a 2-0 loss.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season, Fiers went five innings on Thursday vs. the Yanks and allowed five earned runs and nine hits, including two homers. He pitched one inning against the Royals in the ALDS last year and allowed a run.
away_pitcher_note: Medlen, the team’s fifth starter, makes his first start of the season. He was skipped the first time through the rotation because of the team’s built-in three off days the first week. Medlen went 1-1 this spring with a 5.94 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman worked four innings in his first start of the season Friday in Milwaukee, allowing four runs and five hits. That was Feldman’s first start since Sept. 1 of last year, when he suffered a shoulder sprain that ended his season.
away_pitcher_note: Ventura struggled with his command in his first start of the season last Friday against the Twins, walking six in five-plus innings. He did strike out six and gave up just two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Fister made his first start with the Astros on Saturday in Milwaukee and picked up the win after allowing five hits and three runs in five innings. He went 5-7 with a 4.19 ERA in 25 games (15 starts) with Washington last year.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy was sensational in his Royals debut last Saturday against the Twins, tossing 6 2/3 shutout innings while giving up just five hits and striking out seven.

home_pitcher_note: He’s walked 10 batters in first two starts, including a career-high-tying six on Sunday in Milwaukee. En route to the AL Cy Young Award last year, the lefty went 15-0 with a 1.46 ERA at home. He hasn’t lost at home since July 25, 2014.
away_pitcher_note: The encouragement of a solid Spring Training for the new Tiger dissipated in the Midwestern chill Saturday, when the big right-hander struggled with command en route to six Yankee runs on eight hits over 3 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh’s first two starts could not have been more different. He lasted just one-third of an inning in his 2016 debut April 6 at the Yankees, and then threw seven scoreless innings, allowing eight hits, Monday against the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander spent his side session Wednesday working on his breaking pitches after the Pirates worked him for 111 pitches over 4 1/3 innings Monday. He’ll try to put them to work against an Astros lineup he shut down last August.

home_pitcher_note: After going five innings in his first start of season April 7 at Yankees, Fiers pitched better at home Tuesday, despite losing. He gave up a three-run homer in first but held Kansas City scoreless rest of way (six innings).
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez has taken scoreless performances into the sixth inning in both of his starts this year, only to give up a pair of sixth-inning runs each time. It hasn’t stopped him from racking up wins as he builds up arm strength.

home_pitcher_note: Holland will be pitching on six days' rest after Sunday's start against the Orioles was postponed by rain. He is 7-11 with a 4.89 ERA in 26 career starts with six-plus days of rest. He is 3-2 with a 4.37 ERA in ten career starts against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman was terrific in his most recent start, when he worked 6 1/3 innings against the Royals and allowed only two unearned runs (on his own error). He’s lost his last three starts against his former team (0-3, 6.75 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is on a nine-game winning streak and the Rangers are 13-0 in his last 13 starts. He went 5 1/3 frames in his last start vs. the Mariners and left trailing, 3-1. But the Rangers rallied to win, 6-3. He won his only start vs. the Astros in 2015.
away_pitcher_note: Fister has yet to have a quality start in his first two outings with the Astros, lasting five innings against the Brewers on April 9 and 5 2/3 against Kansas City on Thursday. He hasn’t faced the Rangers since May 31, 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Griffin is 3-0 with a 4.88 ERA in four career starts against the Astros, but he is facing them for the first time since Sept. 6, 2013. Opponents are hitting .214 off him in his first two starts.
away_pitcher_note: After walking 10 batters in 12 2/3 innings in his first two starts, Keuchel threw eight scoreless innings on Friday against Tigers. He was rocked for nine runs and 11 hits in 4 2/3 innings in last start in Arlington, on Sept. 16.

home_pitcher_note: After giving up five earned runs in one-third of an inning in his first start of the season, on April 6 at the Yankees, McHugh has gone 1-1 with a 2.92 ERA, including seven scoreless innings against Kansas City on April 11.
away_pitcher_note: The knuckleballer returns to Houston, the scene of his first -- and worst -- start for the Red Sox. On Aug. 6, 2013, Wright lasted just one inning and threw 38 pitches, allowing one hit, three runs and two walks.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers has allowed 22 hits and 12 earned runs in 16 2/3 innings this season covering three starts. He’s allowing 11.9 hits per nine innings and opponents are hitting .302 against him, so there’s room for improvement.
away_pitcher_note: The righty threw a gem in his only previous start at Minutemaid Park, firing  a complete-game shutout with 12 strikeouts in 2014. Buchholz is coming off his best start of the year, as he pitched 6 2/3 shutout innings against the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: The Astros have yet to win a game in which Feldman started (0-3). His best outing of the season came on April 13, when he didn’t allow an earned run for 6 1/3 innings against the Royals, but his throwing error proved costly.
away_pitcher_note: Owens struggled with command issues in Spring Training, but he earned his way back to a big league start with his time at Triple-A Pawtucket. The lefty was 4-4 with a 4.57 ERA for Boston in 2015, his rookie season.

home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old has been strong in his first three starts (1-0, 1.50 ERA) and picked up his first win on three hits over six innings at Cleveland on Wednesday. Walker is 4-1 with a 4.40 ERA in eight starts against Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Fister received little support in a 2-1 loss to Texas in his last outing, allowing two earned runs in six innings. The Astros were 1-for-12 with runners in scoring position in that game.

home_pitcher_note: Six of the nine earned runs allowed by Karns in three starts have come via the long ball and he’s 1-1 with a 5.28 ERA.  He gave up just one hit and one run in 6 innings in his only prior start against Houston last year while with the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: The reigning AL Cy Young Award winner’s numbers aren’t as good on the road as at home, and Keuchel is coming off a 7-4 loss at Texas in which he allowed 13 hits and six earned runs over six innings. The Astros need a bounceback game from their ace.

home_pitcher_note: The 35-year-old is still seeking his first win of the season (0-2, 3.81 in four starts), but is coming off a strong eight-inning, two-run outing against the Angels. Iwakuma is 4-4 with a 3.77 ERA in 10 meetings with the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh has struggled in the early innings in three of his four starts this season, pitching only 16 2/3 innings. He’s trying to lower his ERA, which is at 7.56. McHugh has given up 10 hits in each of his past two starts, both losses.

home_pitcher_note: A's manager Bob Melvin confirmed on Wednesday that Friday's start belongs to Manaea, who will be called up from Triple-A. The No. 2 prospect in the organization has gone 2-0 with a 1.50 ERA in three starts at Nashville.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers is coming off his best outing of the season when he beat the Red Sox on Saturday in Houston. He’s won his last two starts, allowing 12 hits, six runs while walking only three batters and striking out 11 in 11 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hahn returns to the A's after pitching to a 2.04 ERA in four starts with the Sounds following a disappointing spring in which he compiled an 11.15 ERA and .382 opponents average.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie his making first Major League start after appearing in six games in relief and allowing 11 hits, one run and one walk while striking out 12 batters in 13 2/3 innings. He’s replacing Scott Feldman, who’s being moved to bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Hill's comeback continues, as he pitched seven scoreless innings against the Tigers his last time out. Hill has 37 strikeouts in 26 innings this season and hasn’t allowed more than three earned runs in a start this year.
away_pitcher_note: After beating the Brewers in his first start of the season, Fister has gone 0-3 with a 5.60 ERA in his last three starts, allowing 18 hits in 17 2/3 innings. He walked a career-high seven batters in his most recent outing Monday at Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel, a 20-game winner a year ago, has given up 11 runs on 19 hits over his past two starts after allowing five runs on 14 hits through his first 20 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Berrios, a top prospect, is coming off his first career start, and he will get another chance. He gave up five runs over four-plus innings in his debut against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh won his last start, giving up two runs in five innings. He's been up and down so far this year after a breakout season in 2015. McHugh is 2-0 with a 2.00 ERA vs. the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Meyer is set to make his first big league start, as he's replacing Tommy Milone in the rotation. He had a 1.04 ERA in three starts at Triple-A Rochester.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers is coming off his best start of the season, in which he left after seven innings with a 4-2 lead, but the bullpen couldn't keep it up. He owns a career 4.38 ERA in May, his worst of any month.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes saw his streak of four quality starts snapped against the Tigers on Friday. The right-hander gave up four runs on seven hits and two walks over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Devenski will be making his second Major League start after taking the loss on Saturday in Oakland, giving up two runs and five hits in five innings. This will be just his seventh career appearance after starting in the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: The 29-year-old has a 5.06 ERA in five starts, but has won in his last two outings and is coming off his first career shutout, a five-hit gem against the Royals in Seattle. Miley is 2-0 with a 2.63 ERA in four starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Fister has improved as the season has progressed and is coming off his best outing of the year, throwing 6 2/3 innings on Sunday in Oakland and allowing one run on seven hits. He lost to Seattle on April 25 despite a quality start.
away_pitcher_note: Walker is 2-1 with a 1.80 ERA in five starts, including a win over the Astros on April 25 when he allowed one run with 11 strikeouts in seven innings. The 23-year-old has 29 strikeouts and 3 walks in 30 innings with a 1.03 WHIP.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel is 0-3 with a 8.82 ERA in his last three starts, allowing 16 earned runs and 26 hits in 16 1/3 innings. He had won 17 consecutive decisions at home in the regular season before losing on Monday to the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander is 3-0 with a 3.09 ERA over his last four starts and has allowed just three runs and eight hits over his past 13 innings, including seven shutout frames on two hits against the Astros on April 26 in Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh has won two consecutive starts and has gone 3-2 with a 5.00 ERA since allowing five earned runs in one-third of an inning in his April 6 season debut. He’s tied for sixth place on Minute Maid Park’s all-time wins list.
away_pitcher_note: Iwakuma threw seven innings of one-run ball against the A’s for his first win Tuesday. He gave up a season-high five runs on seven hits in five innings to the Astros in his previous start and is 4-5 with a 4.18 ERA in 11 career games vs. Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers has been up and down in 2016, following a couple two-run outings by allowing four runs in 4 2/3 frames against Minnesota. The culprit has been leaving pitches up in the zone, as he’s surrendered eight home runs through six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kluber has gone 2-0 with a 1.13 ERA, 23 strikeouts, two walks and a .396 opponents' OPS in his past three turns (24 innings). On Wednesday, the righty spun a shutout with 16 outs via grounders at home against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie earned another go in the rotation after two solid starts. He held Seattle to one run in six innings on Thursday but got a no-decision. Despite allowing three runs in 11 innings, Houston has lost both games Devenski has started.
away_pitcher_note: Since moving back to the rotation in place of the injured Carlos Carrasco, Bauer has given up six runs on eight hits in 9 2/3 innings. On Thursday, he gave up three runs in 5 2/3 innings, ending with four strikeouts and two walks.

home_pitcher_note: Fister has arguably been Houston’s most consistent pitcher in 2016, The veteran righty has posted four straight quality starts, including 6 1/3 innings of three-run ball vs. Seattle on Friday, when he exited with a shutout intact.
away_pitcher_note: Salazar has limited batters to a .342 OPS and has 17 strikeouts against three walks in his past two starts (14 2/3 innings). On Friday vs. the Royals, the righty struck out nine and walked one in 7 2/3 shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Price is in the midst of perhaps the toughest stretch of his career, giving up six runs or more in three of his last four starts. The lefty thinks some mechanical adjustments to keep his arms and legs in sync through his delivery will help.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel is looking for his first win since April 15, when he beat Tigers with eight scoreless innings. In four starts since, he’s 0-3 with a 6.94 ERA, allowing 34 hits in 23 1/3 innings. Opponents are hitting .351 in that span.

home_pitcher_note: The knuckleballer has gone at least six innings and given up two runs or less in all six of his starts. Wright pitched his first complete game last time out -- a three-hitter against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: This will be the season debut for McCullers, who suffered shoulder soreness in the spring and was brought along slowly. He had a strong rookie season a year ago, going 6-7 with a 3.22 ERA in 22 regular season games.

home_pitcher_note: Buchholz labored a bit in his last start, giving up four runs while throwing 86 pitches over five innings. The righty is 1-2 with a 5.48 ERA in four starts at Fenway this season.
away_pitcher_note: After giving up five earned runs in one-third of an inning in his April 6 season debut at Yankee Stadium, McHugh has gone 4-2 with a 4.24 ERA in six starts (team is 4-2), including 3-0 with a 3.57 ERA in his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: The righty will make a second straight start, serving as a placeholder for Eduardo Rodriguez or Joe Kelly. His last time out, O’Sullivan earned his first win in the Majors since May 17, 2015, allowing 12 hits and four runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Rookie right-hander has been terrific in his first three career starts, posting a 2.55 ERA while allowing 16 hits and striking out 15 batters in 17 2/3 innings. The Astros have scored three runs total for him in those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Rodon takes the mound for the series and homestand opener, working on six days' rest with two team off-days in between. Rodon is looking for his first win since April 13, when he hurled six scoreless innings against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel is looking for his first win since April 15. He’s gone 0-4 with a 7.98 ERA in his last four starts, allowing 44 hits in 29 1/3 innings. He’s 6-12 with a 4.52 ERA in 20 starts on the road since the start of last season.

home_pitcher_note: After a brilliant start to the season, with six hits and one run allowed over 18 1/3 innings, Latos has leveled off a bit. He remains unbeaten but has allowed 13 runs on 25 hits and eight walks in his last 15 1/3 innings covering three starts

home_pitcher_note: McHugh has been dominant of late, going 2-1 with a 1.53 ERA over his last three starts, but has yet to face the Rangers this season. He struck out eight and allowed one run over six innings to pick up a win over the Angels on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez was called up from Triple-A Round Rock on Friday and allowed three runs in seven innings in a loss to the A's. He faced the Astros twice in a row in June (once in relief) and allowed two runs and six hits over 9 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Morton returns to Minute Maid Park, where he has thrived in his first season with the Astros. The veteran right-hander is 7-3 with a 3.65 ERA in 13 home starts in 2017, with 85 strikeouts in 79 innings. Opponents are batting .214 off him in Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Harvey will make his first start since June 14 after spending more than two months on the DL because of a stress injury to his right shoulder. He is 4-3 with a 5.25 ERA in 13 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock has held opponents to two or fewer earned runs in nine of his past 12 starts, going 7-1 with a 3.10 ERA during that stretch, which included one relief appearance. This will be his third career start against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Lugo, whose Shreveport, La. hometown is approximately a four-hour drive from Houston, will start Game 2 against the Astros. He threw just 70 pitches last time out in his return from the disabled list, and should be good for around 85 this time.

home_pitcher_note: Fiers was roughed up in his last outing, allowing eight runs over four innings against the Rangers at Tropicana Field on Tuesday, closing a 1-4 month in which he posted a 7.44 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Flexen’s walk rate has more than quadrupled since he advanced from Double-A to the Majors, jumping from 1.5 per nine innings in the Minors to 6.6 per nine with the Mets. The trend is worsening; over his last 21 innings, Flexen has walked 16 batters.

home_pitcher_note: The 27-year-old from Nicaragua has been Seattle’s best starter of late, going 1-1 with a 2.25 ERA in his last four outings. This will be his first time facing Houston since 2015 when he beat them in two starts for the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel began the season scorching hot before landing on the disabled list with a neck injury. Since his return to the rotation on July 28, he hasn’t been quite the same, going 2-3 with a 5.35 ERA in seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Miranda is Seattle’s only rotation member to make every start this year, but he’s 1-2 with a 6.84 ERA over his last 10 outings and gave up four homers in 4 1/3 innings at Baltimore his last start. He’s 0-2, with a 5.70 ERA in four starts vs. Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander takes the mound for his highly anticipated Astros debut after looking motivated by trade talks since mid-July. The six-time All-Star went 5-2 with a 2.41 ERA and 78 strikeouts in 67 1/3 frames across his final 10 starts for the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie’s last appearance for Seattle was Aug. 11 when he gave up 6 hits and 4 runs in 1 2/3 innings against the Angels.  He was limited to 4 innings in his last three starts in Tacoma and will likely be asked to do the same in this one.
away_pitcher_note: McCullers hasn’t pitched since July because of back discomfort, and it’s possible those issues were affecting him before landing on the DL. After going 6-1 with a 2.48 ERA through the end of May, he’s gone 1-2 with a 6.25 ERA in June and July.

home_pitcher_note: Cotton made it through just four innings in Seattle on Saturday, allowing four runs on seven hits, including three home runs. He has yielded 24 home runs in 114 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh has allowed two runs or fewer in all but two of his eight starts this year, including the past four. The Astros have won each of his past three starts, with McHugh going 2-0 with a 0.54 ERA and a 1.08 WHIP in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Gossett made 89 pitches in 3 2/3 innings in Seattle on Sunday. He allowed three runs on seven hits, including a homer, and walked a career-high five with five strikeouts. It was the second time in his last five starts he didn't complete four frames.
away_pitcher_note: In nine starts since July 19, Morton is 4-3 with a 3.62 ERA, striking out 61 batters and walking 15 in 54 2/3 innings in that span. The Astros are 13-8 in games he’s started.

home_pitcher_note: Mengden returns from Triple-A Nashville for his first big league start since June 3. He was placed on the Minor League disabled list shortly thereafter with a right oblique strain and went 0-3 with a 6.09 ERA in five starts with the Sounds.
away_pitcher_note: This could be Peacock’s final start before being moved to the bullpen with the the addition of Justin Verlander and the activation of Lance McCullers Jr. As a starter, Peacock is 7-2 with a 3.34 ERA, but he is winless in his past five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Graveman took a hard-luck loss earlier this season in Houston, when he tossed six innings of two-run ball. The righty owns a 3.99 lifetime ERA against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: In eight starts since returning from the disabled list (he missed eight weeks with a neck problem), Keuchel is 3-3 with a 4.86 ERA. He’s coming off a gem, holding Seattle to two runs in 7 2/3 innings on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander makes his first start at Angel Stadium since April 25, 2016. His last start, Sept. 5 in Oakland, was his first outing since suffering a right biceps strain in his season debut on April 5.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander was solid in his Astros debut, allowing one run in six innings Sept. 5 in Seattle. The right-hander struck out seven, extending his streak of striking out at least six to 10 straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty tied a season-high with nine strikeouts in his last start, a six-inning outing at Oakland on Sept. 6 in which he took a loss after giving up three runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers will return to the rotation in place of Lance McCullers Jr., who was scratched with arm fatigue. Fiers, who worked one inning in the bullpen Friday in Oakland, went 1-5 with a 7.90 ERA in his last eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran righty took his 13th loss of the season in his last start on Sept. 8 in Seattle, where the Mariners roughed him up for four runs on six hits in 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Peacock allowed two runs in 5 2/3 innings in Oakland Sept. 9, at one point striking out six consecutive batters. He struck out eight on the day, giving him 124 strikeouts in 94 2/3 innings as a starter this year.

home_pitcher_note: Morton has pitched five innings in each of his last three starts, which includes a win over the Mets on Sept. 2 and a loss at Oakland on Saturday. He’s pitched well at home this year, going 8-3 with a 3.64 ERA in 14 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Paxton returns to the mound for the first time since being placed on the disabled list on Aug. 11. He'll face one of the toughest lineups, but one he's had success against this season -- he owns a 0.45 in three starts against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty has made nine starts since missing eight weeks with neck soreness, going 3-4 with a 5.02 ERA in that span. Only four of those starts have been quality, including Sept. 4 at Seattle when he allowed two runs in 7 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The 27-year-old has been Seattle’s most consistent starter over the past month, going 1-1 with a 2.45 ERA and an opponents' batting average of .192 in 6  starts. He gave up 2 runs and 4 hits in 6 frames to Houston in a no-decision Sept. 4 in Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander makes his home debut after starting twice on the road following his Aug. 31 trade from the Tigers. He's 2-0 with a 0.64 ERA and 16 strikeouts in 14 innings in his first two starts, including eight one-hit innings Tuesday vs. the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old rookie replaces Ariel Miranda and will make his second start since July after throwing six innings of one-hit, one-run ball in relief against Texas. Moore’s last spot start was against Houston on Sept. 6 (6 innings, 3 hits, 2 runs).

home_pitcher_note: McHugh starts for the first time since Sept. 8, when he left after three innings in Oakland with a broken fingernail. This will be McHugh’s 10th start since coming off the disabled list, where he spent the first 3 1/2 months.
away_pitcher_note: Giolito is fresh off his third quality start in four tries. He has had success with his changeup and curveball this season, holding opponents to a .160 batting average on those pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock has gone 8-2 with a 3.22 ERA in 19 starts this year, averaging 11.35 strikeouts per nine innings. In the last week, manager A.J. Hinch has said Peacock is a viable candidate to make the Astros’ postseason rotation.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Shields threw 69 percent of his pitches for strikes en route to his first road win since May 12, 2016.

home_pitcher_note: After missing eight weeks with neck discomfort, Keuchel is 4-4 with a 4.66 ERA in 10 starts since returning, including a win over the Mariners on Saturday. The White Sox rocked him on Aug. 8 for 10 hits and eight runs in four innings in Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie turned in his second consecutive quality start Friday and had good control of all four of his pitches. Manager Rick Renteria said he was happy to see Fulmer maturing and becoming more relaxed.

home_pitcher_note: Since joining the Astros, Verlander has a 0.86 ERA (two earned runs in 21 innings) with 26 strikeouts and only three walks in three starts. On Sept. 12, he tossed eight scoreless innings vs. the Angels, giving up one hit, walking one and fanning nine
away_pitcher_note: In his third start off the disabled list, Richards allowed just three baserunners on a pair of hits and a walk while fanning seven over five innings. He said after the game that he’s ready to up his workload to 100 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: In three September starts, Morton has posted a 2.81 ERA (five earned runs in 16 innings), with 24 strikeouts to just five walks. In two starts this season vs. the Angels, he has a 2.70 ERA (three runs in 10 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Norris will make his second start of the season on Saturday in place of the injured Andrew Heaney, beginning another bullpen game for the Angels. Norris worked two-plus scoreless innings in his last spot start against the Rangers on Sept. 15.

home_pitcher_note: McCullers returns to the rotation to make just his second start since July. After missing a month with a back injury, the All-Star started in Seattle on Sept. 6 before again missing time due to arm fatigue.
away_pitcher_note: Since he was tagged for six runs in two-plus innings against the Rangers on Sept. 1, Skaggs has settled in to post a 2.45 ERA over his past three starts. He’s yielded just five runs through 18 1/3 innings in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Cashner will be making his sixth start against the Astros this season, the most by any opponent. He is 4-4 with a 2.71 ERA in 12 home starts. That's the third lowest ERA at home by a Rangers pitcher since 1994.
away_pitcher_note: After missing one start with a detached fingernail, McHugh returned in fine form on Tuesday, allowing one run in a win vs. the White Sox. In his 18 Sept./Oct. starts with the Astros since 2014, he is 14-0 with a 2.83 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is 7-0 with a 3.50 ERA in 10 starts at home. That's tied for the most wins at home by a Rangers pitcher without a loss in one season in club history. Hamels threw seven scoreless innings in win over the Astros on Aug. 11.
away_pitcher_note: Poor run support led to Keuchel’s loss in his last start after he allowed two runs in six innings. With nine walks in his last three starts, including a bases-loaded walk, command has been an issue. The lefty is 2-1 with a 3.38 ERA vs. Texas in 2017.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez allowed four runs, three earned, in his last start against the A's and is 0-4 with a 6.80 ERA in his last six starts and four relief appearances. He is 0-2 with a 4.58 ERA in four games against the Astros this season.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander has simply been outstanding in Houston, going 4-0 with a 0.64 ERA in four starts. He gave up just one hit and no runs in seven innings vs. the Angels on Friday, striking out six.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty has caught fire down the stretch. In September, Rodriguez is 2-1 with a 1.78 ERA in four starts. At Fenway Park this season, Rodriguez is 2-1 with a 3.81 ERA. He has faced the Astros once in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Peacock’s 12 wins surpass his career total of 11 entering the season. After beginning the season in the bullpen, Peacock has flourished as a starter, going 9-2 with a 3.21 ERA with 133 strikeouts in 106 2/3 innings pitched.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander had been on a roll until struggling mightily in his last three starts, giving up 14 runs over 11 1/3 innings. Fister is 3-6 with a 4.93 ERA in nine appearances at Fenway this season.
away_pitcher_note: Set to make his final regular-season start, Morton has already set a career high in wins (13). In his past 11 starts, he’s 6-3 with a 3.00 ERA and 76 strikeouts in 66 innings. He has a 1.09 WHIP in that span with 10.36 strikeouts per nine.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty’s velocity has dipped in his last two starts, and it showed last time out, when he was hammered for seven hits and five runs over two-plus innings. Pomeranz is three innings from matching the career-high of 170 2/3 he logged  in 2016.
away_pitcher_note: Considering he’s only made two starts since July 30 because of injuries, McCullers’ final regular-season start will determine his availability for the ALDS. He gave up two runs in 3 1/3 innings Sunday against the Angels in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: The Red Sox can now afford to give ace Chris Sale extra rest after clinching their second consecutive AL East title. That means the right-hander Velazquez gets his first start since June 19 as Boston turns its eye toward October.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh could miss out on the Astros’ ALDS rotation despite solid work after missing the first 3 1/2 months of the season with an arm injury. In his last six starts, he’s 4-0 with a 2.12 ERA and 29 hits allowed in 29 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander was tremendous following his trade from the Tigers to the Astros, posting a 1.06 ERA in five starts, striking out 43 and walking just five. His ERA is 3.39 in 16 career postseason starts.
away_pitcher_note: The ace has made 180 starts in his career, but this is the first time he’ll have the thrill of pitching in the postseason. He didn’t face the Astros during his 308-strikeout season, but Sale is 5-1 with a 1.31 ERA lifetime against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel posted a 2.00 ERA over his final three starts of the regular season. In three career appearances (two starts) against the Red Sox, he has a 9.88 ERA. He has made three career postseason appearances, all in 2015, posting a 2.57 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Pomeranz makes his first career playoff start after appearing out of the bullpen for the Red Sox in last year’s postseason. The southpaw faces the Astros for a second straight time after limiting them to one run in six innings on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Fister has made eight career postseason starts, but this will be his first since 2014 with the Nationals. The right-hander posted a career high in strikeout rate with 21.2 percent in 2017, but also had a career-high 4.88 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Peacock won his only start against Boston this season, going five innings and allowing two runs at Fenway Park on Sept. 28.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello’s season was a far cry from his Cy Young campaign a year ago, but he could help Sox fans forget that with a solid start in Game 4. Porcello has a 5.82 ERA in three career postseason starts with Boston in 2016 and Detroit in 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Morton won his only start against Boston this season, going  5 1/3 innings and allowing two runs at Fenway Park on Sept. 29.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel tossed 5 2/3 innings against the Red Sox in ALDS Game 2, giving up one run on three hits, walking three and striking out seven in Houston's 8-2 victory at Minute Maid Park. The left-hander has a 0.96 ERA in three career postseason starts.
away_pitcher_note: In a topsy-turvy season for the righty, the Yankees got the dominant Tanaka when they needed him in Game 3 of the ALDS. Now he will test his mix of pitches on the road, where he was markedly worse (6.48 ERA to 3.22 at home) this season.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander was almost unhittable after joining the Astros on Aug. 31, posting a 1.06 ERA in five starts to finish the regular season. He started ALDS Game 1 vs. Boston, allowing two runs on six hits over six innings, walking two and fanning three.
away_pitcher_note: Baseball’s hardest-throwing starting pitcher seemed to throw even harder in Game 4 vs. Cleveland, topping out at 99.6 mph in the seventh inning. Houston roughed Severino up for nine runs over 7 2/3 innings in his two starts against it this year.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia’s slider helped him outpitch Corey Kluber twice in the ALDS. The left-hander has now gone 9-5 in 20 postseason starts, including 7-2 as a Yankee, with a career 4.46 ERA in October.
away_pitcher_note: Morton gets the nod for Game 3. He held the Red Sox to two runs on seven hits over 4 1/3 innings in the ALDS while striking out six and walking two. His 3.62 ERA during the regular season was his lowest since 2013.

home_pitcher_note: Gray’s command was as off over his last two starts -- his regular-season finale vs. Tampa Bay and his Game 1 start vs. Cleveland -- as it has been all season. The righty allowed three runs on four walks and three hits in his ALDS loss to the Tribe.
away_pitcher_note: McCullers, who was an All-Star for the first time this season, has faced the Yanks twice this year and gave up three runs over 11 1/3 innings with 13 strikeouts and two walks. He's been much more effective at home (3.04 ERA) than on the road (5.14).

home_pitcher_note: Outside of a tough-luck fourth inning, Tanaka was excellent in a six-inning ALCS Game 1 effort against the Astros. The right-hander has allowed just two earned runs in his last three starts while striking out 25 in 20 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel pitched seven shutout frames and struck out 10 batters on Friday in a Game 1 win in Houston. Keuchel was the winning pitcher in the 2015 AL Wild Card Game at Yankee Stadium, with six shutout innings pitched.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander will start for the Astros in Game 6 against the Yankees in Houston. The veteran right-hander tossed a complete-game gem in Game 2, holding New York to just one run on five hits while striking out 13 batters.
away_pitcher_note: Severino says he’s healthy after being removed from his Game 2 start for precautionary reasons, and he tossed a bullpen session Wednesday without issue. Prior to his early exit, he allowed one run and two hits in four innings vs. Houston.

home_pitcher_note: The Astros will turn to Morton to start the winner-take-all Game 7 with a trip to the World Series on the line. He struggled in Game 3 against the Yankees, who tagged him for seven runs in 3 2/3 innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: With a trip to the Fall Classic on the line, Sabathia will start on regular rest after pitching six scoreless frames against the Astros in Game 3. The veteran is 10-0 with a 1.69 ERA in 13 starts following a Yankees loss this season.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw will start Game 1 for the Dodgers on regular rest after helping his club wrap up the NLCS with six innings of one-run ball vs. the Cubs on Thursday. Kershaw owns a 3.63 ERA through 17 1/3 innings this postseason.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel owns a stellar 1.78 ERA in his five career postseason starts and went 1-1 in the Astros’ ALCS triumph over the Yankees while allowing four runs in 11 1/3 innings. The 2015 AL Cy Young Award winner is set to make his first World Series start.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty makes his first World Series start after pitching in independent ball as recently as 2015. While Hill didn't exceed five innings in either of his first two postseason starts, he allowed only three runs on six hits combined in those outings.
away_pitcher_note: The 2017 ALCS MVP held the Yankees to one earned run over 16 innings to record one of the finest single-series pitching performances ever, but Verlander hopes to shake off his career 7.20 ERA in three World Series starts with the Detroit Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: McCullers returns to the Astros' starting rotation after firing four scoreless innings of relief in ALCS Game 7 vs. the Yankees. The right-hander allowed one run on three hits with nine strikeouts in 10 innings throughout the entire ALCS.
away_pitcher_note: Darvish has been the postseason sidekick to Clayton Kershaw the Dodgers envisioned when they acquired him, racking up 14 strikeouts and allowing only two runs in two starts this October. Game 3 marks Darvish’s first World Series appearance.

home_pitcher_note: Morton rebounded from a tough-luck loss in ALCS Game 3 to help propel Houston to a Game 7 victory with five stellar innings to open the contest. The veteran righty permitted two hits and struck out five to earn his first career postseason win.
away_pitcher_note: Wood took the loss in Game 3 of the NLCS against the Cubs, his only previous start this postseason, allowing three runs in 4 2/3 innings. He won his only prior start against the Astros, tossing seven scoreless on June 25, 2014.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel allowed six hits and three runs, including two homers, over 6 2/3 innings in a Game 1 loss to the Dodgers. Keuchel is 2-2 with a 3.00 ERA in four playoff starts overall in 2017.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw was incredibly efficient in a World Series Game 1 win, needing just 83 pitches to rack up 11 strikeouts in seven innings of one-run ball. The lefty is 3-0 with a 2.96 ERA in four starts this postseason, with 27 K’s in 24 1/3 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Hill gave up one run on three hits, walking three and striking out seven over four innings in Game 2. Overall this postseason, he's posted a 2.77 ERA (four earned runs in 13 innings), with seven walks and 19 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Game 6 will go to Verlander, who's 4-0 with a 2.05 ERA in five games (four starts) this postseason. He allowed three runs on two homers in six innings in Game 2. He's 9-0 with a 1.53 ERA in 10 games (nine starts) since joining Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Darvish stumbled in Game 3 after entering the World Series on a hot streak, yielding six hits and four earned runs while recording only five outs and one swinging strike. He'll try to get back on track in a winner-take-all Game 7.
away_pitcher_note: McCullers got the win in Game 3, allowing three earned runs in 5 1/3 innings while striking out three. He has used his curveball even more often lately, throwing it for more than two-thirds of his pitches over his last two outings.
