home_pitcher_note: Hamels is making his fourth Opening Day start and his second for the Rangers. He was 7-2 with a 4.35 ERA in 12 starts at home last year. He was 1-1 with a 5.40 ERA in two starts vs. the Astros last year and is 7-4 with a 4.19 ERA in 16 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander is making his 10th Opening Day start in the past 11 years and first for the Astros. He started on Opening Day for the Tigers from 2008-14 and 2016-17. After being traded to the Astros last August, Verlander went 5-0 with a 1.06 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Fister pitched for the Astros in 2016 and is 1-1 with a 3.44 ERA in three career starts against them. Fister is 1-5 with an 8.73 ERA in seven starts at Globe Life Park. That's his highest ERA in any ballpark in the American League.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel, who started on Opening Day for the Astros the past three seasons, went 14-5 with a 2.90 ERA in 23 starts last year for the Astros. That was his third career season of double-digit wins, an ERA under 3.00 while throwing at least 20 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Moore makes his first start for the Rangers after being acquired from the Giants in the offseason. He is pitching against the Astros for the first time since 2016 and is 3-0 with a 1.42 ERA in three career starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: McCullers earned his first career All-Star nod last year, going 7-4 with a 4.25 ERA in 22 starts. He became the second-youngest pitcher (23) in club history to make the All-Star Game last year after going 7-2 with a 3.05 ERA in the first half.

home_pitcher_note: Minor is making his first Major League start since 2014 when he was with the Braves. He missed all of 2015-16 and was used in relief by the Royals in '17. He made three appearances against the Astros last season, allowing one run in in 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cole, who started on Opening Day for the Pirates last year and was traded to Houston in January, went 12-12 with a 4.26 ERA in 33 starts last season, allowing 55 walks and 31 homers while striking out 196 batters in 203 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Morton is coming off his best season in the big leagues, going 14-7 with a 3.62 ERA in 25 starts. He also was terrific in the playoffs, winning Game 7 of the ALCS against the Yankees and Game 7 of the World Series in relief against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: The righty re-signed a one-year deal with Baltimore this spring and will look to bounce back from a tough season. Tillman pitched to a 7.84 ERA in 2017, including a demotion to the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander threw six scoreless innings on Opening Day against the Rangers on Thursday, allowing four hits and two walks while striking out five batters. In six regular starts since being traded to the Astros on Aug. 31, he had a 0.90 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Wright gets the nod in Houston, after winning the Orioles' fifth-starter spot out of camp. He faces a tall task in the Astros and going up against Justin Verlander.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel allowed seven hits and three runs in six innings Friday against the Rangers in his regular-season debut. In 11 starts at home last year, Keuchel was 6-3 with a 2.26 ERA with a 0.95 WHIP. He's 36-21 with a 2.94 ERA in his career at home.
away_pitcher_note: Bundy made his first Opening Day start on Thursday and tossed seven scoreless innings with five hits, one walk and seven strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: McCullers returns to the mound after striking out 10 batters in 5 1/3 innings in his first start of the season Saturday against the Rangers in Arlington. He allowed just three baserunners his first two trips through the lineup.
away_pitcher_note: It’s only his second start, but Perdomo could be pitching for his job. After a disappointing 2017 campaign, Perdomo struggled in his first outing. He led the NL in ground-ball rate last year but recorded just one groundout Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Cole will be making his home debut after a dominant performance in his Astros debut Sunday in Arlington. He struck out 11 batters -- one shy of his career high -- and allowed two hits and one run in seven innings against Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Acquired from the Yankees in a December trade, Mitchell couldn’t locate his curveball in his Padres debut on Monday. The Rockies, sitting on his fastball, scored five times in five innings. They put at least two men on base in every frame.

home_pitcher_note: Morton makes his second straight start at home. He started the Astros' opener on Monday and threw six scoreless innings, allowing three hits, two walks and striking out six batters. He’s 12-7 with a 3.99 ERA in 22 regular-season starts in Houston.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander grinded his way to six innings of three-run ball in his return to the Petco Park mound Tuesday night. Ross struggled to miss bats, however, recording just two strikeouts and three swings and misses.

home_pitcher_note: Lynn struggled in his debut, giving up five runs over four innings against the Pirates while tying a career high with six walks. All five runs came in the first inning, when he surrendered a grand slam with two outs.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander makes his third start of the season, his second on the road. Verlander has an eight-game regular-season winning streak, including 6-0 with a 1.38 ERA while with the Astros. He’s 17-9 with a 3.15 ERA all time against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Odorizzi had trouble with his command while pitching in a snowy and windy game against the Pirates on Wednesday. The right-hander lasted 4 1/3 innings, allowing three runs on five hits and three walks with two strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel has allowed four earned runs and 12 hits in 11 innings across his first two starts of the season. Keuchel hasn’t pitched in Minnesota since June 6, 2014, throwing six scoreless innings during his breakout season.

home_pitcher_note: Gibson escaped some trouble in the early innings in his last outing against the Mariners on Thursday, but Seattle pushed his pitch count up early and he threw just 4 1/3 innings in a no-decision. He is 1-0 with an 0.87 ERA in two starts this season.

away_pitcher_note: Odorizzi was pitching well against the Indians until running into trouble in the sixth, and he allowed three runs in 5 1/3 innings. He's pitched better of late, as he had a 3.77 ERA in six August outings.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty returns to action after taking a liner off his pitching wrist on Aug. 29. In his seven starts sine the All-Star break, Price is 4-0 with a 1.62 ERA. He beat the Astros on June 2, allowing three runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: After losing three consecutive starts from July 30 to Aug. 10, Cole has gone 3-0 with a 3.57 ERA in his past four starts. His 243 strikeouts are the seventh-most in Astros history for a single season.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez was electric in his return to action, striking out 12 over 5 2/3 innings in a win over the White Sox. This will be the first time Rodriguez has pitched at Fenway since he severely sprained his right ankle there in a July 14 start.
away_pitcher_note: Morton will be activated from the DL to start vs. Boston in his first start since hurling 4 2/3 innings vs. the A’s on Aug. 28. Morton has gone 13-3 with a 3.14 ERA in 26 starts (152 frames) and has missed just one start with shoulder discomfort.

home_pitcher_note: The righty bounced back from a mini-slump with a strong effort against the Braves last time out, allowing one run with one walk and five strikeouts over five innings. Porcello gave up three runs (two earned) in 6 1/3 innings vs. Houston on June 3.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel has gone 8-2 with a 2.57 ERA in 94 2/3 innings in his past 15 starts after going 3-8 with a 4.45 ERA in 85 innings in his first 14 starts. The Astros are 17-12 in games he’s started, winning 11 of his last 14 times on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano gets another rematch with his old club after ending a four-month winless drought Monday with five innings and five strikeouts against the White Sox last Tuesday. He tossed three innings of one-run ball against the Astros in Houston in July.
away_pitcher_note: A little over a year since he made his last start for the Tigers, Verlander returns to Comerica Park as a visitor. Since joining the Astros in a waiver-wire deal last August, the seven time All-Star is is 19-9 with a 2.47 ERA and 291 K's.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has built some late-season momentum with one earned run over 11 innings in his past two starts. He’s 2-3 with a 3.09 ERA in seven career starts against the Astros, striking out 37 batters against six walks over 43 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Valdez has been strong over his first four big league starts, allowing one earned run or fewer each time out. The rookie hurler has earned a decision in each outing, going 3-1 with 11 hits and 10 walks allowed, along with 15 K's, over 19 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: What looked like a lost season for Norris has the makings of a strong finish after the left-hander racked up 14 strikeouts over 9 1/3 innings in two starts back from the disabled list. He’s pitching effectively without his usual mid-90s fastball.
away_pitcher_note: Cole and teammate Justin Verlander are neck and neck for the AL strikeout lead. Cole is also one of only three AL pitchers with an opponent batting average under .200 (.197).

home_pitcher_note: The lefty has gone 7-2 with a 2.81 ERA in his past 13 starts, with 10 quality starts in that span. He’s 3-3 with a 4.00 ERA in six career starts against Arizona, and 12-7 with a 3.89 ERA in 23 career September starts.
away_pitcher_note: Ray has pitched well in his last four starts, going 2-0 with a 1.59 ERA over that stretch while holding opposing batters to a .171 average. Two starts ago, Ray struck out 10 Padres in 6 1/3 scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching for the first time in a week, Morton is seeking a career-high 15th win. Morton’s 27 starts and 157 innings pitched this year are just shy of his career highs of 29 and 171 2/3, respectively, set in 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Godley had a rough outing in his last start, when he allowed five runs on seven hits in four innings in a loss to the Rockies. Over his last two starts -- both losses -- he has allowed nine runs in nine innings.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander is 4-1 with a 3.82 ERA in his past five starts, including a win over Detroit on Monday in his return to Comerica Park. He needs five innings to reach 200 for the season and is 11 strikeouts shy of his career high.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke allowed a pair of runs in the first inning in his last start, against the Rockies, then settled in nicely. The right-hander has had some trouble with the long ball this year, giving up a career-high 27 home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Valdez will make his fifth start since replacing the injured Lance McCullers Jr. in the rotation. The left-hander struggled in his last outing, a no-decision at Detroit, allowing four earned runs, five hits and four walks over four innings.
away_pitcher_note: The 33-year-old is 8-4 with a 3.45 ERA in 24 starts since moving into the rotation and his 146 2/3 innings are a career high already with several outings still to go. He’s 1-1 with an 8.31 ERA in five games against Houston, including three starts.

home_pitcher_note: The hard-throwing rookie will be making his second big league start and fourth appearance, his first against the Mariners. James has struck out 17 batters in 10 2/3 innings and is a candidate to make the postseason bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Leake has allowed just one earned run with 11 hits, one walk and nine strikeouts over 13 innings in his last two outings, both wins over the Orioles and Angels. He’s 0-2 with a 5.00 ERA in three starts against the Astros this season.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel has not missed his turn in the rotation all season and will be making his 32nd start. In his last outing, a no-decision vs. Arizona, Keuchel tossed his 20th quality start, tied for third-most in the league.
away_pitcher_note: The Mariners will roll out an "opener" as part of a bullpen day. Festa, who has been with Double-A Arkansas all year, where he’s worked to a 2.76 ERA, will make his first big league start. As a September callup, the righty has 2 2/3 scoreless IP.

home_pitcher_note: Cole has already struck out a career-high 260 batters in 187 1/3 innings, putting him on pace for his second consecutive 200-inning performance. Cole is 4-0 with a 3.48 ERA in his last six starts, but only two of those have been quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Heaney allowed two runs over five innings in his last start on Saturday against the Mariners. He is 3-1 with a 1.95 ERA in six career starts against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander needs one strikeout to set a single-season best of 270 and has already topped 200 innings for the 11th time. He’s thrown seven innings in each of his last three starts, going 3-0 with a 1.71 ERA and 29 strikeouts in 21 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Barria allowed three runs over five innings in his last start on Sunday against the Mariners. The 22-year-old rookie is 1-1 with a 2.81 ERA in three starts against the Astros this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Astros are spacing out Morton’s final few starts with at least one week of rest in between, meaning he’ll pitch Sunday on eight days of rest. He’s made four starts since Aug. 22, going 3-0 with a 5.66 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Skaggs tossed three hitless innings against the A’s on Tuesday in his first start since returning from the disabled list. He is 4-3 with a 2.96 ERA in nine career starts against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Estrada continues to be plagued by lingering back issues, but it hasn't been enough to force him to miss any recent starts. In his last outing, he battled through pain to allow just one run over six innings during a start vs. Baltimore.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel will try to rebound from a tough loss as well as taking a first-inning comebacker to the head in his previous outing, which ended in a 9-0 loss to Seattle. Keuchel lasted five innings, giving up five runs and six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Gaviglio has allowed just two earned runs in each of his last two starts, but he also has completed six innings just once since July 25. Gaviglio's last win as a starter was back on Aug. 21 against the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie will be making his third start of the season. Last time out, James did not give up a run, limiting the Mariners to four hits over 5 1/3 innings in picking up the win.

home_pitcher_note: Reid-Foley was expected to be shut down after his last start, but an injury to Aaron Sanchez means he will take the mound for one final time in 2018. The rookie is only expected to throw a few innings as Toronto keeps an eye on his workload.
away_pitcher_note: Reliever Chris Devenski (2-2, 4.12 ERA) will get the start for the Astros in what should amount to a bullpen game for Houston. The Astros are expected to use relief pitchers throughout the game, including Lance McCullers Jr., who returns from the DL.

home_pitcher_note: Hess will get one more chance to make a good impression in his rookie season. The righty allowed two runs over five innings, but he got a no-decision in the loss to the Yankees on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: In his final start of the regular season, Cole will be looking to extend his career-high strikeout total (272) and will likely surpass 200 innings. He’s 5-0 with a 3.54 ERA in his past seven starts with 65 strikeouts in 40 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hess will get one more chance to make a good impression in his rookie season. The righty allowed two runs over five innings, but he got a no-decision in the loss to the Yankees on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: In his final start of the regular season, Cole will be looking to extend his career-high strikeout total (272) and will likely surpass 200 innings. He’s 5-0 with a 3.54 ERA in his past seven starts with 65 strikeouts in 40 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The righty will try to end his disappointing season on a high note on Saturday in the opener of a doubleheader against Houston. He surrendered four runs over three innings in a loss to the Red Sox on Monday, needing 90 pitches to get there.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander makes his final case for the 2018 American League Cy Young Award in his final start of the regular season. He threw six scoreless innings in a no-decision on Saturday. He’s already set a career high with 280 strikeouts this season.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old Ramirez has a 6.07 ERA in 16 appearances (11 starts) with the Orioles this season. He'll be pitching on an extra day of rest following Thursday's rainout.
away_pitcher_note: Keuchel, who has completed only five frames in each of his past two starts, looks to add to his 200-plus-innings season. He enters with a 4.82 ERA in September.

home_pitcher_note: Yacabonis has a 6.00 ERA in 11 games (six starts) in 2018, and the rookie right-hander will get a chance to leave on a high note on Sunday afternoon against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Morton is pitching for the first time since he left his Sept. 23 start after one inning when his velocity was down and was diagnosed with a sore shoulder. He'll likely only pitch a few innings in the regular-season finale.

home_pitcher_note: It's no surprise that the defending champs will open the ALDS with their ace. Verlander was sensational last postseason, going 4-1 with a 2.21 ERA and 38 strikeouts in his six outings to help lead Houston to its first World Series title.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a stellar campaign (20-7, 2.89 ERA) that has him in the hunt for a third career AL Cy Young Award, Kluber will take the ball for the Tribe in the opener against Houston. The ace is 4-2 with a 3.54 ERA in eight career playoff starts.

home_pitcher_note: After a breakout first season, in which he formed one of the league's best 1-2 punches with Justin Verlander, Cole gets the ball for Game 2 of the ALDS. Cole made three playoff starts as a Pirate in 2013 and '15, going 1-2 with a 3.94 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Carrasco is slated to take the ball in Game 2 of the ALDS in Houston, where he has a 1.17 ERA with 28 strikeouts vs. three walks in 23 innings in his career. In Game 3 of the ALDS against the Yankees last year, Carrasco logged 5 2/3 shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Over his final 10 starts of the regular season, Clevinger posted a 1.94 ERA with 68 strikeouts vs. 22 walks in 60 1/3 innings, while seeing his velocity tick up. The righty has a 6.17 ERA in two starts against Houston this season.
away_pitcher_note: The 2015 AL Cy Young winner will take the mound when the ALDS moves to Cleveland for Game 3. Keuchel has a solid postseason track record, having gone 4-2 with a 3.24 ERA in eight career playoff starts with the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Sale gets a rematch against Justin Verlander, who beat him in Game 1 of the 2017 ALDS, when Sale allowed seven runs. Sale is coming off an excellent series against the Yankees -- he won Game 1 and pitched a scoreless inning in relief in Game 4.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander tossed 5 1/3 innings in Game 1 of Houston's AL Division Series sweep of the Indians, giving up two earned runs on two hits and two walks while striking out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Price's postseason woes continued in Game 2 of the ALDS, when the Yankees homered off him twice and knocked him out after 1 2/3 innings. Price is now 0-9 with a 6.03 ERA in 10 career playoff starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cole fanned 12 over seven innings of one-run, three-hit ball in Game 2 of the ALDS in his first postseason start since 2015 when he was with the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Keuchel continued his career-long playoff success with a solid start in Game 3 of the ALDS against the Indians, allowing two runs in five innings before the Astros added 10 late runs to secure the sweep. He has a 3.28 ERA in nine postseason outings.
away_pitcher_note: The righty was stellar in his playoff debut in Game 3 at Yankee Stadium last Monday, allowing five hits and a run over seven frames while walking none and striking out five. In five career starts against the Astros, Eovaldi is 1-1 with a 3.19 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Morton is set to make his 2018 postseason debut on Wednesday, as the Astros didn't need him in the three-game sweep of the Indians in the ALDS. He started against Boston in ALDS Game 4 last season, allowing two runs in 4 1/3 innings in a Houston win.
away_pitcher_note: The sinkerballer came up big in Game 4 of the ALDS vs. the Yankees for his first career playoff win, allowing four hits and one run over five frames. Porcello pitched a stellar eighth inning of relief to aid the Sox in their Game 2 win of the ALCS.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander will make his 24th career playoff start as he tries to shut down Boston and force Game 6. He tossed six innings in a Game 1 victory, limiting the Red Sox to two runs on two hits. Over his last six postseason starts, he has a 2.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Price saw his team win a postseason game in which he started for the first time in his career in ALCS Game 2. He was warming in the bullpen during the last two innings of Boston’s Game 4 victory.

home_pitcher_note: As the reigning American League Cy Young Award winner, Snell is set to make the first Opening Day start of his career. Snell is coming off a 2018 season where he became a first-time All Star and led the AL with 21 wins and a 1.89 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his third second-place finish in the AL Cy Young voting, Verlander will make his 11th Opening Day start, second in a row with Houston. The former AL Cy winner and league MVP owns a 3-1 record with a 4.03 ERA in his Opening Day career.

home_pitcher_note: Morton will make his first start with the Rays against the Astros, whom he helped win a World Series in 2017. Morton signed a two-year deal with the Rays this offseason, after two years in Houston, where he was an All-Star in 2018.
away_pitcher_note: In his first season in Houston, Cole finished fifth in the AL Cy Young race after going 15-5 with a 2.88 ERA, 276 K's in 200 1/3 innings, a .198 opponents’ average and a 1.03 WHIP. He led the AL by averaging 12.4 strikeouts per innings as a starter.

home_pitcher_note: Glasnow finished 2018 with the Rays, posting a 1-5 record and a 4.20 ERA in 11 starts, but displayed his potential on the mound. The matchup against the Astros will be the first chance for Glasnow to test his new delivery during the regular season.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh returns to the rotation in 2019 after pitching out of the bullpen full-time last year. He appeared in 58 games in ’18 and ranked fourth among AL relievers with a 1.99 ERA and 0.91 WHIP. He won 19 games in ’15.

home_pitcher_note: Yonny Chirinos will make his first start of the season as the Rays go for the series win over the Astros. In 18 appearances last season as a reliever and a starter, Chirinos finished 5-5 with a 3.51 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty makes his Astros debut after going 5-2 with a 2.57 ERA in 16 regular-season starts for the Brewers last year. He made four starts for the Brewers in the playoffs, allowing two earned runs and 10 hits in 14 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly has missed the last two seasons while recovering from Tommy John surgery and is pitching for the first time since Sept. 26, 2016. He is 1-2 with a 4.96 ERA in three career starts and two relief outings vs. the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Peacock, who went 10-2 with a 3.22 ERA in 23 starts in his 2017 breakout year, pitched mostly in the bullpen last year. He appeared in a career-high 61 games (60 in relief) and posted a 3.46 ERA and struck out 96 batters in 65 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Miller came back from Tommy John surgery and made four starts for the D-backs last summer, going 0-4 with an 11.40 ERA. He was shut down in July because of elbow inflammation but made one relief outing at the end of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander had a typical outing in his Opening Day start vs. the Rays, striking out nine over seven innings, allowing one run on three hits. He had a 2.03 ERA over five starts vs. the Rangers last year and has a career 2.82 ERA in 25 starts vs. Texas.

home_pitcher_note: Minor opened the season vs. the Cubs and allowed six runs in 4 2/3 innings in a 12-4 loss. He allowed five hits, two walks and struck out three. Minor made five starts against the Astros last season and was 1-1 with a 4.88 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Cole took the loss despite pitching well in his 2019 debut, striking out 10 over six innings vs. the Rays. An error led to three unearned runs and a loss for Cole, who has a 2.25 ERA in five career starts vs. Texas.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh struck out nine in his first start on March 30 at Tampa Bay, holding the Rays to two runs over five innings in a 3-1 loss. Last year, McHugh made six appearances in relief against the A's, allowing two runs (one earned) over 7 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The A's believe that they'll get a big year from Montas, who has learned to complement his high-90s fastball with a slider and a splitter. On Sunday against the Angels, he maintained a shutout for 5 2/3 innings before yielding Kole Calhoun's homer.

home_pitcher_note: Miley yielded three earned runs over six innings with six strikeouts in his Astros debut on March 31 at the Rays. The left-hander, who was acquired as a free agent late in the offseason, will be making his first home start as an Astro on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe Brooks, 28, is a late bloomer. Oakland's No. 5 starter certainly pitched like a new man in his regular-season debut on Monday night, surrendering two hits while pitching the first six innings of the A's 7-0 decision over the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock made his first start in more than a year in his 2019 debut April 1 in Arlington. Peacock, who has moved between the bullpen and rotation with the Astros, has plenty of experience vs. the A's. In his career, he has faced them 23 times.
away_pitcher_note: Fiers is filling the role of No. 1 starter nicely. Despite not being overpowering he threw six shutout innings in back-to-back outings against the Angels and Red Sox while improving to 7-3 with Oakland in 13 games (12 starts) since last season.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander is coming off a rough outing against the Rangers on Tuesday in which he gave up four runs and six hits in four innings while struggling to find his control. That came after a solid seven-inning outing against the Rays on Opening Day.
away_pitcher_note: Tanaka has been excellent through two starts, recording 12 strikeouts without a walk. He logged a quality start in his only outing against the Astros last year after starting twice against them in the 2017 postseason.

home_pitcher_note: Cole has pitched well in his first two starts. He’s struck out 19 batters and walked only three in 12 innings across two starts. He’s faced the Yankees only once previously, coming in 2014 while he was a member of the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Loaisiga took a no-decision in his first start of the year, limiting the Tigers to one run on one hit over four innings on April 3. The Nicaraguan-born rookie is facing the Astros for the first time.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh threw six innings of one-run ball in his second start of the season Friday against the A's, allowing three hits and three walks while striking out four batters. He's 5-0 with a 1.18 ERA in his last eight starts at Minute Maid Park (since 2016).
away_pitcher_note: Paxton faced the Astros four times last year as a Mariner, going 4-0 with a 2.05 ERA. He's 7-3 with a 2.89 ERA in 12 career starts vs. Houston. Through two starts as a Yankee, he has recorded 14 strikeouts against three walks over 11 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Mariners have scored 22 runs as LeBlanc has won his first two starts against the Red Sox and White Sox, including six innings of two-run ball in Chicago his last outing. LeBlanc was 1-1, 6.75 ERA in 6 games (4 starts) vs. Houston last year.
away_pitcher_note: Miley makes his third start for the Astros, this one against one of his former teams. He made 19 starts for the Mariners in 2016 before being traded to the Orioles. He pitched 5 2/3 innings in a 6-0 victory over the A’s in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez lasted just one inning in his last start -- on his 33rd birthday -- before being KO'd by a bout of stomach flu after allowing 3 hits and 2 runs to the Royals. He's 1-4 with an 8.56 ERA in six starts vs. Houston over the past 4 years.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander is looking for his second victory after back-to-back no-decisions against the Rangers and Yankees. His body of work with the Astros is nothing short of amazing: 28-11 with a 2.51 ERA in 51 appearances, including the postseason.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzales, a 27-year-old lefty, is just the second pitcher in Mariners history to earn the win in his first four starts of a season, and he'll try to make it five against the Astros, who proved a tough matchup for him in 2018 (0-2, 12.91 ERA in two starts).
away_pitcher_note: Cole is looking for his first victory of the season despite three straight solid appearances. He has pitched at least six innings in all three starts, including a seven-inning, three-run performance against the Yankees on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Marco Estrada (0-1, 4.87) is trying to rebound from a shaky start in the series opener against the Orioles. He allowed six runs in four innings. The Orioles rolled to a 12-4 victory in that game.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh is off to an excellent start this season, having struck out nine in two of his three starts, including his last outing against the Yankees when he generated 13 swings and misses on his blossoming slider.

home_pitcher_note: Montas has been sharp in three starts this season, posting a 3.18 ERA over 17 innings. He hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in any outing, and he has given up only 13 hits while issuing four walks.
away_pitcher_note: Miley labored through 41 pitches in the first inning on Friday in Seattle, but he rebounded to limit the Mariners to only one run in the frame. He allowed just three earned runs, marking his 19th straight start in which he’s limited an opposing team to that mark or fewer.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly was sharp for five innings against the Athletics on Friday, allowing one run on three hits before allowing a single and two walks in the sixth. He allowed one run over three innings in an April 1 start against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander was superb against the stingy Mariners on Saturday, striking out a season-high 11 batters while showing complete command of his entire arsenal. Verlander generated 10 punchouts within the zone, and he registered one on each of his four pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Sampson allowed seven runs over four innings in his first start against the Athletics on Sunday. He had a six-inning relief effort against the Astros on April 1, when he allowed one run on four hits and two walks with three strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Cole has lasted at least six innings and allowed three earned runs or fewer in each of his four outings, explaining why his record is so misleading. Opponents are batting .185 off Cole, who has struck out 36 in 25 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Miller allowed four runs in 4 1/3 innings in his last start against the Angels. He pitched against the Astros on April 2, allowing two runs on six hits and five walks in 3 2/3 innings. It was his first start against them since 2013.
away_pitcher_note: McHugh thrived in his last outing, allowing two hits in six shutout innings at Oakland last Tuesday. Though opponents tend to load their lineup with left-handed batters against McHugh, he has limited lefties to a .125 batting average so far. McHugh has a strikeout-to-walk ratio of nearly 4:1 (27-7) overall.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock has been reinserted into the starting rotation after moving to the 'pen 10 days earlier when the Astros went with a four-man rotation. He made two relief appearances last week after going 1-0 with a 4.63 ERA in two starts to open the season.
away_pitcher_note: Odorizzi will be trying to win his second straight start. He gave up one run in 5 2/3 innings versus Toronto last Wednesday. He has a 3-1 all-time record vs. the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Miley is coming off his best start of the season, allowing two runs on four hits last Wednesday in Oakland. Three of his four starts have come on the road. He threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings in his only home start April 6.
away_pitcher_note: Pineda pitched well in his first three starts, posting a 2-0 record. But he struggled in his last start, giving up six runs on seven hits in 3 2/3 innings in Thursday's loss to the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander won back-to-back starts on the Astros' road trip, allowing two runs on five hits while striking out 19 over 13 innings in wins vs. Seattle and Texas. He matched a season high with seven innings in last Friday's win over the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Stewart is expected to be recalled from Triple-A Rochester to make his second career appearance -- and first start -- in his hometown of Houston. Stewart allowed eight earned runs in 12 innings across three starts for Rochester this season.

home_pitcher_note: Cole is coming off the worst start of his career on Saturday at Texas, where he allowed a career-high nine runs (eight earned) over 4 1/3 innings. It was the first time with Houston he had allowed more than four runs.
away_pitcher_note: Bauer was frustrated by his last outing, when his pitch count reached 120 after just 6 1/3 innings. The right-hander fanned a season-high 10 batters -- the 20th double-digit strikeout game of his career -- and allowed two runs on three hits.

home_pitcher_note: McHugh is coming off the worst start of his career on Sunday at Texas, where he allowed a career-high 10 runs (nine earned) in 3 1/3 innings. McHugh had been terrific prior to that outing, going 3-0 with a 1.96 ERA in his first four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kluber's start last Friday was pushed to Saturday after rain postponed Cleveland’s series opener against the Braves. The Tribe's ace took the mound in Game 1 of the doubleheader, allowing four runs on five hits with eight strikeouts in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Peacock returned to the rotation on Monday against the Twins after a pair of relief outings and allowed three runs and six hits in five innings. He began the year in the rotation and made two starts before being temporarily moved to the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: Bieber will look to bounce back from his worst start of the year, when he allowed seven runs (five earned) on five hits through just 2 1/3 innings against the Braves. Saturday will mark the 23-year-old's first start against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Miley, who retired the final 15 batters he faced in his most recent start Tuesday against the Twins, has made 21 consecutive starts allowing three earned runs or fewer. That's baseball's longest such streak by a traditional starting pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: After a quick scare in his last start, Carrasco will return to the mound Sunday. He was pulled after four frames vs. Miami to get a precautionary MRI on his left knee that came back negative. He allowed two hits and fanned four before his departure.

home_pitcher_note: After starting the season 0-2, Odorizzi has won his last two decisions. He has allowed a combined three earned runs in 11 1/3 innings in those outings. He also faced the Astros in his last start April 21, when he allowed two runs in 5 2/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: Cole was in unfamiliar territory during his first World Series start during the Astros' 5-4 loss in Game 1. away_pitcher_note: Sheffield has faced the Astros just once in his career, but was impressive in that outing, holding Houston to one earned run across six innings with four strikeouts last season.

home_pitcher_note: Javier hasn't allowed a run in his last two starts, throwing five scoreless innings April 8 against Oakland and again Thursday against the Angels. He struck out nine on Thursday and lowered his WHIP to 0.87.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzales turned in his finest outing of the season against the Dodgers last Tuesday, holding the World Series champions to one run over seven innings with six strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke has four quality starts in five outings, which accounts for the only quality starts thrown by an Astros pitcher this year. That included eight scoreless innings in a 1-0 win over Seattle on April 17.
away_pitcher_note: Dunn has made tangible progress with his command after a rough season opener, yielding just three walks with 11 strikeouts in his previous two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia has allowed five runs and 11 hits in 15 innings with 14 strikeouts. In most recent start April 20, he allowed two runs and three hits and struck out six in 5 2/3 innings. He threw 26 pitches in relief Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Kikuchi has been roughed up of late after a solid start to the season, allowing five earned runs in 4 2/3 innings in his previous start against the Red Sox on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing just one run in 10 2/3 innings over his past two outings pitching after an opener, Yarbrough will get the start in the Rays' series opener against the Astros. He held Houston to two runs in five innings in ALCS Game 3 last October.
away_pitcher_note: McCullers Jr., a Tampa native, makes his first road start since April 3, when he allowed one run in five innings at Oakland. He's allowed two or fewer runs in three of his four starts, and is coming off his first quality start of '21.

home_pitcher_note: After following an opener last time out, Fleming will start in his first matchup against the Astros since last year's ALCS. Fleming has been excellent in his first three outings this year, allowing two runs on 10 hits over 14 2/3 efficient innings.
away_pitcher_note: Urquidy has allowed two earned runs or fewer in three of his first five starts, with his only quality start coming Monday when he held Seattle to two runs and five hits in six innings. The Astros are 2-3 in games he's started.

home_pitcher_note: Back from the COVID-related IL, Hill takes the mound for the series finale vs. Houston, which he last faced in the 2017 World Series. Hill, then a Dodger, allowed two runs in 8 2/3 innings over two starts against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Javier enters the game on a 17-inning scoreless streak, which has spanned three starts. He threw five scoreless innings April 8 and April 22, and threw a career-high seven scoreless, with two hits, on Tuesday against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Germán was sharp over seven scoreless innings in his most recent outing at Baltimore, picking up his second victory in as many starts. The righty is 0-1 with a 3.86 ERA in three career appearances (one start) vs. Houston.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke is coming off his shortest outing of the year, a four-inning outing against the Mariners in which he allowed four earned runs. The veteran doesn't have a great track record against the Yankees, owning a 5.05 ERA in 15 career games (12 starts).

home_pitcher_note: Montgomery took a no-decision in his most recent start, holding the Orioles to two runs and six hits over five innings in a 4-3 loss. Montgomery tossed only 74 pitches in that outing, down from a season high of 89.
away_pitcher_note: Despite getting stuck with the tough-luck loss, Garcia continued to impress in his most recent start against Seattle, when he pitched five innings of one-run ball with six strikeouts and no walks.

home_pitcher_note: Cole's 62 strikeouts are the second most of a Bombers hurler in any calendar month, behind only Ron Guidry's 64 in June 1978.
away_pitcher_note: McCullers is coming off his best start of the season, holding the Rays scoreless over seven innings with a season-high nine strikeouts. In his last two starts, McCullers has allowed just two earned runs over 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Following his first scoreless start of 2021, Urquidy will open the series with Toronto. Urquidy has relied more on his slider than in the past (career-high 21.6% usage), but he threw a season-high 31 changeups Saturday against the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Stripling is competing to keep his spot in the rotation and one key will be establishing his curveball. Having thrown 70 pitches in his return from the IL on Sunday, Stripling should be able to push deeper against the Astros if he avoids trouble Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Javier takes a seven-start unbeaten streak into this game, which includes three wins in five outings this season. He will be looking to pitch deeper into games, as he has only worked past the fifth inning in one start this year.
away_pitcher_note: Matz was frustrated to leave his last start and has hit a rough patch after opening the season 4-0 with a 2.31 ERA. He feels that he's just an adjustment away, though, and is eager to bounce back after allowing two home runs his last time out.

home_pitcher_note: The past two starts have been bumpy for Greinke, as he has allowed seven runs in eight innings in a pair of no-decisions. He has only faced Toronto once in the past decade: In 2019, Greinke threw six scoreless innings to earn a win.
away_pitcher_note: Pearson was on track to start for Triple-A Buffalo on Sunday, but instead, he will make his season debut for the Blue Jays. Pearson, MLB Pipeline’s No. 10 prospect, allowed one run and struck out eight in his Minor League debut on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia is making his third consecutive start after bouncing between a starter role and the bullpen the first four games. He's 0-2 with 3.86 ERA as starter, allowing two runs in 3 1/3 innings against the Angels April 5. He's seeking his first MLB win.
away_pitcher_note: Guerra is starting a bullpen game for the Angels, with starting pitcher José Suarez available in relief. Guerra last pitched on Saturday, throwing a scoreless inning of relief against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: McCullers is 1-0 with a 2.37 ERA and 1.11 WHIP in his last three starts. He hasn't pitched at home since he held the Angels to two runs on three hits in six innings on April 25. He's 20-8 in 47 career starts at home.
away_pitcher_note: Ohtani makes his first start on the mound since throwing four shutout innings in at home against the Rays on May 5. It is still yet to be announced whether he will pull double duty as a hitter as well, which would be his third time doing so this year.

home_pitcher_note: Urquidy has flourished in his last three starts, going 3-0 with a 1.80 ERA and 0.75 WHIP. He's allowed four earned runs in 20 innings in those starts, with all four runs coming off solo homers.
away_pitcher_note: Andrew Heaney threw 6 2/3 shutout innings vs. the Rays in his last start, striking out 10 batters and walking one before his night was over. The last time he faced the Astros, Heaney gave up two hits and one run in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Javier didn't allow a run across three consecutive starts April 8-April 27 (17 innings) but has struggled in his past two. He's given up eight runs, including three homers, in 10 1/3 innings (6.97 ERA) vs. the Rays and Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz will have an opportunity to square off against the team that originally drafted him. The right-hander has been a dependable innings-eater for the Rangers thus far, pitching at least five frames in all but one start.

home_pitcher_note: After going 2-1 with a 2.76 ERA and a 1.10 WHIP in 32 2/3 innings in his first five starts, Greinke has posted an 8.25 ERA and a 1.83 WHIP in his last three starts. He's thrown exactly four innings in each of those starts.
away_pitcher_note: Benjamin will make just his second MLB start (and first this year) after being recalled from Triple-A Round Rock on Thursday. He started the season on the Opening Day roster in the bullpen, but struggled with his command, resulting in being optioned to the alternate site. He pitched five shutout innings during his start at Round Rock's Opening Day, allowing just four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia, who's pitching in place of the injured Jake Odorizzi, is still seeking his first Major League win. In five starts this year, he's 0-2 with a 4.13 ERA and 1.13 WHIP, but the Astros are 0-5 in games he's started.
away_pitcher_note: Dunning struck out a career-high 10 batters in his last outing, holding the Mariners to two runs across five innings. Dunning, who has allowed five runs (four earned) across 10 2/3 innings in his past two starts, will make his first career appearance against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: McCullers has blossomed into an ace, going 2-0 with a 2.00 ERA and 0.96 WHIP in last four starts. He's allowed six runs and 15 hits in 27 innings in that span, including eight innings of one-run ball Tuesday against Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Gibson didn't have his sharpest stuff in his last outing against the Giants, but he still put together a quality start, tossing six innings of one-run ball. Gibson was brilliant against Houston last season, allowing no runs in two starts across 15 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Manaea is looking to bounce back from a rough outing against the Red Sox in which lasted just two-plus innings and allowed seven runs on 10 hits. The left-hander fared well in his last start against Houston on April 9, limiting the Astros to one run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Javier has had a rough May thus far. In three starts, he has allowed 11 earned runs across 17 1/3 innings (5.71 ERA). Javier took a step in the right direction last time out, allowing three runs across seven innings with six strikeouts against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Montas has been sharp in the month of May, now 3-0 with a 3.12 ERA over three starts. He limited Houston to one run over six innings in a win on April 10.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke bounced back in his last start, allowing three runs across seven innings after being limited to four innings in each of his three previous outings. The veteran held the A's scoreless across six innings in their first meeting of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Irvin continues to perform as the top starter on the staff. Getting through 6 2/3 innings of one-run ball against the Twins his last time out, the left-hander leads the rotation with a 3.02 ERA and has posted a 1.89 ERA over his last six outings.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia picked up his first career win last time out, holding the Rangers to one run across five innings despite having noticeably diminished velocity. In his last four starts, Garcia has allowed eight earned runs across 20 innings (3.60 ERA).

home_pitcher_note: The 33-year-old Gibson will make his second straight start against a tough Astros lineup. He allowed just two runs Sunday at Houston but got a no-decision in the Rangers' 6-2 loss. His 2.32 ERA ranks third in the American League.
away_pitcher_note: This will be the MLB debut for Ivey, who's Houston's No. 9-ranked prospect. Ivey has a 3.19 ERA in 52 Minor League games, including 38 starts. He appeared in two games at Triple-A Sugar Land this season, posting a 7.11 ERA in 6 1/3 innings

home_pitcher_note: Lyles' roller-coaster season hit a peak Monday when he had one of his best starts in a win over the Yankees, going six innings and allowing just one run. He'll look to stay hot against the Astros after the Rangers were swept by their in-state rivals last week.
away_pitcher_note: McCullers has been terrific in his last five starts, going 2-0 with a 1.64 ERA. He's struck out 36 batters and given up three homers in 33 innings in that span, with the Astros going 4-1.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz has struggled with letting poor innings spiral into poor outings. He allowed five runs in the fourth inning against the Yankees on Tuesday after starting with three innings of shutout ball. He'll need to keep his command and velocity under control to get back on top against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: After going 3-0 with two earned runs allowed in 20 2/3 innings in his four starts, Javier has gone 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA in his last four starts. He struck out 27 batters in 23 1/3 innings, but has given up seven home runs.

home_pitcher_note: After throwing four innings in three consecutive starts, Greinke has won his last two starts, allowing four earned runs and 11 hits in 15 innings. The Astros are 8-2 in his starts. Greinke won 51 games for the Dodgers from 2013-15.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw had a quality start in his last outing against the D-backs, allowing two runs across six innings with eight strikeouts. For Kershaw, this will be his first time pitching at Minute Maid Park since the 2017 World Series.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia picked up his first and second Major League wins in his last two starts, throwing five innings each time. He's allowed 29 hits in 40 innings, but eight of those hits have been home runs. He has a 2.53 ERA at home.
away_pitcher_note: Bauer embraced the role of heel in his first outing against the Giants since joining the Dodgers, striking out 11 across 6 1/3 innings and playing to the booing crowd as he walked off the field. Bauer has been phenomenal in May, compiling a 1.14 ERA across 23 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Valdez is scheduled to be activated and make his first start of 2021. The lefty, who fractured his left ring finger on March 2, made two rehab starts at Triple-A Sugar Land, throwing four scoreless innings on 54 pitches on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: Lamet has made three relief appearances before his return to the rotation. It's unclear how much leash he'll be given, as the Padres have treated him with caution this year, but Lamet's three innings and 41 pitches on Saturday were both season highs.

home_pitcher_note: Odorizzi is set to rejoin the rotation for the first time in a month. He made two rehab starts at Triple-A Sugar Land, throwing 77 pitches in 4 2/3 innings on Monday. He suffered a right pronator strain in his third start on April 24.
away_pitcher_note: Darvish has been the Padres' MVP this season, with their offense in flux due to IL stints and their bullpen heavily taxed. Darvish is averaging more than six innings per start, and the Padres have won nine of his 10 outings.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke, who surpassed 3,000 career innings on Tuesday, has six quality starts in 11 outings this year. The Astros are 8-3 in games he's started. He's thrown at least six innings in each of his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Snell has yet to put it all together as a Padre, but his stuff has been excellent. He simply hasn't been in the strike zone enough, having compiled 28 walks in 44 innings. Snell has faced the Astros in the playoffs five times to the tune of a 2.51 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Urquidy returns from the IL (inflammation in right shoulder) to make his first start since May 12. He’s 3-0 with a 1.52 ERA in his last four starts, walking just two batters and allowing four earned runs and 15 hits in 23 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: All eyes will be on the struggling lefty when he opens the road trip. After a strong start to the season, Rodriguez has had a rough May, going 1-3 with a 6.48 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia's ERA (2.92) and WHIP (1.02) are the best among Astros starters this year, though the Astros are 3-7 in games he's started. He's 3-0 with a 1.69 ERA and 0.94 WHIP in his last three starts, during which the Astros are 3-0.
away_pitcher_note: The lanky righty continues to roll. In his past six starts, Richards is 4-1 with a 2.65 ERA. He's battled a bit with control of late, walking four in each of his past two starts. Richards is 5-5 with a 3.02 ERA in 16 career games (13 starts) vs. the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Valdez gave up one run and two hits in four innings in his first start of the season Friday against the Padres. He missed the first two months of the season after breaking his left ring finger in his first start of the spring on March 2.
away_pitcher_note: Pivetta is unbeaten since joining the Red Sox last season, going 8-0 with a 3.53 ERA in 12 starts. The righty struck out nine over six innings in his last start against the Braves to get the win. This is his first career start in Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Odorizzi suffered a right pronator strain in his third start of the season April 24 and missed a month. He returned Saturday vs. the Padres and held them to one run and three hits in 5 1/3 innings, throwing 87 pitches in his best start.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty has been Boston's top starter in recent weeks, going 3-1 with a 2.43 ERA in his past six starts. Pérez is 1-1 with a 2.91 ERA in four road starts this season. He has pitched well in Houston in his career, notching a 2.97 ERA in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ryu's last outing was him at his best, even if it didn't show in the stat line, as he battled ugly weather in Cleveland to earn the win. With a 2.62 ERA and some of the best control he's ever shown, the ace is absolutely locked in.
away_pitcher_note: After going four innings in three consecutive starts, Greinke is 2-1 with a 2.45 ERA and 0.77 WHIP in his last three starts, two of which were eight innings. He struck out 17 batters and walked only four in his last 22 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Stripling carried a 7.20 ERA into late May, but has allowed just one run over 12 innings in his last two starts. Serious adjustments have been made, so now it's a matter of sustaining this newfound success.
away_pitcher_note: Urquidy returned from an 18-day stint on the injured list and held the Red Sox to one run and three hits in six innings Monday. He's 4-0 with a 1.53 ERA and 0.71 WHIP in his last five starts, during which the Astros are 5-0.

home_pitcher_note: Matz's up-and-down season has settled in at a 4.22 ERA, but the lefty is never far from a standout performance. Keep an eye on his velocity, which ticked up as he struck out 10 back on May 25.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia is 4-0 with a 1.57 ERA in his last four starts, throwing a career-high seven innings of one-run ball against the Red Sox in his last start. His 2.60 ERA through his first 10 career starts is seventh-lowest in Astros history.

home_pitcher_note: After going 0-2 in his first seven starts, Pérez has now won each of his past four. He has a 1.82 ERA in that span, with 20 strikeouts vs. six walks. Pérez is coming off a season-high 7 2/3 innings against the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Valdez's third start since coming off the injured list with a broken left ring finger suffered March 2. Valdez held the Red Sox to one run on five hits in seven innings in his previous start Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Eovaldi has 14 strikeouts over his past two starts, which marks his highest strikeout total in a two-start stretch this season. His home ERA, which is 4.47, is more than two runs higher than his road ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Odorizzi has made two starts since coming off the IL (right pronator strain) and has been hit and miss. He held the Padres to one run in 5 1/3 innings May 29 and gave up three runs in three innings against Boston on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: The past five starts have not been kind to Rodriguez, who has racked up a 7.92 ERA in that span. That includes a loss to Houston in which he allowed six runs on seven hits in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke threw his first complete game in more than four years when he held the Blue Jays to one run and six hits Friday in Buffalo. In his last five starts, he's 4-1 with a 2.37 ERA and 0.84 WHIP in 38 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ober will start in place of Matt Shoemaker, who allowed nine runs in one-third of an inning in his last outing. Ober has allowed five runs in eight innings across two MLB starts, including a one-run effort against the Royals last time out on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: After a remarkable month of May (1.14 ERA in four starts), Urquidy did not fare well in his first start of June. Urquidy allowed a season-high six earned runs in 4 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Berríos allowed four runs in six innings in his last start. He's yielded four or fewer runs in his past 23 outings, dating back to July 30, 2020. He last faced the Astros in the 2020 AL Wild Card Series, when he allowed one run in five frames in Game 2.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia has been steadily effective all season, but now that success is showing up in the win column. After an 0-3 start through his first seven games, he's won each of his past five. He has just two homers allowed in his past 29 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Pineda cruised through four innings last time out against the Yankees, before he allowed two runs in the fifth, including a bases-loaded walk. He has allowed seven runs over his past two starts after posting a 2.62 ERA through his first eight.
away_pitcher_note: Valdez is finally healthy and built up, and his abbreviated work this season has been stellar. His past two outings have both lasted into the eighth inning, and he has 22 strikeouts versus just four walks in 18 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: McCullers will be activated from the IL for his first start since May 22. The righty, who developed fluid in his bursa sac in his right shoulder after his last outing, will be followed by Jake Odorizzi in a "piggyback" outing.
away_pitcher_note: The Rangers' ace returns to the mound to face the divisional rivals on regular rest. It'll be just his third start since coming off the injured list. In the two previous outings, he pitched a combined 11 1/3 innings, allowing just two earned runs on nine hits with 10 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke followed up a complete-game effort against the Blue Jays on June 4 -- his first in four years -- by allowing four runs on seven hits in three innings last Thursday in Boston. The Astros are 10-4 in games Greinke has started this year.
away_pitcher_note: Lyles has been on a roll lately, lowering his ERA from 7.39 at the beginning of May to 5.37 heading into the matchup with the Astros. In his only other start against the in-state rivals this season, Lyles surrendered four runs in six innings as he took a no-decision at home.

home_pitcher_note: Urquidy gave up three solo homers last Friday against the Twins, but those were the only blemishes in his seven-inning effort. He’s allowed 11 homers and issued 11 walks in 62 innings this season and has five quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cease will be making his second career start against Houston but his first appearance at Minute Maid Park. Cease has allowed two runs and struck out 17 over his last 12 innings in two starts, both coming vs. Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia had won five consecutive starts before giving up four runs (three earned) in 4 1/3 innings in last Saturday's loss to the Twins. As a starter, he has a 3.14 ERA and 1.06 WHIP in 57 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Rodón took a no-hitter into the seventh inning Sunday against the Tigers but settled for his third start this season of allowing no hits or one. Rodón has recorded 97 strikeouts over 66 2/3 innings while allowing only 39 hits.

home_pitcher_note: Valdez was dominant in his most recent outing at Minnesota on Sunday, holding the Twins to two runs (one earned) over seven innings. He has a 1.27 ERA and a 0.94 WHIP over three starts in June.
away_pitcher_note: Lynn had a personal six-game winning streak come to an end Monday night in a 5-2 setback to the Rays. Lynn fanned eight over six innings, marking his fifth start this season with eight or more strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: McCullers was on a pitch count in his start vs. Texas on Tuesday, his first since returning from the IL with shoulder soreness. He yielded an earned run over 4 1/3 innings, using only a fastball-changeup combination in the first three innings.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander pitched the first seven years of his career for the Astros but will be making his first start as a visitor at Minute Maid Park. Lance McCullers Jr., whom Keuchel referred to as being like his son, starts for Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Akin endured a strange start his last time out, allowing eight runs while stiking out seven over 5 2/3 innings against Cleveland. The rookie lefty pitched to a 2.63 ERA over his first three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Jake Odorizzi opens the series at Camden Yards for the Astros. The right-hander is 3-3 with a 4.83 ERA in 10 career starts in Baltimore.

home_pitcher_note: López allowed five runs while not completing five innings in each of his past two starts, both losses. The right-hander has an 8.36 ERA in three June outings.
away_pitcher_note: Zack Greinke hasn't pitched through six innings in his last two starts after going the distance with a complete game on June 4. He looks to return to form and deliver a quality start against the Orioles.

home_pitcher_note: Eshelman returned to the Majors and held the Blue Jays to one run in 4 2/3 innings in his first start. He is filling in for rookie left-hander Bruce Zimmermann, who remains sidelined with left biceps tendinitis.
away_pitcher_note: Jose Urquidy hasn't faced the Orioles in his three-year career, but he will get his first shot in the series finale at Camden Yards.
